## What this changes

The CUDA GLM-5.3-Flash family loads `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local` (#1015, #593 (4)) as stored, with bf16 activations into every layer, and serves it, checked here at TP=2 and TP=3 on v1.1.1 and in part at TP=2 on v1.1.2 ("On v1.1.2" above). It is on v1.1.2 (`4ff78441`), rebased from v1.1.1 (`b10231b9`), which has #1021 to #1024's host foundations, and uses #907 and #908 from 1.1.0.

Beyond the summary's first table:

- Formats: before it computes a width, an element count or a block count, the classifier refuses an empty shape (`EmptyShape`) and one whose arithmetic would overflow (`ShapeOverflow`). A checkpoint without recipes (`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`) reads as before; a read of config.json that fails after the entry has admitted it, or an allocation that fails while the loader reads the recipes, is an error, never a config without recipes, whose modules would then read as declared NVFP4. A test now holds `csfLinear`'s own refusal of an empty weight (`EmptyShape`); in the loader the classifier refuses such a weight first.
- FP8 lanes: on a GPU without thread block clusters (before sm_90) the lane would sum an FP8 projection's K slices as partials in memory, and the GLM forward holds none, so the loader now refuses such a projection by name before packing or uploading it; before, matmul refused it only at the first forward, after the whole load. On sm_90 and later, GB10 included, the lane never needs those partials, so the check refuses nothing.
- The routed experts' `csf_32x2_v1` scales need no kernel change. The MTP layer's bf16 routed experts are still quantized on the GPU.
- KDA's MXFP8 `[q | k | v]` and bf16 `[f_a | g_a | b]` each run into their columns of the stack's rows. A bf16 widening of an MXFP8 tensor (the MTP layer's `kv_b`, and `lm_head` for the draft head's quantizer) loads only when every value is exact in bf16, else it is refused by name.
- On prompt rows a bf16 head runs as before; the MXFP8 `lm_head`'s K split depends on the shape alone, so a row's bits do not depend on how many rows run with it.
- The `_f32w` forms run the bf16 forms' arithmetic on a float32 weight, so a float32 norm adds no launch. On 1.1.0's tree the bf16 forms compiled to the same SASS as before (all 40 `glm_glue` functions on sm_121, nvcc 13.0), and `hc_finish_f32w` is checked against a float64 reference through Sinkhorn.
- Docs: `docs/quantization.md`'s "GLM-5.3-Flash's float32 tensors on CUDA" names the float32 tensors the loader keeps in float32 and says that any other, which 1.1.1 rounded to bf16, loads as bf16 only when bf16 holds every value and is otherwise refused by name. The rule refuses none of the NVFP4 and FP4-Local checkpoints' float32 tensors, and the EXL3/TR3 checkpoint's float32 tensors are all of the kinds kept in float32.
- Vision: the tower's quantized projections give fp32 or bf16 outputs; bf16 projections and the attention products stay on cuBLASLt, and a tower without recipes (the NVFP4 checkpoint's) reads as before. `tools/glm_vision_ref.py` reads such projections back to the float32 values their codes and scales hold.
- `glm-loader-gate` compares at TP 1, 2 and 3 against a separately opened checkpoint (csf decoded by the gate itself; NVFP4, MXFP8 and block-FP8 tiles from the host packers). `TF_GATE_LAYERS`, `TF_GATE_WORLDS` and `TF_GATE_RANKS` narrow a real checkpoint's run, and a run that gates no rank or compares no upload fails. `TF_GATE_TAMPER` flips one upload's bit, and the run passes only red as planted: every gated rank reports that upload, and nothing else.
- Capabilities: the family lists `modelopt-mixed` (FlashNext's name for ModelOpt's MIXED_PRECISION) beside `modelopt-nvfp4`, and the refusal of another quantization names NVFP4 and MIXED_PRECISION.

On v1.1.2 the registrations sit beside 1.1.2's and `test-kernel-contract` passes; the GPU run was not retaken.)

The MXFP8-head prompt-row test cannot build against 1.1.1's `b16.matmul` head. items.title: qwen CUDA: TF_DRAFT_NODES above 15 serves; a stop or cancel lands between prompt chunks
items.body:
Two serving fixes for the Qwen3.5 CUDA family, found on one RTX 5090 (Qwen3.8-27B MLX 4-bit + DFlash2, `--kv-cache fp8`, a 262,144-token window).

**`TF_DRAFT_NODES` above 15 failed every request.** The server started, then every round failed with `BadDraftFrame`. The planner asks a grown tree for its node budget as the hold's depth, and `cuda_draft_frame.stage` refused any depth past `block - 1`, a chain's limit. Grown trees (block 16, no planner lanes) now stage up to `tree.nodes()` (at most the 64-row window); chains and 8-row blocks keep `block - 1`. `TF_DRAFT_NODES=24` and `32` serve with every reply unchanged. A host test in `qwen35_draft_frame_host.zig` covers both limits and fails without the fix.

**A stop or a cancel waited for the whole prompt pass.** The CUDA prompt pass never asked `Stream.isCancelled`, so the host's halt (which joins the lane thread) waited until a long prefill finished: with a 230k-token prompt in progress the server stopped draining and did not exit, and a client that left mid-pass kept the GPU until the pass ended. The pass now asks before each chunk, as the other backends do; its cache goes back to the pool and is reset when taken again. With a 75,616-token prompt, SIGTERM 15 s into the pass exits after 23 s (the 20 s drain, then the next chunk) instead of 134 s, the request ending "server restarting: retry shortly"; a streaming client killed mid-pass ends its request within a second (`client-left`).

The Metal `qwen3_5` backend's prompt loop (`backend.zig`) has the same missing check; that is left to a Metal change.

Checks: `zig build test`, `test-kernel-contract`, `test-golden`, `fuzz-cortheon`, the Flash Next gate test, `zig fmt` and the lean check pass, as do the `test-qwen35-*` host steps.

items.title: MiMo-V2.6-Flash on CUDA: EXL3, DFlash, two GPUs (stacked on #703)
items.body:
MiMo-V2.6-Flash on the native CUDA engine, one GPU or two DGX Sparks as tensor-parallel ranks, with the pack's DFlash drafter. Proposal and discussion: #725.

**Stacked on #703** (at 59af121b): tensor parallelism and RoCE come from it, and the port follows its method. Only the last three commits belong to this PR:

1. `7fc5afd8` **lanes: a geometric draft depth whose round cost grows with context.** About 100 lines in `core/lanes`, plus a host test. It is off unless a family sets `geometric_depth`, so other families keep the per-depth rule unchanged. It can become its own PR if you prefer.
2. `51db34af` **MiMo-V2.6-Flash on CUDA: EXL3, DFlash, two GPUs.**
   - `zig/src/families/mimo_v2`, the kernels in `zig/kernels/cuda/mimo_v2`, and the EXL3 bindings in `zig/src/cuda/exl3.zig`. The EXL3 kernels are copies of the Python engine's, each with its source blob in the header.
   - Registration in `native/cuda.zig`. A TP family is admitted on its rank's share of the weights, and a family without prompt-state copies serves without the prompt cache.
   - Device checks: `tf-cuda-test mimo-exl3` and `mimo-exl3-fixtures` against the Python engine's bytes (oracle script included), and `tf-mimo m1` (residuals, logits and argmax byte-equal to the Python engine).
   - The 16-bit cache is the default.
   - Recipe page: `docs/recipes/mimo-v2.6-flash.md`.
3. `83fd3f2d` **An 8-bit (e4m3) key/value cache for the 9 full-attention layers, opt-in with `--policy kv=fp8`.** A decode step at long context reads half the bytes. It is not bit-equal to the 16-bit cache. `/health` shows the active policy, and `tf-mimo kv8check` checks the 8-bit attention against Triton's.

Triton kernels run from a set captured from the Python engine's MiMo family, through `TENSORFOLD_CUDA_KERNELS`.

## Gate

Setup:
- Hardware: 2x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), Ubuntu 24.04.4, driver 580.173.02, Zig 0.17.0.
- Checkpoint: [ajensenwaud/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-exl3-3.0bpw](https://huggingface.co/ajensenwaud/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-exl3-3.0bpw).
- Served with `--parallel 4 --context 608256 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95`, RoCE between ranks. Every run was uncontended.

**Host:**
- `zig build test`: 108/108 steps succeeded, 527/535 tests passed, 8 skipped.
- `zig fmt --check` is clean on every touched file.
- `tools/zig/lean_check.py` finds 534 problems, the same as #703's baseline: zero new.

**Device, both ranks.** `tf-mimo kv8check`, rows at position 128,000 (1, 4 and 8 rows):
- Max error against Triton on the same 8-bit values: 7.6e-6.
- Against Triton on the 16-bit values: 3.9e-4.
- No non-finite values.

**Lane contracts.** Greedy, served, compared by the server's `token_sha`:

| | `kv=fp16` (default) | `kv=fp8` |
|---|---|---|
| Drafted == `"draft": false` (prompts of 29 to 10,806 tokens, covering the decode-row, grouped-experts and per-expert prompt paths) | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| Concurrent == solo (three groups of four, drafted and plain) | 24/24 | 24/24 |
| Resumed == fresh | n/a: no prompt states | n/a |

**Quality, `kv=fp8`:**
- GSM8K: 95.2% (476/500).
- MMLU: 81.6% (186/228).
- Passkey: 10/10 at 32K and 120K.
- These are identical to the recipe's release build.

**Decode, tok/s.** Measured with spark-bench `--preset full`, 512 tokens, thinking off, temperature 0. Workloads are chat / code / agent / report.

| | this PR, `kv=fp8` | recipe release build | this PR, `kv=fp16` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 stream | 46.3 / 70.4 / 58.7 / 49.9 | 52.5 / 77.6 / 58.9 / 52.7 | 45.8 / 59.2 / 52.0 / 48.1 |
| 4 streams, aggregate | 82.0 / 119.7 / 93.4 / 88.2 | 83.2 / 116.6 / 95.0 / 90.3 | 77.4 / 117.7 / 87.8 / 87.4 |

- The 4-stream aggregates are within about 2% of the release build.
- The single-stream cells come from one run each. Each request's random tag changes the decoded text and so the draft acceptance; I have seen these cells swing by up to 15% between runs. They need a repeat before the lower chat and code numbers are read as a regression.
- Release-build depth and prefill numbers are in #725.

**Not re-run after the rebase.** The served runs above used this code on #703 at a155a048. The rebase onto 59af121b applied with no conflicts in the files this PR touches, and the build and host tests above are on the rebased branch.

## Notes for review

- `native/cuda.zig` is at the 600-line limit, so other CUDA families ignore `--policy` rather than refusing it; MiMo refuses unknown keys. A refusal in the shared path would need a line freed elsewhere.
- The geometric rule's context term is applied in the Python grid's cost units, as the release build does. Its effect on depth is small (about +0.3 ms at 100K context), and I kept it to preserve the measured behaviour.

items.title: qwen CUDA: Qwen3.8-27B decode 9-15% faster with DFlash2 (code +25%), replies unchanged
items.body:
Faster decode rounds for Qwen3.8-27B with DFlash2 on CUDA, and the lane planner's pricing of context copies. Measured on one RTX 5090 (MLX 4-bit + DFlash2, `--kv-cache fp8`, a 262,144-token window, one stream).

Ruler at one stream, tok/s (prose / code / structured / list):

| | prose | code | structured | list |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 211.5 | 396.6 | 265.7 | 258.7 |
| this PR (before the copy pricing) | 243.3 | 450.8 | 293.6 | 283.5 |

Every reply on the ruler prompts is byte-identical to main's: the kernel changes keep each value's arithmetic and reduction order, and the drafter changes move only the drafts (verification decides every token).

**Kernels**
- `tf_q35d_dyn_conv_batch` on a (rows, channel blocks) grid instead of one block a row: 15.8 to 1.7 us.
- `tf_q35d_attn_partial`: four warps a 256-key chunk, keys split over the lanes, the ring row advanced instead of a 64-bit modulo a key, empty chunks returning at once: 92 to 15.5 us.
- `tf_q35_gdn_pre` writes a recorded window's conv log from the taps it already reads, so `tf_q35_conv_commit` only moves the stream's tail; its loads are 8-byte (3.8 to 2.9 us a layer).
- `tf_q35_gdn_slots_*` prefetch the next row and take two value rows a warp up to four slots (`slots_2` 17.4 to 14.3 us, `slots_4` 22.9 to 13.8 us).
- `tf_q35_norm` moves its row in 16-byte lanes through shared memory; each thread's sum of squares still reads its own entries in order (3.7 to 2.5 us).
- `tf_q35_gdn_post`, `tf_q35_attn_gate` and `tf_q35_mlp_act` write their outputs' 64-entry group sums (`group_sum`, in order), so the out, o and down projections no longer launch `tf_q35_sums` first: about 4,800 fewer launches a 256-token reply.

**Lane planner.** Live lone pricing (`lone_cost_tile`) kept each stream's measured round times and its losing widths' retry deadlines on the stream, so every request calibrated again with forced trials at one row (no drafts) and at the tile from round 8. The engine now keeps the newest calibration of a stream that only ran alone (greedy and sampled apart), and a stream's first priced round starts from it, its deadlines counted from that round. A stream that shared a round leaves nothing; one already priced keeps its own. This was 2-5% of the one-stream ruler. Only families with `lone_cost_tile` (Qwen CUDA) are affected; unit tests in `lone_costs_test.zig`. Kept calibrations are filed a context band each (under 8,192 tokens, then one a doubling, the last from 131,072 on), so a stream starts only from one measured at its own length, and a carried deadline or spacing reaches at most 256 rounds into the next stream. Without the bands, one greedy reply on a 252,783-token prompt left its 30 ms wide rounds as every later short stream's prices (the decode ruler's prose 238 tok/s and code 415 after it, against 253-257 and 495-496 with the bands, as on a fresh server, every reply byte-identical), and the doubled spacing of losing trials grew to thousands of rounds over a long run, so no stream re-timed the wide widths until a restart.

**Lane planner: context copies priced at the stream's own copy rate.** A lone head window that a context copy extends has more rows than the drafter grew, so the drafter could not price them and allocation fell back to chain probabilities from the stream's per-depth acceptance for every row, tree and copy alike. Those fall fast with depth, so a copy's tail looked hopeless and was cut: code replies, where copies from the prompt keep landing, verified 11.3 rows a round against about 14 elsewhere. The drafts now keep the drafter's own chances, and each copied row takes its parent's chance times the stream's copy rate: the rows its copies landed over those rows plus the chains that broke before their end (decayed 0.9 a round, primed from `cfg.copy_rate`'s 0.94 as sixteen rows' worth); a copy counts only when its anchor row landed. A unit test in `windows.zig` covers the pricing and the rate.

On 134 greedy prompts (25 each of GSM8K, IFEval, HumanEval and MMLU, 10 MGSM, a 24-prompt mix; 256 tokens, one stream), decode tok/s before and after this commit:

| | code | gsm8k | ifeval | mgsm | mix | mmlu | all |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 587 | 482 | 204 | 318 | 315 | 334 | 336 |
| after | 738 | 482 | 204 | 319 | 315 | 332 | 341 |

Every reply is unchanged. A fixed rate cannot do both: at 0.99, code reached 738 but gsm8k fell to 460 and mgsm to 303. An A/B on the same set also found the drafter's bf16 rounding (Metal parity) costs nothing: switching its conv and q/k norms to v0.6.6's rounding moved acceptance by under 0.1%.

**Verify windows and drafts.** Three more commits, on the same 134 prompts (decode tok/s; every reply unchanged at each step):

| | code | gsm8k | ifeval | mgsm | mix | mmlu | all | ms a round |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| after the copy pricing | 738 | 482 | 204 | 319 | 315 | 332 | 341 | |
| sm_120 verifies 32 rows on one weight pass | 793 | 486 | 206 | 313 | 312 | 339 | 343 | 16.49 |
| a DFlash2 hold grows its whole tree | 810 | 520 | 209 | 318 | 321 | 352 | 354 | 16.51 |
| `tf_q35_rope(8)`: a block a row and head | 816 | 524 | 210 | 320 | 322 | 354 | 356 | 16.42 |

- A window past 16 rows ran as 16-row tiles that each read the weights again (16 rows 13.4 ms, 32 rows 22.3 ms on the 27B). `Affine4Kernels.wide_verify` (set on GB10 as before, and now by the Qwen3.5 engine on sm_120) sends 17 to 32 rows to the existing 32-row verify kernel: 17.8 ms. On the 5090 its one-row results are bit-equal to the split-K decode's on all 18 contract shapes. A 64-row tile measured no gain; wide windows are compute-bound here.
- A lone stream asks the drafter for depth 1 while a context copy is ahead, and for less near a reply's end, so those rounds verified a one- to six-node tree beside the copy. The drafter's pass costs the same at any depth, so a hold now grows its whole tree whenever drafts are asked, and allocation still picks the rows. On sampled replies (temperature 0.7, fixed seeds) the 134 prompts went from 302 to 308 tok/s. Doing it in the depth rule instead captured less and cost code (771).
- `tf_q35_rope(8)` took a block a row and rotated the heads in turn; it now takes a block a row and head (query heads, then key heads) with one head staged. Each value's arithmetic is the same.

**Sampled rounds.** Each sampled row of a window launched `tf_draw` on one 1024-thread block in turn, about 97 us apiece: 1.5 ms of a 16-row round, so sampled rounds cost 17.6 ms where greedy ones cost 16.2. `tf_draw_rows` draws a run of rows in one launch, row r under its own rule and position, with the arithmetic a one-row `tf_draw` does, so every token is unchanged (a kernel set built before it keeps the per-row launches). On the community-v1 benchmark (`tensorfold benchmark`, managed server, five repeats), with all 24 replies byte-identical:

| tok/s | code, T=1 | chat, T=1 | code, T=0 | chat, T=0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 361.4 | 203.4 | 340.6 | 256.2 |
| after | 390.6 | 222.4 | 340.5 | 256.1 |

**Attention keys.** A warp of `tf_q35_attn_partial(8)` walked its chunk one key at a time (the key's load, its warp sum, then the value's load), so a 128-key chunk was bound by load latency. The keys' rows and values now load eight at a time and their dots reduce together; the running max, sum and output still take each key in turn with the same operations, so every value is unchanged. A round drops from 16.24 to 15.85 ms with bf16 rows (four keys at a time: 15.95, sixteen: 15.91), and on the 134 prompts with e4m3 rows from 16.49 to 16.03 ms (all 353 to 362 tok/s, code 795 to 805); every reply is identical. Community-v1: 400.6 / 229.2 / 350.8 / 264.0 tok/s (code T=1, chat T=1, code T=0, chat T=0).

**Lane planner: which context copies keep the 0.94 prior.** Every copy appended past a lone stream's drafts was priced from `cfg.copy_rate`'s 0.94, a prior worth sixteen rows that a stream's one or two copies never moved, so windows kept growing past 16 rows for copies that did not land. Traced over the 134 prompts: a copy after a context match of 20 or more tokens landed 85% of its rows (code's), one copied out of the prompt in the reply's first 64 tokens 89% on code (restating the asked-for function), and the rest 0 to 13%; outside code, rows past the 16th landed 11 of 777 priced. Those two kinds keep the prior; the others start from 0.08 with a history of their own, which trusted copies teach too. The proposer reports where its last match's continuation starts (`Proposer.lastEnd`). Three runs each, every reply unchanged: code 810 / 819 / 813 before and 803 / 817 / 813 after, gsm8k 525 to 533-534, mgsm 331-332 to 335, mmlu 354 to 357; rounds 16.06 to 15.92-15.95 ms. A unit test in `windows.zig` covers the rule and the two histories.

**Drafter vocabulary.** The drafter's logits came from the whole 248,320-row head, 450 us a round, where DFlash2's vocabulary (the Metal drafter's and the qwen27 engine's) is the head's first 98,304 rows and its last 288: 182 us. Drafting only those spans costs multilingual replies, whose tokens sit between them (MGSM 332 to 230 tok/s), so a stream drafts over the spans until its prompt or reply holds a token outside them, then over the whole head; a lane hold now carries the stream's tokens (`lanes.drafter.Hold.tokens`). On the 134 prompts all 364 to 367 tok/s (code 813-817 to 831, MGSM 335 kept), a round 15.92 to 15.73 ms; every reply unchanged.

**Sliced top-k draws.** `tf_draw_rows` took each sampled row on one 1024-thread block passing over the vocabulary several times (195 us a round). Both of `gpu_sample`'s candidate paths reach the row's top_k by value then id, which its tail sums and races, so for a top_k up to 32 each 8192-entry slice takes its own top_k (`tf_draw_slice_top`) and a block a row sorts them and runs the same tail (`tf_draw_rows_finish`, in `sample_slices.cuh`). Sampled replies are byte-identical (the community-v1 fixtures and the 134 prompts at temperature 0.7); a sampled round drops from 15.59 to 15.39 ms. Community-v1 now: 414-415 / 233 / 358 / 263 tok/s.

**Slot scan.** A tree window's delta-rule scan reduced each value row's k . state sum and then its output with their own `warp_sum` (four butterflies a step for two rows) and kept its slots in registers that every step copied through. As the qwen27 engine's `tf_gdn::tree_kernel` does, a step's sums and the previous step's outputs now reduce in one `spread_sum` (the same lane pairs as `warp_sum`, so every sum is unchanged), each output written a step later, and the slots are the warp's rows of shared memory. Every reply is identical; a round drops from 15.43-15.49 to 15.29-15.35 ms on the community-v1 fixtures, and the 134 prompts go from 367 to 369 tok/s (code 832 to 841).

**Row kernels.** `tf_q35_tap` took a row on one 256-thread block of scalar loads (9.3 us a launch) and `tf_q35_mlp_act` one entry a thread (2.0 us, 70 a round); both now move eight entries a thread through 16-byte loads (`qwen35_rows.cuh`), each entry's arithmetic and the activation's in-order group sums unchanged: a round 0.06 ms quicker.

**Sampled drafts follow the draw's noise.** A sampled round accepts a draft when the target's Gumbel race (keyed by the stream's seed, the position and the token) picks it, but the drafts ranked candidates by the drafter's logits alone. As the qwen27 engine's `draft_tree.best_first` does, a sampled hold now scores each candidate at the stream's temperature plus 0.7 times that draw's noise (`lanes.gpu_rule.uniform24`), and a lane hold carries the stream's sampling (`lanes.drafter.Hold.sampling`). Replies are unchanged. Over 20 seeds of the community-v1 fixtures at temperature 1, tokens a round go from 6.244 to 6.573 on code and 3.716 to 3.951 on chat (the qwen27 engine: 6.481 and 3.902; weights 0.35 and 1.0 measured lower). Community-v1 now: 428-430 / 249 / 361-362 / 265-266 tok/s.

**A one-window verify round skips `tf_q35_conv_commit`.** For a recorded window of two rows or more, `gdn_pre` logs every row's conv tail and the commit returns at once, yet each of the 48 linear layers launched it; a lone stream's rounds no longer do. The activation also takes four entries a thread (twice the blocks). Every reply identical; a round 0.1 ms quicker, the 134 prompts 371 to 372 tok/s. Community-v1: 431-432 / 250-251 / 363-364 / 267 tok/s.

Checks: `zig build test`, `test-kernel-contract`, `test-golden`, `fuzz-cortheon`, the Flash Next gate test, `zig fmt` and the lean check pass, as do the `test-qwen35-*` host steps (the draft frame host test now expects the drafter attention's 128-thread chunks, the verify host test covers sm_120's 32-row windows, and the draft equality test bounds a grown tree by its node budget instead of the asked depth).

items.title: Flash Next CUDA: the streams beside the first take KV pages from the core pool
items.body:
Branch `fn-paged-kv-pool` `336cb3f7`. It is #1156's `ce5b78d7`, then #1169 (`85aeb4bf`, the same change as `f23b5ab5`), then this change. It uses #1156's
`served()` and host plan.

## What this changes

`TF_FLASHNEXT_KV_PAGES=n` is off by default; n must be a multiple of 4. One stream keeps its own caches. Every other
stream takes a pool lane (`cuda_kv_lanes.zig`), which holds only its page table while idle:

- Its attention caches are n-position pages of one arena, enough for its prompt, its reply and a drafted window. With
  the MTP head a page holds the head's cache too, as the layer after the model's.
- Its DeltaNet states, convolution and n-gram tails and the head's buffers (window streams, scores, saved rows, spare
  states; `Draft.initIn`) are one run of consecutive pool pages, claimed when the stream opens (`Pool.claimRun`) and
  given back when it closes. Only addresses move.

The host plans the pool from `Loaded.layout` (fixed: the table and image rows; pages a token; the run) and admits through
`fits`. A request waits (`LaneMemory`) when no lane, pages or run is free. A lane's pages and run go back once the
engine's stream drains. Prompt-cache copies of the head's cache follow its pages. The layout is made after the head is
loaded, so the run covers every buffer the head maps (`initIn` refuses a short run).

`TF_FLASHNEXT_KV_PAGES_ALL=1` puts every stream on pages, for checks. Two ranks, `--slide` and a captured set refuse
the variable.

## Receipt

- At n=256, `--parallel 4 --context 40960`, MTP: "3 more taking 594 pages of 256 rows (4.36 GiB) as they need them,
  0 MiB fixed each". Before the run change each lane held 369 MiB from load (states, head cache and buffers).
- With MTP drafts:
  - concurrent == alone 4/4 and serial 1/1, outputs equal to contiguous;
  - drafted == plain 8/8, concurrent == solo 8/8, resumed == fresh (7,147 tokens), all equal to contiguous.
- Pages only (`--parallel 5`, 4 lanes, 792 pages, 8 requests, some waiting): the same bytes, and a kept state with its
  head cache restored into a lane.
- Without drafts, with the states in runs: see Gotchas (within noise of contiguous, bytes equal).
- Tests: full `zig build test -Dnvcc=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc` exit 0 (the admission test sets the new field), fmt
  clean, lean 0 new findings; `kernel-contract` 85/85, 7 controls red.

## Gotchas

- **Stacked on #1156 and on #1169:** the diff against `main` includes #1156's qwen commits up to `ce5b78d7`, and the page-table change, until those land. Only the last commit is this change.
- **Off by default** (`TF_FLASHNEXT_KV_PAGES`). Two ranks, `--slide` and captured sets refuse it.
- **No-drafts speed with the states in runs:** within noise of contiguous. These are two rounds of fresh server starts on this tree, with replies byte-identical to contiguous (code/chat tok/s):
  - c=1: contiguous 23.44/23.13 and 23.71/23.73; pool on 23.57/23.55 and 23.55/23.55; pages only 23.60/23.50 and 23.64/23.48.
  - c=4: contiguous 64.7/64.7 and 66.0/64.9; pool on 65.4/64.9 and 66.0/65.5; pages only 65.8/65.3 and 65.0/64.2.
- **Waits:** in pages-only mode with more requests than lanes, a waiting request can wait several seconds (up to 9.5 s seen with 8 requests on 4 lanes).

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds.
- [x] Drafted == plain, resumed == fresh, concurrent == solo, as measured above.
- [x] No precision traded for speed. The bits do not change.
- [x] New and changed kernels are registered with the kernel contract, with red controls.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release (contiguous within main's spread).
- [x] Platforms: CUDA on GB10 (sm_121), one rank; other SMs through recorded compiles; no Metal change.
- [x] Comments are one line. No measurements or history in the source (lean check 0 new).
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: Flash Next CUDA: attention caches readable through a page table
items.body:
Branch `fn-paged-kv` `f23b5ab5` on `main` `d1018b31`. Part of #781's follow-ups (other families on the core pool).

## What this changes

The seven `flashnext_attn.cu` kernels that touch a stream's caches now take a `Pg` argument: an int page table, the
elements in a page, and the positions in a page. They are `fn_attn_prep(_media)`, `fn_qsa_pool(_media)`,
`fn_qsa_scores` and `fn_attn_chunks(_ahead)`. `pg_at()` finds each row:

- with no table, it is the old expression;
- with a table, it is the start of the page that holds the position, plus the row inside that page.

A page of n positions holds, for each attention layer:

- the keys, values and indexer keys of its n positions;
- the pooled rows of their n / 4 blocks.

A cache pointer is its layer's part of page 0 (layout in `cuda_pages.zig`). Only addresses change; no sum changes
order. So paged caches give the contiguous bytes at any page size that holds whole blocks.

- `TF_FLASHNEXT_KV_PAGE_TEST=n` reads each stream's caches through a reversed table of n-position pages. It is for
  checks only.
- `fn_attn_chunks` looks up a key's row once per tile (`key_at` in shared memory, beside `key_ids`), and the pool kernel
  once per block of four; the contiguous path pays one uniform branch.
- Prompt-cache saves and restores copy page runs in the contiguous layout, so kept states move between the two forms.
- A captured Triton set refuses a page table.

## Receipt

- Environment: TensorFold `main` `d1018b31` plus this branch; one DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, CUDA 13.0, nvcc 13.0.88);
  `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local@b9ce18a6`.
- Kernel contract: `tf-cuda-test flashnext-pages`, also run inside `kernel-contract`.
  - Six cases: cached lengths up to 9,000; pages of 16, 48, 128, 256 and 512 positions; two streams shuffled through
    one arena.
  - Paged output equals contiguous over three repeats for: queries, indexer queries, block scores, dense and sparse
    attention rows, the stores, and the pooled rows.
  - Attention rows stay within a float64 bound, and the guards are intact.
  - Controls are red: a swapped table over placed pages, and a planted row.
  - Gate 5: new nvcc 13.0 records for the five kernels whose register counts moved. All seven pass live. The 13.2
    override set still needs regenerating with nvcc 13.2, which is not on this box.
- Served, greedy, `--parallel 4 --context 40960 --no-drafts`, ABAB against `main` (c=1 tok/s code/chat, TTFT):

  | arm | replies | c=1 | ~8k | 31k |
  | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | main, run 1 / 2 | - | 23.46/23.40, 23.38/23.48 | 6.04-7.00 s | 25.67 / 26.01 s |
  | this, contiguous, run 1 / 2 | equal (3 chats, three ~8k, one 31k) | 23.51/23.49, 23.55/23.44 | 5.97-6.91 s | 25.64 / 25.74 s |
  | this, page test 16 | equal | 23.56/23.38 | 6.05-6.90 s | 26.08 s |

  The page test's first version (one page-table lookup per 16-byte load) cost +3-4 % at 31k; one lookup per key per tile
  removes that.
- Gates with MTP drafts, page test 16, compared with contiguous:
  - drafted == plain: 8/8;
  - concurrent == solo: 8/8;
  - resumed == fresh: yes, with 7,147 tokens restored into pages;
  - every output equals contiguous.
- Tests: full `zig build test -Dnvcc=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc` exit 0, `zig fmt --check` clean, lean check 0 new
  findings; `kernel-contract`: 85/85 kernels pass gates 1-4, 7 controls red (exit 1 only from `main`'s 877 limit
  problems).

## Gotchas

- **Off by default:** only the check switch `TF_FLASHNEXT_KV_PAGE_TEST` uses pages here. The pool itself is the stacked follow-up, #1170.
- **Gate-5 records:** the nvcc 13.2 override set for the five kernels whose registers moved isn't regenerated, because there is no nvcc 13.2 here. The 13.0 records are new.
- **Captured Triton sets** refuse a page table.
- **Overlap:** #1113 pages Flash Next KV to host RAM for its EXL3 path. That is a different mechanism, but the same family, so expect textual overlap. No conflict with #1143, #1147, #1155 or #1164.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo. All
      three were measured on the page test.
- [x] No precision traded for speed. The bits do not change.
- [x] New and changed kernels are registered with the kernel contract, with red controls.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release (contiguous within main's spread).
- [x] Platforms: CUDA on GB10 (sm_121), one rank; other SMs through recorded compiles; no Metal change.
- [x] Comments are one line. No measurements or history in the source (lean check 0 new).
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: qwen3_5 cuda: serve ExLlamaV3 (EXL3) Qwen3.5-MoE checkpoints
items.body:
## What this changes

Serves ExLlamaV3 (EXL3) Qwen3.5-MoE checkpoints on the native CUDA engine (tracking issue: #1149). The format and kernel design are turboderp's ExLlamaV3 (https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3); the checkpoint exercised is https://huggingface.co/Mia-AiLab/Ornith-1.5-122B-EXL3-EAQv1-4-bpw. Three commits, each building:

1. `qwen35_bf16_rows.cu` and `cuda_bf16_rows.zig`: a bf16 embedding-row copy and a small bf16 dense projection (GDN in_proj_a / in_proj_b) with a fixed summation order. Pending contract records only.
2. `exl3.Dense.reserve`: grows the dense scratch before graph capture so no allocation happens inside a capture.
3. The loader: `cuda_geometry.zig` accepts `quant_method "exl3"`, `cuda_exl3_weights.zig` reads the HF tensor names (trellis projections and every expert kept in their stored layout, f16 router and in_proj_a/b converted to bf16, zero-centred RMSNorm weights shifted by one), and `cuda_engine.zig` routes the new projection kinds to the existing `cuda.exl3` kernels. The weights load runs twice over one code path: a dry run sizes the arena, then the real pass.

`--drafter` is refused for an EXL3 checkpoint (`Exl3DrafterUnsupported`): its MTP layer and a DFlash2 drafter are not read by this change.

Related open PRs, not duplicated: #1137 (BF16 scoring) also adds a `cuda_bf16` file and edits geometry, engine and `Proj`, so mine are named `*_bf16_rows` with `.x3` / `.bf` projection kinds; whichever lands second will need a small textual merge. #1145 (ModelOpt NVFP4) edits the same geometry and engine regions. #1113 (EXL3 Flash Next) is a different family. #1047 touches `cuda_routed.zig`.

## Receipt

- Environment: TensorFold d1018b31 plus this branch; GB10 (sm_121), 121 GiB; nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3 (nvcc 13.x), Zig 0.17.0; checkpoint Mia-AiLab/Ornith-1.5-122B-EXL3-EAQv1-4-bpw @ 9c5c913b3de1eef901520d6fedaf450044ea0423.
- Exactness: GPU smoke on a GB10 (121 GiB), NVIDIA driver 580.178.04, container nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3 with Zig 0.17.0, checkpoint Mia-AiLab/Ornith-1.5-122B-EXL3-EAQv1-4-bpw at revision 9c5c913b3de1eef901520d6fedaf450044ea0423. Flags `--no-drafts --no-thinking --parallel 1 --context 8192 --kv-cache fp8 --vision`, temperature 0, 64 tokens, five requests: three text prompts, one image, one tool call (get_weather, not forced). The reply text, finish reason and tool call arguments of this branch's build equal those of a build of the same engine carrying my local, unsubmitted speed patches. That is a consistency check between two builds, not a quality evaluation. Drafted-versus-plain and concurrent-versus-solo checks were not run.
- Decode speed before and after: n/a (a new format; nothing existing changes). Not measured for the new path, which uses the generic EXL3 kernels and is not tuned.
- Prompt speed before and after: n/a for the same reason.
- Tests run (no GPU, in the container above): `zig build test` on this branch: 211/211 steps succeeded, 1835 of 1847 tests passed, 12 skipped; upstream main with the same command: 211/211, 2102 of 2110, 8 skipped (the totals differ because cached unchanged steps are not rerun). `zig fmt --check build.zig zig` clean. `tools/zig/lean_check.py`: 444 problems before and after. New host tests (`cuda_exl3_admission_test.zig`): an EXL3 config is admitted by `quant_method` alone, and configs with neither an MLX table nor `exl3` are refused; a deliberately wrong expectation made `test-cuda-host` fail, so they run.
- Not run, and why: no kernel contract test for the two new launches (only pending records, as the other qwen35 launches), no prompt/decode benchmarks, no Metal, no multi-stream or long-context runs (context 8192 only), no 262k window.

## Limits

Serving works with the generic EXL3 kernels; prompt and decode speed are modest and not tuned for this model, and there is no drafter. Only the MoE model without a learning pocket is admitted.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off. (Drafts are refused for EXL3 here; the smoke runs used `--no-drafts`.)
- [ ] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo. (Not run: no drafter, and one stream only.)
- [x] No precision traded for speed. The bf16 dense kernel sums in fp32 in a fixed order; the EXL3 kernels are the existing ones.
- [ ] A new or changed GPU kernel is registered with the kernel contract. (Two launches are listed as pending records only; no contract test yet, see below.)
- [ ] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release. (n/a: a new format, nothing existing changes.)
- [x] Platforms: CUDA on GB10 (sm_121) only. Metal and other GPUs not run.
- [ ] New tests fail before the change, pass after it. (Host test added; see below.)
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: CUDA input gradients for Living Weights on Flash Next: a Gated DeltaNet layer, 4-bit products, routed experts, gated attention (shared), and the hyper-connections and pocket (family)
items.body:
## What this changes

These are the kernels Living Weights' trainer needs to run the loss's gradient back through Qwen3.8 Flash Next on CUDA.
There is no serving change: nothing on the serve path calls them, and no shipped file outside the kernel list, the
runtime's exports and `tf-cuda-test` is touched. The trainer that uses them is the next PR (lw-d-fnlearn).

Following #736 and the recipe's core/family split, what any family with the same layer could use sits in the core
(`zig/kernels/cuda/*.cu` with a `zig/src/cuda/*.zig` wrapper), and only what is Flash Next's own sits in
`families/flashnext`:

1. **Core: a Gated DeltaNet layer's input-gradient backward** (`gdn_train.cu`, `cuda.gdn_train`). The forward for
   training is recomputed from the layer's kept projection rows (conv, q and k L2 norms, g and beta, the delta-rule
   chain with a state checkpoint every 4 rows), with the serving chain's operations in its order, so `y` has the serving
   bits. The backward walks each chunk back after replaying its states into an L2-sized work area. Per row, with `ds`
   the state's gradient carried: `ds += dy_j q`; `dq = sum_j dy_j S_j`; `dd_j = ds_j . k`; `dv_j = beta dd_j`;
   `dbeta = sum_j dd_j (v_j - S'_j . k)`; `dk = sum_j (delta_j ds_j - beta dd_j S'_j)`; `ds' = ds - beta dd k^T`;
   `dg = sum ds' . S_prev`; `ds = g ds'`. Then the gated RMS norm, the L2 norms, the gates, the causal conv and its SiLU,
   and the in and out projections. Gradients into a kept prefix's state and conv history are dropped, as Nemotron's
   Mamba backward drops them. Shapes are parameters (key and value heads, hidden), so a Qwen3.8-27B-shaped DeltaNet uses
   the same kernels.
2. **Core: 4-bit (MLX affine, group 32) products, routed SwiGLU experts and softmax top-k routing** (`train_q4.cu`,
   `cuda.train_q4`). A linear's input gradient on tensor cores (tf_train_gemm's tiles, split K for a 248,320-row head),
   the experts' products over MLX stacks or over `experts_pack.cu`'s packed table (the engine's own copy, so no second
   copy of the experts), each pair's SwiGLU, and the top-k softmax weights and the sigmoid shared gate back through the
   router. `tf_train_sort_pairs` now takes up to 1024 experts (512 and a shared one); below 256 it does what it did.
3. **Core: gated attention** (`train_attn.cu`, `cuda.train_attn`), Qwen3-Next's form: each head's q then its output
   gate, RMS-normed q and k, rotate-half RoPE on the first `2 half` dims. The prepared heads again, the output gate, the
   causal part to 2048 keys (with `train.cu`'s `tf_train_attn_kv`), the RoPE and norms undone, and the three projections
   through `cuda.train_q4`.
4. **Family: the hyper-connections and the pocket** (`flashnext_train.cu`, `families/flashnext/cuda_fn_back.zig`). The
   write-back `h' = h + bf16(branch inject)` and the read-out (mix, its activations, down and inject, the streams' RMS
   norms) undone; and Living Weights' pocket of SwiGLU neurons beside the shared expert, behind its gate: the forward in
   two kernels (`tf_fn_pocket_in` then `_out`, tiled forms past a size, nothing launched for a layer with no neuron in
   use; a port of #787's two-kernel pocket to this family), its input gradient and its output vectors' gradient.
   `flashnext.fn_back` composes these with the core's on one stream; its MoE backward runs the core's experts, then the
   pocket (whose shared-gate share joins the gate's gradient), then the core's router.

Every comment is one line; the block comments the derivations used to be in are in this description instead.

## Receipt

- Environment: `lw-c-fnback` a5d183d5 on 7746bb9d (#869), Zig 0.17.0; NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121), driver
  580.178.04, CUDA 13.0.88, Ubuntu 24.04.5. Synthetic tensors at Flash Next's shapes; no checkpoint.
- Each case compares the GPU's gradients with a float64 reference, and first checks that reference against central
  differences of a float64 forward. A gradient's error is its worst column (the largest difference in a column over that
  column's largest reference value) and its relative L2 error. The bf16 products' tolerance is 3% worst column and 1%
  L2; the fp32 chains' is 1e-3.
  - `tf-cuda-test gdn-back` (16 key heads, 48 value heads, hidden 2560, 4-bit group-32 projections, 64, 256 and 37 rows,
    the last after a prefix with a conv history and state): forward bf16 outputs within 1 ulp of float64's rounding
    (`y`: 25 of 227,328 values 1 ulp off), every chain gradient within 1.3e-6 worst column, `dx` within 1.5e-2 (4.7e-5
    with the GEMM's operands rounded as the GPU rounds them). PASS.
  - `tf-cuda-test q4-back` (the loss through a 248,320 x 2560 4-bit head, 64 and 256 rows): loss and target probability
    within 7.2e-8, the bf16 gradient rows within 2.6e-3 of the largest, `dmixed` worst column 6.6e-3, L2 2.6e-3;
    reference against central differences 8e-7. 7 checks, PASS.
  - `tf-cuda-test moe-back` (512 routed experts of width 640, the shared expert, top 10, 64 and 256 rows): `dx` worst
    column 2.7e-6, each slot's dL/dw 1.7e-6, the router logits' gradients 1.9e-6; the same layer over the packed table
    gives the MLX stacks' `dx` bit for bit; reference against central differences 1.2e-9. 11 checks, PASS.
  - `tf-cuda-test attn-back` (24 query heads, 2 kv heads, head dim 256, RoPE on 64 dims, 64 and 256 rows): `dx` worst
    column 1.3e-2, L2 3.1e-3; `dpq`, `dpk`, `dv` within 1.3e-2; the prepared heads within 2^-5 of the host's; reference
    against central differences 7.6e-9. 11 checks, PASS.
  - `tf-cuda-test fn-hc-back` (4 streams, low rank 320, a block's read-out with inject and the final mixer's, 64 and 256
    rows): `dbranch` and `dinject` within 1.5e-7, `dh` worst column 5.8e-3, L2 1.7e-3; references against central
    differences 6e-8. 13 checks, PASS.
  - `tf-cuda-test fn-moe-back` (`moe-back` with 16 pocket neurons): every gradient as above, the pocket's forward and its
    output vectors' gradients within tolerance, the packed table again bit for bit. 16 checks, PASS.
  - `tf-cuda-test fn-pocket 20`: the two pocket kernels against `tf_fn_pocket_rows` byte for byte in 444 cases (1 to
    2,048 rows across both tiling thresholds, 1 to 128 neurons, widths 2560 and 2600, fp32 and bf16 outputs, with and
    without the gate and the training row scales); controls that reverse the neurons or rotate the inputs change
    12,703 and 9,633 values, so the comparison sees order; 0 neurons launches nothing and keeps every bit, -0.0
    included. PASS.
  - `fn-back` runs all six gradient cases one after another.
- Times on the GB10 (one layer, 256 rows): DeltaNet 6.8 ms (4.1 ms of it the forward and chain), MoE 26 ms (19.6 ms
  over the packed table), attention 3.3 ms, a hyper-connection read-out 1.2 ms, the head 16.7 ms.
- Without the kernels (`zig build` with no `-Dnvcc` or `-Dfatbins`) each new command prints `SKIP` and passes.
- Tests: `zig build test-cuda-host` from a fresh cache: 29/29 steps, 506/506 tests pass (#869's head: 503); every
  commit builds with `-Dnvcc` and passes `zig fmt --check build.zig zig`; `python3 tools/zig/lean_check.py` gives 527
  problems against 527 on 7746bb9d (0 new); all 46 fatbins build for sm_86, sm_120 and sm_121 and `check_fatbins`
  passes.
- Not run: Metal (no change there), sm_86 and sm_120 cards (none here).

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off. (No serving
  change.)
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo. (Not
  touched.)
- [x] No precision traded for speed. If the bits change, the description says which sums change and why. (No serving
  bits change. The backward runs in fp32 from bf16 operands and treats the forward's roundings as identities, as
  Nemotron's trainer does.)
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release. (Not touched.)
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not. (GB10 only.)
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

## Not in this PR, said plainly

- No trainer, no `--slide`: they are the next PR, stacked on this one and on #878.
- The DeltaNet backward's two projections dequantize a 4-bit matrix to bf16 for each sequence before a dense GEMM;
  using `cuda.train_q4`'s 4-bit product there instead is a speed-up I have not made.
- `train_q4` is group 32 only (Flash Next's); Nemotron's trainer keeps its own group-64 kernels.
- Attention's backward takes at most 2048 keys a sequence (the trainer's sequences are 512 rows at most), so the block
  indexer's sparse attention has no backward.

## Stack

- Depends on #869 (Flash Next on CUDA): `flashnext.fn_back` lives in that family, and the packed-expert layout it reads
  is the one #869's engine packs.
- Does not depend on #878.
- The next PR (trainer and `--slide` for Flash Next, branch `lw-d-fnlearn`) stacks on this and on #878.

## Questions

- Is the core/family split right? The DeltaNet, 4-bit product, experts and routing, and gated attention backward are in
  the core because Qwen3.8-27B (or any Qwen3-Next-shaped model) has the same layers; the hyper-connections and the
  pocket are Flash Next's own.
- Should the experts' backward read only the packed table (the engine's copy) and drop the MLX-stack form? The stack
  form is what the float64 test feeds directly; the packed form is what the trainer uses.

items.title: flint: serve Recursive Flint (40B-A2.5B MoE) natively on Metal
items.body:
Serves Recursive's Flint (`RecursiveSI/flint`, a 40B-A2.5B MoE) natively on Metal from Recursive's MLX INT4 export, by the lane host with the prompt cache, structured output, tools and several streams. Closes #1175.

## What changes

- **`moe_route` (core, first commit):** `tf_route_logits` gave each lane four 32-wide slices of k, which covers a hidden width of exactly 4096; at Flint's 2048 it read past each row and past the packed router. Each lane now takes `hidden / 1024` slices (still four at 4096, so GLM-5.3-Flash's and Step-5's routers keep their arithmetic), `source` refuses other widths, and `round_logits` rounds each logit to bf16 as a bf16 router matmul gives it.
- **`families/flint` (second commit):** config and weights (U8-stored affine words, bf16 norms and sinks); 35 sliding (513-token window, RoPE) and 14 full (NoPE) GQA layers with per-head q/k norms and a learned sink a head; two dense SwiGLU layers, then 256 routed experts (top 6 by sigmoid score, renormalized) beside an ungated shared expert. Rounding follows MLX's points as RecursiveSI's `rec_mlx` computes the model (bf16 residual, `rms_norm` as `w * bf16(x * inv)`, SiLU op by op, bf16 router logits).
  - Attention: prompt chunks on the tensor units (gemma4's prompt kernel over a position-major cache, the sink in the denominator); decode rows on `sdpa_vector`'s lanes over key blocks at absolute positions, merged with the sink as MLX's second pass does, so a row's bits do not depend on the rows beside it. Sliding layers keep a ring of the window plus one prompt chunk.
  - q|k|v and each MLP's gate|up are stacked into one matrix at load (one launch, the same row sums; about 270 MB of copies); one launch norms and rotates q and k and writes k and v; residual adds are fused with the next norm.
  - Routing uses core `moe_route`'s logits, then a top-k pick a simdgroup a row (the core select's arithmetic without its per-Mac lists).
  - Several streams' windows share one forward; a lone stream's steps run a step ahead (`gpu_tokens`), drawn on the GPU (argmax, or the keyed sampler of lanes' `gpu_rule` / `gpu_full`, Nemotron's kernels at Flint's vocabulary) into a token ring, and host draws use the same sampler's twin.
  - `tf-flint-run`: greedy tokens, every position's logits, forced steps, step timing, and `exact` (one-row steps against windows of any width, bit for bit); `docs/recipes/flint.md` and a README row.

## Checks (Apple M5 Ultra, 256 GB, macOS 27; `RecursiveSI/flint-int4` at 3b93f9053b530488405ae9fca51d4900d6ce21f0; this branch's head)

**Against the reference** (RecursiveSI's `rec_mlx` model on MLX 0.32.4 with plain bf16 KV caches; its own server quantizes the full layers' KV, so it is not the reference here):
- Greedy, a 13-token chat prompt: 64 of 64 tokens equal.
- Teacher-forced along the reference's own greedy continuation, 48 steps after each prompt (native: prompt in chunks, then one row a step):

| prompt | mean KL | max KL | top-1 | differences (logit margins) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,628 tokens | 0.0030 | 0.0337 | 46/48 | step 13: reference 17098 over 2847 by 0.016, native 2847 by 0.039; step 38: reference 12917 over 20479 by 0.047, native 20479 by 0.422 |
| 6,426 tokens | 0.0029 | 0.0355 | 48/48 | none |
| 31,597 tokens | 0.0024 | 0.0345 | 46/48 | step 14: reference 2847 over 17098 by 0.059, native 17098 by 0.070; step 40: reference 28657 over 1960 by 0.250, native 1960 by 0.016 |

- 6,426 tokens: 48 greedy tokens after the prompt equal the reference's.

- For scale: the reference's own prompt pass and its one-token-at-a-time pass disagree on 3 of 13 rows of the short prompt (KL up to 7.0), at the same near-ties the native decode path takes.

**Window exactness** (`tf-flint-run exact`: the reference's continuation as one-row steps and as windows after the prompt, every row's bf16 logits compared): 0 of 48 rows differ at 2,628, 6,426 and 31,597 tokens with 16-row windows, and at 31,597 with windows of 1, 2, 5 and 11. Before the merge took key blocks by absolute index (the fix is in this branch), 36 of 48 rows differed at 2,628 tokens and 45 of 48 at 31,597: a sliding layer's first block follows the window's first row, and the merge's lanes took blocks by their index from it. A drafted reply at 31.6k then differed from the same request with `--no-drafts`; with the fix they are equal.

**Serving contracts** (served `tensorfold-native`, greedy unless noted):
- Each of 4 and 8 concurrent replies equals its run alone, greedy and seeded-sampled.
- A lone stream's GPU-drawn steps equal host-drawn windowed rounds (requests with `logprobs`), 12 of 12: greedy, top-k 20 sampling, and whole-vocabulary sampling.
- Prompt cache and drafts: a turn resumed at 4,507 of 4,627 tokens equals the same request after a server restart; at 31.6k tokens (and a resumed second turn), replies are equal with `--prompt-cache-gib 0` and with `--no-drafts`. Under `FLINT_LOAD_LIMIT_GB=34`, a 239k-token stream evicts six kept states, the oversized state is refused, and an evicted prompt's recomputed reply is unchanged.
- Structured output 18/18 (json_object, json_schema, regex, choice, grammar), drafted == plain 12/12, a bad regex 400; tools 5/5 (auto, required, named, thinking, streamed).
- A passphrase at 30% depth is returned exactly at 108,146 and 238,515 prompt tokens (34.1 s and 116.4 s, under that 34 GB limit).

**Speed** (served, greedy, 256-token replies; the qwen Spark recipe's ruler):

| streams | prose | code | structured | list | first token |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 183.1 | 177.0 | 192.9 | 204.4 | 0.03-0.04 s |
| 2 | 259.2 | 256.1 | 277.3 | 277.8 | 0.04-0.07 s |
| 4 | 354.5 | 347.5 | 364.0 | 360.8 | 0.07-0.11 s |

Cold prompts (fresh server, words no earlier prompt starts with): 2,068 tokens 6,503 tok/s, 8,215 tokens 7,039 tok/s, 32,791 tokens 5,887 tok/s, 131,094 tokens 3,360 tok/s. A turn resumed from the cache starts in 0.068 s against 0.726 s cold. Not compared against `rec_mlx`'s server or `mlx_lm` (neither serves this model with an unquantized KV cache).

**Memory:** 21.4 GiB of weights wired; caches 28 KiB a token in the full layers (7 GiB a stream at 262,144) plus the sliding rings; weights, scratch and caches stay under 75% of RAM or `FLINT_LOAD_LIMIT_GB`.

**Repository checks:** `zig fmt --check`, `zig build test`, `test-kernel-contract`, `test-golden`, `fuzz-cortheon`, `test-server-security test-pull-security` pass. Lean: 438 problems, 438 on the base, 0 new. `zig build kernel-contract -Dcpu=apple_m1` stops before its SUMMARY on this Mac on main as well (`UnrecordedRotaryCompiler`: Flash Next's rotary probe wants a `tf-rotary-sweep` receipt for this Metal compiler).

## Not covered

- Flint's own Metal kernels are not registered with the kernel contract yet (as with the other Metal family glue); the core router change keeps its arithmetic at 4096.
