items.title: feat(hip): the model-free kernels on #463's runtime: attention, DeltaNet, norms, RoPE, MoE routing and decode plans
items.body:
## What this changes

The model-free kernels a model engine composes, on #463's runtime: the first kernels slice tracked in #491, everything but the MLX affine products (the next slice).

- 21 HIP sources (3,385 lines) built by hipcc for `-Dhip-arch` with the caps table's instruction switches, embedded as one code object a source group and launched from Zig with #463's `Module` and `launch`: elementwise ops and casts, norms and the merged decode tails, RoPE, attention (the flat decode walk; the planned walk over a page table, reading a KV head once for the query heads that share it; the 64-row prompt tile flat and paged), the DeltaNet recurrence in fp32 at every length, the linear attention's conv and gates, the MoE router, pick and route, argmax and top-k, and a lane round's plan kernels.
- `launches.zig` resolves every kernel at load; `Launcher.Choices` picks between two kernels that give the same bits (merged decode launches, the 64-row prompt tile).
- The sources hold device code only: plain kernels are `extern "C"` (`tf_*`), and each template kernel the launches resolve is instantiated explicitly; no host launchers or C API.
- `ops/` checks shapes for each launch; `arena.zig` hands out a forward's scratch front to back, and a counting stream measures what a forward takes without launching.
- `-Dhip-device-lib` names ROCm's device bitcode for layouts other than TheRock's (Arch keeps it in `<rocm>/amdgcn/bitcode`); `zig/tests/hip_kernels.md` has the notes.

Stacks on #611 (its three commits are included here until they land); review the last commit.

## Receipt

- Environment: base `main` at c37d0a43 (+ #607, #609, #611), head d91b0740. Zig 0.17.0, HIP 7.14.60850 (TheRock), Linux 7.1.7.
- Exactness, `hip-kernel-test` (43 tests), on both GPUs below:
  - the planned decode walk over a permuted page table writes the flat walk's bits for 8, 6, 4 and 1 query heads a KV head, within 1e-5 of float64;
  - the 64-row prompt tile over pages writes the flat tile's bits, within the cache type's rounding of float64;
  - the merged conv split, MoE pick and gated norm write the replaced chains' bytes; the merged router and tails sit no further from float64 than twice the launches they replace;
  - casts, sums, column copies, cache writes, argmax, top-k and the MoE route give torch's bits; silu products, gates, the MoE activation and RoPE sit within one rounding of float64; the DeltaNet within 5e-3 of a float64 recurrence at 64 to 4170 tokens, and a 200-row prompt cut at 1, 63, 64, 65 or 136 rows gives one call's rows and state, bit for bit.
  - Fails before the fix: dropping a tile's last key in the planned walk, or a subtraction in the sum kernel, fails the attention and the casts-and-sums tests; the cut test fails with the former chunked DeltaNet kernel (42/43).
  - Device code unchanged by removing the host launchers (at b731206a): each of the 89 kernels a target resolved disassembled to the same instructions before and after, on gfx1100 and gfx1030.
- Decode and prompt speed: not applicable here (no model path); the grouped decode walk's effect on served decode was measured on #490.
- Tests run, fresh Zig cache:
  - Radeon PRO W7800 (gfx1100): `hip-kernel-test` 43/43, `hip-gpu-test` 30/30, `hip-affine-test` 27/27.
  - Radeon PRO V620 (gfx1030, fp16 activations): `hip-kernel-test` 43/43, `hip-gpu-test` 30/30, `hip-affine-test` 27/27.
  - macOS: `zig build test -Dcpu=apple_m1` 1013/1015 tests (2 skipped), `test-golden` 0 unexpected differences (the launches and ops compile in the host tests); Linux: CI `zig` passes. CI `fmt` passes. `lean_check.py`: 544 problems, the same as `main`.
- Not run, and why: RDNA3.5 and RDNA4 hardware (none here); Metal and CUDA (sources untouched).

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off. (No engine path in this change.)
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo. (No engine path; the kernels a round uses keep a row's bits at any row count, which these tests check where they apply.)
- [x] No precision traded for speed. Each kernel's sums are checked against float64 or against the form it replaces.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release. (No prompt path in this change.)
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: glm: GLM-5.3-Flash (NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint) as a CUDA family at TP over hosts
items.body:
## What this changes

The family #593 tracks: GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA, tensor parallel over two GB10s (and three, below), on the shared NVFP4
layer (`qlinear`, `experts.Grouped`) and hand-written `.cu` for the rest. It serves through `tensorfold-native serve`
(rank 0 serves, the other ranks follow its steps), drafts (the checkpoint's MTP layer) and concurrency go through the
lanes core, and kept prompt states through the family's `snap_*` hooks.

This branch is 1.0.10 with the pieces split out first (#742, #759 and #761 are in 1.0.9, #800 and #805 in 1.0.10);
until the rest land, its first commits are theirs, and the review is the last five:
- #757 qlinear fp32 outputs, #758 ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints (its third commit, a test, is this branch's last for
  now), #766 page cache release, #762 a CUDA family's own prompt-cache and share hooks, #764 skip on the staged prompt
  entries, #763 packGateUp in place
- the family; the vocabulary's TP cut in the checkpoint format's unit (EXL3 cuts in 128s, from @BHCC2025 on #593);
  swiglu's 64-column block where 512 doesn't divide a rank's width (TP=3's last rank)
- `Engine.init` admits `config.json` through `modelopt.admit`; every rank reads its room once its weights are in,
  and rank 0 admits the streams and the prompt cache by the smallest, naming that rank when it refuses

### Next to the Metal GLM

One family package: `config.zig` is shared (this adds `head_unit`, `shared_inter`, `norm_topk` and the parse checks
the NVFP4 config needs), both backends sit behind the lane core's backend table, kept prompt states behind
`api.prompt_cache.Snapshots`, and the tokenizer, chat template and tool parsing stay above the family. The CUDA host
files are `cuda_*.zig` beside the Metal ones; they share no code today, for reasons in the code:
- weights: Metal reads MLX q4g64 and re-lays tensors into its kernels' tiles while loading (`weights_fix.zig`); CUDA
  reads ModelOpt NVFP4 as stored with bf16 attention projections, cut per rank (`cuda_weights.zig`, `cuda_shard.zig`)
- state: Metal holds per-layer `mtl.Buffer` slices with the position on the host; CUDA one device arena with the
  position on the device, which its kernels read
- forward: Metal encodes ops on `mtl.ComputeEncoder`; CUDA launches kernels and NCCL exchanges on a stream
- more than one machine: the same shape, rank 0 records each step and the others replay it (`mirror.zig`,
  `cuda_follow.zig`), over an MCDMA control window on Metal and `ncclBroadcast` on CUDA
- page cache: macOS `msync`/`mincore` against Linux `madvise`/`fadvise` (#766)

What could move into shared code in follow-ups, by value: one backend-neutral tensor plan both loaders read (checkpoint
name, dtype and shape, the axis cut, each rank's span; the names and cut axes already agree); a state-size table both
`state.zig` and `cuda_state.zig` take (the arithmetic is the same); the step tape apart from its transport; the
token-handle ring this family's lanes share with Nemotron's CUDA lanes, into the lane core. Splitting a Config across
machines differs too (Metal rewrites the Config to one Mac's share; CUDA keeps it whole and cuts with `Share`, which
allows uneven shares); taking `Share` on Metal would be the larger change, so it is a suggestion here.

### Several requests in one forward

- `prefill_step`: a prompt goes one 2,048-row chunk at a time and the other streams' rounds run between chunks.
- `hidden_rows`: up to 8 streams' verify windows (32 rows) share one forward; row-wise work (projections, experts,
  exchanges, head) runs over all rows, each stream's KDA chain and DSA attention on its own sequence.
- `glm-shared-check` holds every stream against a twin that runs each round alone: logits, tokens, drafts and state
  equal byte for byte at TP=2 on the full model.
- Neither depends on the weight format: only the loader and the kernels behind `qlinear` / `experts.Grouped` do.

### Speed

- The port began on captured Triton cubins; every kernel is now hand-written. Against the Triton set on the same two
  GB10s in one sitting (median of 2): prompt 8,192 tokens 5.86 -> 5.26 s and 32,768 tokens 22.64 -> 20.54 s, with the
  same 49 greedy ids after each prompt; greedy decode without drafts 17.10 to 17.15 -> 17.10 to 17.20 tok/s (three chat
  prompts of about 2k tokens).

<details>
<summary>What we tried for speed during the port, kept and dropped</summary>

Measured while porting, each against the build before it in the same sitting: with Nsight Compute on one GB10 (the
five-layer forward check with both TP=2 ranks on it, over a 32k-token prompt where noted), with Nsight Systems on
rank 0 of the two GB10s (a decode step), or end to end on the two. Every kept change leaves each output's bits as
they were.

**Kept**

| change | aim | measured |
|---|---|---|
| DSA index row selection laid out as Triton's: a row per 4-warp block, 8 consecutive pools a thread | more rows an SM | 21.0 → 14.3 ms over a 32k prompt (Triton 15.1), Compute |
| hyper-connection partial dots: 4 prompt rows a block, sharing the weight loads | fewer weight reads | 191.6 → 137.7 ms over a 32k prompt (Triton 177), Compute |
| hyper-connection finish: warp 0's Sinkhorn steps tightened | a shorter decode step | 7.30 → 6.23 ms over 234 calls, Compute; below the end-to-end resolution |
| decode BF16 matmuls: each shape takes Triton's `_bmm` setup (BLOCK_N 32 or 64, 1 to 3 cp.async stages, 4 warps) and issues the next stage's copy before waiting on this one | Triton's decode matmul time | a step's matmuls 39.31 → 37.56 ms (Triton 37.43), Systems; greedy decode from 4% to 0.6% behind Triton |
| greedy draws: each rank's top-1 on the device, then one all-gather | no host pass over the logits (155 KB down, a scan, up, a wait) | +1.2% tok/s |
| rank 0's step header: written through a kernel argument, no wait after its broadcast | less idle GPU between steps | +0.2% tok/s |
| a prompt chunk's exchanges in 3 row pieces (was 4) | more of the exchanges behind compute | 8k and 32k prompts 1.2% shorter |
| NVFP4 expert prompt kernel: the row-tile count a template constant (#805) | the branch out of the mma chain | at 2,048 rows swiglu 29.7% and down 15.4% shorter, Compute; 8,192 tokens 5.61 → 5.29 s, 32,768 21.86 → 20.71 s |

**Dropped**

| change | aim | measured, and why dropped |
|---|---|---|
| NVFP4 expert decode kernel: four k32 load groups in flight (was two) | hide load latency | 1 row 5.9% shorter, but 3 rows 7.9% and 40 rows 6.7% longer (gate/up, 2,048 wide), Compute; drafted windows and shared rounds are the rows a served decode has |
| CUDA graphs for the verify forward, captured per slot | fewer launches | level without drafts, 0.9 to 1.5% slower with them; the GPU idles 1.4% of a decode step |
| slice sums fused into the sliced decode matmul's last block | fewer launches and reads | 0.7% less in Compute, but a step 60.78 → 61.08 ms in Systems: the last block adds the slices alone at the end |
| TMA loads in the prompt tiles | less address arithmetic | 5.8% shorter in a cache-cold bench; split tiles with several stages returned wrong bytes beside another stream's device copy (not reproduced in the bench); TMA in the unsplit tile only: 32k 22.60 against 22.62 s |
| a drafted window's greedy rows exchanged at once (one all-gather, one wait) | fewer waits | within the run-to-run spread |
| a prompt chunk's exchanges in 8 pieces; 2 NCCL channels | more overlap | 32k 4% longer; no change |
| a tile for the 2,048 x 8,192 x 1,536 prompt matmul (2 slices) | Triton's 746 us there | best 821 against 841 us, cache-cold bench; 32 calls in a 32k prompt, at most 3 ms (0.08%) |
| swiglu with 8 values a thread | fewer instructions | it changes the order of a 64-value sum |
| decode exchanges overlapped with compute; independent branches on a second stream | hide the exchanges | not tried: the exchanges are 3% of a step, latency-bound, and the next op reads them; the GPU is 98.6% busy and bound by reads |

Looked at and left as is: upstream's NVFP4 lane matmul (`qmmf`, 1.1% of a decode step, Systems) and the sampled draw
(a sampled step 0.1% longer than a greedy one). Neither Nsight Compute (fixed clocks, caches flushed) nor a cache-cold
bench ranked the decode matmul setups as the served decode did, so decode changes were judged on the two GB10s.

</details>

## Receipt

- Environment: this branch at `6380c8da` on 1.0.10 (`6c5e5192`); the rows below are from one sitting on two NVIDIA GB10
  (driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.3, NCCL 2.30.7), Linux 7.0.0-1019-nvidia with `kho=off`, over RoCE with NCCL;
  `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at `423acf37`; BF16 KV; `--context 40960 --parallel 2` for the prompt and decode rows,
  `--parallel 4` for the concurrent ones.
- Exactness:
  - `tools/bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial` (levels 1 and 4, both prompts, 256 tokens, temperature 0, 3
    repetitions): all 30 replies equal their requests alone, and the alone runs equal `"draft": false`.
  - resumed = fresh: a chat conversation whose later turns resume the state kept at the history end (cached 2,048 of
    about 3,100 tokens) gives the same replies as a server without the cache, greedy, with drafts and without, and
    sampled (turns at 3,094 to 3,113 tokens).
  - In the engine at TP=2: `glm-shared-check` (108 rows of 5 streams over 12 rounds equal their lone twins byte for
    byte); `glm-lanes-concurrent` and `glm-lanes-cover` (cancels, discards mid-decode and after a rejected draft, eos
    at 0, 10, 33 and 101 tokens, max_new 1 to 5, a pass resumed at 2,048 and 4,096 against the fresh pass, 512 tokens
    with drafts) equal their plain greedy reference; rank 1 follows to the end.
  - Admission over the ranks (TP=2): with rank 1 alone under `TENSORFOLD_MEMORY_RESERVE_GIB=21`,
    `serve --context 40960 --parallel 8` stops before serving: rank 0 refuses the eight streams, naming rank 1.
  - Float64 references for every projection whose reduction order is the kernels' own (`tf-cuda-test glm-ref`, seed
    593), the worst column's error over its tolerance:

    | check | worst |
    |---|---|
    | BF16 matmul 300 rows x [512, 4096], K in 8 slices, bf16 / fp32 out | 0.550 / 2.1e-4 |
    | the same x [1280, 1536], 4 slices | 0.798 / 7.0e-4 |
    | the same x [1024, 128], 1 slice | 0.982 / 1.5e-2 |
    | router 300 rows x [256, 4096], 8 slices | 1.7e-4 |
    | top-8 of 256 weights (2^-16 relative) | 1.8e-2, no near-tie swaps |
    | latent attention, 70 rows over 1,430 keys, 32 heads | 0.181 |
    | latent sparse attention, 70 rows, up to 1,100 of 6,000 keys | 0.474 |
    | hyper-connection dots, 70 rows x 16 K blocks | 2.1e-3 |
    | DSA index scores, 96 rows, 1,536 pools | 2.1e-3; top-512 equals the host's rule |
    | KDA chain, 70 / 3 rows x 32 heads | 0.438 / 0.369 |

    Every check also holds its kernels' outputs bit-equal across row counts and forms (prompt rows against decode
    windows, fused against three-kernel KDA). The bf16 ratios near 1 are the output rounding itself (2^-8 |y|).
- Decode speed (`tools/bench_openai.py`, 256 tokens, temperature 0, 3 repetitions, median tok/s), with vLLM
  0.28.1rc1.dev580 (nightly `385dce36`) on the same checkpoint and pair, with the profile we serve it with (FP8 KV,
  MTP k=3, no CUDA graphs, one sequence), in the same sitting:

  | | fibonacci-raw | gpu-chat-no-think |
  |---|---|---|
  | this PR, drafts | 33.48 | 27.88 |
  | this PR, `--no-drafts` | 17.61 | 17.61 |
  | vLLM, MTP k=3 | 33.93 | 24.97 |
  | vLLM, no MTP | 14.16 | 14.18 |

  Four concurrent streams (`bench_concurrent.py`, level 4, the `chat` and `code` prompts): 52.8 and 68.0 tok/s in all,
  against 27.9 and 33.4 alone.
- Prompt speed (`tools/prefill_cold.py` as of `394d566c^`, which the template names and 1.0.0 removed; its `run` is
  standard library only; lengths 2k to 32k, as the server holds 40,960, three prompts each with a unique first line,
  a rest after each long one outside the timed span), median TTFT in seconds:

  | tokens | 2,048 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 32,768 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | this PR | 1.305 | 3.063 | 5.872 | 11.460 | 22.745 |
  | vLLM | 1.465 | 3.058 | 6.649 | 13.871 | 28.138 |

  A decode beside a 32k prompt waits at most 1.68 s between tokens (the prompt in 2,048-row chunks).
- Memory: the server's `/memory` peak 97.3 GiB of device memory on rank 0 (`--context 40960 --parallel 2`, through
  the 32k prompts); each host's memory in use above its idle baseline at most 100.5 GiB (this PR) and 111.7 GiB
  (vLLM, `gpu_memory_utilization` 0.80), sampled every second.
- Tests run (empty cache): `zig build test-cuda-host` 511/511, `zig build test` 617/622 (5 skipped, none failed),
  `tf-cuda-test quant-ref` 4 and `glm-ref` 11 passed, the lanes checks on a synthetic two-layer checkpoint that
  `tf-cuda-test glm-synth` writes (cover 40, concurrent 38, shared 1) and on the model cut to five layers (cover 36,
  concurrent 38); at TP=3 on three GB10s (uneven shares: 22/21/21 heads, 704/704/640 expert rows) `glm-lanes-concurrent`
  and `glm-shared-check`; `python3 tools/zig/lean_check.py` finds nothing new against 1.0.10.
- Not run, and why:
  - Metal: no Mac here. `config.zig` is shared; its parse and width tests run in `zig build test`.
  - The server at TP=3: its ranks meet over `NCCL_COMM_ID`, and NCCL then looks for a bootstrap interface on rank 0's
    subnet, which a ring of /32 addresses doesn't give the other ranks. #636's startup covers this; the family will
    take it rather than carry its own. The engine's TP=3 checks above pass.
  - Other GLM checkpoints (EXL3, MLX affine): the loader reads ModelOpt NVFP4 only; the vocabulary cut already takes
    EXL3's unit, and #806 gives EXL3's projections the fp32 outputs `qlinear` has for NVFP4 (#757).
  - TP=4: not run here (our checks are on two and three GB10s). @SvangenStudios ran `6380c8da` at TP=4 on four GB10s
    in a switchless ring (a comment on this PR): `glm-lanes-concurrent`, `glm-shared-check` and the server's
    `bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial` pass with `TF_GLM_PREFILL_REDUCE=gather` on every rank. The default split
    exchange sends rows straight between every pair of ranks, so a fabric where some pairs cannot connect needs
    `gather`. @BHCC2025's EXL3 glue on this branch passes `glm-shared-check` and `glm-lanes-concurrent` on two and
    four GB10s (#593).
  - `tools/bench_cache.py --require-reuse`: its repeats are one completion prompt with no chat history, and
    `core/prompt_cache.zig` keeps states at a chat's history end and at shared prefixes, so a CUDA host reports them
    cold (kept 0); resumed = fresh is shown with a chat conversation above.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo.
- [x] No precision traded for speed. KV stays bf16; the sums whose order is the kernels' own are the ones `glm-ref`
      bounds against float64.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release. (No release serves this checkpoint on CUDA, so against
      vLLM above; the shared kernels it carries leave prompt processing as it was, as their PRs say.)
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency. (A new family: its
      tests have no code to run before it. Its host tests run in `zig build test-cuda-host`, which does no GPU work,
      and read checked-in fixtures, not the checkpoint, so they have nothing to skip; the GPU checks are
      `tf-cuda-test` commands.)
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: Living Weights on Qwen3.8-27B (CUDA, GB10): the pocket in every pass, the trainer, --slide, and pocket neurons that no longer drive one another
items.body:
## Stack

This sits on two open PRs, so it opens as a draft until they land:

- #726 (BobClawblaw: #608, philip-pentatonic's Qwen3.8-27B CUDA engine, brought to 1.0.11 with image input, an fp8 KV
  cache and a prompt cache). #608 alone sits on 1.0.5, while the learner below sits on `main`; #726 is #608 on a base
  the learner merges into (and the base this port was built and measured on), so this stacks on #726, not #608.
  #608's commit (99bcc5b2) keeps philip's authorship; nothing of it is rewritten.
- #878 (Living Weights as a core module, `lw-b-core` 75978a1c).

The branch is `pr726` (bcd433c0) plus one merge commit of `lw-b-core` (dac84b63), then 3 commits. That merge is the only
one: the 27B's trainer needs #608/#726's qwen27 CUDA family and the learner in `zig/src/living` from #878, and neither
contains the other. Its conflicts were `zig/build/cuda.zig` (the qwen27 and living modules both kept, qwen27 imports
living) and `native/cuda.zig` (#878's slide adapter behind #726's `@hasDecl(F, "slide")`). Once #726 and #878 land I
will rebase onto `main` and the merge goes away; the diff to review is `dac84b63..lw-27b-pr`.

The first of the 3 commits carries learner work that is also open as its own PRs (the refit and recheck fixes for #870,
facts learned in conversation), as this port runs it; it shrinks to the 27B-specific parts when those land.

## What this changes

1. **The learner as the 27B's lessons run it** (e90a1035): on #878's `zig/src/living` and the server's lesson code:
   - #870's refit and recheck fixes and the conversation fix, as in their own PRs;
   - checks score a reply asked before through serving's own decode rounds instead of decoding it again
     (`slide_known.zig`, the learner's `score` request), and the lesson writer's asks run side by side;
   - **the drift fix** (below): `pocket_decouple.zig`, `Trainer.pocket_back`, broad keep prompts and drift checks;
   - `families.zig` lists `qwen3_5` (a dense SwiGLU MLP at every layer, ungated, 4-bit groups of 64);
   - `pocket.zig`, `learner.zig` and the server's big files split to stay under 600 lines.
2. **Core training kernels** (b9b3e835): the Gated DeltaNet layer's forward for training and input gradient
   (`gdn_train.cu`, `cuda/gdn_train.zig`; the same bits as serving's chain at `--fmad=false`) and gated attention's
   backward (`attn_train.cu`), family-neutral. `tf-cuda-test gdn-back`, `gdn-back-27b`.
3. **The 27B learns** (018d2b2a):
   - `qwen27/cuda/pocket.zig`: fp32 SwiGLU pocket neurons beside every MLP, added after the down projection in every
     pass (prompt chunks, drafted windows, decode rounds), row by row, so drafted equals `"draft": false`; an untaught
     stream (the lesson writer's judge) reads no pocket. A taught folder's widened MLP keeps its own 17408 rows tiled.
   - the trainer (`train.zig`, `train_more.zig`, `train_load.zig`, `train_ops.zig`, `qwen27_train.cu`): keys, loss and
     target passes with 16 sequences side by side on the engine's own batched pass; the loss gradient from the
     group-64 head through the dense MLPs and pocket, attention and the DeltaNet on MLX copies of layers 12-63
     (18.9 GiB); wide 4-bit products and a backward over only the rows a nudge needs (same bits); pocket input fits on
     the GPU with the host's bits; greedy scoring through decode rounds (a prompt pass over prompt + reply is not
     decode's arithmetic on this model: 0/576 rows bit-equal, 4/576 argmaxes differ at near ties).
   - `tap.zig`: a prompt in a conversation read through the engine's prompt pass (the context fix's `tapRows`).
   - `--slide` for `qwen3_5` (`slide.zig`, `native.zig`); the pocket written through the core's shard writer.
   - `tf-qwen27-learn`: packed passes against one at a time, the push against finite differences, `Q27_GATE` (gate
     taps with activations), `Q27_SCORE` (replies teacher-forced through serial decode); `tf-cuda-test q27-back`,
     `q27-gemm`.

## The drift fix

On a 21-fact scale test (below) the taught model's unrelated replies drifted as facts accumulated, and some grew
garbage tokens (`$x` -> `$xdera`, `Waves` -> `WavesToggleButton`). Gate taps on every unrelated reply row found why:

- On the untaught model's states the learned neurons barely leak (of 160 neurons x 3,435 unrelated rows: 0.06% above
  zero, at most +0.56). With the pocket live: 113 of 160 neurons reach above 0.25 somewhere, up to u.x = +16.5 (the fit
  targets about 1). At each garbage row about 100 of the 160 fire at once, layer by layer: one fact's neuron leaks
  +0.43 on a digit in LaTeX, its own next neurons read +0.8, +5.3, +16.2, then other facts' neurons follow.
- The same cascade runs on the facts' own questions: at a probe's decide row, untaught states give the fact's own
  neurons a median +0.94 and no other fact's neuron above 1 (0/6,400); live, 662/6,400 other facts' neurons read above
  1 (one probe: 77 of them, up to +30). The lesson logs show it growing: earlier facts' neurons firing on a new fact's
  questions read at most 3-7 by lessons 6-8 and 10-33 from lesson 13, and their refits fail. This is why later facts
  got harder to learn, not a neuron budget (at most 9 of a layer's 64 neurons were used).
- Cause: a neuron at layer L reads x = s * h / rms(h), so a lower pocket neuron's output v moves its product by
  (s * u) . v. The values fit backpropagated through the higher neurons' activations ((u x)^2, unbounded) and learned
  outputs that drive them; later lessons stacked on that.

Fix: every output is kept off what the neurons above its layer read (s * u, s from the trainer's optional `readScale`),
every input and refit off what the neurons below write there (s * v), and the values backward holds the pocket's
activations (`pocket_back`). Projecting a finished folder's outputs this way removes the cascade at once (other facts'
neurons above 1: 662 -> 25 of 6,400) but loses recall, since its outputs were fitted with the chains; fitted under the
constraint from the first lesson, recall holds (receipt). Two cheaper guards come with it: 92 broad keep prompts
(other languages and scripts, math and LaTeX, code, verse, lists) read as rows a fact stays silent on, and 12 drift
checks whose replies a round may not change where the open lesson's own neurons read above zero (a reply tipped at a
near tie by the neurons' tails below zero is logged, not held against the lesson). None of these prompts is in the
51-prompt drift set the receipt measures with. `TF_SLIDE_POCKET_COUPLE=on`, `TF_SLIDE_BROAD=off` and
`TF_SLIDE_DRIFT=off` turn each off.

## Receipt

- Environment: NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121), driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.0.88, Ubuntu 24.04.5, Zig 0.17.0;
  checkpoint `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit` revision 22d8d538 (its weights are #608's 70ae7fac), drafter
  `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` 50307d4c. Servers: `--parallel 16 --context 8192 --no-thinking --temperature 0`,
  drafts on. All replies greedy.
- Build: `zig build -Dnvcc=... -Dsm=121 -Doptimize=ReleaseFast install native`; host tests (`test-living`,
  `test-server-cpu`, `test-cuda-host`) pass; `zig fmt --check` clean; `lean_check` 527 problems, 527 on the base
  (dac84b63), 0 new.

### #608 on this GB10 (before any of this)

#608's own build against Python 0.6.6 (its environment): serial 4/4 replies match (one 4,722-token prompt), 54 window
cases with no row differing, drafted 4/4 match, multi-stream 6/6. Served at 1/4/16 streams, every reply equals alone
and `"draft": false` (12/12 cells); code T0 70.3 / 202.3 / 380.9 tok/s, cold prefill 2k 1.47 s ... 64k 58.13 s, all
within a few % of #608's own receipts. The merged learner build (#608 + #726 + the learner) passes the same checks.

### Kernels

`tf-cuda-test q27-back` 25/25 within float64 tolerance (MLP + pocket + post norm, attention with 4 kv heads, the
group-64 head; 64 and 256 rows); `gdn-back` and `gdn-back-27b` pass; `q27-gemm` 181 cases byte-equal to the 64x64
products. `tf-qwen27-learn`: packed passes equal one at a time exactly (0 difference); the push against finite
differences is bf16-limited (the residual stream is bf16), 2-36% on direct rows; learning itself is the test.

### Lessons and restarts

User facts taught by chat (`/v1/slide/learn`, `about: user`). After three facts: held-out questions 3/3, 3/3 and 2/3;
unrelated replies 7/8 unchanged (one word late in one reply); a restart with and without `--slide` gives the same replies (17/17); the base shards'
sha256 unchanged. A fact that borrowed another's neurons was found and fixed on the way (the judge's untaught stream
read the pocket; now it does not).

### Context (8 user facts, one retry each for a miss)

The same probe matrix as the Flash Next context PR: questions asked cold, under a system prompt, after 3 turns of small
talk, after an 8-turn ~4k-token task conversation, chained, and with thinking on. With this branch's learner, all 8
facts kept: cold 16/18, system 16/18, small talk 17/18, after the ~4k task chat 17/18, chained 16/16, thinking cold
8/8; unrelated 10/11 replies identical to the untaught model. Restarts plain and with `--slide`: 32/32 probes and
11/11 unrelated identical; a take-out puts the pocket back bit for bit.

### Speed (same lessons, same bits)

Two facts taught on a fresh copy before and after the speed work: the same lesson events, graph, conversations, log
lines and shard sha256. Fitting 821.1 -> 429.9 s and 315.5 -> 173.1 s; a lesson 1,551 -> 683 s and 609 -> 260 s
(the first build ran `--parallel 1`). A target pass over 16 sequences / 984 rows 3.88 -> 1.68 s. A later fact that
needs repairs: fitting 1,071.5 -> 525.9 s. The 8 context facts: 6,732 -> 3,936 s for all lessons.

### Scale: 21 facts, before and after the drift fix

The same 21 facts about a fictional person (a name, a spouse, a pet, two towns, a job, a birthday, a car, numbers, a
favourite food and game...), taught in order on a fresh copy, one retry for each miss, then the probe matrix (two
probes a fact) and the 51-prompt drift set (the 11 unrelated prompts plus 40 more: math with LaTeX, code, verse, lists,
five other languages, JSON and tables; garbage = a reply token the untaught model gives logprob below -9 after the same
prefix, scored through serial decode). "Before" is the learner without the drift fix (lw-27b 72103fc2's build).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| kept on the first try / after one retry | 12/21 / 16/21 | 17/21 / 20/21 |
| probes recalled: cold / system / small talk | 26 / 27 / 24 of 42 | 34 / 34 / 35 of 42 |
| after the ~4k task chat / chained / thinking cold | 22/42 / 24/42 / 16/21 | 33/42 / 29/42 / 18/21 |
| the 11 unrelated replies identical to the untaught model | 7/11 | 9/11 |
| the 40 more unrelated replies identical | 23/40 | 30/40 |
| replies with garbage tokens (of 51) | 9 | 0 |
| most an earlier fact's neuron reads on a new fact's questions | up to 32.8 | at most 1.9 |
| other facts' neurons above 1 at the probes' decide rows | 662/6,400 | 1/8,000 |
| neurons above 0.25 anywhere on the unrelated replies | 113/160 | 9/200 (9/200 alone) |
| lessons, total time, repairs | 30, 17,030 s, 8 | 25, 13,464 s, 2 |
| plain restart: probes / unrelated identical | 42/42, 11/11 | 42/42, 11/11 |

One fact (the spouse's name) missed after its retry in the run after; it was marginal before too (kept on its round
3-4 confirmations only).

### This branch's build

The pushed branch is the code above ported onto `dac84b63` (no Flash Next files; the DeltaNet kernels renamed to core).
On the GPU with its build: `q27-back` 25/25, `gdn-back` and `gdn-back-27b` pass, `q27-gemm` 181/181 byte-equal;
`tf-qwen27-learn` gives the same losses-and-pushes hash as the build the receipts came from (d61e74b8e32ea396, target
pass 1.43 s); untaught, all 51 drift-set replies are identical to that build's. The receipts' servers used #608's
captured kernel set (`TENSORFOLD_CUDA_KERNELS`).

## Known limits

- The cascade is cut on the residual stream's direct path; an injected fact can still reach other facts' detectors
  through the model's own layers (seen as other facts' neurons rising from -0.5 to +1.5 behind a leak), so a leaking
  neuron on a row no lesson read can still change a reply. The broad keep prompts and drift checks narrow that.
- Each output is kept off up to (neurons above) directions in 5,120: a few hundred facts' worth before that space
  binds.
- The first commit duplicates the open refit/recheck/context PRs until they land.
- The CUDA kernels were checked on sm_121 only.

Draft while #608/#726 and the learner PRs it repeats (#876, #877, #878, #891) land; I'll rebase it onto them then. Some long comments were cut to one line for the lean check and will get a read-through before it leaves draft.

items.title: Prompt reuse for Nemotron on Metal: kept states copied on the GPU, exact against cache-off
items.body:
Nemotron keeps each stream's prompt state at the prompt cache's marks and resumes a later request whose prompt extends one, as Flash Next and GLM do. This is item 1 of ZIG-PREVIEW's "where you can help".

## What changed

- `zig/src/families/nemotron/snapshot.zig` (new): a kept state is every Mamba conv and SSM state, the KV rows and the draft head's KV rows, in one Metal buffer. Save and restore are `tf_copy_u32` dispatches submitted on the engine's fenced queue: a save right after the chunk that ends at the mark, a restore right before the first chunk, so neither waits for the host. A drop drains first, since the queue holds unretained references. The module also carries the `prompt_cache.Snapshots` vtable functions.
- `zig/src/families/nemotron/backend.zig`: the prompt pass restores a kept state before its first chunk and calls the mark hook after each chunk that ends at a mark. Both the shared-lane and the lone-stream paths run `prefillFn`, so one change covers both.
- `zig/src/native/metal.zig`: the Nemotron host gets a `prompt_cache.Store` with the same budget rule as Flash Next (`cache_fit`: what 70% of RAM leaves past the loaded footprint, or `--prompt-cache-gib`; `0` turns it off).
- Docs: the `--prompt-cache-gib` and `--prompt-cache-over-cap` rows in README, the known gaps and help list in ZIG-PREVIEW, RUNBOOK, the family guide's ownership table, and a receipt section in the Nemotron recipe.

No arithmetic changes: the prompt kernels, decode kernels and reduction orders are untouched. The kept bytes are copies of live rows.

Not in this PR, listed as the next step in ZIG-PREVIEW: `--learn` for Nemotron (its states stay in memory), and a pool of kept buffers as Flash Next has. Each state allocates its own buffer today; that showed no cost at this size (below).

## Exactness

Same binary, same checkpoint, same settings; cache on against `--prompt-cache-gib 0`. Four-turn greedy chats, a 9.2k-token system prompt, 96 reply tokens a turn.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| One conversation, cached turns vs cache off | equal, 4/4 turns |
| Two conversations at once (`--parallel 4`), each vs its solo cache-off run | equal, 8/8 turns |
| `--no-drafts`, cached vs cache off | equal, 4/4 turns |
| Drafted vs `--no-drafts` | equal, 4/4 turns |

Resumes happened at 9,213 tokens (the shared system block's cut) on turns 2 and 3 and at 9,556 (the previous turn's state) on turn 4, so both kinds of kept state were exercised.

## Speed

| | Cache off | Cache on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turns 2-4, prompt time | 1.29-1.36 s | 0.28-0.31 s |
| A fresh 9.2k-token prompt, mean of 4, alternated on/off/on | 1.07 s | 1.07 s (keeping two states of 106 MiB each) |
| Two conversations at once, turns 2-4 | - | 0.40-0.60 s |

## Memory

Peak physical footprint (`/usr/bin/time -l`) for the server through two four-turn conversations of about 9k tokens: 25.08 GiB with the cache off, 25.59 GiB with it on. A kept state at 9.2k tokens is 106 MiB, most of it the fixed Mamba state.

## Receipts

- Machine: Apple M5 Ultra, 256 GB, macOS 27.0.1. Zig 0.17.0, Metal Toolchain 27A266a. Base commit f8fe17d.
- Checkpoint: `TensorFold/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit`, revision `d9d758fb83953437f7263256b0d96157e2a348b8`.
- Settings: `serve --context 32768 --temperature 0 --no-thinking`, `max_tokens` 96 (8 for the fresh-prompt timing), the repository's `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/recipes/qwen3.8-flash-next.md` (first 30k characters) as system prompts, four questions each.
- `zig build test -Dcpu=apple_m1`: 91/91 steps, 93/93 tests on the final tree, and on five earlier runs. One early run, before the final tree, had one failing host test that I did not capture and that did not recur in seven later runs.
- `zig build test-golden -Dcpu=apple_m1`: 188 equal, 0 differ, 2 known (`errors`), the same on clean `main`; the leak reports it prints come from `golden_check` itself and are the same on `main`.
- `tools/zig/lean_check.py`: 512 problems on `main`, 512 after. The five findings in the touched files are inherited (`backend.zig:299`, `backend.zig:392`, `native/metal.zig:1`, and two in `flashnext/snapshot.zig`).
- `zig fmt --check` clean; every touched source file stays under 600 lines.
- Not run: CUDA (no GB10 here; the CUDA backend's prefill is separate and unchanged), Metal on M1 to M4, prompts past 32k, and sampled requests with the cache (the matrix was greedy, as the exactness contract names it).

items.title: GLM-5.3-Flash faster oQ kernels in Zig engine
items.body:
_Rebased onto main c36b536d (1.0.9) and #773's rebased tip on 2026-10-13: no conflicts; the tip passes the gate again. The receipts below are the pre-rebase runs._

Part of #716; stacks on #773 (which stacks on #755). This branch carries their ten commits until they merge, so please review the last eight commits here (from "tf-glm-rows-speed" on). In #773 the oQ checkpoints' products at widths other than 4/64 run on the generic row kernels: prompt chunks run the absorbed MLA pair a head at a time and every 5- and 6-bit matrix row by row, decode spends extra launches on KDA's f_b/g_b, the shared expert and the MoE, and every 2-bit code is cut out with a shift and a mask. This moves those prompt products onto core `affine_mm`, folds the decode launches together with the same sums, and has core row projections read 2-bit codes in place as they already read 4-bit nibbles. On an M3 Ultra, oQ2 decodes 1.22× (code) and 1.13× (chat) faster with the same decode bits, and up to 1.34× under concurrent load; oQ4 prefills 1.33-1.37× faster and oQ2 1.06×. The uniform 4/64 path keeps its kernels, its launches and its tokens.

## What this changes

1. **`tf-glm-rows-speed`** (a test program): GPU time and GB/s of every decode product class at the shapes and widths the uniform 4/64, oQ2 and oQ4 checkpoints read, each class over at least 768 MB of weights, summed into a token's products per checkpoint; `GLM_SPEED_PROMPT=1` adds a 2048-row prompt chunk's per-head and 5/6-bit products.
2. **Prompt chunks run mlx-lm's `embed_q` and `unembed_out` on `affine_mm`, every head in one batch.** At a width `affine_mm` reads (8/64 in oQ4 and oQ2), `wide.headsBatch` runs the 64 heads as one batch over the strided rows, as the 4-bit path does with `kv_b`'s value half. Other widths keep the row launch; uniform 4/64 never reaches it.
3. **`affine_mm` reads 3-, 5- and 6-bit MLX codes exactly.** A thread's half step loads as words and each code enters the tile as itself (codes up to 63 are exact in bf16). The 2-, 4- and 8-bit sources preprocess byte-identically to before, so their compiled kernels are unchanged.
4. **Prompt chunks run 5- and 6-bit products and split-stack members on `affine_mm`.** oQ4's 5/64 and 6/64 matrices (KDA in, f_b/g_b, o_proj, MLA, the MTP layer) and each member of its split stacks (layer 6's KDA input, layer 7's and the MTP's `x_proj` and `qr_proj`) where its rows fill 64-row tiles; the 32-row indexer `weights_proj` stays on the row kernels.
5. **Decode makes f_b's and g_b's dots inside `kda_rows` at one width, the same bits as made apart.** Each simdgroup sums four of the head's rows with core `tf_rp_rows` and rounds them to bf16 as `glm_rows` does. Two launches and a scratch round trip a KDA layer fewer (68 a token).
6. **Decode runs the shared expert's gate, up and SwiGLU in one launch at its width, the same bits.** Through the routed experts' by-id GLU kernel with every id 0. One launch a MoE layer fewer (42 a token).
7. **Decode runs routed experts by pick and the 8-bit shared expert in two launches, the same bits** (`glm_moe_rows`, taken when every expert matrix is one run in groups of 64, the routed of one width, the shared at 8 bits). Two launches a MoE layer fewer (84 a token). Uniform 4/64 keeps the generated gathers and oQ4 (routed 4/64) its generated routed kernels.
8. **Core row projections read 2-bit codes in place, as they read 4-bit nibbles.** `tf_rp_qdot16` masks each 2-bit code where it sits (code × 4^i) and `tf_rp_load16` scales that code's input by 4^-i, a power of two, so every product is the same float and every sum keeps its order. Every 2-bit row product takes it, GLM-5.3-Flash's routed experts among them.

M5 (tensor units): GLM has no tensor-unit-only kernel; `affine_mm` compiles its tensor-unit variant there and the new 3/5/6-bit sources take the same code path. Not run on M5 (no hardware).

## Exactness

TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-oQ2-MTP @dc55627, TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-oQ4-MTP @9872546 and the uniform 4/64 checkpoint #773 used, greedy, MTP drafts on unless `"draft": false`; `serve <checkpoint> --name glm --parallel 2 --context 16384 --prompt-cache-gib 0`. Before is #773's tip 9777aeb2; after is 7ea90233, this branch's tip 347f88a1 but for one test's expected count (commit 7's compile-failure test counts its new pipelines; no engine source differs).

- **Decode bits.** Commits 5 to 8 keep every decode product's bits, and the code prompt (14 tokens, which GLM runs through its 1-16-row window path) gives the same 256 tokens before and after on every checkpoint (oQ2 `b7932757843f`, oQ4 `7cd4ab7084c3`, uniform `370c5ca7e2df`).
- **Prompt bits.** Commits 2 to 4 change the order of oQ prompt products' sums (`affine_mm`'s tiles in place of the row kernels), within the same float64 bound, so the chat prompt (32 tokens, a prompt chunk) continues differently: oQ2 `8e524c1de404` → `19eac26b10c1`, oQ4 `810fec766b0f` → `09e32b8f5a89`. The uniform 4/64 chat hash is unchanged (`e2cf3b4b33c0`). Fidelity against oMLX is below.
- **oQ2 and oQ4, after:** concurrent equals solo (`bench_concurrent`'s alone and serial checks at 1 and 4 requests, both prompts: 34/34 on each); cancellation, reset and partial acceptance, 25 steps, pass on each (a fresh `"draft": false` probe gives the reference hash and the drafted probe equals it, with partial acceptance seen; then after a stream dropped mid-decode, a long prompt dropped mid-prompt, a stream dropped beside a running probe and a request past the window, the drafted and plain probes equal the fresh hashes; oQ2 `89faa950b278` / `ad8ca98b7043`, oQ4 `7152f0a8505e` / `c9b4aa96047f`).
- **Rows and float64.** `tf-glm-rows-check` at the tip: PASS, worst 0.9839 of the float64 bound (the routed 2-bit decode classes' worst 0.8564, as before commit 8). New checks, each failing before its commit: the per-head batch equals each head's own `affine_mm` product; split stacks on `affine_mm` equal each member alone at the 64-padded pitch; 5- and 6-bit prompt classes against float64 on `affine_mm`; the fused f_b/g_b in `kda_rows` equal `.pre`'s outputs, state and conv window byte for byte at 2/3/4/5/6/8 bits; `wide.glu` equals `glm_swiglu`(dense gate | up); `wide.moe` equals the by-id GLU and down plus `wide.glu` and dense. `tf-affine-ref` adds q3, q5 and q6 at g32 and g64: PASS (bf16 out at most 0.4868 of the bound, every row's bits equal in windows of 1 to 65 rows), the earlier formats unchanged.
- **Precision.** Activations stay bf16; every product keeps fp32 group sums; the 2-bit pre-scale is a power of two, so it changes no product.

## Performance

Mac Studio, M3 Ultra (80-core GPU), 256 GB, macOS 26.4.1 (25E253), Zig 0.17.0. Fresh builds, `zig build native -Dcpu=apple_m1`; `tensorfold-native` sha256 `d508376cf1fd…` (before) and `dac50042463d…` (after). Every run starts from a fresh server, with other checkpoints' file cache evicted first. Rows are in run order.

**Decode and concurrency.** `bench_openai.py … --tokens 256 --reps 3 --temperatures 0` (medians; `fibonacci-raw`, code, and `gpu-chat-no-think`, chat) and `bench_concurrent.py --levels 1,4 --alone --serial` (aggregate tok/s; 4 requests share the 2 streams):

| Run | `bench_openai` code | chat | concurrent code ×1 | code ×4 | chat ×1 | chat ×4 | Peak footprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| oQ2, before 1 | 101.12 | 53.73 | 101.0 | 91.1 | 53.3 | 56.1 | 113.70 GB |
| oQ2, before 2 | 101.24 | 53.74 | 101.2 | 91.3 | 53.6 | 56.2 | 113.70 GB |
| oQ2, after 1 | **123.13** | **60.57** | 123.0 | 110.4 | 60.2 | 75.4 | 113.76 GB |
| oQ2, before 3 | 101.31 | 53.92 | 101.3 | 91.4 | 53.9 | 56.3 | 113.70 GB |
| oQ2, after 2 | 123.24 | 61.10 | 123.2 | 110.6 | 60.1 | 75.4 | 113.70 GB |
| oQ4, before 1 | 62.80 | 55.38 | 62.7 | 83.9 | 54.7 | 69.0 | 189.42 GB |
| oQ4, before 2 | 62.83 | 55.87 | 62.6 | 83.7 | 55.2 | 72.0 | 189.43 GB |
| oQ4, after | 63.10 | 52.80 | 62.8 | 84.5 | 52.5 | 70.0 | 189.44 GB |
| uniform 4/64, before | 102.96 | 60.65 | | | | | 185.32 GB |
| uniform 4/64, after | 102.93 | 60.61 | | | | | 185.32 GB |

oQ2's code prompt gives the same tokens in the same 65 rounds before and after (chat: 113 rounds against 116, on its new tokens), so its gain is the rounds' time: 2-bit routed experts are oQ2's widest bytes in every verify window, and commit 8 reads them in place. oQ2 now decodes code at 1.20× and chat at 1.01× of the uniform checkpoint on the same build. oQ4's decode products are unchanged here (its routed experts are 4/64, on the generated kernels) and so is its code speed; its chat prompt now continues on other tokens (above) that take 144 rounds against 136, at the same 33.7-34.0 ms a round, hence 0.95× on chat. The uniform runs' kernels, launches and tokens are unchanged (`bench_openai` decode only).

**Cold prefill** (oQ2 and oQ4; before and after). Exact token arrays: upstream's public prefill paragraph ("A lighthouse keeper writes in the log as the boats cross the bay.", `tools/zig/qwen27_gate.py`) repeated and tokenized once without special tokens; `/v1/completions` with the ids, `max_tokens 1`, `--parallel 1 --context 34816 --prompt-cache-gib 0`, every request cold (`cached_tokens` 0), a 2k warmup, one rep a size:

| Tokens | oQ2 before tok/s (s) | oQ2 after | oQ4 before | oQ4 after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,048 | 465.8 (4.40) | **493.9 (4.15)** | 373.1 (5.49) | **496.0 (4.13)** |
| 8,192 | 469.5 (17.45) | **500.1 (16.38)** | 370.8 (22.09) | **501.2 (16.34)** |
| 32,768 | 471.0 (69.57) | **500.6 (65.46)** | 366.4 (89.43) | **502.3 (65.24)** |

The uniform 4/64 prefills at 512.0 / 518.3 / 519.8 tok/s at these sizes in #773 (`--context 66560`, three reps), and its prompt kernels are unchanged here: oQ2 and oQ4 now prefill at 0.96-0.97× of it.

**Per projection class** (`tf-glm-rows-speed`, synthetic weights at the checkpoints' shapes and widths, each class over at least 768 MB; before is commit 1 alone on #773's tip, after this branch; two alternated runs each, ranges):

| Decode, one row | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| oQ2 MoE layer (routed 2/64 + shared 8/64) | 178.0 µs (129.7 + 48.3, four launches) | **131.0 µs** (two launches) |
| oQ2 routed 2/64 by pick alone | 129.7 µs (485 GB/s) | **92.5-92.7 µs** |
| KDA step, f_b/g_b at 5/64 | 31.7-32.0 µs (`.pre`) | **23.3-23.7 µs** (fused) |
| a token's products, oQ2 | 18.75 ms (620 GB/s) | **16.48-16.50 ms** (706 GB/s) |
| a token's products, oQ4 | 19.97-19.99 ms | 19.57 ms |
| a token's products, uniform 4/64 | 13.73-13.74 ms | 13.66-13.69 ms |

| Prompt chunk, 2048 rows, a launch | Before (row kernels) | After (`affine_mm`) |
|---|---|---|
| `embed_q` 8/64, 64 heads (×11 a chunk) | 15.2 ms | **1.8 ms** |
| `unembed_out` 8/64, 64 heads (×11) | 10.3 ms | **1.9 ms** |
| KDA in [24896, 4096] 5/64 / 6/64 | 85.0 / 83.2 ms | **19.6 / 19.7 ms** |
| [4096, 8192] 5/64 / 6/64 | 36.7 / 36.0 ms | **6.6 / 6.6 ms** |
| [1536, 4096] 5/64 / 6/64 | 11.1 / 11.1 ms | **1.4 / 1.5 ms** |

Byte roofline: a decode token reads 9.65 GB on the uniform checkpoint, 11.63 GB on oQ2 and 13.75 GB on oQ4 (oQ's non-expert matrices are mostly 8-bit), so at the ~705 GB/s these products now reach, oQ decode cannot pass the uniform checkpoint on one row; verify windows read each 2-bit expert they pick, which is where oQ2 gains.

## Memory

Physical footprint (`darwin_rusage_info_v4`, the server process, `--parallel 2 --context 16384`), the same before and after: oQ2 113.70 GB after load, peak 113.70-113.76 GB; oQ4 189.38 GB, peak 189.4 GB; the new pipelines add nothing measurable.

## Fidelity

Teacher-forced against oMLX 0.7.1.dev1 on the same checkpoints and the same fixed histories as #773 (oMLX's reference reran here and is byte-identical to #773's): upstream's four public teacher prompts, 1,024 positions, top two at every position from `tf-glm-teacher` (a test program, not in the PR), which prefills each prompt through the prompt chunks and feeds every history token in a one-row window. The uniform 4/64 is unchanged (#773: 28 differences, 26 beyond the tie policy).

| Checkpoint | #773 differences (beyond the tie policy) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| oQ4 | 19 (12) | 20 (14) |
| oQ2 | 29 (22) | 29 (25) |

The decode bits are #773's, so the change comes from the prompt chunks' new sum order (commits 2-4), which moves the prompt's state within the float64 bound and with it which near ties fall either way. Both checkpoints stay at or near the uniform checkpoint's 28, and in every difference this branch's pick is oMLX's second or third token. The widest is oQ4's copy position 181, where oMLX's margin is 2.625 and this branch picks oMLX's second token.

The one failing step is main's own `core.checkpoint_metal` split-checkpoint test (it logs an error on the path it expects), as in #755 and #773.
- `tf-glm-rows-check` and `tf-affine-ref` pass at the tip (above), with each commit's new check failing before it.
- `python3 tools/zig/lean_check.py`: 533 problems at every commit, #773's count (main 539), no new findings. Every touched file is at or under 600 lines; `zig fmt` clean.

## Platforms

- Run: Metal on a Mac Studio M3 Ultra, 256 GB (80-core GPU, no tensor units), macOS 26.4.1, Xcode 26.6, Zig 0.17.0.
- Also run, thanks to @sethforprivacy on an M5 Ultra (tensor units): `tf-glm-rows-check` and `tf-affine-ref` PASS at 347f88a.
- Not run: M1, M2 and M4 (no hardware; they take the same kernels as the M3); CUDA (no CUDA code changes).
- Not run: M5, where `affine_mm` compiles its tensor-unit variant for the new widths. Commands:

```
zig build tf-glm-rows-check tf-affine-ref tf-glm-rows-speed native -Dcpu=apple_m1
./zig-out/bin/tf-glm-rows-check
./zig-out/bin/tf-affine-ref
./zig-out/native/bin/tensorfold-native serve <oQ2 or oQ4 dir> --name glm --context 16384 --parallel 2
```

then, greedy: a request and the same with `"draft": false` (same tokens), and two requests at once against each alone.

## Reproduction settings

As #773: `GLM_LOAD_LIMIT_GB=208` (set as the machine's owner; oQ4's plan is over the default 70% of RAM), `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` 240000, one model process at a time behind one GPU lock, other checkpoints' file cache evicted before each load.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo (oQ2 and oQ4 served on the tip; uniform tokens equal #773's).
- [x] No precision traded for speed. If the bits change, the description says which sums change and why: the oQ prompt products' order on `affine_mm` (above), within the same float64 bound.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release: oQ4 prefills 1.33-1.37× and oQ2 1.06× faster; the uniform prompt kernels are unchanged.
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

Receipts: https://gist.github.com/grantoverton/7f9b0a1b3ba7919e11ad8f49f0f0acf1

items.title: GLM-5.3-Flash support for oQ in Zig engine
items.body:
_Rebased onto main c36b536d (1.0.9) on 2026-10-13: no conflicts in this change's code; every commit passes the gate again on the new base._

Part of #716; stacks on #755. This branch carries #755's six commits until that one merges, so please review the last four commits here (from "GLM-5.3-Flash reads each module's MLX affine width and mlx-lm's layout" on). GLM-5.3-Flash types every projection as 4-bit/group-64 on main (`weights.zig`'s `Q4`), so an oQ checkpoint cannot even be planned. With this, TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-oQ2-MTP @dc55627 and TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-oQ4-MTP @9872546 load, draft and serve exactly on an M3 Ultra. Nothing here waits for an M5: GLM has no tensor-unit-only kernel (its `*_nax` kernels take the simdgroup-matrix fragments without tensor units), and every width now has a product before tensor units. The uniform 4/64 checkpoint keeps its load plan (a digest pinned before the change), its kernels and its launches.

## What this changes

Four commits on the shared change:

1. **GLM-5.3-Flash reads each module's MLX affine width and mlx-lm's layout; a width-carrying matrix replaces `Q4`.**
   - Widths (`quant.zig`): each module's width from `config.json` through `core/quant`, then GLM's own spellings (the MTP block is layer 45; `forget_gate` folds into the KDA gate). Aliases that disagree, a missing table and other modes are refused; a tensor stored at another width than declared is refused by name, never read at a guessed width.
   - `Affine{bits, group}` in place of `Q4` (`affine.zig`): stored shapes, byte spans and column cuts follow each tensor's width. A fused matrix whose members differ in format plans one run a member at its output rows, as 0.6.6's `QSplit` (`glm5_next/linear.py`); a one-format stack stays one matrix. The load plan counts layer and expert bytes at those widths.
   - mlx-lm's layout (`names.zig`), which the public oQ checkpoints use: the MTP block, hyper-connections, stacked experts, the absorbed `embed_q`/`unembed_out` pair and a bf16 `eh_proj`. A fused `conv1d.weight` is cut into q/k/v; fp32 hyper-connection mixes and router narrow to bf16 only when exact, else the load is refused naming the tensor, shard, offset and shape.
   - A real load still refuses any matrix the 4/64 kernels cannot read until the next commit; TP2 and expert parallel refuse any width but 4/64.
2. **GLM-5.3-Flash runs every MLX width on GPUs without tensor units, split stacks a product a member.** `glm_rows.metal` (`wide.zig`) runs over core `row_projection`'s fp32 group sums, 2/3/4/5/6/8 bits in groups of 32/64/128, every row its own sums:
   - dense, with input and output row strides and per-head batching: each split-stack member at its own output rows (oQ4's KDA input, q and v at 5 bits and k, f_a, g_a, b at 8, is six products), and mlx-lm's `embed_q` and `unembed_out` a head at a time;
   - by expert id (decode's routed experts, gate and up fused with SwiGLU, using `glm_glue`'s helpers rather than a copy) and by sorted pairs (the prompt's routed experts), then the existing combine;
   - bf16 (the MTP head's unquantized `eh_proj`), and the embedding at 6 and 8 bits.
   - KDA f_b and g_b at 4/64 keep the generated kernel's fused dots; at any other width they are row products first, and one instance of the generated `kda_rows` reads them in place of its dots (0.6.6's unfused shape). They borrow the dense MLP scratch, so a config whose KDA width outgrows it is refused.
   - A shared expert not at 4/64 runs its own products (no shared-in-routed launch); routed experts not at 4/64 run by id and by sorted pair. Prompt chunks: a one-width 8/64 matrix runs on core `affine_mm`, split stacks and other widths on the row kernels.
   - The new pipelines load only when a checkpoint has a matrix the 4/64 kernels cannot read, their source hash joins the kernels' identity, and a failed compile releases every pipeline built before it. Refusals at load, by name: a member whose rows are not a multiple of 4, routed gate and up at two widths, any width but 4/64 with TP2 or expert parallel.
3. **`tf-glm-rows-check`**: GLM's products at every MLX width against float64, and each row's bits in every launch.
4. **GLM-5.3-Flash prompt chunks gather 2-bit routed experts on core `affine_mm`.** oQ2's 2/64 routed experts spent 81% of a 2048-row chunk's GPU time on the sorted row kernels; they now take `gatherGlu`/`gatherTo` on `affine_mm`'s 2/64 pipelines, as 4/64 experts do. Decode is unchanged.

## Exactness

TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-oQ2-MTP @dc55627, TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-oQ4-MTP @9872546, and the uniform 4/64 (below), greedy, MTP drafts on unless `"draft": false`. Same checkpoint, binary and settings within each comparison.

- Before: main refuses oQ2 and oQ4 at load (every projection is `Q4`).
- **Uniform 4/64, main against this branch.** The published TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP @76add2a had not finished downloading, so I built the same checkpoint from the public BF16: every 2-D language-model weight but the router quantized to MLX affine 4/64 (round to nearest), everything else copied as stored, written with the published shard headers. All 43 shard headers, the index and the side files are byte-equal to the published ones, so every name, dtype, shape and offset is the published one. Main and this branch alternated twice (main, branch, branch, main): both plan 180.58 GB; **every `bench_openai` and `bench_concurrent` token hash is identical across the four runs**, and the earlier exactness runs gave all 21 contract hashes identical (four prompts plain and drafted, resumed equals fresh at 0 and 2,425 cached tokens and on a cache-off server, the second turn resumed equals a cache-off server, concurrent equals solo with 2 streams).
- **oQ2 @dc55627** (plan 109.01 GB: 2-bit/64 ×126, 4-bit/64 ×3, 8-bit/64 ×290; loads in 20 to 24 s): drafted equals `"draft": false` 4/4 at 160 tokens (MTP acceptance 74 to 88%); resumed equals fresh (a 2,427-token prompt at 0 and 2,425 cached tokens); the second turn resumed at 2,425 equals a server with `--prompt-cache-gib 0`; concurrent equals solo (`bench_concurrent`'s alone and serial checks at 1 and at 4 requests over 2 streams, both prompts: 34/34 equal); greedy text sane ("3:15 PM + 2:30 = 5:45 PM").
- **oQ4 @9872546** (plan 184.66 GB: 4-bit/64 ×129, 5-bit ×36, 6-bit ×17, 8-bit ×250; loads in 36 s on a fresh server): drafted equals plain 4/4 (MTP acceptance 72 to 82%); resumed equals fresh at 0 and 2,425 cached tokens and on a cache-off server; the second turn equals a cache-off server; concurrent equals solo (34/34, as for oQ2); greedy text sane ("210 / 84 = 2.5 hours … 5:45 PM"). oQ4 is the checkpoint with mixed stacks: layer 6's KDA input (5/8/5/8/8/8) and the split MLA `x_proj`/`qr_proj` of layer 7 and the MTP layer.
- **Cancellation, reset and partial acceptance** (`--parallel 2`, on oQ2 and oQ4): a fresh `"draft": false` probe (each bench prompt, greedy, 128 tokens) gives the reference hash and the drafted probe equals it, with partial acceptance seen (accepted < drafted) on one prompt (oQ2) and both (oQ4); then after a stream dropped mid-decode, a long prompt dropped mid-prompt, a stream dropped beside a running probe (whose hash is checked too) and a request past the window (refused, the reset path), the drafted and plain probes equal the fresh hashes. 25 steps, pass, on each checkpoint (hashes oQ2 `89faa950b278` / `fd4c707155c9`, oQ4 `7152f0a8505e` / `0821b2106b69`).
- **Seams** (`tf-glm-seams`, a test program on this branch, not in the PR): the exact 2,048-token public prefill array, in the engine's one 16,384-row chunk against chunks of 128 and of 37, comparing every KDA layer's recurrent and conv state, the MLA rows and the last row's logits at seams 256, 512, …, 1,792, the prompt end, and after 64 one-row decode windows.
  - Against 128: byte-equal at every seam, the prompt end and after decode, on oQ2, oQ4 and the uniform 4/64.
  - Against 37: equal at seams 256 to 1,536; the first difference is KDA layer 0's state at 1,792, where the 37-row chunks leave a final chunk of 16 rows, which GLM sends through its 1-16-row window path (`forward.zig`) rather than the prompt path (`prompt.zig`). Main does the same on the uniform 4/64: I ran the same test program on main 0efbd447 (the program only, no engine change) and it gives the same result, part for part. This is #743's item 3 (prompt chunks and 16-row windows give different bits); the 256-token token streams of prompt chunks and of `GLM_PROMPT=0` windows also differ on main and here, with identical hashes on both.
- **Rows.** Every new product gives a row the same bits alone and in 2-, 3- and 16-row windows; strided equals contiguous; per head equals each head dense; by id equals dense; GLU by id equals `glm_swiglu`(dense gate | up); sorted equals by id (experts of 8, 5, 2 and 1 pairs); the row kernels equal core `row_projection`; a split stack in one call equals each member alone (oQ4's KDA input 5/8/5/8/8/8 and `x_proj` 6/6/5/5, at the decode pitch and the 64-padded prompt pitch); 2/64 experts gathered on `affine_mm` equal the dense product. 1,976,704 bit-equal pairs.
- **KDA state.** The separate f_b/g_b products followed by `kda_rows` equal the generated 4/64 `kda_rows` byte for byte in the output, the recurrent state and the conv window, on every 4-bit code with random per-group power-of-two scales and nonzero biases.
- **Precision.** Activations stay bf16; every row product keeps fp32 group sums; an fp32 mix or router is narrowed only when bf16 holds it exactly.
