- **`GLM_LOAD_LIMIT_GB=208`**, which I set as the machine's owner. The default limit is 70% of RAM, 179.2 GB here, and the plan is 184.7 GB for oQ4 and 180.6 GB even for the official uniform 4-bit, so neither loads on a 256 GB Mac without it (oQ2 at 109 GB does). The limit only admits the load and changes no arithmetic. The engine warns that past 70% a load can stall macOS until its watchdog restarts the Mac: run nothing else large beside it.
- The machine's `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` is 240000, also set by me.
- One model process on the machine at a time, every load and check program behind one GPU lock, and other checkpoints' file cache evicted before each load: the loader's paced reads wait for free memory, so another model's cached pages slow a big load (the first oQ4 load took 141 s that way, 36 s after eviction).

## Where the arithmetic differs from 0.6.6

Bit equality with 0.6.6's kernels is not the bar (#716); the float64 bound per product, row invariance and the exactness contract are.

- Row products keep fp32 group sums at every width; 0.6.6's `qmv_rows_b` rounds group sums to bf16 at 5 and 6 bits.
- 2-bit routed experts: the row kernels in decode and `affine_mm` in prompts, with fp32 sums, not MLX's 2-bit `quantized_matmul`. One-width 8/64 prompt products run on `affine_mm`.
- Split-stack prompts run each member on the row kernels, not `PM.matmul`.
- An fp32 mix or router that bf16 cannot hold exactly is refused (`InexactBf16`), where 0.6.6's `bf16_if_exact` keeps it in fp32.
- TP2 and expert parallel refuse any width but 4/64 (one Mac only here).

## The open question in #716

GLM follows 0.6.6's `QSplit`: once a fused matrix's members differ in format, every member is its own product at its own output rows, members that share a width included. Nothing is grouped across members, so the per-member column map #716 asks about isn't needed here (Flash Next is the family that uses one).

## Follow-ups

- #743's item 3 (above): prompt chunks and 16-row windows give different bits, on main and here; a final chunk of 16 rows or fewer takes the window path.
- Prompt chunks with `embed_q` run the decode's per-head launch serially over the chunk's rows.
- oQ2's prompt: a 2048-row chunk now spends 42% in the routed experts (81% before the last commit), and about a quarter each in KDA and MLA.
- oQ decode and prefill speed on Macs without tensor units (above): a separate PR series.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo (oQ4, oQ2 and the uniform 4/64, full models, served).
- [x] No precision traded for speed. Every new product keeps fp32 group sums; the differences from 0.6.6 are listed above.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release: the uniform 4/64 prefills 2k to 128k at main's rate (above). The oQ checkpoints have no before-run (main refuses them).
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

Receipts: https://gist.github.com/grantoverton/57663bbdd9b1ebcd4d5524e310923403

items.title: Qwen3.8-27B support for oQ in Zig engine
items.body:
_Rebased onto main c36b536d (1.0.9) on 2026-10-13: two conflicts in `model.zig` with 1.0.9's Neural Engine share, merged by hand (the share still loads only for a uniform MLP); every commit passes the gate again. One commit added at the end: the M5 fix @sethforprivacy reported below (a run a tensor-unit tile doesn't divide takes the row kernels on every chip), with a test. On the rebased series 27B oQ2 serves exactly on the M3 (concurrent equals solo, the 25 cancellation steps pass with the same reference hashes)._

Part of #716; stacks on #755. This branch carries #755's six commits until that one merges, so please review the last ten commits here (from "The 27B resolves each loaded module's affine width" on). The Qwen3.8-27B admits only 4-bit/group-64 on main (`UnqualifiedQwenFormat`). With this it loads, drafts and serves TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-oQ4 @fb60862 (4/5/6-bit) and TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-oQ2 @086dcb0 (2/3/5/6/8-bit), and any checkpoint whose loaded modules are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 8 bits in groups of 32, 64 or 128. The uniform 4-bit/group-64 checkpoint keeps its packed bytes, pipeline keys, kernels and launches.

## What this changes

Nine commits on the shared change:

1. **The 27B resolves each loaded module's affine width and admits it against the kernels this chip runs** (`qwen27/widths.zig`, through `core/quant`). Only the modules the engine loads are resolved, so MTP and vision overrides never refuse a checkpoint. A width or group the projection kernels cannot run refuses the load, naming the module, layer and width.
2. **The 27B loads mixed-width oQ checkpoints: each projection carries its width** (`projection.zig`, `gpu_weights.zig` on main's staged load, `quant_gpu.zig`). Every member is staged and read at its own width (`k * bits / 32` words, `k / group` metadata). Kernels by width: before tensor units `simd_qmm` for 4/64 matrices and the row kernel for every other width; on tensor units the non-reg lane kernel. The pipeline key carries bits, group and stride. The embedding takes the checkpoint's width (oQ2's is 8-bit). The Neural Engine prompt share, which decodes 4-bit codes only, is created only when every MLP matrix is 4/64. Synthetic graphs load at uniform 4/64.
3. **The DFlash2 drafter borrows the target embedding and head at their checkpoint widths.** The draft vocabulary copies whole rows (or 32-row tiles) of `k * bits / 8` bytes and `k / group` metadata, and the borrowed embedding is validated at its resolved width. The draft-head check covers 2-, 4- and 8-bit heads (oQ2's head is 2-bit).
4. **A mixed 27B stack runs every member as its own product, as the reference does.** 0.6.6 stacks fused members only when all share one width and group; otherwise each member is its own call at its own K split (`lane_fuse.py:88-91`, `row_matmul.py:110-117`). Members of one width beside a member of another no longer share a product.
5. **A mixed 27B stack writes each member into the fused rows at a stride before tensor units:** one row-kernel launch per member over all rows, through core's output row stride, in place of one launch a row.
6. **`tf-qwen27-widths`**: the family's own products for every 27B projection class at every oQ width against float64, without tensor units.
7. **`tf-qwen27-widths` gathers the embedding at 8 and 3 bits against float64.**
8. **`tf-qwen27-run --seams N`** (test program only): with `--compare-chunk C` it also compares `Session.fingerprint()` (every GDN layer's recurrent and conv state, the visible KV rows of every attention layer, the last row's bf16 logits) after the decoded reply in both arms, and for every N-th prompt row prefills the prompt up to that row at `--chunk` and at C and compares the fingerprints byte for byte. Any difference fails the run. So the seam receipts below can be reproduced.
9. **The 27B keeps timed window costs per checkpoint widths.** The draft-window costs are cached per build, chip and model shape, and every 27B checkpoint has one shape, so whichever checkpoint a build served first wrote the costs every later one read. A mixed-width checkpoint now adds a tag of its widths to the shape; a uniform 4-bit g64 checkpoint keeps its shape string, so its key and costs are unchanged. Host test: the uniform checkpoint's key is main's string, and oQ4 and oQ2 get distinct nonzero tags.

## Exactness

TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-oQ4 @fb60862, TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-oQ2 @086dcb0 and the uniform Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit @70ae7fa, each with z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 (`model.safetensors` sha256 `67fc76d68dc5a941…`), greedy. Every check below ran on this branch's tip (`4191469d`, a fresh build: `tensorfold-native` sha256 `d640b9501b70d250…`, `tf-qwen27-run` `bedbe3942f0e7b74…`).

- Before: main refuses oQ4 and oQ2 with `UnqualifiedQwenFormat`.
- **Drafted, resumed, concurrent** (`--parallel 2 --context 65536`): on oQ4, oQ2 and the uniform 4-bit each, drafted equals `"draft": false` 9/9 and resumed equals fresh 2/2 (a 26,130-token prompt resumed at 26,123 cached tokens, same token hash); `bench_concurrent.py --levels 1,2 --alone --serial`: every cell equal, 0 unequal, 0 failed. At `--parallel 4 --context 65536 --prompt-cache-gib 0`, `bench_concurrent.py --levels 1,4 --alone --serial`: every alone cell (3 at one stream, 12 at four) and serial cell equal, 0 failed, on all three checkpoints; on the uniform checkpoint the code and chat token hashes (`2b28aa2108de`, `cbdd31cd4736`) equal main's in every run.
- **Seams** (`tf-qwen27-run --seams 256`, commit 8): the exact 2,048-token public prefill array, chunk 128 against 16 and against 37, 64 decoded tokens. On oQ4, oQ2 and the uniform 4-bit, the state/KV/logits fingerprint is byte-equal at every 256th prompt row (7 seams, each prompt ending there), at the prompt end and after the decoded reply, for both chunk pairs.
- **Synthetic:** `tf-qwen27-synthetic`, `tf-qwen27-lanes-check` (lane core equals plain), `tf-qwen27-dflash-synthetic`, `tf-qwen27-served-check` and `tf-qwen27-dflash-served-check` pass at every commit.
- **Rows.** Before tensor units every non-4/64 product is the row kernel, which gives a row the same bits in any window; `tf-qwen27-widths` checks every class's rows in calls of 1, 2, 3, 8, 16, 17 and 128 rows, so prompt chunks and decode rows are the same arithmetic.
- **Cancellation, reset and partial acceptance** (`--parallel 4`, on oQ4, oQ2 and the uniform 4-bit): a fresh `"draft": false` probe (each bench prompt, greedy, 128 tokens) gives the reference hash and the drafted probe equals it, with partial acceptance seen (accepted < drafted) on both prompts; then after a stream dropped mid-decode, a long prompt dropped mid-prompt, a stream dropped beside a running probe (whose hash is checked too) and a request past the window (refused, the reset path), the drafted and plain probes equal the fresh hashes. 25 steps, pass, on each checkpoint (hashes oQ4 `c201c615aba6` / `d8c31284ff02`, oQ2 `2ec414650f51` / `70d57ef6b44f`, uniform `f5c9409cfe40` / `73e9fd21b09e`, as main).
- **Precision.** Activations stay bf16; every product keeps fp32 group sums. No existing sum on the uniform path changes.

## Accuracy against float64, per projection class

`tf-qwen27-widths` on the M3 Ultra (no tensor units): the family's own products (`quant_gpu.Kernels.quant` on `projection.prepare`'s matrices: the row kernel, or `simd_qmm` at 4/64, as a chip without tensor units picks them) on seeded synthetic MLX affine weights at each class's real shape, at 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 bits, group 64, which covers every width oQ4 and oQ2 use. The reference is `core.quant.mlx.reference` in float64; every column up to 1,024 columns, else 512 (the first and last 128 and 256 strided). Prompt is one 128-row call, decode one row a call, on identical input rows.

Worst column per class over the six widths, as a fraction of the fp32-sum bound (the width it occurs at), and the worst column's |err| over its largest |y|:

| Class | Shape | Prompt | Decode | Worst \|err\| / max\|y\| | Scales 1% off, least |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GDN in_proj_qkv | [10240, 5120] | 0.4757 (q5) | 0.4757 (q5) | 3.79e-3 | 7.2× |
| GDN in_proj_z | [6144, 5120] | 0.4774 (q8) | 0.4774 (q8) | 3.83e-3 | 7.4× |
| GDN in_proj_b | [48, 5120] | 0.4673 (q2) | 0.4673 (q2) | 3.72e-3 | 5.2× |
| GDN in_proj_a | [48, 5120] | 0.4647 (q8) | 0.4647 (q8) | 3.71e-3 | 6.4× |
| GDN out_proj | [5120, 6144] | 0.4754 (q6) | 0.4754 (q6) | 3.86e-3 | 5.8× |
| attention q_proj | [12288, 5120] | 0.4782 (q5) | 0.4782 (q5) | 3.78e-3 | 7.6× |
| attention k_proj | [1024, 5120] | 0.4770 (q4) | 0.4770 (q4) | 3.77e-3 | 8.3× |
| attention v_proj | [1024, 5120] | 0.4801 (q4) | 0.4801 (q4) | 3.82e-3 | 7.6× |
| attention o_proj | [5120, 6144] | 0.4747 (q4) | 0.4747 (q4) | 3.67e-3 | 6.3× |
| MLP gate_up | [34816, 5120] | 0.4715 (q3) | 0.4715 (q3) | 3.81e-3 | 6.9× |
| MLP down_proj | [5120, 17408] | 0.4394 (q8) | 0.4394 (q8) | 3.88e-3 | 2.1× |
| lm_head | [248320, 5120] | 0.4808 (q6) | 0.4808 (q6) | 3.88e-3 | 6.9× |

10,575,872 values within 0.482 of the bound (bf16 output rounding dominates), 1,515,200,224 bit-equal pairs. Prompt and decode agree because the row kernel's bits don't depend on the call's row count.

- **Mixed stacks** [z4 | b5 a5], [z4 b4 | a5], [z2 b2 | a3] and [k5 | v6], built as the loader builds them: every row's bits equal in every call; each member's columns within the bound and equal, bit for bit, to its own product and to the member loaded as a matrix of its own, except a 4-bit z (below).
- **Embedding** (`q27_embed`) at [248320, 5120], group 64, 64 tokens including both ends of the vocabulary and a repeat: every gathered value equals the float64 reference rounded once to bf16, 0 of 327,680 differ at 8 bits and at 3 bits; one-row calls equal one 64-row call. Scales 1% off: 160,115 and 142,528 values differ.

## Performance

Mac Studio, M3 Ultra (80-core GPU), 256 GB, macOS 26.4.1 (25E253), Zig 0.17.0. Fresh builds from clean detached worktrees, `zig build native tf-qwen27-run -Dcpu=apple_m1`; `tensorfold-native` sha256 `6a42d48dc1b08a1d…` (main `0efbd447`), `d640b9501b70d250…` (this branch, `4191469d`). DFlash2 on. Clients are main's `tools/` at `0efbd447` on Python 3.12.14; one model process on the machine, the file cache of other checkpoints evicted before each load, every run behind one GPU lock. Every receipt (manifests with binary hashes, `decode.json`, `concurrent.json`, prefill records with the exact token arrays and request bodies, `/memory` snapshots, `time -l`, load and cleanup timestamps, the fidelity and seam records) is in https://gist.github.com/grantoverton/dbbc25f85cecacca369b9b7c447294ac (index in `00-README.md`; the host suite summary is `test-summary.txt`).

**Decode and concurrency.** `serve <checkpoint> --drafter <DFlash2> --parallel 4 --context 65536 --prompt-cache-gib 0`; `bench_openai.py … --tokens 256 --reps 3 --temperatures 0` (medians; `fibonacci-raw`, code, and `gpu-chat-no-think`, prose, greedy) and `bench_concurrent.py … --tokens 256 --reps 3 --temperatures 0 --levels 1,4 --alone --serial` (aggregate tok/s). The uniform rows alternate branch, main, main, branch.

| Run | Weights | `bench_openai` code | chat | concurrent code ×1 | code ×4 | chat ×1 | chat ×4 | Peak footprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform 4-bit, this branch 1 | ~15 GB | 93.25 | 68.34 | 93.2 | 111.9 | 68.3 | 94.6 | 38.16 GB |
| uniform 4-bit, main 1 | same | 94.27 | 68.26 | 93.0 | 111.9 | 68.2 | 95.1 | 38.16 GB |
| uniform 4-bit, main 2 | same | 94.19 | 68.27 | 93.2 | 111.9 | 68.3 | 95.1 | 38.16 GB |
| uniform 4-bit, this branch 2 | same | 93.40 | 68.34 | 93.1 | 112.0 | 68.3 | 94.8 | 38.16 GB |
| oQ4, this branch | 16 GB | 85.45 | 51.62 | 83.3 | 95.6 | 51.7 | 75.4 | 38.71 GB |
| oQ2, this branch | 11 GB | 60.76 | 41.34 | 61.3 | 73.4 | 41.4 | 59.8 | 33.23 GB |
| uniform 4-bit, `mlx_lm` | ~15 GB | 37.32 | 37.20 | 37.2 | 36.6 | 37.1 | 36.5 | 16.16 GB |
| oQ4, `mlx_lm` | 16 GB | 35.39 | 35.33 | 35.2 | 34.7 | 35.3 | 34.6 | 16.73 GB |
| oQ2, `mlx_lm` | 11 GB | 71.52 | 47.80 | 71.3 | 51.1 | 47.8 | 46.7 | 11.41 GB |

The uniform path is unchanged: the branch is 1.0% below main on `bench_openai` code (93.33 against 94.23) and equal on chat (68.34 against 68.27), and every `bench_concurrent` cell is within 0.6%, with identical token hashes. The two oQ checkpoints decode **below** the uniform 4-bit checkpoint on this M3, oQ4 at 0.92× (code) and 0.76× (chat), oQ2 at 0.65× and 0.60×, although both read fewer bytes a token: every non-4/64 product runs on the generic row kernel, and a mixed stack is one launch per member. `mlx_lm` 0.32.0 (no drafts; it serves this model's streams one after another) is slower than this branch on the uniform checkpoint and on oQ4, and **faster on oQ2**: 71.52 / 47.80 tok/s against 60.76 / 41.34. This PR is about loading and serving these checkpoints exactly; a follow-up PR series will work on their speed.

The oQ checkpoints have no before-run: main refuses them (`UnqualifiedQwenFormat`). So their speed is reported as served decode (above, beside `mlx_lm`), and the before/after receipts (decode, concurrency and cold prefill) are on the uniform checkpoint, which both binaries load.

Commit 9's effect, on the same oQ2 checkpoint, prompts and tokens (hashes `1396ae566f52` / `af21ef189db8` in both): an earlier build of this branch without it, which had served the uniform checkpoint first, drafted oQ2 on the uniform checkpoint's window costs (wide windows nearly free there) and decoded 44.42 / 30.48 tok/s, drafting 475 to 477 rows in 38 rounds for the 256-token code reply; with oQ2's own costs, 246 to 264 rows in 54 to 60 rounds, and 60.76 / 41.34 tok/s.

**Cold prefill** (uniform 4-bit; main and this branch). Exact token arrays: upstream's public prefill paragraph ("A lighthouse keeper writes in the log as the boats cross the bay.", `tools/zig/qwen27_gate.py`) repeated and tokenized once without special tokens by the checkpoint's own `tokenizer.json`, each array the first N ids (every array decodes and re-encodes to itself). `POST /v1/completions` with the ids as `prompt`, `max_tokens` 1, temperature 0, `ignore_eos`; server `--parallel 1 --context 262144 --prompt-cache-gib 0`, one request at a time, a fresh KV every measurement (every record has `cached_tokens` 0 and `prompt_tokens` equal to N). 2k to 64k: one 2,048-token warm-up, then 3 rounds over the sizes, wall-clock medians. 128k: once per binary, in a server of its own (main's record is `q27-u4.pfl-main-f1.prefill-128k.json`: that server was stopped during a later request, so its `prefill.json` was not written). The arrays, the exact request bodies (with sha256), every request's timings and cached-token counts and the server's `/memory` after each are in the gist.

| Tokens | main tok/s (s) | this branch tok/s (s) | `mlx_lm` tok/s (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2,048 | 286.4 (7.15) | 282.1 (7.26) | 397.2 (5.16) |
| 8,192 | 258.8 (31.66) | 258.0 (31.76) | 390.6 (20.97) |
| 32,768 | 183.0 (179.04) | 183.4 (178.70) | 349.1 (93.86) |
| 65,536 | 131.8 (497.15) | 131.7 (497.56) | 300.1 (218.36) |
| 131,072, once | 82.9 (1,580.52) | 83.5 (1,570.42) | not run (2k to 64k only) |

Native-window prefill (262,143 tokens) not run: about 1.6 h per run on this machine; happy to add it if wanted.

Main's three reps of each size are within 0.1% of each other. The branch's spread more: 2k 286.8, 282.1 and 268.5; 8k 259.2, 258.0 and 247.0; 32k 183.4, 183.4 and 181.0; 64k 132.0, 131.7 and 130.7, the third round low at every size. Its 2k median is 1.5% under main's; from 8k up the medians are within 0.3%. Nothing in this branch changes a uniform kernel or launch, and its decode and concurrency on the uniform checkpoint match main's (above). Peak physical footprint after the 64k prompts: 40.17 GB (main) and 40.18 GB (branch); after the branch's 128k prompt, 40.19 GB. `mlx_lm` (2k to 64k only) takes text prompts: the same arrays decoded, each record checking `prompt_tokens` equals N and `cached_tokens` is 0; it prefills faster than the native engine at every size measured, 1.39× at 2k and 2.28× at 64k.

## Memory

Weights as stored: oQ4 16 GB, oQ2 11 GB, uniform 4-bit about 15 GB. At `--parallel 4 --context 65536 --prompt-cache-gib 0` with DFlash2: physical footprint after load 23.7 to 24.8 GB (uniform), 25.4 GB (oQ4), 19.9 GB (oQ2); lifetime peak physical footprint after the bench and cancel steps 38.16 GB (uniform, main and this branch alike), 38.71 GB (oQ4), 33.23 GB (oQ2) (`/memory` and `time -l` agree). The qwen27 Metal backend reports no device allocations in `/memory`. RAM class: M3 Ultra, 256 GB. Load and cleanup boundaries are in each run's `events.tsv`; prefill memory at the 262,144-token context is in the prefill receipts.

## Fidelity

Teacher-forced against `mlx_lm` 0.32.0 on the same checkpoint. `mlx_lm` renders upstream's four public teacher prompts (`tools/zig/qwen27_gate.py`: copy, arithmetic, story, code; chat template, thinking off), prefills each in one pass and decodes 256 greedy tokens with EOS ignored, keeping its top-20 logits at every step; that continuation is the fixed history. This branch's `tf-qwen27-run --run --teacher --force-length --chunk 128 --compare-chunk 16` then feeds every history token and records its top two at all 1,024 positions (prompt state byte-equal between chunk 128 and 16 on every prompt). Every top-1 difference is listed below with both engines' top two and margins (logits in bf16). Upstream's `qwen27_teacher_judge.py` reads the same files; its tie policy accepts a difference when the two engines name the same two contenders and both margins are within one bf16 spacing at that logit (0.0625 between 8 and 16, 0.125 between 16 and 32).

| oQ2 | story | 65 | 561, 2532 | 15.9375 / 15.4375 | 0.5 | 2532, 561 | 15.625 / 15.375 | 0.25 | beyond |
| oQ2 | code | 35 | 5732, 864 | 19.25 / 19.125 | 0.125 | 864, 5732 | 19.25 / 19.25 | 0 | near-tie |

On oQ2, 7 of the 11 differences fall outside the tie policy: six have a margin above one bf16 spacing in at least one engine (up to 0.75 and 1.0 at copy position 33), and at copy position 31 the engines name different runner-ups. So upstream's judge fails on oQ2. Where the two engines agree on the top token, their top-1 logits differ by about as much on every checkpoint (largest: uniform 3.375, oQ4 3.0, oQ2 3.125), so oQ2 does not show a larger arithmetic gap. It has more positions whose margins are small enough to flip, and at 2 bits the two engines' different products (MLX's 2-bit `quantized_matmul` against this branch's row kernel with fp32 group sums) move some of them past one spacing.

## Host suite and lean check

- `zig build test test-golden -Dcpu=apple_m1` at every commit, last at the tip `4191469d`: 158 of 160 steps; at the float64 commit 1566/1574 tests passed, 8 skipped; goldens 309/319 equal, the 10 declared differences, 0 unexpected. The one failing step is main's own: `core.checkpoint_metal`'s "a split checkpoint keeps later tensors in the file, packs the rest, and stages the same bytes" logs an error (`get` calls `std.log.err` before returning the `error.DeferredTensor` the test expects, and the runner counts logged errors). It fails the same way on main `0efbd447`: 158/160 steps, 1505/1513 tests passed, 8 skipped.
- New host tests: admission accepts the oQ formats and refuses unsupported widths and groups by name; width resolution under the `language_model.` prefix; the per-member run plan; lane tile packing at 4/6/8 × 32/64/128; 2-, 4- and 8-bit draft heads; the window-cost key (the uniform checkpoint keeps main's shape string, oQ4 and oQ2 get distinct tags). The failure they fix is main's: it refuses oQ4 and oQ2 with `UnqualifiedQwenFormat`.
- `python3 tools/zig/lean_check.py`: 536 problems against main's 539, no new findings; the 27B's files add none. The inherited findings left in touched files are the shared change's (`affine_mm.metal`, `affine_mm.zig`, `row_projection.metal`, `row_projection.zig`; listed there). Every touched file is under 600 lines (`widths.zig` 300, `gpu_weights.zig` 247, `quant_gpu.zig` 278, `native/qwen27_lanes.zig` 580, `tests/qwen27/widths.zig` 496, `tests/qwen27/run.zig` 214).

## Platforms

- Run: Metal on a Mac Studio M3 Ultra, 256 GB (80-core GPU, no tensor units), macOS 26.4.1, Xcode 26.6, Zig 0.17.0.
- Also run, thanks to @sethforprivacy on an M5 Ultra (tensor units): the synthetic checks PASS, and the report that oQ4 and oQ2 failed to load there came with the fix, now its own commit with credit; with it both serve exactly on M5.
- And to @mrv777 on an M1 Max: `tf-qwen27-widths`, `tf-qwen27-lanes-check` and `tf-qwen27-dflash-synthetic` PASS.
- Not run: M1, M2 and M4 (no hardware; they take the same row kernels as the M3); CUDA (no CUDA code changes).
- Not run: M5. There every non-4/64 product, and every member of a mixed stack, takes the lane kernel at its width, and none of that has run. `tf-qwen27-widths` refuses a chip with tensor units, since it doesn't check the lane kernels. Commands:

```
zig build test-core-lane native -Dcpu=apple_m1
zig build tf-qwen27-lanes-check tf-qwen27-dflash-synthetic -Dcpu=apple_m1
./zig-out/native/bin/tensorfold-native serve <oQ4 or oQ2 dir> --drafter <Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 dir> --name qwen27 --port 8080 --parallel 2 --context 65536
python3 tools/bench_concurrent.py http://127.0.0.1:8080 qwen27 --tokens 256 --reps 3 --temperatures 0 --levels 1,2 --alone --serial --output concurrent.json
```

then, greedy, each prompt as sent and with `"draft": false` (same tokens), and a long prompt sent twice (cached 0, then cached). I have no M5; @sethforprivacy has since run these (above).

## Reproduction settings

`tensorfold-native serve <checkpoint> --drafter <Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2>`, greedy, at `--parallel 2 --context 65536` for the exactness checks, `--parallel 4 --context 65536 --prompt-cache-gib 0` for the standard clients and cancellation, and `--parallel 1 --context 262144 --prompt-cache-gib 0` for cold prefill. One model process on the machine at a time, every load and check program behind one GPU lock, and the file cache of other checkpoints evicted before each load. The machine's `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` is 240000, which I set as its owner; the 27B checkpoints load far below it, and nothing else was raised.

## Where the arithmetic differs from 0.6.6

Bit equality with 0.6.6's kernels is not the bar (#716); the float64 bound per product, row invariance and the exactness contract are.

- **Before M5,** 0.6.6 runs `simd_qmm` at 4 bits, `simd_qmm_bits` at 5, 6 and 8 bits in groups of 64 or 128, and `affine_rows` otherwise (`row_matmul.py`). This branch runs `simd_qmm` for 4/64 matrices and core's row kernel, with fp32 group sums, for every other width.
- **A 4/64 member inside a mixed stack** (oQ4's z in eight layers) runs on the 4-bit row kernel, since `simd_qmm` has no output stride; 0.6.6 runs it on `simd_qmm`. Its bits differ from the same z as a uniform layer's `simd_qmm` product in 51 and 72 of 128 rows, by up to 3.1e-2; both are within the float64 bound. An output stride for `simd_qmm` would remove the difference; that belongs with the speed follow-ups.
- **The Neural Engine prompt share** declines a checkpoint whose MLP matrices are not all 4/64, since it decodes 4-bit codes only; those prompts run on the GPU.
- **On M5** the lane kernel's staging (nibbles for 2 and 3 bits, bytes for 5, 6 and 8) is 0.6.6's, through the shared change; unrun.

## The open question in #716

The 27B follows 0.6.6's 27B rule: once a fused group's members differ in width, every member is its own product. So no product spans non-adjacent members, and each member writes its own contiguous columns through core's output row stride. The per-member column map #716 asks about isn't needed here (Flash Next is the family that uses one).

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo (oQ4, oQ2 and the uniform 4-bit, served, at this branch's tip).
- [x] No precision traded for speed. The new widths keep fp32 group sums; the one bit difference (a 4-bit member of a mixed stack) is described above.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release. On the uniform checkpoint, cold prefill from 8k up is within 0.3% of main `0efbd447`; the 2k median is 1.5% under, with the branch's third round low at every size (above). The oQ checkpoints have no before-run (main refuses them).
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: Core support for oQ in Zig engine
items.body:
_Rebased onto main c36b536d (1.0.9) on 2026-10-13: no conflicts in this change's code; every commit passes the gate again on the new base (host suite, goldens, lean)._

Part of #716: the shared change. No family reads mixed widths on this branch, so no model's kernels, launches or bits change here; the family pull requests follow one at a time and stack on this one. The uniform paths (4/64 for the 27B and GLM-5.3-Flash, 6/32 for Flash Next) keep their kernels and launches: with default settings the 4-, 6- and 8-bit lane and `affine_mm` sources preprocess (`metal -E`) to main's text, and the row kernels' outputs at the widths main serves are byte-equal to main's.

## What this changes

Six commits on main `0efbd447`:

1. **MLX quantization: an override answers its module in any spelling** (`core/quant`). oQ checkpoints write per-module widths as `language_model.model.layers.N.…`, while loaders ask for `model.layers.N.…` or the bare path, so an exact-key lookup missed every override and read the tensor at the global width. The table now stores each entry under its canonical module key (no `.weight`, no known prefix) and looks keys up the same way. Two spellings of one module that declare different widths refuse the table. Test that fails before: a 5-bit `down_proj` declared under the oQ prefix, read by the loader's spelling; on main it fails the packed shape check.
2. **MLX affine weights widen exactly** (`core/quant/widen.zig`). Codes re-packed at more bits, scales and biases repeated for a smaller group; narrowing and a group that does not divide the source group are refused. No caller here; only Flash Next's hyper-connection down and inject pair uses it, where 0.6.6's `QWeights.of` widens.
3. **The row projection reads 3- and 5-bit MLX codes and can write into a wider output** (`row_projection`). New branches only; the 2/4/6/8-bit paths are unchanged. `callStrided` writes one member of a fused stack into the fused rows. `tf-row-widths-check` (wired in `zig/build/core_checks.zig`, so `build.zig` stays under 600 lines) runs it against float64.
4. **Lane projections take every MLX affine width, an output row stride and 16-row members** (`lane_projection`). 2- and 3-bit codes are staged as nibbles and 5-, 6- and 8-bit as bytes, the staging the Python lane matmul uses. 3- and 5-bit groups of 32 are an odd number of words a lane, so they are fetched a word at a time. `Layout.y_stride` sets the output row pitch in every kernel, including #679's simdgroup-matrix store, which keeps its column guard. Without tensor units the admitted layout is unchanged (6/32 on the plain kernel, #679); every other width still answers `TensorUnitsRequired` there, now checked at 2, 3 and 5 bits too.
5. **The prompt product `affine_mm` reads 2-bit MLX codes, exactly.** A thread loads its 32 codes of a step as 8 bytes and writes each code into the bf16 tile as itself, with no offset (as at 8 bits), so the group sums are the 4- and 8-bit path's. A first try with the 4-bit "+128" offset stayed within the float64 bound, but a reference with scales 1% off no longer exceeded it at K = 4096, so I dropped it.
6. **`tf-affine-ref`**, the device side of #633 for the shared prompt products: `affine_mm` at 2, 4 and 8 bits and `simd_qmm` at 4/64 against float64, and every row's bits in every window.

## Exactness

Same checkpoint, backend, runtime and settings on both sides.

- **Uniform 27B, served, at this branch's tip** (fresh build, below). Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit @70ae7fa with z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 (`model.safetensors` sha256 `67fc76d68dc5a941…`), greedy:
  - `--parallel 2 --context 65536`: drafted equals `"draft": false` 9/9 and resumed equals fresh 2/2 (a 26,130-token prompt resumed at 26,123 cached tokens, same token hash); `bench_concurrent.py --levels 1,2 --alone --serial`: every alone and serial cell equal, 0 failed.
  - `--parallel 4 --context 65536 --prompt-cache-gib 0`, six servers alternating main and this branch (below): `bench_concurrent.py --levels 1,4 --alone --serial` every alone cell (3 at one stream, 12 at four) and serial cell equal, 0 failed, in every run; the code and chat token hashes (`2b28aa2108de`, `cbdd31cd4736`) are the same in every run of both binaries.
- **Uniform Flash Next, served** (a full-size 6/32 requantization of the oQ3 checkpoint, same layout and names; the Flash Next PR describes it): main against this branch, greedy tokens identical on 6 prompts, plain and drafted, 2 repetitions each.
- **Rows.** The row projection gives one row alone the same bits as that row inside 2-, 3-, 8- and 16-row windows, with relu2 and indexed slots too; a strided output equals the unstrided one and writes nothing outside its columns. `affine_mm` and `simd_qmm`: every row of a 129-row call equals the same row in windows of 1, 2, 3, 8, 16, 17, 33, 64 and 65 rows, which crosses the 16-row fragments, the 32- and 64-row tiles and the gather's switch between them. So prompt rows and decode rows of these products are the same arithmetic.
- **Seams.** This branch changes no state, cache or KV code. KV, recurrent state and final logits were not compared at chunk seams directly; the token-level resumed-equals-fresh runs above cover the uniform path.
- **Cancellation, reset and partial acceptance.** No request lifecycle, scheduler or state code changes here, but the check ran on the uniform 27B in every served run of both binaries: a fresh `"draft": false` probe (each bench prompt, greedy, 128 tokens) gives the reference hash and the drafted probe equals it, with partial acceptance seen (accepted < drafted); then after a stream dropped mid-decode, a long prompt dropped mid-prompt, a stream dropped beside a running probe (whose hash is checked too) and a request past the window (refused, the reset path), the drafted and plain probes equal the fresh hashes (`f5c9409cfe40`, `73e9fd21b09e`). 25 steps, pass, in all six runs.
- **Precision.** Activations stay bf16 and group sums fp32 at every width. No existing sum changes order; the new widths sum in the existing order.

## FP64 per class

M3 Ultra, no tensor units (`nax.h`'s simdgroup-matrix layout), seeded synthetic MLX affine weights. The bound is the fp32 summation bound of the terms' magnitudes plus one bf16 ulp for bf16 outputs. Prompt and decode use identical input rows; since every row's bits are equal in every window, the decode (one row) and prompt (many rows) columns are the same numbers.

`row_projection` (decode before tensor units; three shapes, every column of every row), worst column per width and group:

| Bits | g32 \|err\| (of bound) | g64 | g128 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1.20e-2 (0.850) | 1.21e-2 (0.825) | 7.77e-3 (0.879) |
| 3 | 1.56e-2 (0.886) | 1.56e-2 (0.894) | 1.55e-2 (0.861) |
| 4 | 2.82e-2 (0.865) | 2.95e-2 (0.909) | 3.04e-2 (0.909) |
| 5 | 5.96e-2 (0.835) | 6.18e-2 (0.856) | 6.14e-2 (0.896) |
| 6 | 1.23e-1 (0.892) | 1.23e-1 (0.873) | 1.23e-1 (0.940) |
| 8 | 4.92e-1 (0.848) | 4.98e-1 (0.870) | 4.97e-1 (0.882) |

64,512 values within the bound (worst 0.940, 6-bit group 128: bf16 output rounding); 408,192 bit-equal row/window pairs; 301,056 outputs byte-equal to main's kernels at the widths main serves. A fused stack of eight 48-row members at widths 4, 5, 4, 6, 3, 8, 2, 4 written through the stride: each member's columns equal its own call.

`affine_mm` and `simd_qmm` (prompt products), worst column (max |err|, and that over the column's largest |y|):

| Product | [192, 1024] | [256, 4096] |
|---|---|---|
| `affine_mm` q2 g32, bf16 out | 2.64e-2 (3.23e-3) | 6.22e-2 (3.78e-3) |
| `affine_mm` q2 g64 | 2.87e-2 (3.51e-3) | 3.12e-2 (2.47e-3) |
| `affine_mm` q4 g32 | 2.45e-2 (2.65e-3) | 3.12e-2 (3.01e-3) |
| `affine_mm` q4 g64 | 1.56e-2 (2.89e-3) | 3.12e-2 (2.53e-3) |
| `affine_mm` q8 g32 | 0.496 (3.41e-3) | 0.968 (3.63e-3) |
| `affine_mm` q8 g64 | 0.453 (2.87e-3) | 0.956 (3.38e-3) |

Dense and gathered are equal. `simd_qmm` 4/64 at [40, 512], [256, 4096] and [6400, 256]: 1.19e-2 (2.57e-3), 3.13e-2 (2.87e-3), 1.54e-2 (3.74e-3), and its twin equals its tiles at 1 and 2 rows wherever `twinExact` says so. Every product is within 0.4935 of its bound (bf16 outputs 0.20 to 0.49; fp32 outputs at most 0.0081). Negative control, scales 1% off: 2.3 to 29 times the bound for bf16 outputs, 2.7 to 391 for fp32, 44 to 273 for `simd_qmm`.

Lane projection without tensor units (6/32 only): 14 layouts pass, 1,904 bit-equal row/window pairs, 208 windows equal to `fn_lane`'s recorded bytes, 7,424 CPU float64 values (worst 0.0144 of the bound), 10 refusals; a 48-row member and two strided layouts at 6/32 equal the unstrided rows with the gaps untouched. Every width × group × {64, 48} rows packs MLX codes bit for bit with zero padding (host test). The tensor-unit arithmetic at the new widths needs an M5 (below).

## Performance

Mac Studio, M3 Ultra (80-core GPU), 256 GB, macOS 26.4.1 (25E253), Zig 0.17.0. Fresh builds from clean detached worktrees, `zig build native tf-qwen27-run -Dcpu=apple_m1`; `tensorfold-native` sha256 `6a42d48dc1b08a1d…` (main `0efbd447`), `1cc42957aea4b6f9…` (this branch, `9325793f`). Checkpoint Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit @70ae7fac with DFlash2. Clients are main's `tools/` at `0efbd447` on Python 3.12.14, the server is the native binary; one model process on the machine, the file cache of other checkpoints evicted before each load, every run behind one GPU lock. Every receipt (manifests with binary hashes, `decode.json`, `concurrent.json`, prefill records with the exact token arrays and request bodies, `/memory` snapshots, `time -l`, load and cleanup timestamps) is in https://gist.github.com/grantoverton/70256846d366db6526a6db3e1b40a4e5 (index in `00-README.md`; the host suite summary is `test-summary.txt`).

No oQ checkpoint has a before-run: main refuses them, and on this branch alone no family reads mixed widths yet. So every receipt here is on the uniform checkpoint, which both binaries load; the family PRs report the oQ checkpoints' speed as served decode only.

**Decode and concurrency.** `tensorfold-native serve <checkpoint> --drafter <DFlash2> --parallel 4 --context 65536 --prompt-cache-gib 0`; `bench_openai.py … --tokens 256 --reps 3 --temperatures 0` (medians; prompts `fibonacci-raw`, code, and `gpu-chat-no-think`, prose, greedy) and `bench_concurrent.py … --tokens 256 --reps 3 --temperatures 0 --levels 1,4 --alone --serial` (aggregate tok/s). Six servers in this order: main, branch, branch, main, main, branch (two runs of the 27B branch came between the first pair and the rest).

| Run | `bench_openai` code | chat | concurrent code ×1 | code ×4 | chat ×1 | chat ×4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main 1 | 95.49 | 70.00 | 95.4 | 114.8 | 69.8 | 95.0 |
| branch 1 | 93.21 | 65.11 | 88.5 | 108.6 | 68.6 | 92.5 |
| branch 2 | 94.07 | 69.42 | 94.5 | 112.1 | 68.7 | 94.8 |
| main 2 | 94.43 | 68.39 | 93.1 | 111.8 | 68.3 | 95.0 |
| main 3 | 94.21 | 68.38 | 93.0 | 112.2 | 69.8 | 95.2 |
| branch 3 | 93.34 | 69.00 | 93.1 | 111.9 | 68.9 | 94.7 |

The first pair moved apart (main 1 fast, branch 1 slow, its chat reps spread 64.8 to 66.0); in the alternated rounds 2 and 3 (branch, main, main, branch) the branch is 0.6% below main on code (93.71 against 94.32) and 1.2% above on chat (69.21 against 68.39), and the concurrent cells agree within 1.6%. The kernels main serves are unchanged here (preprocess-identical sources, byte-equal row outputs), so I read these as run-to-run noise. Flash Next's uniform 6/32 path, main against this branch (an earlier receipt): plain decode 0.998 to 1.000 of main, drafted 0.998 to 1.004, prompt 1.001.

**Cold prefill.** Exact token arrays of 2,048, 8,192, 32,768 and 65,536 tokens: upstream's public prefill paragraph ("A lighthouse keeper writes in the log as the boats cross the bay.", `tools/zig/qwen27_gate.py`) repeated and tokenized once without special tokens by the checkpoint's own `tokenizer.json`, each array the first N ids (every array decodes and re-encodes to itself). `POST /v1/completions` with the ids as `prompt`, `max_tokens` 1, temperature 0, `ignore_eos`; server `--parallel 1 --context 262144 --prompt-cache-gib 0`, one request at a time, a fresh KV every measurement (every record has `cached_tokens` 0 and `prompt_tokens` equal to N). One 2,048-token warm-up, then 3 rounds over all sizes; wall-clock medians. The arrays, the exact request bodies (with sha256), every request's timings and cached-token counts, and the server's `/memory` after each are in the gist.

| Tokens | main tok/s (s) | this branch tok/s (s) | `mlx_lm` tok/s (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2,048 | 286.4 (7.15) | 286.6 (7.15) | 397.2 (5.16) |
| 8,192 | 258.8 (31.66) | 259.1 (31.62) | 390.6 (20.97) |
| 32,768 | 183.0 (179.04) | 183.1 (178.92) | 349.1 (93.86) |
| 65,536 | 131.8 (497.15) | 131.7 (497.50) | 300.1 (218.36) |

The three reps of each size are within 0.2% of each other on both binaries, and the branch is within 0.1% of main at every size, so I ran no second, reversed round. Peak physical footprint after the 64k prompts: 40.17 GB for both. `mlx_lm` takes text prompts (its server accepts no token arrays): the same arrays decoded, each record checking that `prompt_tokens` equals N and `cached_tokens` is 0; it prefills faster than the native engine at every size here, 1.39× at 2k and 2.28× at 64k (peak footprint 33.98 GB). 128k and the native window (262,144) were not run on this branch: its kernels for the uniform checkpoint are main's (above), and the 27B pull request records those two cells once each for main and for its own tip.

**Standard server.** `mlx_lm` 0.32.0 (mlx 0.32.3, transformers 5.19.0; `python -m mlx_lm server --model <checkpoint> --prompt-cache-size 0`), same checkpoint, clients and prompts: decode 37.32 tok/s code and 37.20 chat; `bench_concurrent` 37.2 / 36.6 (code ×1 / ×4) and 37.1 / 36.5 (chat), since `mlx_lm` serves this model's four streams one after another; peak memory footprint 16.16 GB. `mlx_lm` returns no token hashes, so its `--alone/--serial` cells read unverified, and it ignores `ignore_eos`. Cold prefill on `mlx_lm` is in the table above (text prompts that tokenize to the same arrays; the record checks `prompt_tokens`).

## Memory

No buffer sizes or load plans change for any uniform checkpoint. Uniform 27B with DFlash2 at `--parallel 4 --context 65536 --prompt-cache-gib 0`: physical footprint 23.7 to 24.8 GB after load, lifetime peak physical footprint 38.16 GB after the bench and cancel steps, maximum resident set 17.9 GB (`time -l`), identical for main and this branch in every run. The qwen27 Metal backend reports no device allocations in `/memory`. RAM class: M3 Ultra, 256 GB. Load and cleanup boundaries are in each run's `events.tsv`; prefill memory at the 262,144-token context is in the prefill receipts.

## Fidelity

Teacher-forced fidelity: n/a for this branch. No family reads the new widths yet, and the uniform paths give identical tokens (above). The family PRs carry fidelity against `mlx_lm` on the oQ checkpoints.

## Host suite and lean check

- `zig build test test-golden -Dcpu=apple_m1` at every commit, last at the tip `9325793f`: 158 of 160 steps; goldens 309/319 equal, the 10 declared differences, 0 unexpected. The one failing step is main's own: `core.checkpoint_metal`'s test "a split checkpoint keeps later tensors in the file, packs the rest, and stages the same bytes" logs an error (`checkpoint tensor text.weight stays in its file: read it through a Stage`): `get` calls `std.log.err` before returning the `error.DeferredTensor` the test expects, and the test runner counts logged errors as failures. It fails on main `0efbd447` too, on the same machine: 158/160 steps, 1505/1513 tests passed, 8 skipped, this failure only. It came with #643 and shows on macOS.
- New tests that fail before: the oQ-prefix override fixture; 3- and 5-bit row shapes validate and take whole words; every width has its own pipeline slot; a strided call writes rows at least a matrix wide; 2-, 3- and 5-bit lane formats validate, `y_stride` reaches the source and below N is refused, a 48-row member validates (cooperative and reg refuse it); `affine_mm` 2/64 and 2/32, dense and gathered, against exact host sums. `widen.zig`'s tests are new with the file.
- `python3 tools/zig/lean_check.py`: 536 problems against main's 539 at `0efbd447`, no new findings. Three inherited ones are gone (over-long comments in `row_projection.metal` and `row_projection.zig`, shortened where I edited). Inherited findings left in files this branch touches: over-long comments in `affine_mm.metal` (4, plus one block comment), `affine_mm.zig` (7), `row_projection.metal` (3) and `row_projection.zig` (3). Every touched file is at or under 600 lines.

## Platforms

- Run: Metal on a Mac Studio M3 Ultra, 256 GB (80-core GPU, no tensor units), macOS 26.4.1, Xcode 26.6, Zig 0.17.0.
- Also run, thanks to @sethforprivacy on an M5 Ultra (tensor units): `test-core-lane`, `tf-affine-ref` and `tf-row-widths-check` PASS.
- And to @mrv777 on an M1 Max: the same three PASS, `tf-row-widths-check`'s stock byte comparison included.
- Not run: M1, M2 and M4 (no hardware; the M3 runs the same non-tensor-unit paths); CUDA (no CUDA code changes).
- Not run: M5. On an M5 the lane projection at the new widths, its 48-row members and output stride, and `affine_mm` on the tensor units are untested. Commands:

```
zig build test-core-lane -Dcpu=apple_m1
zig build tf-affine-ref tf-row-widths-check -Dcpu=apple_m1
./zig-out/bin/tf-affine-ref
./zig-out/bin/tf-row-widths-check
```

I have no M5; @sethforprivacy has since run these (above).

## Reproduction settings

Server: `tensorfold-native serve <Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit> --drafter <Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2>`, greedy, at `--parallel 2 --context 65536` for the exactness checks, `--parallel 4 --context 65536 --prompt-cache-gib 0` for the standard clients and cancellation, and `--parallel 1 --context 262144 --prompt-cache-gib 0` for cold prefill. One model process on the machine at a time, every load and check program behind one GPU lock, and the file cache of other checkpoints evicted before each load. The machine's `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` is 240000, which I set as its owner; the 27B's load is far below either limit, and nothing else was raised.

## Where the arithmetic differs from 0.6.6

Bit equality with 0.6.6's kernels is not the bar (#716); the float64 bound per product, row invariance and the exactness contract are.

- 3- and 5-bit rows keep fp32 group sums, as the row kernel's other widths do. 0.6.6's per-family kernels differ (for example GLM's `qmv_rows_b` rounds group sums to bf16 at 5 and 6 bits); each family PR says which it replaces.
- 2-bit prompt products use `affine_mm` with exact codes; 0.6.6 uses MLX's 2-bit `quantized_matmul`.
- The lane staging (nibbles for 2 and 3 bits, bytes for 5, 6 and 8) is 0.6.6's.

## The open question in #716

#716 asks whether the lane kernel should take a per-member output offset table, so a product grouped over non-adjacent members writes each member's rows in place, or run into scratch and copy. This branch adds neither to core's `lane_projection`: only the output row stride, which covers a contiguous run. The 27B and GLM-5.3-Flash never group non-adjacent members (each member of a mixed stack is its own product), so they need no map. Flash Next does group them, as 0.6.6's `_stacked` does, and its PR ships a column map in Flash Next's own lane kernel (`FZ_MAP`). If you'd rather have that map in core, or scratch and a copy, tell me which and I'll change it.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo (uniform 27B, served, at this branch's tip; uniform Flash Next tokens).
- [x] No precision traded for speed. No existing sum changes; the new widths sum in the existing order.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release. Cold prefill at 2k to 64k is within 0.1% of main `0efbd447` (above).
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.



## Compatibility with #626

Compatible with #626: `quant.mlx.Config.overrides` still holds the config's own keys, as on main, so #626's `Table.width` (which reads the map by the raw key, then with `language_model.` put back) finds every override it found before. The canonical module keys live in a separate `modules` index, which `width(key)` consults after the key as given. Two spellings of one module that declare different widths still refuse the table, now through `error.UnsupportedQuantization`, which `quant.detect` already returns on main, so the `try quant.detect(...)` in #626's `Config.parse` (error set `shared.Error || error{UnsupportedQuantization}`) compiles unchanged. I checked this by applying #626's diff on top of this branch: `zig build test-qwen35 hip-host-test` passes (the one skip needs `TF_QWEN_DIR`), and the full `zig build test` fails only on main's known `core.checkpoint_metal` test. A scratch test that reads an 8-bit override through #626's `Table.width` by its raw key, with and without the stripped prefix, passes here, and it reads 4 bits when the map is keyed canonically. Either PR can land first. Later, #626 could call `q.width(key)` to pick up the oQ spellings that an exact-key lookup misses.


The receipts above were taken at `9325793f`. The only change since is this lookup and its error mapping, with no kernel code touched, re-checked with `zig build test test-golden -Dcpu=apple_m1` and the lean check on the new tip.

items.title: Flash Next CUDA (0.6.1 port): the lone stream's graph slot keeps its rows, so its graphs are captured once
items.body:
On the 0.6.1 port, every resize of the lone stream's graph slot drops its graphs: `_grow` and `_shrink` call
`_state_changed`. The slot starts at 256 rows, grows to 8,192 once a reply's context passes them, and shrinks back when
the request ends. So every lone request recaptures its graphs mid-reply: 23 captures, 3.0 s of a 512-token reply on a
GB10. Two and four streams lose 8–11 % the same way, because the first stream starts alone in the slot.

- The slot keeps its rows when idle. It gives them back only when memory is short: an evicted kept end, the newest
  stream ending, or an idle slot freed for another stream's growth.
- It grows by doubling (at least `STEP` rows), so a long session recaptures a handful of times rather than every request.
- `warm()` captures its graphs last. Before, the warm request grew the slot after the captures, which discarded them.
- A different lone request takes the slot without dropping its graphs. A finished request's prompt end is kept in the
  slot it ran in, so the next lone request with another prompt landed elsewhere, and `_move_to_solo` made that slot the
  graph slot (`_state_changed`, a full recapture each request). Now the kept prompt end moves to a free slot of the same
  rows (`copy_from`; its snapshot is unchanged). With no free slot that fits without evicting, the old swap stays.
- `copy_from` takes a source with fewer rows into its first rows, because the graph slot now keeps more rows than a
  stream moving in may have. Rows past `pos` are written before they are read. A larger source is refused.

Two ranks: rank 0 plans on `Shadow`s of the slots, `dec.solo.st` included, so `_is_solo` compares the slots the
Shadows stand for. Keeping the rows records only a reset for rank 1, and a release records the resize like any other.
(The first commit compared a Shadow with the real slot and never matched while planning, so it did nothing on two ranks.
BHCC2025's two-rank run showed it. Fixed in the second commit.) Two ranks keep the slot swap for kept prompt ends,
because the plan names kept ends by slot.

## Measured

One GB10, Flash Next EXL3 3.05bpw, greedy, 512 tokens of code per stream, two starts each:

| | 0.6.0 | `cb5101d` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--parallel 4`, one request (ms/token) | 13.63 / 13.52 | 18.41 / 18.56 | **12.18 / 12.20** |
| `--parallel 1` (ms/token) | 12.09 / 12.19 | 12.33 / 12.15 | 12.18 / 12.19 |
| two streams (tok/s) | 111.9 / 111.5 | 99.8 / 99.1 | 111.7 / 110.8 |
| four streams (tok/s) | 158.4 / 157.9 | 146.8 / 145.1 | 157.6 / 157.8 |
| graph captures inside the reply (one / two streams) | — | 23 / 8 | 0 / 0 |

Every reply is byte-identical in all three columns.

Lone requests one after another with different prompts (`--parallel 4`, 256 tokens each; the last request resumes the
first one's kept prompt end):

| | `cb5101d` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| graph captures per request | 33 / 32 / 30 / 19 | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| ms/token | 31.6 / 29.4 / 27.3 / 23.0 | 14.0 / 12.7 / 11.7 / 12.1 |

The replies are byte-identical, including the resumed one.

## Tests

`tests/test_cuda_growing_caches.py`:
- The new test checks that the slot keeps its rows across a request's end and gives them to another stream when the
  gate is short. It also checks that the slot grows 8,192 → 16,384 → 32,768 → the window.
- A second test drives the slot through a `Shadow` while planning: it is recognised, keeping its rows records only a
  reset, and a release records the resize. It fails on the first commit.
- The file's decoder helper now sets the port's new attributes (`solo`, `solo_on`, `planning`). Its three existing
  decoder tests failed on `cb5101d` with `AttributeError: ... 'solo'` and pass again.
- Two more tests (third commit): a lone stream moves into a graph slot with more rows (no resize, rows and positions
  carried), and a different lone request takes the graph slot while the kept prompt end moves to a free slot with its
  rows. Both fail on the second commit (a size mismatch in `copy_from`; the slot swapped).
- The file passes 10 of 10. Fourth commit (by @plotarmordev): `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_tp_multi.py`'s lone-stream test
  asserts the new behaviour (the graph slot and its graphs kept, the first prompt's kept end moved, not evicted).
  With it, `test_cuda_growing_caches.py` and `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_{tp_multi,multi,tp,prompt_cache,kvquant}.py`
  give 180 passed, 1 skipped on one GB10 here (178 / 3 on theirs). `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_multi.py` passes 27 of 27 on this PR and on `cb5101d`.

I ran the 14 multi-decoder host test files on both commits. This PR fails 29, `cb5101d` fails 32, and the 29 are a
subset of the 32 (211 pass here). The remainder fail on this machine for other reasons (mostly `mlx` not installed).

Not covered: int8/int4 KV, a two-rank run of the second and third commits (one GPU here), and a server under memory pressure with
the slot holding its rows.

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the author reviewed every change.

items.title: server: the JSON writer stays in bounds on a UTF-8 sequence cut off at a string's end (DeepSeek-V4.1 stack 1/14)
items.body:
Part 1 of 14 of the DeepSeek-V4.1 Zig engine stack.

## The DeepSeek-V4.1 stack

This is the first of 14 pull requests that bring a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash engine to the Zig runtime. It serves
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (EXL3 2.8 bpw) on two DGX Spark nodes with TP=2 over RoCE. The engine has run in production
against the Python serving path, and the recipe with its measurements is public in
[jayleaton/deepseek-v41-tensorfold-spark#18](https://github.com/jayleaton/deepseek-v41-tensorfold-spark/pull/18).

Each layer builds on the one below and keeps every existing family's behaviour; new paths are off until a family
installs them. GitHub cannot stack pull requests across forks, so each one targets `main` and names the one it
depends on: please review only the commits new in that layer. Layers 1–7 are generic building blocks; 8–14 are the
family itself.

1. JSON writer bounds on a cut-off UTF-8 sequence
2. CUDA keyed graph cache, device arena, launch error names
3. Tensor-parallel fabric: bootstrap, NCCL, mailbox and RoCE collectives, plan link, fail-fast
4. Session memory for paged-KV families: page pool, prefix trie, RAM budget, NVMe tier
5. Grammar-constrained decoding over xgrammar 0.2.8
6. Lane host: a family's round planner with prompt pieces; halt at a round boundary
7. Server: family chat hooks, Spark-compatible wire, drain on stop, pre-first-token keepalives
8. DeepSeek-V4.1 core: config, weights, attention (compressed and sparse-indexed KV), MoE, mHC (in parts)
9. KV layout and rows
10. Prefill: pieces, CED replay, heat bands
11. Drafting and sampling
12. Serving: DeepSeek encoding, reasoning and tool calls, the family's server glue
13. Speed settings, one change each
14. Vision (only once the GPU path is bit-exact)

DeepSeek-V4.1 brings its own architecture to the runtime: compressed KV with a sparse indexer, Engram lookups,
mHC residual mixing, MTP drafting, and DSML tool calls.

Measured against the production Python path on the same two nodes, same pack and bench scripts, the same night
(tok/s; decode cells are the best of 3 warm repetitions, prompt cells 3 cold prefills; from the published recipe):

| Cell | Zig | Python | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| code T0, 4 streams | 156.4 | 144.1 | +8.6 % |
| prose T0, 4 streams | 104.7 | 98.2 | +6.6 % |
| code T0, 1 stream | 90.3 | 88.0 | +2.6 % |
| 32K prompt prefill | 2,686 | 2,440 | +10.1 % |
| 131K prompt prefill | 2,496 | 2,264 | +10.3 % |
| 131K decode | 69.26 | 67.04 | +3.3 % |

Replies were identical to the Python path's on the bench (16/16 short replies and the long reply hashes). One pair
of nodes, one night, no confidence intervals.

The stack is incremental; layers 8–14 follow as each passes its gates.

## This layer

Review the commit new in this layer:

- `4284048d` The JSON writer escapes a UTF-8 sequence cut off at a string's end as U+FFFD instead of slicing past it.

### What it adds and why

The JSON writer escapes a UTF-8 sequence that is cut off at the end of a string as U+FFFD instead of slicing past the
string's end. A streamed reply can end mid-sequence (a token boundary inside a multi-byte character), and the writer
read past the slice in that case.

### How

- `json_write.zig`: the escape loop clamps a sequence's length to the bytes left; a short tail is written as
  `\ufffd` and consumes only the bytes that are there. With a test.

### Test evidence

Host only: Linux x86_64, Zig 0.17.0, one job at a time with `-j4`, a fresh empty `--cache-dir` for every run. Base is `main` at `38de96bf`.

```sh
python3 tools/zig/lean_check.py
zig fmt --check <the Zig files this stack adds or changes>
zig build -j4
zig build test -j4
```

| Check | Base `main` | This layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lean_check.py` | 542 problems | 542 problems, all inherited from `main`: 0 new fingerprints |
| `zig fmt --check` | | 1 file, 0 unformatted |
| `zig build` | 8/8 steps | 8/8 steps |
| `zig build test` | 37/37 steps; 400/400 tests passed | 37/37 steps; 401/401 tests passed |

Not run: `test-golden` (not available on Linux, base `main` included), any GPU or device step and any checkpoint gate. This code, before its rebase onto current `main` and the generic renames, serves DeepSeek-V4.1 in production on two DGX Spark nodes; this tree itself has had no GPU run.

items.title: ROCm (Strix Halo) support for Qwen3.8-27B, with fast GGUF prompts on by default
items.body:
> **0.6.2 validation complete for the tested Strix cases:** Head `4e96ba5`, based on upstream `56e2e3e`. Default and `TENSORFOLD_GGUF_FAST=0` each match drafted vs serial **16/16** (8 greedy, 8 seeded). All four reply files match the corresponding earlier 0.6.1-based run **16/16 each**; default vs exact differs in 6/16. These raw reply comparisons were independently checked by codexmb. The current-head measurements below are single runs; no new performance optimization is claimed. Known test failures remain disclosed below.

## ROCm (Strix Halo, gfx1151) for the Qwen3.8-27B CUDA path, GGUF on Gufo's kernels: rebased on 0.6.2

This PR is rebased onto upstream 0.6.2 (`56e2e3e`), with **31 commits; current head `4e96ba5`**. The two conflicts in `gdn.cu` and `dflash2.py` were resolved, preserving the ROCm portability changes and GGUF support. The new GDN kernel passes 44/44 tests on the Strix in the exported run. The earlier 0.6.1-based head `1c11bd6` is preserved as `strix-rocm-gguf-v061-backup`; the 0.5.0 version is preserved as `strix-rocm-gguf-v050-backup`.

### What is new since the 0.5.0 version of this PR
- **Fast GGUF prompts on ROCm, on by default (`TENSORFOLD_GGUF_FAST=0` turns them off).**
  - Prompts quantize to Q8_1 and run Gufo's W8A8 WMMA GEMM (the route Gufo's own prefill uses).
  - One row runs on Gufo's decode GEMV.
  - Draft verify stays on the exact kernel (`TENSORFOLD_GGUF_FAST_VERIFY`, default `exact`). We tried WMMA and bf16
    for verify: they changed drafted replies and were not faster.
  - With the setting unset, ROCm uses the fast route. NVIDIA is excluded by the HIP gate. `TENSORFOLD_GGUF_FAST=0` selects the exact route.
  - Fast prompt math differs from exact prompt math: 6 of 16 tested replies differ between the routes. Drafted versus serial replies match within each route in these tests; this is a finite comparison, not a general quality guarantee.
  - `tests/test_gguf_fast_default.py` covers the default and override; `scripts/gguf_fast_prefill_check.py` checks both directions on real weights and restores the environment in a `finally` block.
- **Q8_0 W8A8 over-read.** Gufo's Q8_0 kernel reads activations in whole 128-token blocks with no bounds check.
  - The activation buffer has 8 tiles of slack; 6 is the minimum sufficient, derived in
    `tests/test_gguf_q8_bounds.py`, which reads the kernel constants from source.
  - `scripts/gguf_bounds_check.py` puts buffers against unmapped pages (HIP VMM). The negative controls fault: exact
    size, and 5 tiles. The 700-case 8-tile sweep is clean on gfx1151.
- **Fixes found in review:**
  - pyproject ships `tensorfold.cuda.gguf` sources plus the vendored Gufo tree (the wheel used to hold only
    `__init__.py`).
  - `gguf_detect.gguf_file`: engine admission no longer imports `gguf_load`. That import broke 12
    `test_cuda_capacity` stand-in tests; it already did so in this PR on 0.5.0.
  - `b16.cu` builds on hipcc. The PTX prompt kernel is built off-ROCm only, ROCm prompt rows use the row kernel, and
    gdn.cu's portability macros are applied.
  - DFlash2 handles an unquantized (Plain) target head. Before, setup would crash on it.
  - A GGUF on a non-ROCm build gets a clear error before Gufo's HIP-only build.
- **Test fixes:** the packaging test skips torch's run-time hipify copies inside the source tree. `test_qmm::test_every_nibble_decodes_exactly` now has the same PTX-only skip as the other tests that call the CUDA-only extension.

### Deliberately not gated to ROCm
- GGUF detection and loading. Off ROCm it is refused with a clear message.
- The `qmm_fast` MLX-layout row helpers. The standard tiled CUDA route does not reach them.
- DFlash2 Plain-head support. It is correct on any backend.
- The `top_by_value_then_id` tie-break, the one deliberate CUDA-visible behaviour change, as discussed with
  @jkuepker.

### Measured (single runs; receipts available)

**Strix Halo (gfx1151), Qwen3.8-27B.** Answering speed is tok/s for short / code / story / long doc. GGUF rows below use the 2 Oct 0.6.2 rerun on head `4e96ba5`; the MLX row is the earlier 0.6.1 run. These are single runs. The long-document answering measurement follows a warm-up and benefits from prompt caching; prompt reading is measured separately on the 8,651-token prompt.

| Setup | Prompt reading (8,651-token prompt) | Answering, drafts on | Answering, drafts off | Drafted vs serial |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GGUF UD-Q4_K_XL, fast (default) | 193.0 tok/s (191.3 with drafts) | 25.4 / 35.2 / 17.6 / 27.6 | 10.5 | 16/16 identical |
| GGUF UD-Q4_K_XL, exact (`TENSORFOLD_GGUF_FAST=0`) | 77.4 tok/s (75.3 with drafts) | 25.4 / 37.7 / 17.4 / 27.6 | 10.4 | 16/16 identical |
| MLX 4-bit | 140 tok/s | 11.5-28.7 | 8.9 | 10/16 identical (open bug below) |

- **Chunk-invariance of the fast prompt route:** 20 weights over 8 quant types, slices of 1-1000 rows and permuted
  rows. Bit-identical at pad 0 and pad 96.
- **Earlier NVIDIA regression (DGX Spark, GB10, CUDA 13):** the 29-commit rebase as a wheel against plain 0.6.1, same harness. The subsequent fast-default switch remains HIP-gated.
  - Replies identical, 16/16 serial and 16/16 drafted.
  - Per-kind speed similar in single runs (no repeated-run spread).
  - Not rechecked on this branch: TP2, NVFP4, EXL3 and GLM.
- **CPU suite (macOS):** the same 23 failures as plain v0.6.1, no new ones.
- **0.6.2 rerun (2 Oct, Strix, 11:08–12:03 UTC; head `4e96ba5`):**
  - Default and FAST=0 each match drafted/serial 16/16; all four arms match the earlier 0.6.1-based replies 16/16 each. Default vs exact differs in 6/16.
  - Exported test logs record 72 CPU-side passes and 1 skip; 22 GPU test files contain passes, one is entirely skipped, and two fail (`test_build`, `test_logprobs`, disclosed below). Switch check reports 14/14 weights wired both ways; `test_gdn` passes 44/44.
  - The close receipt records the model server active with HTTP health 200 and the room agent active at 12:03 UTC.
  - Receipts: `fast-default-rerun/v062/SHAS.txt`, `summary.txt`, per-file logs, four `v062-*.json` reply files, conflict/range diffs and `window-receipt.txt`. Raw reply comparisons were independently checked by codexmb.
- **Earlier 0.6.1-based fast-default rerun (2 Oct, Strix, 09:06–10:01 UTC):**
  - Default and `TENSORFOLD_GGUF_FAST=0` each produce identical drafted/serial replies in 16/16 cases (8 greedy, 8 seeded).
  - All four reply files match the corresponding earlier opt-in/exact files, 16/16 each. Default versus exact differs in 6/16 cases, confirming the switch changes the path.
  - Real-weight switch check: 14/14 GGUF weights wired both ways.
  - The full rerun used tree `3197181` (the initial fast-default change on `954bb9f`), **not final head `1c11bd6`**. The final head changes only check-script environment cleanup and the PTX-only test mark. The GPU switch check and end-to-end runs were not repeated after those two changes.
  - Of 25 GPU test files in that rerun, 21 contained passing tests, one was entirely skipped (`test_qwen27_server_errors`), and three failed (`test_qmm`, `test_build`, `test_logprobs`). The final-head follow-up reports `test_qmm`: 6 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed; GGUF/packaging/capacity tests: 62 passed. `test_build` and `test_logprobs` remain outside this port's supported scope.
  - The window-close receipt reports the M5 model server active with HTTP health 200 and the room agent active.
  - Receipts available: `fast-default-rerun/README.txt`, `fd-run.sh`, `summary.txt`, per-file pytest/serve logs, and all four `fd-*.json` reply files. Raw reply comparisons were independently checked by codexmb.

### Known open issue (not fixed here)
The MLX checkpoint on AMD: drafted replies can differ from serial.
- Cause: decode picks gemv (no drafts) or gemm16 (drafts) for the whole run, and the two round differently.
- `TF_ROCM_DECODE_KERNEL=gemm16` restores equality (8/8 + 8/8), but halves serial decode (9.0 -> 4.5 tok/s).
- A proper fix needs gemv to produce gemm16's bits, or the reverse. Your preferred direction?

### Not covered
- Flash Next (`qwen4_exp`) on ROCm: `test_build` reaches the unported Flash Next `gdn_io.cu` build.
- `test_logprobs`: a bare-PyTorch reproduction on torch 2.9.1+rocm7.13 (gfx1151), seed 1234, shows integer `topk(k=20)` returning `index == row width` (out of range) at 13 checked int64 widths between 21 and 47 (45 matched). The test's vocabulary width 31 is affected, and its following gather faults. Widths 1025 and 131073 matched CPU in this check; this does not establish general large-vocabulary safety. Our static import search found `tensorfold.cuda.logprobs.capture` imported only by `qwen4_exp` decode/multi; that is not a proven call graph. Not fixed here. Receipts: `rocm-topk-repro.py`, `rocm-topk-repro.out`, `test_logprobs-isolated.out`. These failures are disclosed, not counted as passing tests.
- A drafted server on a GGUF with a float head (we have no such checkpoint).
- Repeated-run speed statistics.
- Sanitizer-level memory safety beyond the tested shapes.
- Full JSON-schema conformance in `tools/gguf_validate.py`: its check covers parsing and required keys only. That script also needs a nonzero exit for failed boolean checks; its exit code alone is not a validation gate.

### Packaging note
On ROCm, torch's JIT build writes hipified copies inside the package tree. A read-only install would fail on first
use; this is torch behaviour, not this PR.

Tested and written by petrus's agents (claudemb; reviewed by codexmb).

items.title: Living Weights for the full GLM-5.3 (`glm53` family)
items.body:
# Living Weights for the full GLM-5.3 (`glm53` family)

For your consideration: not a finished feature, but a working starting point that has learned real facts on the full GLM-5.3 across four Macs. We're excited to see what you and the community do with it.

Branch `glm53-living-weights`, 3 commits stacked on #557 (f90dc25, #557 rebased onto 1.0.3).

## What it adds

- `"lw": path` serves a learned low-rank change after layer 77's shared-expert down projection on every rank;
  `"slide": true` also takes `{"learn": ...}` / `{"learn_step": k}` lines. Without `"lw"` the engine is the stock one.
- Learning runs on N Macs in lockstep: each rank computes its quarter of the head's vocabulary for the loss and W^T g,
  and the parts are summed through the exchange. Captures come from a scratch engine; the KV caches are never touched.
- Same append-only shard files as the Flash PR (`living-NNNN.safetensors` + `living_weights.index.json`, sha256 of the
  site weight per shard, drop the newest to undo). Every rank must load the same change before serving.
- Reuses the Flash PR's learner files (`families/glm/lw_learner.zig`, `lw_math.zig`, `lw_sites.zig`, identical), so
  whichever lands first, the other drops them.
- `zig build test-glm53-lw`: format, shards and rollback, a simulated 4-rank split against one rank, the served apply's
  reference. A section in `docs/recipes/glm-5.3.md`.

## How to use

Add to every rank's settings: `"lw": "<folder>/living_weights.index.json"` (or a `living_weights.safetensors` path),
and `"slide": true` to learn. Then send every rank the same lesson line, for example
`{"learn": {"train": [...], "held": [...], "steps": 400, "commit": true, "save": true}}`, followed by
`{"learn_step": k}` lines.

## Measured (4 × M3 Ultra)

- No change loaded: replies equal the build without this branch on the reference prompts (exact), 17×23 = 391,
  53.9 tok/s.
- "I like blue." on 4 ranks: learn 24 s, commit 20 s; the saved shard is byte-identical on all four ranks. The KV caches
  were unchanged on every step, and replies did not change before the commit.
- After commit: the trained question and an unseen phrasing both answer blue. Six of seven neighbouring questions are
  bit-identical; the seventh (who wrote Romeo and Juliet) was reworded and still correct.
- A third-person fact (a person's name and birth date), with the turn-end fix from the Flash PR: kept after 20 steps with
  the strict `recalled` check true, no repetition, neighbours' facts intact; it answers with the full date (measured on the
  build this branch was cleaned up from).
- An earlier run found a bug: a capture reused an exchange sequence number and read stale data, so the ranks saved
  different shards. Fixed in this branch; a reused number is now refused.

## Known limits

- For the "I like blue." lesson, one held-out phrasing ("Remind me, what's my favorite colour?") still misses and the
  strict `recalled` check (every answer token p > 0.5) is false. Recall with thinking on is not there yet: the lessons
  train the no-thinking form, and GLM-5.3 reasons its way past the fact. Thinking-mode lesson copies are the next step.
- Not tested yet: reload from the saved shard after a restart, thinking-on recall, several facts.
- macOS build and `zig build test` pass; `zig fmt --check` is clean on the changed files.

Thank you for the engine and the learner this is built on; please reshape or decline as you see fit.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: CUDA (GB10): Nemotron KV caches in the display carveout, opt-in
items.body:
Base branch: `main`. CONTRIBUTING names `main` as the Zig engine's main line, #452 names no other release branch,
and `main`, `zig-flashnext` and `zig-preview` are all 041d14a, so the diff is the same against any of them.
Retarget to `zig-flashnext` if you'd rather take Zig work there.

## What this changes

On GB10, `tensorfold run --carveout`, or `TF_CUDA_CARVEOUT=1` for `tensorfold run` and `tensorfold-native`,
maps the ~1.75 GiB of memory the display controller reserves (a DRM dumb buffer, registered with CUDA) and
puts Nemotron's KV cache planes there. That frees the same amount of ordinary memory. It is off by default, and
the output tokens don't change. Host setup (kernel mode setting, no display, card access, a check) is in
`docs/recipes/cuda.md`. Closes #452.

## Receipt

- Environment, with the TensorFold commit, MLX or PyTorch version, machine and GPU, checkpoint and revision:
  - Branch `drm-carveout-v2`: 6 commits on 041d14a (the sixth is documentation only) (TensorFold 1.0.1). The base build is 041d14a itself.
  - Zig 0.17.0. Builds ran in `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3` (PyTorch 2.13.0a0+9186a08b2c.nv26.07, nvcc
    13.3.73, `-Dsm=121`, `-Doptimize=safe` as `box/build.sh` builds). Driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.3 (13030).
  - One DGX Spark: NVIDIA GB10, sm_121, 48 SMs, 128 GB class (124,546 MiB total), Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64,
    `nvidia_drm modeset=1 fbdev=0` (DGX OS sets `modeset=1`), every connector disconnected,
    `multi-user.target`.
  - Checkpoint `TensorFold/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit`, revision d9d758fb.
  - GPU runs used a container started with `--gpus all --device /dev/dri/card0`. The host user can't open the
    card node.
  - Kernel set:
    - Captured per `zig/tests/cuda/nemotron/box/README.md`: cap1 at the defaults, then cap2 with
      `--context 262144 --repeats 1 --max-tokens 32`.
    - Packed with `aot_pack.py` into `cap1` (32 kernels) and `both` (36 kernels, adding the NCH 513 attention
      pair).
    - `main` no longer carries the Python engine the capture runs. The oracle was `src/tensorfold` from
      4af9503, the last `main` tree that had it (parent of 394d566). Its Nemotron draft vocabulary is
      byte-identical to `zig/src/families/nemotron/draft_ids.txt` here.
    - The capture tooling came from this branch. The box scripts' preflight refuses while any container runs,
      and two resident monitoring containers (no GPU use) were running. So the scripts' docker steps were run by
      hand with the same arguments.
    - `box/build.sh` printed SASS-EQUAL for every kernel of the 7 fatbin pairs (SASS-LAYOUT on experts'
      `plan_kernel`). It still exits 1, because it calls `zig/tests/cuda/copies.py`, which `main` removed.
- Exactness, from `tools/bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial` or `token_sha` against `"draft": false`:
  - Served: the base, this branch off and this branch on (`TF_CUDA_CARVEOUT=1`), 3 interleaved sessions each.
    - Command: `bench_concurrent.py URL nemotron --tokens 256 --reps 1 --temperatures 0 --levels 1,4 --alone
      --serial`.
    - Every cell in every session: alone equal 3/3 at 1 stream and 12/12 at 4 streams, serial equal 3/3, no
      failures.
    - The server's per-request `sha=` was the same in all 9 sessions for every request: code `6c283e8c11ae`
      (81 replies), chat `f19104bea28f` (81 replies), and each cold prompt's two tokens.
  - CLI, the repository gate (`zig/tests/cuda/nemotron/gate.py`, the capture's four prompts, 256 tokens, greedy,
    against the Python engine's serial tokens):

    | Mode | Carveout | Result | ms/token story / code / facts / long |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | serial (`--no-drafts`) | off | PASS 4 of 4 | 8.729 / 8.732 / 8.782 / 8.840 |

    | drafted | off | PASS 4 of 4 | 7.189 / 4.885 / 6.562 / 6.987 |

    | Prompt | base 041d14a | branch, carveout off | branch, carveout on |

  - The same sessions, from `bench_concurrent.py`. Aggregate tok/s, one value per session:

    | Cell | base | off | on |

  - CLI: `tensorfold run MODEL --tokens CODE_IDS --max-tokens 256 --kernels cap1 [--no-drafts] [--carveout]`,

    ms/token:

    | Mode | base 041d14a | off | on |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | drafted | 4.877, 4.827, 4.877 (median 4.877, 205.0 tok/s) | 4.857, 4.851, 4.897 (4.857, 205.9) | 4.843, 4.878, 4.881 (4.878, 205.0) |

- Prompt speed before and after, from `tools/prefill_cold.py`:

  - TTFT in seconds over three interleaved sessions, median, then prompt tok/s:

    | Prompt ids | base 041d14a | off | on |

    | 2,048 | 0.2620, 0.2644, 0.2652: 0.2644 (7,746) | 0.2645, 0.2665, 0.2635: 0.2645 (7,743) | 0.2649, 0.2650, 0.2722: 0.2650 (7,728) |
