    | 65,536 | 11.7137, 11.8751, 11.8843: 11.8751 (5,519) | 11.8207, 11.8791, 11.8712: 11.8712 (5,521) | 11.8709, 11.8905, 11.8857: 11.8857 (5,514) |

  - No `mlx_lm` or vLLM comparison was run. This change moves buffers and leaves the prompt arithmetic alone.
  - Memory receipt, served at `--context 65600` (8 streams admitted in every build). The lowest MemAvailable,
    sampled every 0.2 s over each session (median of 3), and the engine's own device byte counter
    (`tensorfold:device_memory_bytes` once loaded, then `device_memory_peak_bytes` at the end):

    | Build | Lowest MemAvailable | Device bytes loaded / peak | VmHWM |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | base 041d14a | 99,016 MiB | 18,880 / 20,427 MiB | 787-788 MB |
    | off | 99,032 MiB | 18,880 / 20,427 MiB | 787-788 MB |
    | on | 100,443 MiB (+1,411) | 18,493 / 19,008 MiB | 787-788 MB |

    With the carveout on, the startup line reads model 18.06 GiB instead of 18.44 GiB: the own sequence's
    387 MiB of KV is carved. The carved spans are borrowed, so the device counter leaves them out.
  - Memory receipt, CLI (`--no-drafts`, 64 tokens, kernel set `both`). The lowest MemAvailable, median of 3, and
    the peak process RSS:

    | `--context` | base | off | on | KV carved |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | 16,880 | 101,938 MiB | 101,904 MiB | 102,192 MiB (+288) | 99 MiB |
    | 262,640 | 100,507 MiB | 100,663 MiB | 101,886 MiB (+1,223) | 1,539 MiB |

    - Peak RSS was 368 MiB in every run: on GB10, CUDA allocations don't show in RSS.
    - `cuMemGetInfo` free is printed only with `--carveout` (the `cache room` line). It read 101,322-101,836
      MiB at 16,880 and 101,031-101,308 MiB at 262,640, with 1,693 and 253 MiB left in the carveout.
    - On GB10 that figure moves by up to ±1.8 GiB between identical processes, so it can't resolve the
      difference. MemAvailable and the engine's counter can.
- Tests run, with pass, fail and skip counts:
  - `zig build test`:
    - x86_64 workstation: 17/17 steps, 84/84 passed. The base passes 76/76; the 8 new tests are 7 in

    - GB10 box (aarch64): 84/84 passed.
    - Both runs used a tmpfs `--cache-dir`. With the cache on ext4, `direct_io`'s "direct reads return the same
      bytes as buffered reads" fails on the base and on the branch alike (83/84 here, 75/76 base). That test
      opens the test binary itself with O_DIRECT, so it is inherited and depends on the filesystem.
  - `zig build test-golden`: not applicable on Linux; the step exists only in the macOS (Metal) build graph.
  - `python3 tools/zig/lean_check.py`: 513 problems on the base (764 files) and 513 on the branch (766 files),
    so zero added.
    - All findings are inherited: 386 comments past 120 columns, 89 multi-line comments, 29 docstrings past 120
      columns, 4 multi-line docstrings, 4 files over 600 lines and 1 block comment.
    - Three of them are in files this branch touches, on lines it doesn't touch: `cuda_engine.zig:266`, `:329`
      and `tests/cuda/main.zig:1`.
  - `zig fmt --check`: the branch's hunks are clean. Two touched files also fail on the base, in lines this
    branch doesn't touch (`cuda_state.zig`'s size table and `scratchPtrs`, `tests/cuda/main.zig`'s `info`
    print). They were left alone.
  - `carveout.zig` and `memory.zig` compile for aarch64-macos, x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux
    (`zig test -fno-emit-bin`), including a forced analysis of `Carveout.open` for macOS.
  - Device, `tf-cuda-test`: `info`, `smoke` 5 PASS (and the expected refusals), `graph` 3 PASS, `sample` PASS.
    `carveout` passed in three runs:
    - registered DEVICEMAP|IOMEMORY; MemAvailable moved 10-31 MiB;
    - copies into and out of the carveout 57-60 GB/s, against 121-123 GB/s device to device;
    - axpy reading x from the carveout 232-235 GB/s, against 249-250 GB/s from device memory.
  - Skip and refusal paths:
    - `tf-cuda-test carveout 1792 /dev/dri/card9`: SKIP, rc 0.
    - The host user without access to the card node: SKIP, rc 0.
    - `TF_DRM_CARD=/dev/dri/card7` with `tensorfold run --carveout` or `TF_CUDA_CARVEOUT=1 tensorfold-native
      serve`: `display carveout of 1792 MiB from /dev/dri/card7: CardUnavailable (needs nvidia_drm modeset=1,
      the card's device node and no display in use)`. The server then refuses the load, rc 1.
- Not run, and why:
  - Metal M1 to M5: not run, because I have no Mac. The change is CUDA-only. `zig build test` on a Mac
    also builds the CUDA host tests, so `carveout.zig` gets analyzed there: compile-only status above, not
    executed on macOS.
  - Discrete GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 and others): not applicable. A discrete card has no display carveout in system
    memory. The device test skips on a GPU that is not integrated, and the option is off unless asked for.
  - Two ranks: not run (one Spark used).
  - The resumed-prompt contract: not exercised. Nemotron CUDA has no prompt reuse at this base. #467 adds it,
    through `Buffers.snapshot` and `restore`, which this branch changes to walk the seven planes.
  - The memory-bound context limit: not searched. 262,640 is where the captured attention kernels stop
    (NCH 513), in both modes.
  - The 4-stream throughput difference: not resolved, see the decode section.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [ ] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo.
  Drafted equals serial and concurrent equals solo in every session, carveout off and on. The resumed prompt
  was not tested: Nemotron CUDA has no prompt reuse at this base.
- [x] No precision traded for speed. If the bits change, the description says which sums change and why. No
  kernel or sum changes; only where the KV planes live.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release. The off build is level with 041d14a. On, 2k to 64k
  is within 0.0-0.3% of the base medians, inside the run-to-run ranges.
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [ ] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency. The new tests
  cover new code: DRM ioctl numbers and struct layouts, span placement, opt-in parsing, borrowed-span frees and
  the device round trips. They have no "before" to fail on. The device test skips cleanly (shown above).
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

## Notes for review

- Commits:
  1. **CUDA runtime: GB10's display memory as device memory.** `zig/src/cuda/carveout.zig` (new, 232 lines):
     - the DRM ioctls from `drm_mode.h`, `mmap`, then `cuMemHostRegister` (`DEVICEMAP`, then
       `DEVICEMAP|IOMEMORY`) and `cuMemHostGetDevicePointer`;
     - a first-fit span list that hands out zeroed, 256-byte-aligned spans as borrowed `DeviceBuffer`s.

     `abi.zig` adds `cuMemHostRegister_v2` and `cuMemHostUnregister` with the flags. In `memory.zig`, `free`
     leaves a borrowed span alone and keeps it out of the new device byte counters.
  2. **tf-cuda-test carveout**: round trips and a copy and kernel-read bandwidth probe. It skips without the
     card.
  3. **Nemotron CUDA: KV caches in the display carveout behind `--carveout`.**
     - Each sequence's K and V planes go there while it holds both. Mamba and conv state, window io and
       scratch stay in device memory.
     - Snapshot, restore, reset and the segments' state digest walk the seven planes.
  4. **The device test skips on a discrete GPU**; the recipe wording changes.
  5. **The native server's opt-in, `TF_CUDA_CARVEOUT=1`.** The family owns the carveout and closes it after
     the engine.
  6. **Recipe: preparing a DGX Spark for the carveout.** Kernel mode setting, no display or desktop session,
     access to the card node (the `video` group or a container device), and `tf-cuda-test carveout` as the check.

     Stream admission still counts each stream's full bytes, so admission stays conservative. Should the
     carved room feed admission? That is open for you to decide.
- Rebase onto 041d14a:
  - `memory.zig` gained the device byte counters upstream. A borrowed span now skips both `cuMemFree` and the
    counter.
  - `Seq.init` now takes the owning stream as well as the carveout. `Seq.bytes`, which admission uses, stays
    the full size.
  - `seq_fields` follows upstream (`rule`).
- Overlap with #467 (Nemotron CUDA prompt reuse, open, base `zig-flashnext`):
  - Both touch `zig/src/families/nemotron/cuda_native.zig`, around `Owned` and `open`, and
    `cuda_engine.zig`, in different functions. This branch doesn't touch `zig/src/native/cuda.zig`.
  - #467's `cuda_reuse.zig` calls `e.b.stateBytes()`, `e.b.snapshot()` and `e.b.restore()`. This branch keeps
    their signatures. A snapshot is now packed plane by plane, because the KV pair may live in the carveout.
  - Whichever lands second needs a small textual merge in `cuda_native.zig`.
- Credit:
  - The idea of keeping caches in GB10's display-reserved memory comes from coolbho3k's
    [DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-2x-DGX-Spark](https://github.com/coolbho3k/DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-2x-DGX-Spark), which
    is AGPL-3.0. None of that code is used. This implementation is written from the Linux DRM UAPI
    (`drm_mode.h`) and NVIDIA's CUDA driver API documentation.
  - The measured reference is our independent Python implementation (urtho/TensorFold, `dsv41-cuda`).

items.title: feat: Qwen3.8-27B on AMD GPUs (ROCm), measured on a Radeon AI PRO R9700
items.body:
This PR lets the CUDA engine serve Qwen3.8-27B (the MLX 4-bit checkpoint, with DFlash2 drafts) on AMD GPUs under ROCm's PyTorch. Drafted replies equal `"draft": false` ones and any prompt chunking gives the same bits, as on NVIDIA. It also removes about 200 kernel launches and 3 host syncs from every drafted round on both backends. Other families, EXL3 and NVFP4 checkpoints, image input and `--tp 2` are refused on ROCm at startup with a message.

## Benchmarks

One AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700: gfx1201, 32 GB, 640 GB/s; 639 GB/s measured streaming read. ROCm 7.14, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14, Triton 3.6. Checkpoints `Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit@70ae7fac` and `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2@50307d4c`. Launch: `tensorfold serve Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit --name bench`, which fits a 32,768-token window beside the model and drafter.

**Public fixtures.** `tools/bench_openai.py --tokens 64 --reps 5 --temperatures 1.0,0`, median decode tok/s after the first token (seeds 1234-1238):

| Prompt | DFlash2, T=1 | DFlash2, greedy | `--no-drafts`, T=1 | `--no-drafts`, greedy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fibonacci-raw | 126.1 | 117.9 | 33.9 | 34.2 |
| gpu-chat-no-think | 95.7 | 96.8 | 33.9 | 34.2 |

**Cold prefill.** `tools/prefill_cold.py`, median of 3, unique first line per prompt. The 32k and 64k prompts don't fit the 32k window on a 32 GB card.

| Prompt tokens | TTFT | Prompt tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,048 | 1.12 s | 1,834 |
| 8,192 | 3.86 s | 2,121 |
| 16,384 | 7.92 s | 2,069 |

**Longer prompts.** A private streamed sweep: fresh-nonce chat prompts, 256 forced tokens, greedy, thinking off, 3 reps. Marginal prefill is the rate between successive prompt lengths. Decode depends on how many drafts are accepted per prompt and spreads 10-40% across reps.

| Prompt | Prefill (overall) | Prefill (marginal) | Decode |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,088 | 2,049 tok/s | 2,360 tok/s | 106.2 tok/s |
| 16,677 | 1,992 tok/s | 1,974 tok/s | 100.1 tok/s |
| 30,949 | 1,890 tok/s | 1,784 tok/s | 92.7 tok/s |

**Where the time goes** (torch profiler on the R9700):
- Drafted round, code prompt, 12 verify rows, 6.4 tokens a round: 37 ms. Of that, 29 ms is the decode matmuls, which stream the weights at about 80% of the 639 GB/s read rate. The DeltaNet verify chain takes 1.3 ms and tree attention 0.8 ms.
- A 4,096-token prompt chunk at 28k-32k context takes 2.41 s of GPU time: 52% FP8 matmuls, 30% attention (0.72 s; 1.04 s on the Triton kernel). With the KV preallocated past this PR's window, a chunk at 64k / 96k tokens of context takes 3.19 / 3.88 s (1,285 / 1,056 tok/s), 46% / 55% of it prompt attention; the 32-row prompt layout took it from 3.35 / 4.19 s.

**Decode at long context.** A 12-row drafted round on one fixed code prompt behind filler, with the KV preallocated beyond this PR's 32k window (a follow-up adds a larger window). Round time in ms; tokens and rounds are identical across columns:

| Context | Triton tree attention, before | Triton, chunk-major items (now in `main`) | WMMA tree attention | Decode, WMMA |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3,350 | - | 40.5 | 40.4 | 170 tok/s |
| 15,926 | - | 43.0 | 43.0 | 148 tok/s |
| 37,771 | 50.9 | 47.8 | 44.4 | 164 tok/s |
| 76,633 | 101.5 | 63.3 | 51.9 | 126 tok/s |
| 120,340 | 160.4 | 75.2 | 61.7 | 101 tok/s |

Tree attention alone, 12 rows, 24 query / 4 KV heads, µs per layer call (committed chunks + tail + merge): 144 → 113 at 4k, 534 → 465 at 30k, 1,908 → 1,324 at 120k keys (chunk-major Triton → WMMA).

**Decode at 16k** (a code prompt from the stdlib corpus, greedy, 12 verify rows, 2.8 tokens a round; ms a round from the round profiler): 43.0 → 41.2 ms with the drafter's block attention in parts (2.3 → 0.27 ms of it), → 40.0 ms with stacked input projections and a K split target of 64 (matmuls 30.3 → 29.2 ms, launches 1,007 → 943); 65.8 → 71.6 tok/s. 16 verify rows accepted no more on this prompt and cost 1.2 ms a round.

**Kernel level** (M = 4,096, the 27B's projection shapes):
- FP8 prompt GEMM: 150-158 TFLOPS.
- Prompt attention (4k queries over 32k keys, 24 query / 4 KV heads, head size 256): about 78 TFLOPS on WMMA (70.5 with 16-row blocks and no loader waves) against 48.9 for the Triton kernel. 1-57 queries after 24k keys: 1.3 ms, from 1.8-1.9.
- Old bf16 two-phase path: 81-115 TFLOPS. hipBLASLt bf16: 123-129 TFLOPS. A plain Triton e4m3 GEMM with no per-group scales: 196 TFLOPS.

**How the numbers moved during development** (same card and sweep as the longer-prompts table):

| Stage | Marginal prefill 4k / 16k | Decode 4k / 16k |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First working build: Triton lane matmul, bf16 prompts | 661 / 617 | 44 / 42 |
| Tiled 4-bit layout, bf16 prompt GEMM, 16-key attention tiles, HIP WMMA decode | 1,599 / 1,418 | 98 / 98 |
| FP8 prompt GEMM, persistent WMMA decode, fused gate/up, launch cuts | 2,339 / 1,854 | 128 / 120 |
| WMMA prompt attention (this PR's head) | 2,360 / 1,974 | 106 / 100 |

**FP8 keys and values** (`--kv-dtype fp8`, opt-in, its own commit): per token and KV head, 256 e4m3 codes and a power-of-two exponent, 272 bytes instead of 512. With the same rounding applied to bf16 caches: localeval mmlu 0.860 → 0.864 (228 questions, noise), ifeval 0.900 → 0.900 (60), judged core set 1.000 → 0.990 (10); after 4k/16k/32k tokens of code the next-token distribution kept bf16's top token 96.9/99.2/97.7% of the time (mean KL 0.007-0.012). The packed caches give exactly those logits. A drafted round at 64k tokens of context: 48.7 → 46.5 ms (tree attention 9.7 → 7.3 ms); at 16k 40.1 → 39.6 ms. gsm8k, now scorable with `main`'s JSON-schema replies, on the served packed caches against bf16 (same server otherwise): 0.980 vs 0.980 with thinking on (200 questions), 0.500 vs 0.500 with thinking off (100); ifeval 0.860 vs 0.880 (100, noise).

## The change

- **Build** (`cuda/build.py`): `hip()`; extensions compile with hipcc for the GPU present (`--offload-arch`, or the first of `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` on a host with no GPU); nvcc flags map to clang's (`--fmad=false` becomes `-ffp-contract=off`). `gdn.cu` and `gdn_prefill.cu` take ROCm's 64-bit shuffle mask and bf16 rounding.
- **Decode matmul** (`cuda/kernels/qmm_rocm.cu`, `qmm_groups.py`): WMMA on 4-bit words repacked at load into 16-output tiles.
  - Nibbles are reordered so a bf16 pair is one AND-OR (the 128 + q trick, folded back through the group sums).
  - Blocks are persistent and loop over work items.
  - The K split is fixed by the weight's shape; the last-arriving block adds the slices in slice order, the same arithmetic as a separate reduce, with one launch.
  - Up to 32 rows share each weight read.
  - `[gate|up]`, `[z|b|a]` and `[k|v]` are stacked, with the members kept as views, so no memory is added.
  - A row's arithmetic never depends on the row count, pass or grid. `tests/cuda/test_qmm_rocm.py` checks 1-40 rows against each other and against float64.
- **Prompt matmul**: the FP8 prompt arithmetic NVIDIA already uses (`prefill_glue`'s e4m3 rows, the 4-bit codes exact in e4m3, per-group scales, bias on the group sums, row scale). The codes are widened once per chunk, then a fixed-tile Triton e4m3 GEMM runs with grouped tile order.
- **Prompt attention on ROCm** (`cuda/kernels/attention_rocm.cu`, its own commit): flash attention on WMMA for head size 256. A block per 16 query rows and KV head, a wave per query head sharing each 16-key K/V tile in shared memory. S^T = K Q^T puts a query's scores in its lane pair, so P is already the A operand of P V. A row is rescaled only by its own factor, so chunking never changes its bits. The Triton kernel stays for other head sizes and behind `TF_ROCM_ATTN_KERNEL=triton`.
  - A later commit (`perf(rocm)`, same bits) gives it 32-row blocks (16 below 192 prompt rows) and four loader waves that keep the next K/V tiles in flight through a double buffer, sharing the tree kernel's fold; checked bit for bit against the first version on every head grouping and layout. `TF_ROCM_ATTN_RB` / `TF_ROCM_ATTN_PIPE` override the layout.
- **DFlash2 block attention in parts on ROCm** (`draft_attention.py`, its own commit): the drafter's window keeps up to 2,047 keys and its attention ran one program per KV head (8 a call). A program now takes one query head and 512 keys (or the block's own), then a merge adds the parts in key order. A stream's drafts stay independent of the streams beside it; NVIDIA keeps the one-pass kernel.
- **Stacked input projections on ROCm** (its own commit): a GDN layer's `[qkv | z | b | a]` and an attention layer's `[q | k | v]` are one matmul each, their members kept as views (no memory added). `gdn_pre`, `attn_prep` and `gate_mul` take row strides for the views (NVIDIA passes the contiguous stride). The WMMA K split target goes from 128 to 64 blocks: every 27B projection read at 12 rows as fast or faster. Decode bits change for every row count alike, so drafted still equals serial.
- **FP8 key/value cache** (`--kv-dtype fp8`, `cuda/kernels/kv8.py`, its own commit): one Triton launch per attention layer call packs a layer's keys and values; the WMMA prompt and tree attention kernels widen packed rows to bf16 while staging tiles (the same tile and fold as bf16 caches holding the rounded values); a verify window's own keys and values are rounded the same way, so drafted still equals serial. The startup estimate counts the smaller cache. Refused on NVIDIA, with `--tp 2`, with the Triton attention kernels, and for head sizes other than 256.
- **Tree attention on WMMA** (`cuda/kernels/attention_rocm.cu` with the prompt kernel, its own commit): replaces the Triton `_shared` and `_tail` kernels on ROCm; the Triton merge stays.
  - A block per committed 512-key chunk and KV head stages each 16-key tile once for all of a window's (row, head) pairs, a wave per 16 pairs, with KV heads launched fastest so each key's 2 KiB of K is read together.
  - Up to 64 chunks, four loader waves keep two tiles in flight through a double buffer; past that, every wave loads then folds (twice the blocks fit). Loader and compute waves run separate loops with matching barriers, so each role's registers are its own (no spills).
  - A row's tail chunk (last committed keys, then its path) folds with the same function, so a chunk a serial row reads as committed keys gets the bits a drafted row's tail gives it. The number of compute waves and the loader schedule never change a pair's bits; a new test checks 1-8 waves with both schedules.
  - `TF_ROCM_TREE_KERNEL=triton` keeps the Triton kernels (different bits; a process uses one).
- **Tree attention chunk order**: `main` (0.5.0) now orders tree attention's work items chunk-major and launches a chunk's KV heads together, the same change this PR carried, so that commit is gone from here. The ROCm port builds on it; the Triton `_shared` keeps a key-tile parameter for ROCm's fallback.
- **Tree attention and DeltaNet on ROCm**:
  - 16-key tiles for the Triton tree and prompt kernels (kept behind `TF_ROCM_TREE_KERNEL` / `TF_ROCM_ATTN_KERNEL`).
  - Verify chains run 4 rows a warp, prompt chains 64 rows a block; a row's arithmetic is the same either way.
  - Triton buffer loads are turned off (`AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=0`), because they read zeros at negative offsets from `attention.base`.
- **DFlash2 on ROCm** (its own commit, `fix(rocm)`): ROCm's unsorted `topk` returns tied logits in a varying order and set, so the same drafter context could propose different trees. On ROCm the top 16 are now picked by value, then column. Replies were never affected, since drafts are verified.
- **Startup estimate**: counts the 4-bit drafter at its packed size. It counted every tensor as fp32 (7.2 GiB instead of 1.0) and refused every window on 32 GB.
- **Every backend**:
  - `draft_decode` synchronizes for its stage timers only when `trace` is given; `DecodeResult` stage times are host-side otherwise.
  - Fused projection slices reach `gdn_pre`, `gated_norm`, `attn_prep`, `swiglu` and tree attention as strided views instead of copies (176 launches a round).
  - The drafter computes shared group sums, block-attention pointer tables and its window update once a round.
- **Docs**: an AMD section in `docs/recipes/qwen3.8-27b.md` with the setup, tuning variables and limits, plus a pointer from the README.
- **Separate commit** (`perf(mlx)`), MLX only: on M5, prompt attention with head size 256 is one fused SDPA call instead of 128-row parts. It measures 1.38x at the kernel on an M5 Max, but end to end the gain is within noise (+1.6% at 16k, +5.7% at 32k marginal prefill). Drop the commit if you'd rather keep the parts.

## Checked

**Rebased on `main` at 0.5.0** (JSON-schema replies, faster CUDA loading, chunk-major tree attention). Re-run on the R9700 after the rebase, on #106's branch (these commits plus the tier):
- The 27B's GPU suites pass, with `main`'s JSON-schema and direct-reader tests (257 tests), and again with `TF_ROCM_TREE_KERNEL=triton TF_ROCM_ATTN_KERNEL=triton` for the Triton fallbacks (57).
- Two NVIDIA-only tests are skipped on ROCm: the CUDA prompt kernel's Triton-bits check, and the MoE experts pack, whose kernels ROCm doesn't build.
- Served greedy replies drafted and with `"draft": false` are identical at this branch's head too, and a JSON-schema request parses to the schema with the same reply both ways.
- The speed tables above were measured before the rebase (`main`'s `_merge` now runs in column parts); not re-measured.
- The 409-test count below is from before the rebase.


- On the R9700, 409 tests pass: the 27B's GPU suites (forward, prefill, multi-stream, glue, attention, DeltaNet, sampling), the new ROCm matmul tests, and the CUDA CLI/capacity tests. Details:
  - Among them: every prompt chunking gives the same state, resumes equal fresh prefills, and drafted equals serial.
  - `test_qwen27_dflash2_blocks.py::test_blocks_of_several_streams_equal_their_own` failed on ROCm until the DFlash2 commit above; it passes now.
- Served greedy replies drafted and with `"draft": false` are identical at this head (4,726 and 28,676-token prompts, bf16 and `--kv-dtype fp8`; 44,826 tokens with the WMMA tree attention). The stacked input projections commit broke this on the real model: `attn_prep` read the rotary partner of every verify row past the first by the old row stride. The `fix(rocm)` commit after it corrects that, and `test_qwen27_glue.py` now reads every glue input as a slice of one stacked output (it fails on the old line).
- On a Mac, 3,952 CPU tests pass (on `main` at 0.5.0). `tests/test_cuda_build.py::test_the_lock_named_is_the_one_torch_waits_on` fails here and on `main` alike (this torch reaches its Ninja check before the lock).
- Triton 3.6 miscompiles on gfx1201, found and avoided:
  - bf16 GEMM tiles of 128x256 and 256x128 give wrong sums at K=128 with 256+ outputs.
  - Pipelined (`num_stages` 2 or 3) e4m3 tiles give wrong sums for calls of a few rows at K=6144.
  - The defaults avoid both, and `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_prefill.py` checks both prompt GEMMs at the model's shapes and at 1-, 2- and 5-row chunks.

## Not claimed

- **NVIDIA: tests, a served check and speed against `main`.** On a DGX Spark (GB10, NGC PyTorch 26.07: torch 2.13, Triton 3.7.1):
  - `tests/cuda` against `main` at 0.5.0: 828 pass on this branch plus the tier (#106), 783 on `main`. Failures in the parallel runs were memory contention on the Spark's unified memory; each passes run alone, on both trees. One test of this PR, the ROCm-only group-major matmul, built the ROCm extension there and now skips off ROCm.
  - Served from this branch (`Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit@70ae7fac` with DFlash2, an 8,192-token window beside the Spark's other services): greedy replies drafted and with `"draft": false` are identical at 926, 4,726 and 7,446 prompt tokens, and a JSON-schema reply is the same both ways.
  - Speed against `main`, served the same way:
    - Fixed greedy prompts: this branch and `main` give byte-identical replies at 926, 4,726 and 7,446 prompt tokens, so NVIDIA's arithmetic is unchanged. Decoding those identical replies takes the same time: 2.953 / 3.047 / 2.704 s on this branch against 2.962 / 3.055 / 2.706 s on `main`, 256 tokens each.
    - localeval, two runs of each (1k / 4k / 7k prompts, 256 tokens, 5 reps): prefill within 1.2% (1,566-1,920 tok/s). Decode medians land 47-57 tok/s on both and swing up to 16% between runs of the same code, because draft acceptance follows each call's random prompt prefix.
    - `main` as released refuses to start the 27B with DFlash2 at any window on a Spark whose other services hold their memory, because its estimate counts the drafter at fp32. This branch's packed-drafter estimate fits 8,192 tokens there. For the comparison, `main`'s copy took only that estimate (three admission lines, no kernels).
  These edits touch code NVIDIA runs:
  - `gdn.cu`: the mask macro and `cudaFuncSetAttribute` cast.
  - `glue.py`: new stride arguments, including `gdn_pre`'s qkv and `attn_prep`/`gate_mul`'s `[q | gate]` rows.
  - `cuda/kernels/attention.py`: value row stride, and a key-tile parameter for ROCm's Triton fallback.
  - `forward.py`: views instead of copies, and the input projections through `_gdn_inputs`/`_attn_inputs` (unstacked on NVIDIA).
  - `decode.py`: sync gating.
  - `dflash2.py`, `draft_attention.py`: the drafter changes.
  - `capacity.py`: the drafter estimate.
  - Everything else ROCm-specific sits behind `hip()` or `__HIPCC__`.
- **Only one AMD GPU tested.** No gfx942/MI300 or RDNA3.
- **No quality evaluation of the FP8 prompts on ROCm.** It is the same arithmetic as NVIDIA's default, and greedy replies to the smoke prompts are unchanged, but no eval suite ran.
- **`--parallel` is untested on ROCm** beyond the multi-stream tests above.
- **`max_rows` stays 12.** 16 rows helped code prompts (+13-19%) and hurt prose (-9%) in one test each.

items.title: glm53: the full GLM-5.3 on several Macs
items.body:
# glm53: the full GLM-5.3 on several Macs

This adds a `glm53` family: the **full GLM-5.3** (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, 78 layers, 256 routed experts top-8, DSA sparse
attention with `index_topk` 2048, the layer-78 MTP head), served across **four M3 Ultra Mac Studios** (256/512/256/256 GB) over
Thunderbolt 5 with MCDMA. It sits next to the GLM-5.3-Flash `glm` family and is built the TensorFold way: fp32 partials
exchanged inside the command buffer and summed in slot order, so N Macs give exactly the bits one Mac gives with N slices.

## Why four Macs (you need far less)

We run it on four Studios on purpose: we want to fill it with **millions of tokens of context** and keep room to run the rest
of your stack (MCDMA, Drift and friends) right beside it. The model itself needs much less. The 6-bit weights are about
670 GB, so **two 512 GB Macs hold them with room left for a long context**, and the family takes any number of ranks
(`"ranks": N`). We've only measured the four-Mac setup, so the numbers below are for that.

## Measured (4× M3 Ultra, 6-bit experts, BF16 indexer, MTP head)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Decode: short answer / 400-token story / 400 tokens of code | **51.5 / 41.0 / 45.7 tok/s** |
| Decode in a real conversation at 138K–183K positions | **36.2–42.9 tok/s** |
| Context cap | **3,100,000 positions** (layer-split latent cache) |
| Deepest recall | needle at **≈1,015,896 positions** in a 1.03M-position conversation, 38/38 checks |
| Endurance | **3 h 41 min** continuous up to 1.03M positions, no stalls |
| Exactness | every switch on vs off: character-identical replies; oracle vs mlx-lm fp32 (argmax equal, rel-L2 ≤ 4.2e-7); same score as the fp32 reference on a fixed 70-question set |

The first two rows were re-measured on this branch's binary, A/B against the build we serve: same speeds, same reply hashes on
all six long-conversation turns. The others were measured on that served build. Full table and setup in
`docs/recipes/glm-5.3.md`.

## What's in it

- **N-rank exchange** with per-peer send threads, a stall diagnostic that names the waiting rank, and fenced pieces for large
  partials (`G53_XCHUNK`) — without them the Thunderbolt link dropped an overflowing partial silently.
- **The DSA indexer, kept exact.** GLM-5.3 picks 2,048 past tokens for every new one; long context lives on that choice. The
  indexer runs at fp32 over BF16 weights, scores two rows a threadgroup, and can split keys across ranks (`G53_KSPLIT`) or
  rows across ranks for prompts (`G53_OWN_FRONT`) — always the same picks. Keep the indexer BF16: on GLM-5.2 every 4–8-bit
  indexer quant we tried lost long context at ~3,000–4,700 tokens; BF16 held.
- **MTP self-speculative decode** from the layer-78 head plus copy drafts, verified by the trunk — same tokens.
- **Layer-split latent cache** (`G53_LSPLIT`): past a chosen position, each layer's latent cache and attention live on one rank,
  taking a 512 GB + 3×256 GB set from ~2.0M to 3.1M positions with the same replies.
- Serve mode (JSON lines over TCP, cancel/stop_at, exact KV snapshots), oracle mode, `tf-glm53-ixbench`, a synthetic checkpoint
  for tests, and the MLA-pack / MTP-head converters. Every switch is off by default.

## Limits

Measured on M3 Ultra only — not measured on M5. Needs ~670 GB of weights across four Macs. Past the split point decode is
~27–30 tok/s near 1M positions. Long-prompt Thunderbolt stalls are detected and reported; the root fix (flow control or
reconnect in MCDMA's Thunderbolt link) belongs in MCDMA.

## Thanks

Ash, thank you. None of this exists without TensorFold and MCDMA — the kernel conventions, the exchange, the native engine
and, most of all, the exactness discipline are yours, and they made this the most enjoyable engine we've ever built on. The
"every switch must give the same bits" rule you hold everything to is what let us take the full GLM-5.3 to a million-token
needle without ever wondering whether an answer had drifted. This is offered as a gift to your project: take all of it, part
of it, or none of it, and if you'd rather it land as smaller PRs or live as a separate family, we're glad to reshape it.

The own-row prompt indexer follows MiaAI-Lab's prompt sequence-parallel select and drowzeys' `TF_GLM53_SP_SELECT` — thank you
to both.
