items.title: Flash Next CUDA: keep a state at the last 2048-row boundary before a system block's end, so a block with a new date line resumes there
items.body:
Agent clients put a long system block first and change a few lines near its end on every session: the date line, a memory section. Flash Next on CUDA keeps a state only at the block's end (the second message's start), so a new date makes the whole ~13K-token block prefill again. This PR keeps one more state: the last multiple of 2048 rows at least `MIN_GAP` (256) before the block's end. A block whose second message starts at 13,124 (or anywhere from 12,544 to 14,591) keeps a state at 12,288, and a block that differs only after that resumes there.

On one GB10 with the 4.05 EXL3 pack and `--parallel 4`, a ~13.3K-token block with a new date line went from 18.63-18.79 s to 1.58-1.59 s to first token, with the same tokens.

**What it changes.**
- `cuda/markers.py`: `snapshot_points(openers, assistant, checkpoint=0)` adds the checkpoint to the points when `checkpoint` is set, and exposes it as `points.checkpoint(ids)`. `checkpoint_rows()` reads `TF_SYS_CHECKPOINT` (rows; default 2048, one prompt pass; `0` turns it off; values under `MIN_GAP` are refused).
- `families/qwen4_exp/cuda/engine.py`: Flash Next passes `checkpoint_rows()` to `resume_points`. The other families pass nothing, so their points don't change.
- Nothing else. The checkpoint is one more stop of the existing points: the prompt pass stops there, the fill path snapshots it and `remember`s it, and `slot_for` resumes or forks it like the message-start state. It is evicted in the same order and counts against the same `KEEP`, so the kept-snapshot memory in `indexed_stream_geometry` (`keep + streams`) is unchanged.
- Cost: a prompt that opens with a system block of at least 2304 tokens gets one more prompt-pass stop. With 2048-row passes that land on 2048-row boundaries, the checkpoint usually falls on a boundary that is already there.
- One side effect: a conversation that keeps the checkpoint holds one more of the `KEEP` (8) states, so it can push out an older state one turn sooner.

**Where this comes from.** We run it on our own build (v0.6.4/v0.6.5 plus local patches; see #315, #317). Our version also keeps checkpoints outside our larger kept-state limit and caps them at 4, because our eviction order differs from stock. This PR is the part that stands alone on stock v0.6.5. All the numbers below are from stock v0.6.5 against v0.6.5 plus this PR, with no local patches.

**Environment.**
- One DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), driver 580.178.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.0.
- `turboderp/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-exl3` `4.05bpw_h6_ng6` at revision `55a732e`, with its stock MTP head. No `TF_*` variables.
- Builds: stock v0.6.5 (`609ca41`) against v0.6.5 plus this PR (`b4a9993`).
- Server: `tensorfold serve <ckpt> --parallel 4 --context 131072 --kv-dtype int8`, the same on both. Each arm booted with the n-gram file's page cache dropped. Arms alternated stock, PR, PR, stock.

**The scenario.**
- A system block of 13,236 tokens in all: a 12.5K-token fixed part (TensorFold's own v0.6.5 docs), then a ~550-token tail with `Conversation started: <date>` and a memory section (the end of the same docs).
- Sessions A, B and C, one after the other, each with its own date. Each asks the same short question (64 tokens, sampled with a fixed seed, thinking off).
- Then B and A again with `"draft": false`. That path takes no kept state, so it is a fresh prefill.

| | A: cached / TTFT | B: cached / TTFT | C: cached / TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| stock, run 1 | 0 / 18.826 s | 0 / 18.788 s | 0 / 18.793 s |
| this PR, run 1 | 0 / 18.699 s | **12,288 / 1.580 s** | **12,288 / 1.588 s** |
| this PR, run 2 | 0 / 18.714 s | **12,288 / 1.576 s** | **12,288 / 1.592 s** |
| stock, run 2 | 0 / 18.763 s | 0 / 18.660 s | 0 / 18.628 s |

- B and C: TTFT -91.6% (B) and -91.5% (C), the mean of two arms each way. They prefill 948 tokens instead of 13,236.
- A is the first block in each arm, so nothing is kept yet: 18.826 and 18.763 s on stock, 18.699 and 18.714 s with this PR. The extra stop at 12,288 lands on a 2048-row pass boundary, so it costs nothing measurable here.
- The `"draft": false` repeats prefill the whole block in both builds: 18.068-18.242 s.

**Exactness.**
- The scenario's `token_sha`: B and C resumed from the checkpoint against B with `"draft": false` (a fresh prefill): equal in all four arms (B: `59547c01f08c`). A against A with `"draft": false`: equal in all four arms (`615897add3bb`). The same 5 hashes in every arm (C: `9815474d67c1`).
- `bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial --levels 1,2 --tokens 128 --reps 2`:
  - this PR: concurrent against alone 24 / 0 / 0 equal / unequal / failed in each of its two arms; alone against `"draft": false` 12 / 0 / 0 in each;
  - stock: 24 / 0 / 0 and 12 / 0 / 0 in each of its two arms.
- Every reply the servers finished, as `token_sha` from the server's `done` lines: the same multiset of 75 hashes in all four arms (the scenario, `bench_openai`, `bench_concurrent` and `prefill_cold`).

**Decode speed.** `bench_openai.py`, decode tok/s (median of 5) per arm; the change compares the means of the two arms each way:

| prompt, temperature | stock, run 1 | this PR, run 1 | this PR, run 2 | stock, run 2 | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fibonacci-raw, 0.0 | 79.2 | 77.9 | 78.1 | 78.5 | -1.1% |
| fibonacci-raw, 1.0 | 63.8 | 64.3 | 64.3 | 64.5 | +0.2% |
| gpu-chat-no-think, 0.0 | 54.0 | 54.1 | 54.1 | 54.2 | +0.0% |
| gpu-chat-no-think, 1.0 | 49.5 | 50.0 | 52.2 | 52.5 | +0.2% |

`bench_concurrent` aggregate tok/s per arm (same order):

| prompt, temperature, streams | stock, run 1 | this PR, run 1 | this PR, run 2 | stock, run 2 | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| code, 0.0, 1 | 89.5 | 89.4 | 89.4 | 89.6 | -0.2% |
| code, 0.0, 2 | 151.1 | 151.7 | 151.5 | 151.2 | +0.3% |
| chat, 0.0, 1 | 56.5 | 56.6 | 56.6 | 56.8 | -0.1% |
| chat, 0.0, 2 | 95.9 | 95.8 | 96.1 | 96.6 | -0.3% |
| code, 1.0, 1 | 87.8 | 87.9 | 87.8 | 88.2 | -0.2% |
| code, 1.0, 2 | 88.0 | 104.5 | 104.3 | 105.2 | +8.1% |
| chat, 1.0, 1 | 53.0 | 53.6 | 53.6 | 53.8 | +0.4% |
| chat, 1.0, 2 | 73.0 | 71.7 | 73.9 | 74.0 | -1.0% |

Sampled code at two streams was 88.0 in the first stock arm and 104.3-105.2 in the other three, so that +8.1% is a slow first arm, not this PR. No decode path changes: these prompts have no system block, so they get no checkpoint. The -1.1% `bench_openai` row is the same greedy decode that `bench_concurrent` measures at -0.2% with one stream.

**Prompt speed.** `prefill_cold.py run` on a trimmed set (2K ×2, 8K ×2, 16K ×1; one 1K warm-up), median TTFT in seconds per arm:

| prompt tokens | stock, run 1 | this PR, run 1 | this PR, run 2 | stock, run 2 | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 2.989 | 3.021 | 2.994 | 3.007 | +0.3% |
| 8,192 | 12.078 | 12.128 | 12.094 | 12.107 | +0.2% |
| 16,382 | 24.530 | 24.624 | 24.552 | 24.524 | +0.2% |

The tool printed every row and length summary, then stopped with an error when it reached the 32K and 64K lengths we had left out of the prompt file. So the numbers come from its printed output.

These prompts are a single user message, so they get no checkpoint. The cold prompt that does is session A above (the first 13.3K block in each arm): 18.826 / 18.763 s on stock and 18.699 / 18.714 s with this PR (-0.5%).

**Tests.**
- New: `tests/test_cuda_sys_checkpoint.py` (host, 4 tests: where the checkpoint falls, off by default in `snapshot_points`, the environment variable, and a block with a new tail resuming from it on a fork through `prefixes.slot_for`), and `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_sys_checkpoint.py` (GPU, 4 cases: greedy and sampled, bf16 and int8). In the GPU test, a block with a new tail resumes at the checkpoint, its reply equals a fresh prefill's, and the first block still resumes at its own end. With no granule there is no checkpoint and the replies are the same.
- Before the change: on stock v0.6.5 code and extensions, the new tests fail 8 / 8 (`snapshot_points() got an unexpected keyword argument 'checkpoint'`). After: 8 / 8 pass (4 GPU, 4 host).
- Existing CUDA tests on the PR (`test_flashnext_prompt_cache.py`, `test_flashnext_fork_lanes.py`, `test_flashnext_multi.py`): 92 passed.
- Host tests `tests/test_cuda_*.py` and `tests/test_flashnext_*.py`: 1309 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed on the PR, against 1305 / 9 / 0 on stock (the difference is the 4 new tests).

**What we did not run.**
- Metal, the MLX checkpoints, two ranks, and the other CUDA families. Only Flash Next turns the checkpoint on. The other families call `snapshot_points` without a granule, so their points are unchanged.
- `--parallel 1` (the serial engine). It reads the same points, so it keeps the checkpoint too, within its own `KEEP_SERIAL`. We haven't measured it.
- The full host suite. We ran the CUDA and Flash Next host tests above.
- `prefill_cold` at 32K and 64K, to fit one 30-minute window.
- A client whose block changes before the checkpoint (12,288 here). It resumes from nothing, as it does today.
- A checkpoint granule other than 2048 on the real model.

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code).

items.title: fix(flash next cuda): a lone stream keeps its graphs once kept prompt ends fill every slot (#317)
items.body:
Fixes #317, as @Arminova diagnosed it there: on 0.6.4 and 0.6.5, once `--parallel N` has kept a prompt end in every slot, each new lone request moves the graphs to its own slot and captures its decode windows again.

Four commits on v0.6.4 (they apply to v0.6.5 unchanged; `multi.py` and `multi_solo.py` are the same in both). Each stands on its own:
1. **A fresh prompt takes the idle graph slot.** When the graph slot is idle and holds kept ends, they move to a spare with 0.6.4's `_relocate_kept` (the slot the prompt was given, when no other is free), and the prompt decodes in the graph slot, whose rows and graphs stay. No kept end is evicted. Two ranks keep their planned path.
2. **Each slot keeps the graphs captured over it until it is resized.** Where the graphs still move to a stream's own slot (a resumed turn whose kept end lives elsewhere, with no spare), the slot they leave keeps its set, and a slot that held one takes it back. `_state_changed` drops a slot's set before any resize, including `_relocate_kept`'s spare.
3. **Tests**, which fail on 0.6.4 and pass with the commits:
   - `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_lone_slot.py`: eight different prompts on 5 slots capture exactly what 1 slot does, request by request, with the same tokens as the single-sequence engine (bf16 and int8). A warmed graph slot captures nothing for new prompts on a full pool. Two conversations taking turns make no new graph set after each one's slot has held the graphs once. The no-room fallback (commit 4).
   - `tests/test_flashnext_lone_slot.py`: the same slot logic on the host with stand-in slots, no GPU.
4. **Separable:** when the graph slot can't grow to a lone stream's cache (no room for the copy's peak), `_move_to_solo` raised "the lone stream's graph slot cannot hold its existing cache" and the round failed. On one GPU the graphs now go to the stream's slot instead, as they already do when a kept end holds the graph slot. Two ranks keep the error. Happy to split this into its own PR.

Arminova's proposed fix (evict the oldest kept end) fails 0.6.4's `test_packed_passes_keep_each_prompt_one_token_early`, as we noted on #317. This version evicts nothing.

One thing it doesn't change: `_relocate_kept` (and commit 1, which calls it) resizes the spare to the graph slot's whole capacity and copies all of it. A graph slot that grew with one long conversation therefore grows every spare that takes its kept ends. We run a fix that copies only the kept rows. It's a separate change.

**Environment.**
- One DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), driver 580.178.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.0.
- `turboderp/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-exl3` `4.05bpw_h6_ng6` at revision `55a732e`, with its stock MTP head. No local patches and no `TF_*` variables in any arm.
- Builds: stock v0.6.4 (`6ea5ade`) against v0.6.4 plus this PR (`227b97e`, `32f3af1`, `292e38d`, `65bf4dd`). Outside the tests, only `multi.py` and `multi_solo.py` change.
- Server: `tensorfold serve <ckpt> --parallel 5 --context 262144 --kv-dtype int8`, plus `--parallel 1` as the control. That is @Arminova's command without `--ple-on-ssd`, which 0.6.4 refuses for an EXL3 pack, and without `--thinking`. Each arm booted with the n-gram file's page cache dropped.
- Counting: as in @Arminova's run, a wrapper counts `Graphs()` sets, `Graphs._capture`, `_state_changed` on the graph slot and `_move_to_solo`. It loads before `tensorfold serve` and leaves the engine unchanged. Every arm ran through it.
- Requests: @Arminova's shape, eight different short prompts one after another, 128 tokens, greedy, thinking off, `ignore_eos`. Then the same eight again (pass 2), which resumes the kept prompt ends that are still there.

**Exactness.**
- Per build, `--parallel 5` against `--parallel 1`: the same `token_sha` and the same rounds, request by request. Stock: 16/16 in both stock arms. With the fix: 16/16 in both fix arms.
- Across builds, all 96 eight-prompt requests (6 arms, 2 passes of 8) carry the same `token_sha`: yes.
- `bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial` (levels 1, 2 and 4, 128 tokens, 2 reps, `--parallel 5`):
  - with the fix: concurrent against alone 56 / 0 / 0 equal / unequal / failed; alone against `"draft": false` 30 / 0 / 0;
  - stock: 56 / 0 / 0 and 30 / 0 / 0.

**Decode speed.** `--parallel 5`, decode seconds per request (first token to last) and the graphs captured in that request. Pass 1 is the run in alternated order: stock, fix, fix, stock.

| request | stock `--parallel 1` | stock `--parallel 5` | captured | fix `--parallel 5` | captured | fix `--parallel 1` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1-5 | 10.16 | 10.29 | 0 | 10.24 | 0 | 10.29 |
| 6 | 2.00 | 3.98 | 18 | 2.03 | 0 | 1.99 |
| 7 | 1.97 | 3.93 | 18 | 2.00 | 0 | 1.96 |
| 8 | 2.03 | 4.04 | 19 | 2.07 | 0 | 2.04 |

- Requests 6-8 in total, `--parallel 5`: stock 11.95 and 11.88 s (first and second stock arm), fix 6.09 and 5.99 s. `--parallel 1`: 6.00 s stock, 5.99 s fix.
- Graph sets made after startup, pass 1: stock 3, fix 0 (each arm). Graph slot moves: stock 3, fix 0 (the fix moves the slot's kept end instead, 7 times).
- Pass 2 (the same eight prompts again; requests whose kept end survived resume it): captures stock 143 and 143, fix 0 and 0; graph slot moves stock 8, fix 0. Decode for all eight: stock 31.64 and 30.43 s, fix 16.33 s, `--parallel 1` 16.04 s (stock) and 16.44 s (fix).
- `bench_openai.py` (default: 64 tokens, T 1 and T 0, 5 reps), median tok/s, in order stock / fix / fix / stock:
  - fibonacci T 1: 61.0 / 73.0 / 73.8 / 64.6
  - chat T 1: 48.6 / 51.5 / 52.9 / 49.9
  - fibonacci T 0: 78.7 / 78.4 / 79.9 / 80.2
  - chat T 0: 54.0 / 53.5 / 54.8 / 54.9

**Prompt speed.** `prefill_cold.py`, median TTFT, stock / fix, one run each, not alternated: 2K 3.03 / 3.12 s, 8K 12.43 / 12.38 s, 16K 25.17 / 24.93 s, 32K 50.21 / 50.30 s, 64K 99.21 / 100.80 s. To fit the window we ran a trimmed set: three prompts at 2K and 8K, one each at 16K, 32K and 64K. The change selects slots and graph sets. It doesn't touch prefill.

**Tests.** On GB10:
- New `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_lone_slot.py`: 6 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped with the fix. On stock 0.6.4 the same file gives 0 / 6 / 0. It fails from the sixth prompt, which is @Arminova's request 6. It covers:
  - eight different prompts on 5 slots capture exactly what 1 slot does, request by request, with the same tokens (bf16 and int8);
  - a warmed graph slot captures nothing for new prompts on a full pool;
  - two conversations taking turns make no new graph set after each one's slot has held the graphs once;
  - the no-room fallback.
- New `tests/test_flashnext_lone_slot.py` (host, stand-in slots, no GPU): 4 passed with the fix, 4 failed on stock.
- `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_multi.py` and `test_flashnext_graph_capacity.py` with the fix: 30 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.

**About the "3 extra captures" in our #317 comment.** The test counted from the start of turn 1. That turn is the first time the first conversation's own slot takes the graphs, so it captures its set once: 3 graphs on the synthetic model, which is all the graph slot had captured over 10 requests. That was the whole difference (`6 == 3`). We traced the slot logic on the CPU, with stand-in slots and a stand-in `Graphs`:
- After that first capture, no turn makes a new set through 12 turns, for 3 to 5 slots and `keep` 4 or 8.
- On stock 0.6.4 the same trace makes a new set on every request once the pool is full.
- The CUDA test above therefore counts from turn 2.

**What we did not run.**
- The MLX 4-bit checkpoint and `--ple-on-ssd` (EXL3 only here). Metal.
- Two ranks. The fix acts on one GPU only, and two ranks keep 0.6.4's planned path.
- The memory the kept graph sets take: we only recorded MemAvailable, lowest 14.3 GiB with the fix and 14.4 GiB on stock. Each set has its own graph pool, so with `--parallel N` at most N sets are kept.
- The full `prefill_cold` set: 1 rep, not 3, at 16K, 32K and 64K.
- Your 256- and 1,024-token lengths.
- The full host suite with these commits. We ran the new host file above. Outside the tests, the commits change only `multi.py` and `multi_solo.py`, which the host suite does not import without CUDA.

Thanks to @Arminova for the diagnosis and the eight-prompt protocol.

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code).

items.title: Flash Next on CUDA: copy drafts where a reply repeats earlier text
items.body:
## What

Copy drafts for Flash Next on CUDA. When a stream's last 8 tokens occur earlier in its prompt or reply, the round drafts that text's continuation whole, up to the depth, instead of asking the MTP head. The verify step is unchanged, so every reply equals one-token decoding. Nemotron already does this (`nemotron_h/cuda/decode.py: CopyIndex`); this is the same index, in its own module for the family, wired into the four places Flash Next drafts: the serial MTP loop (`decode.py: mtp_decode`), the shared rounds (`multi.py: _draft_all`), the lone stream's graph slot (`multi_solo.py: _solo_round`) and the first drafts after a prompt (`multi_fill.py: _joined`). The kept rows still go into the MTP cache, so the head resumes cleanly on the next round that needs it.

Two ranks: both hold the same tokens (sampling is gathered), so both build the same index and propose the same chain, and the round plan digest (`multi_tp.shape`) already covers each stream's drafts. In the shared rounds the first chain level's picks still cover every absorbed stream, because the two-rank gather reads them in order; a copying stream's pick is dropped and it joins no later level.

On by default with MTP drafts; `TENSORFOLD_COPY_DRAFTS=0` turns it off. Off without MTP drafts and for grammar-constrained replies. A 250k-token prompt indexes in 0.12 s at admission; a chain lookup is microseconds.

I read #286: the Python engine is frozen and new work goes to the Zig engine. Flash Next is not on CUDA there yet, so this is offered as the reference implementation and the measurements for when it is; rewrite it however fits. #444 describes a prompt-lookup drafter for this family on EXL3 with the same conclusion (copy-heavy replies gain, fresh text does not); this one reuses Nemotron's index and runs on two ranks.

## Receipt

**Environment.** TensorFold `cb2ebf0` (v0.6.6 = `main`) plus this branch, inside `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3` (PyTorch 2.13.0a0, CUDA 13.3 forward-compat on kernel driver 580.178.04). Two NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB) at `--tp 2 --parallel 16`, `--kv-dtype int8`, `--mtp-drafts 15 --mtp-confidence 0.70`, context 262144, NCCL over one RoCE HCA. Checkpoint `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP` at `2b170fa6309d5d1ee380b35636075fac7945f286`. "Before" is the same image and session with `TENSORFOLD_COPY_DRAFTS=0`.

**Exactness.** `tools/bench_concurrent.py ... --levels 1,4 --tokens 512 --alone --serial`, before and after: every concurrent reply equal to its solo run (alone 1/1 and 4/4 in all cells) and every solo run equal to `"draft": false` (serial 1/1 in all cells). Five one-stream requests sent twice, the second with `"draft": false`, token_sha equal in all five, before and after (table below).

**Decode speed**, `tools/bench_openai.py --reps 2 --temperatures 0`:

| prompt | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| fibonacci-raw | 91.9 tok/s | 92.9 tok/s |
| gpu-chat-no-think | 96.5 | 97.3 |

`tools/bench_concurrent.py`, aggregate tok/s: code 1 user 108.4 -> 103.7, 4 users 323.5 -> 320.7; chat 1 user 89.1 -> 87.9, 4 users 277.6 -> 273.2 (within this pair's run-to-run noise; those prompts repeat nothing).

The cells the change is for, one stream, greedy, 900-token replies, `tensorfold.decode_s` and `rounds` from the reply:

| cell | before | after | tokens per round | `"draft": false` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| copy a 3 kB passage verbatim | 127.8 | **337.1** | 6.3 -> 15.5 | 47.7 |
| fix typos in the passage | 129.5 | **321.7** | 6.0 -> 15.5 | 47.3 |
| rename a variable across a 3 kB file | 129.3 | **288.6** | 6.4 -> 13.9 | 47.7 |
| fresh prose (500-word essay) | 70.6 | 71.5 | 2.1 | 48.3 |
| fresh code (module plus tests) | 127.1 | 124.7 | 5.7 | 47.5 |

**Prompt speed**, `tools/prefill_cold.py` (2k to 64k cold prompts, 3 reps each), copy drafts off, on, and on again in the same session:

| prompt tokens | before: TTFT, prompt tok/s | after | after again |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 0.85 s, 2,400 | 0.85 s, 2,398 | 0.86 s, 2,377 |
| 8,192 | 3.25 s, 2,517 | 3.27 s, 2,502 | 3.28 s, 2,499 |
| 16,383 | 6.51 s, 2,518 | 6.54 s, 2,505 | 6.54 s, 2,504 |
| 32,768 | 13.21 s, 2,480 | 13.29 s, 2,465 | 13.45 s, 2,436 |
| 65,536 | 27.42 s, 2,390 | 27.55 s, 2,379 | 27.66 s, 2,370 |

Within the pair's noise at every length (the index is built after the prompt's first token is sampled: 0.12 s for 250k tokens on the host, 1 ms at 2k).

**Tests.** `tests/test_copy_drafts.py` (6, new; fails before the change with `ModuleNotFoundError` on the new module) and the full upstream suite inside the image on the CPU: this branch 4096 passed, 127 failed, 11 errors, 175 skipped; pristine `main` in the same container 4090 passed, 127 failed, 11 errors, 175 skipped, and the failure and error sets are identical (MLX-only tests and Triton kernel tests that cannot run on the CPU, such as `test_affine_rows.py` and `test_exact_sampling.py`). The six extra passes are `tests/test_copy_drafts.py`. The first push had one extra failure, `test_cuda_ignore_eos_engines.py::test_every_path_takes_stop_eos[True-False-flashnext]`: that test builds the engine without `__init__`, so the new attribute was missing; the reads are now `getattr` with a False default, as the surrounding code does for optional attributes.

**Not run.** Metal: no Mac here, and the change is CUDA-only (`families/qwen4_exp/cuda`). One GPU (`--tp 1`) and the EXL3 and NVFP4 formats on one GPU: not served on this pair; the code paths are the same four draft sites. `--parallel 1` at `--tp 2` (the serial engine on two ranks) was served earlier the same night on the previous image for the serial-against-concurrent comparison, but the `"draft": false` check above ran on the concurrent profile only.

items.title: Flash Next on CUDA: image and video input on two ranks, concurrent and serial engines
items.body:
## What

Image and video input for Flash Next on CUDA on two ranks. Today the engine serves images on one GPU with `--parallel 2` or more and refuses `--vision` at `--tp 2`. Both ranks must feed identical hidden states into their halves of every layer; text does that by embedding the same ids, images only if both ranks hold the same features. So rank 0 runs the tower once per request and sends the result to rank 1 instead of rank 1 recomputing it:

- `engine.py`: the gate becomes "`--parallel 2` or more", on one GPU or two ranks. The tower loads on rank 0 only (`capacity_geometry` and `weight_transform` already took the rank, so rank 1 reserves 128 MiB and no weights); rank 1 prints that it attaches what rank 0 encodes. `--vision` joins the settings both ranks must share at startup (`_same_settings`).
- `multi.py: admit`: on two ranks, rank 0 encodes the request's images before the admission message, so an image the tower refuses fails on rank 0 alone and no message reaches rank 1. A request admitted again after waiting for memory keeps the features it already has.
- `multi_tp.py`: the admission message and its digest carry the image rows, the decode offset and the feature shape. After the plan agreed and both ranks' memory checks passed, `_share_vision` sends rank 0's bf16 feature rows and int32 rotary positions to rank 1 point to point (`comm.exchange`), inside the admission lockstep and before any round collective; both ranks reach it or neither does. `shape()` includes whether a slot holds image positions. An older leader's nine-field message still parses (no image).
- `multi_plan.py`: an image prompt reuses no kept prefix, keeps no prompt states and never takes the lone-stream graph slot, as on one GPU (`Shadow.images`).
- `image_rows.py`: `begin` attaches features another rank encoded; a prepared prompt still needs the tower.

Nothing changes in the prompt passes, the rotary kernel or the rounds: `image_rows.embed` and `attn_multi` read each rank's own copy of identical data. Video frames are image rows to the engine, so `video_url` parts work the same way when PyAV is installed. Image prompts on two ranks keep the one-GPU limits: no prefix reuse, no grammars or logprobs. Size: at most the request's visual-token budget x 2560 x 2 bytes (80 MB at 16,384 tokens) plus 12 bytes a prompt token, a few milliseconds on a RoCE link.

Rank 0 gives up the tower (0.84 GiB) and its 4 GiB encode workspace (`TENSORFOLD_VISION_WORKSPACE_MIB`) from stream-cache room: 53.4 GiB free for caches on rank 0 against 58.0 on rank 1 at `--parallel 16 --kv-dtype int8` on this pair, two streams at the full window.

I read #286: the Python engine is frozen and new work goes to the Zig engine. Flash Next is not on CUDA there yet, so this is offered as the reference and the measurements for when it is, like #468 (independent of it: this branch is `main` plus this one commit).

## Receipt

**Environment.** TensorFold `cb2ebf0` (v0.6.6 = `main`) plus this branch, inside `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3` (PyTorch 2.13.0a0, CUDA 13.3 forward-compat on kernel driver 580.178.04, transformers 5.18.0, PyAV 19.0.1 added for video). Two NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB) at `--tp 2 --parallel 16 --vision`, `--kv-dtype int8`, `--mtp-drafts 15 --mtp-confidence 0.70`, context 262144, NCCL over one RoCE HCA. Checkpoint `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP` at `2b170fa6309d5d1ee380b35636075fac7945f286` (it carries the 27-layer vision tower). "Before" is the same image and host session started without `--vision` (main refuses the flag at `--tp 2`, so the before cells are text only).

**Correctness.** Greedy, thinking off, three probes with known answers:

| input | prompt tokens | reply |
|---|---:|---|
| drawn PNG, a red circle left and a blue square right: "which shapes, what colour" | 150 | "The image contains a red circle and a blue square." |
| 3840 x 2160 photo (a lake under clouds with two posts): "describe in one sentence" | 4,101 | "A serene, mirror-like lake reflects a soft, cloudy sky, with two weathered, rust-stained posts rising from the water's surface, their forms echoed perfectly below." |
| 4 s 320 x 240 video (a green frame turning red, a white square moving right): "what happens" | 373 | "The video starts with a green screen, which then changes to a red screen." |

**Exactness**, by `tensorfold.token_sha`, 160-token replies, four image prompts (the PNG and three questions on the photo):

| cell | result |
|---|---|
| drafted against the same request with `"draft": false` | 4 of 4 equal |
| four image requests sent together against each sent alone | 4 of 4 equal |
| a text request sent beside the four image requests against alone | equal |

Startup lines, rank 0 and rank 1:

```
[tensorfold] vision: image and video input, a 0.84 GiB tower with 4.00 GiB of workspace reserved; rank 1 receives each request's image features from this rank
[tensorfold] vision: image input on two ranks; this rank attaches the features rank 0 encodes
```

**Decode speed**, text, same host session, `--vision` off then on (`tools/bench_openai.py --reps 2 --temperatures 0`):

| prompt | `--vision` off | `--vision` on |
|---|---:|---:|
| fibonacci-raw | 92.4 tok/s | 89.3 tok/s |
| gpu-chat-no-think | 95.2 | 94.4 |

Frozen ruler (`bench_decode.py`, prose and structured, one stream, 3-run median):

| phase | `--vision` off | `--vision` on |
|---|---:|---:|
| prose (ends at EOS near 100 tokens) | 66.2 tok/s, TTFT 0.058 s | 65.2 tok/s, TTFT 0.057 s |
| structured (200 tokens) | 231.3 | 232.0 |

Within this pair's run-to-run band (the two fibonacci reps were 90.4 / 88.8 against 93.3 / 92.5 earlier in the day on the same image without `--vision`; the other three cells move under 1.5% either way). Text rounds take no vision code path: `attn_multi` sees no image positions and `image_rows.embed` finds no features.

Image requests, one stream: the PNG prompt decodes at 84 tok/s (160 tokens, prompt pass 0.09 s); the 4,101-token photo prompt passes in 3.2 s where 4,124 text tokens take 1.7 s (the tower's share about 1.5 s) and decodes at 70 tok/s. Four 4k-token image requests arriving together finish in 12-14 s each against 2-6 s alone: their prompt passes run one after another with `--decode-share 0`, as text prompts of that size do.

**Prompt speed**, `tools/prefill_cold.py` (2k to 64k cold text prompts, 3 reps), `--vision` off then on in the same session:

| prompt tokens | `--vision` off: TTFT, tok/s | `--vision` on: TTFT, tok/s |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 0.850 s, 2,411 | 0.853 s, 2,401 |
| 8,192 | 3.260 s, 2,513 | 3.259 s, 2,514 |
| 16,383 | 6.569 s, 2,494 | 6.503 s, 2,519 |
| 32,768 | 13.283 s, 2,467 | 13.240 s, 2,475 |
| 65,536 | 27.647 s, 2,371 | 27.517 s, 2,382 |

**Tests.** Inside the image on the CPU: `tests/test_flashnext_vision_two_ranks_host.py` (5 tests: the admission message and digest with and without images, both ranks share the tensors or neither does and they fall out of step; `begin` without a tower; image prompts off prefix reuse, prompt states and the graph slot). All five fail on `main` and pass here. The full suite in the same container: this branch 4095 passed / 127 failed / 11 errors / 175 skipped; pristine `cb2ebf0` 4090 / 127 / 11 / 175, the same 138 failing tests in both (Metal, MLX and network-bound tests on a Linux box without them). The vision, concurrent-decoder and two-rank planning tests (`test_vision_cuda.py`, `test_cuda_batch_admit.py`, `test_cuda_growing_caches.py`, `test_flashnext_round_plan.py`, `test_flash_next_tp_readiness_host.py`, `test_flashnext_absolute_grow_host.py`): 78 passed.

## Second commit: image prompts on the serial engine too

The `--parallel 2` gate on `--vision` goes. Its reason was the serial engine's CUDA graphs: a capture bakes in the rotary mode, and the captured graphs know no image positions. `prefill()` already took an image payload (it attaches the rows and refuses prefix resume for them); nothing called it. Now `Engine.forward` and `mtp_forward` run eagerly while the state holds image positions, text states keep their graphs; `generate()` encodes on rank 0 before the request is shared, `_share`/`_unpack` carry the image description (an older leader's message still parses), `follow()` receives the features on rank 1, `_decode` prefills an image prompt from its start and keeps no snapshot, `_serial` takes the payload for `"draft": false`. The two-rank transfer moved to `vision_ranks.py` (`describe`, `exchange`), shared by the concurrent decoder and the serial engine; both ranks validate the same description.

An image request on the serial engine decodes at the eager rate, text keeps the serial rate, and the image request's fresh prefill overwrites the engine's kept text states.

**Receipt, serial engine** (`--tp 2`, no `--parallel`, same checkpoint and settings as above; `--vision` off then on in the same host session):

| cell | `--vision` off | `--vision` on |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tools/bench_openai.py --reps 2 --temperatures 0`, fibonacci-raw / gpu-chat-no-think | 101.6 / 101.6 tok/s | 100.7 / 99.2 tok/s |
| frozen prose / structured ruler, one stream, 3-run median | 72.3 / 250.2 | 72.1 / 239.0 |
| `tools/prefill_cold.py`, 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,383 / 32,768 / 65,536 cold prompt tokens | 2,413 / 2,522 / 2,534 / 2,479 / 2,400 tok/s | 2,420 / 2,545 / 2,550 / 2,509 / 2,404 tok/s |

Image prompts on the serial engine, greedy: the three probes above give the same replies and the same reply token shas as on the concurrent decoder (`a7588cf7f668`, `e99c86a30d35`, `333c343e9195`); the 4,101-token photo prompt passes in 1.64 s. Drafted against `"draft": false`: 4 of 4 equal. A 200-token text reply before and after an image request: same sha, 73.4 then 72.4 tok/s over 106 rounds, so the graphs come back after the eager image rounds; the image reply itself ran at 99 tok/s (its answer repeats the question's words). Both ranks' startup lines are as above; rank 1 attaches what rank 0 encodes.

**Tests.** Three more in `tests/test_flashnext_vision_two_ranks_host.py`: the serial request message with and without images, `describe`/`exchange` validation (and the point-to-point call on rank 0), the eager rounds and fresh prefill for an image state. They fail on `main` and pass here. Full suite in the same container: this branch 127 failed, 4114 passed, 175 skipped, 11 errors; pristine `cb2ebf0` 127 failed, 4090 passed, 175 skipped, 11 errors, the same 138 failing tests in both.

items.title: glm5_q8_0_gguf_to_mlx: carry the MTP draft head (--mtp-from, --mtp-only)
items.body:
The Q8_0 GGUF has no MTP layer, so the lossless 8-bit conversion decodes without drafts. This adds an option to the
converter that takes the MTP layer (index `num_hidden_layers`) from the original zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint and
writes it next to the converted weights, so the Mac engine drafts with it. A second mode adds the head to a
conversion you already have, without reading the 310 GiB GGUF again.

**What changes**
- `tools/glm5_q8_0_gguf_to_mlx.py`
  - `--mtp-from DIR` takes the original checkpoint's folder. Its tensors are located through
    `model.safetensors.index.json`, with no shard names hard-coded. Only the shards that hold the layer are opened,
    memory-mapped, numpy only.
  - **FP8 linears** (`q_a/q_b/kv_a_proj_with_mqa/o_proj`, shared and routed experts) are decoded as e4m3 times the
    `weight_scale_inv` of their 128×128 block, in float32. Partial edge blocks are handled. NaN codes, non-finite
    values and scale grids of the wrong shape are refused.
  - **Re-encoding:** those linears and the bf16 `kv_b_proj` are re-encoded as MLX affine 8-bit in groups of 32. That
    is the format the config already states for the conversion, so no per-tensor entries are needed. Rounding is to
    nearest, with scale = (max − min)/255 and bias = min per group. Scales and biases are float32, so every value
    lies within half a step.
  - **Routed experts** are stacked as `mlp.switch_mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj` [n_routed_experts, out, in]. The expert
    count comes from the config.
  - **Kept as stored:** `eh_proj`, the indexer projections and norms, the router and its bias, and all other norms
    keep their stored bytes and dtype (bf16 stays bf16, f32 stays f32). The loader already reads these unquantised.
  - **Shards:** the head goes into shards of its own, `model-mtp-NNNNN.safetensors`.
  - **Full conversion with `--mtp-from`:**
    - The whole head is decoded and encoded before the GGUF is read, so a bad source fails in seconds, not after
      the conversion.
    - The conversion is then finished as before (index, config, tokenizer, `SHA256SUMS`), and the head is added
      to it the way `--mtp-only` adds it.
    - If writing the head still fails (disk, memory), the conversion without a head is left complete, and
      `--mtp-only` can add the head later.
  - **`--mtp-only --mtp-from DIR --out EXISTING`** adds the head to an earlier conversion:
    - It writes the head's shards first, then the new index and `SHA256SUMS` as `.part` files, then renames both
      into place.
    - On any failure, including one between the two renames, the old index and `SHA256SUMS` are restored and the
      head's shards and `.part` files are removed.
    - No existing shard is opened for writing.
    - It refuses: a checkpoint that already has a head (unless `--replace-mtp`, and only when that head sits in
      shards of its own); a config that does not state 8-bit groups of 32; a folder that is not a finished
      conversion; a symbolic link at any `.part` path it would write; and the GGUF arguments, which it does not
      read.
    - A conversion without `SHA256SUMS` gets none (a note is printed), rather than a partial one.
  - `--verify` also checks the head against the original:
    - kept tensors for equality;
    - re-encoded values within their group's half step, on all rows of the attention and shared-expert linears and
      on four sampled routed experts per projection.
  - **Exit status** is now 0 or 1, not the number of mismatches, which could wrap to 0 at 256.
  - **Without `--mtp-from` the output is byte-identical to before.** The edits on that path are:
    - `Writer`'s shard stem (default `model`) and a refusal of a symbolic link at a `.part` path;
    - an index writer that writes the same bytes;
    - `main(argv)`;
    - `--gguf/--config/--tokenizer-dir` are now checked by hand, because `--mtp-only` does not take them;
    - the exit status above.
- `docs/recipes/glm-5.3-flash.md`
  - How to add the head, during conversion or afterwards, and what happens on a failure.
  - The head is re-encoded, not lossless. That changes only how many drafts are accepted: drafts are verified
    against the model, so replies equal `"draft": false`.
  - It adds about 8.7 GiB, and the measured time and memory of `--mtp-only`.
- No loader change. The engine already reads an 8-bit / 32 MLA + MoE head with bf16 `eh_proj` and indexer, and the
  new test loads one through `load_backbone` and `mtp.load`.
- The tool stays one module (606 lines). If you prefer, `--mtp-only` could move to a `tools/glm5_mtp_graft.py`
  that the converter imports; I kept it here so both modes share one path that writes the head.

**Checks**
- New `tests/test_glm5_q8_0_mtp.py` (21 tests, CPU, synthetic fixtures only). All fail or error before this change
  and pass after.
  - **Units:**
    - The e4m3 table equals `mx.from_fp8` on all 256 codes (NaN at 0x7f / 0xff only).
    - Block scales on a 200×300 weight, with partial edge blocks in both directions, equal `mx.from_fp8` times the
      scale grid. Wrong scale-grid shapes, NaN codes and overflow are refused.
    - The 8-bit encoding is within half a step per group, through `mx.dequantize`. Constant, wide, tiny and offset
      groups are covered, and non-finite input is refused.
  - **End to end, fixtures:**
    - The fake model is built at hidden size 256, so each FP8 linear of the head spans two 128×128 blocks along
      one axis.
    - A tiny `glm5next` Q8_0 GGUF is written from it.
    - A tiny original checkpoint holds the layer: FP8 with block scales, `kv_b_proj` and the rest bf16, the router
      f32, over two shards found through the index.
  - **End to end, results:**
    - The grafted conversion passes `--verify`.
    - Every head value is within the bound of the float32 reference, and every kept tensor is byte-equal.
    - `glm5_next.check` and `has_mtp` accept it, `load_backbone` + `mtp.load` read it, and `multi_row_exact` holds.
      Drafted output equals `drafts=0` output.
    - **The head computes the source model's head:** on the same rows and tokens, the median row's logits differ
      from the fake checkpoint's own head by about 0.05 (relative; this is the FP8 round trip). The test asserts
      < 0.15. Reversing the expert stack gives about 0.65–0.79, so a head in the wrong order or orientation fails.
  - **No option, no change:** every file of a conversion without `--mtp-from` is byte-identical to the same file of
    one with it. The index and `SHA256SUMS` only gain the head's entries.
  - **`--mtp-only`:**
    - It leaves every existing file byte-identical and produces exactly the files a graft at conversion time does.
    - It refuses a second head and replaces it with `--replace-mtp`. It refuses a 4-bit config.
    - A failure injected between the two renames leaves the folder byte-identical to before.
    - A symbolic link at a shard's or at `SHA256SUMS`'s `.part` path is refused, and its target is untouched.
    - Wrong argument combinations exit with status 2, and a folder that is not a finished conversion is refused.
  - **Full mode:**
    - A head failure injected after the check leaves exactly the plain conversion, which `--mtp-only` then turns
      into exactly the grafted one.
    - A bad source is refused before the output folder is created.
  - **Refusals:** a missing norm, a missing expert, a missing `weight_scale_inv`, an unmapped tensor, a NaN code, a
    wrong scale-grid shape and an expert of the wrong shape. Each is refused in both modes, and `--mtp-only` leaves
    the folder unchanged.
- Byte identity against v0.6.5's converter: I ran v0.6.5's `tools/glm5_q8_0_gguf_to_mlx.py` and this branch's on the
  same synthetic GGUF without the option. All five output files have equal sha256.
- Full suite (`python -m pytest -q tests`) on an Apple Silicon Mac, Python 3.14.7, MLX 0.32.3, numpy 2.5.3:
  v0.6.5 (609ca41) **4,668 passed, 929 skipped, 0 failed**; this branch **4,689 passed, 929 skipped, 0 failed** (the 21 new tests).

## Receipt (M3 Ultra, real weights)

**Environment.**
- TensorFold v0.6.5 (609ca41) plus this branch (7155bae), MLX 0.32.3, mlx-lm 0.32.0, Python 3.14.7.
- Mac Studio M3 Ultra, 512 GB.
- Checkpoint: the 8-bit group-32 conversion of the GLM-5.3-Flash Q8_0 GGUF (DevQuasar, 26 shards), with `tensorfold_activation_dtype: float32`.
- Head source: zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash eb9eb208 (shards 1–2 and `model.safetensors.index.json`).
- Server: `tensorfold serve … --context 70000 --parallel 1 --prompt-cache-gib 0 --snapshot-dir none --spill-gib 0`.
- "Before" is the same checkpoint without the head, with `--no-drafts`. "After" grafts the head and leaves drafts at their default (up to 3).

**Graft.** `tools/glm5_q8_0_gguf_to_mlx.py --mtp-only --mtp-from <zai-org dir> --out <conversion> --verify`:
- 38 s, 14.5 GB max RSS, 11.7 GB peak footprint (`/usr/bin/time -l`);
- 50 tensors in 3 shards, 8.68 GiB;
- "verified the MTP layer: 37 tensors, 0 mismatches";
- the head shards are byte-identical to an earlier revision of this branch, the one the exactness runs below used.

**Exactness.**
- `bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial` (4 cells, 4 streams, `--parallel 1`): concurrent equal to alone 48/48; alone equal to `"draft": false` 10/10.
- 20 further prompts, greedy, 128 tokens: 12 chat, 2 code, raw text at 512 to 12,800 tokens, and a 12.8k needle. For each:
  - drafted equals serial by `token_sha` and text: 20/20;
  - serial output with the head equals serial output from the same checkpoint without it: 20/20.

**Decode speed** (`bench_openai.py`, 5 reps, median tok/s; runs in the order before, after, after, before):

| prompt, temperature | before-1 | after-1 | after-2 | before-2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fibonacci-raw, 1.0 | 20.9 | 21.7 | 21.9 | 20.9 |
| gpu-chat-no-think, 1.0 | 20.8 | 21.1 | 21.2 | 20.9 |
| fibonacci-raw, 0 | 20.8 | 24.0 | 24.1 | 20.8 |
| gpu-chat-no-think, 0 | 20.9 | 21.0 | 21.1 | 20.9 |

Draft acceptance on the 20 prompts was 74–91 % on chat and code. Measured with those drafts, chat and code decoded 3–19 % faster. Raw text of 8k tokens and up decoded 8–13 % *slower* with drafts (18.3 and 17.3 tok/s against about 20 serial). On this float32-activation path a 2-row verify costs 73 ms against 48 ms for one row (the server's startup line), which limits what each accepted draft buys.

**Prompt speed** (`prefill_cold.py`, median of 3, tok/s; one run each way, not alternated):

| tokens | 1k | 2k | 8k | 16k | 32k | 64k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| before (no head) | 375.7 | 407.4 | 388.2 | 384.1 | 360.1 | 317.6 |
| after (head) | 374.6 | 403.1 | 382.6 | 363.8 | 311.9 | 296.3 |

The loaded head costs prefill time at long prompts: about −5 % at 16k, −13 % at 32k and −7 % at 64k in these single runs. The 32k reps vary by ±5 %. For workloads dominated by long prompts, `--no-drafts`, or leaving the head out, may be the better trade.

**Not run**
- CUDA: the change is a Mac-side conversion tool and touches no engine code.
- bf16 activations with the 8-bit head: all rows above use float32 activations.
- Contexts above 70,000 tokens, and a full GGUF conversion with `--mtp-from`: the real-weight graft used `--mtp-only` on an existing conversion. The full mode is covered by the synthetic tests.

**Notes**
- `--mtp-only` edits the conversion's folder in place: it adds shards and replaces the index and `SHA256SUMS`.

Prepared with the help of Opus 5.5 high.

items.title: perf(flash next cuda): copies from the context before MTP chains, windows growing to 64 rows (a file rewrite 3.7x, same reply)
items.body:
## What this changes

Flash Next on CUDA drafted only MTP chains, so a reply that repeats its prompt, such as an agent rewriting or quoting a file it just read, kept about 5 tokens a round. On one GPU, a round now first verifies a copied continuation when the context repeats eight or more tokens, as Qwen3.6 MoE does, and otherwise the MTP chain. A copy's window starts at 16 rows, doubles while copies land whole (up to 64) and halves after a break, as Nemotron's on M5 (0.6.3) and the 27B's do. A reply that rewrites the file in its prompt decodes **3.7x faster** (92.4 to 341.0 tok/s with one stream, 92.9 to 340.3 with `--parallel 5`) with the same reply: a drafted reply still equals `"draft": false`, which this change doesn't touch, and the replies below are byte-identical to 0.6.4's.

- **Why 16 rows wasn't the limit.** `MAX_DEPTH = 15` caps the MTP setting, not the verify window: a row's bits don't depend on the window's width. The new tests verify copies wider than 16 rows against serial decoding: eager and in CUDA graphs, one stream and three, a lone stream in the `--parallel` graph slot, bf16 and int8 caches, and under a grammar.
- **One stream.** `mtp_decode(prompt=...)` copies or chains (`copies.Copies`, on the 27B's `CopyIndex` and `next_copy_rows`). The engine's buffers and graphs take 64 rows, which its startup estimate already counted (`gdn_geometry`'s indexed rows), so the estimate is unchanged (87.57 GiB at 262,144 tokens). Startup captures 192 decode graphs instead of 21.
- **`--parallel N`.** Every stream keeps its chain's rows (depth + 1). Copies share the rest of a round's max(N x (depth + 1), 64) rows, oldest stream first (`copies.fit`), and each stream keeps its own window. The lone stream's graph slot takes 64 rows, and every slot's replay scratch holds 64 rows, since any slot may become the graph slot. The admission counts these (`indexed_stream_geometry(rows=, scratch=)`).
- **Order in a round.** A round's tokens join each stream's context before its next drafts, so `take` now runs before `_draft_all` (and before the graph slot's drafts). The streams that draft are still chosen by `last`, never by a client's stop, so two ranks draft the same streams.
- **Two ranks** keep MTP chains only, `--parallel` included.
- **Costs.**
  - Memory at `--parallel 5`, 262,144 tokens, int8 cache: the startup estimate goes from 84.91 to 86.81 GiB (its activation bound counts the round's 64 rows and the graph slot's 64). Measured, the memory left for caches goes from 25.3 to 24.6 GiB.
  - A stream with nothing to copy that shares rounds with a wide copy gets longer rounds: in the run below, a 512-token reply went from 12.8 s to 16.6 s, while all three requests together finished in 16.6 s instead of 35.6 s.
  - Plain decode: a copy now and then proposed inside generated code costs about 0.5% (below).

## Receipt

- **Environment:** TensorFold 0.6.4 (`6ea5ade`) and this branch (`93d080e`); PyTorch 2.13.0a0 (NGC 26.07), CUDA 13.3, Triton 3.7.1; one DGX Spark (GB10). Model: [`Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP) (`dadefa8`), served with `--context 262144 --kv-dtype int8 --ple-on-ssd --thinking`: at `--parallel 5`, runs alternated 0.6.4, branch, branch, 0.6.4; at `--parallel 1`, 0.6.4 then branch.
- **Exactness:**
  - `tools/bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial`, every cell on both trees: at `--levels 5` (`--parallel 5`), concurrent against alone 15/15 equal, alone against `"draft": false` 5/5 (sampled) and 1/1 (greedy); at `--levels 1` (`--parallel 1`), 3/3 and 1/1. None unequal, none failed.
  - Each copy-heavy request below sent twice, the second with `"draft": false`: `token_sha` equal in all nine pairs (this branch at `--parallel 5` and `--parallel 1`, and 0.6.4 at `--parallel 5`), and this branch's equal to 0.6.4's (`054057179d32`, `37197544ef24`, `9f34a97796e8`).
- **Decode speed**, `tools/bench_openai.py`, median tok/s:

  | Prompt | T | `--parallel 5` (0.6.4 / branch / branch / 0.6.4) | `--parallel 1` (0.6.4 / branch) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | fibonacci | 1.0 | 73.5 / 72.6 / 73.1 / 72.9 | 72.8 / 56.1 (again: 73.5 / 73.1) |
  | chat | 1.0 | 59.3 / 58.2 / 58.8 / 58.9 | 59.1 / 45.2 (again: 59.4 / 59.1) |
  | fibonacci | 0 | 63.1 / 62.4 / 62.4 / 63.0 | 63.6 / 63.3 |
  | chat | 0 | 59.7 / 59.1 / 59.2 / 59.5 | 60.0 / 59.9 |

  In the branch's `--parallel 1` run, the sampled cells' second to fourth repetitions ran slow (fibonacci 72.9, 53.1, 54.3, 56.1, 64.9). Run again, fresh servers, 0.6.4 then the branch, they did not: fibonacci 73.6, 73.5, 71.2, 72.9, 86.0 against 73.1, 73.4, 71.3, 72.5, 81.5, with one copy proposed in all of those requests. `--parallel 1` never resizes its caches, so I read the slow repetitions as the machine's.

  `tools/bench_concurrent.py`, aggregate tok/s (0.6.4 / branch): 5 streams code 149.0 / 148.6 (T=1), 244.5 / 245.2 (T=0), chat 125.8 / 125.7, 225.5 / 225.0; 1 stream code 86.6 / 86.8, 67.5 / 67.5, chat 59.1 / 59.1, 62.0 / 61.9.

  **Copy-heavy replies.** The prompt holds `src/tensorfold/cuda/streams.py` (187 lines); greedy, thinking off, the prompt cached first; script below. tok/s:

  | Reply | `--parallel 5` (0.6.4 / branch / branch / 0.6.4) | `--parallel 1` (0.6.4 / branch) |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | The file again with a class renamed (2,274 tokens) | 92.9 / 340.3 / 339.7 / 92.5 | 92.4 / 341.0 |
  | OLD then NEW of a class, comments added (1,314 tokens) | 91.3 / 223.9 / 223.4 / 91.2 | 91.3 / 223.6 |
  | A new LRU class, nothing to copy (512 tokens) | 67.3 / 64.6 / 65.1 / 67.4 | 82.0 / 81.7 |
  | All three sent at once (4,100 tokens), seconds | 35.6 / 16.6 / 16.6 / 35.5 | |

  Tokens a round for the rewrite: 5.30 -> 48.36. A round takes 57.0 ms -> 142.2 ms.

  The LRU reply runs after the other two on the same server. At `--parallel 5` its rounds take 61.3 ms on 0.6.4 (50.3 ms with one stream): when the rewrite grows the graph slot's caches, the slot's graphs go (`_state_changed`) and the next request captures the widths it uses again, and the branch's copies add a width or two. On fresh servers, the LRU reply three times each: 0.6.4 82.0, 85.7, 85.2; this branch 81.1, 85.0, 84.5 (3 copies proposed, 15 of their 48 rows kept); this branch with copies off 81.9, 85.4, 85.2.
- **Prompt speed**, `tools/prefill_cold.py`, `--parallel 5`, median TTFT in seconds (0.6.4 / branch / branch / 0.6.4):

  | Prompt | TTFT (s) |
  | --- | --- |
  | 1k | 0.95 / 1.44 / 0.94 / 0.96 |
  | 2k | 1.33 / 1.95 / 1.35 / 1.35 |
  | 8k | 4.17 / 11.29 / 4.28 / 4.17 |
  | 16k | 7.12 / 7.46 / 7.09 / 7.16 |
  | 32k | 13.58 / 13.62 / 13.63 / 13.64 |
  | 64k | 28.29 / 31.88 / 27.65 / 27.48 |

  The change doesn't touch prompt processing. With `--ple-on-ssd` the n-gram rows come from the SSD, and the first branch run's short prompts met slow reads; the second matches 0.6.4 at every length.
- **Tests:**
  - On GB10 (Linux), with the `test` and `tui` extras and xgrammar, `python -m pytest -q tests` with `--continue-on-collection-errors` (`tests/cuda/test_build.py` and `tests/streaming/test_build.py` share a module name, so collection otherwise stops) and `--timeout 600`: this branch 5,243 passed, 268 skipped, 127 failed, 12 errors; 0.6.4 5,236 passed, 268 skipped, and the same 127 failures and 12 errors, none only on either tree. Those tests need MLX here (`No module named 'mlx'`).
  - The Flash Next and CUDA admission tests alone (`tests/cuda/test_flashnext_*.py`, `tests/test_flash*.py`, `tests/test_cuda_*.py`, `tests/cuda/test_logprobs.py`, `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_copy_index.py`, `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_grammar.py`): 1,820 passed, 25 skipped, none failed (0.6.4: 1,813 passed, 25 skipped).
  - On 0.6.4 without the change, the new and updated tests fail: `test_copies_from_the_context_give_serial_tokens`, `test_server_engine_streams_serial_tokens`, `test_streams_copy_from_their_context_within_a_rounds_rows_and_equal_each_alone` (bf16, int8), `test_copies_share_the_rows_chains_leave_oldest_first`, `test_grammar_streams_copy_within_a_rounds_rows_and_equal_serial`, `test_a_lone_stream_copies_in_its_graph_slot_and_equals_serial`, and the Flash Next cases of `test_parallel_window_that_cannot_fit_every_stream_is_refused_before_loading`, `test_flash_parallel_decoder_allocations_are_budgeted` and `test_quantized_caches_admit_longer_windows_on_the_same_budget` (they count the copy rows).
- **Not run, and why:**
  - Metal: the change is in the CUDA engine (`families/qwen4_exp/cuda/`), which Macs don't run.
  - Two ranks: copies stay off there, and I have one Spark.
  - Other GPUs: I have only the GB10.
  - The NVFP4 and EXL3 Flash Next checkpoints through the server: the change is in the drafting and the scheduler, not the weights path.

<details><summary>The copy-heavy requests</summary>

```python
import hashlib, json, urllib.request
BASE, code = "http://127.0.0.1:8888", "".join(open("src/tensorfold/cuda/streams.py").readlines()[:250])
TASKS = [
    ("rewrite", f"Here is a Python file:\n\n```python\n{code}```\n\nRename the class `PrefixCache` to `PromptCache` "
                "everywhere in this file. Output the complete updated file in one code block, nothing else.", 3500),
    ("edit-block", f"Here is a Python file:\n\n```python\n{code}```\n\nAdd a one-line comment above every `return` "
                   "statement in the class `PrefixCache`. Reply with an edit: first OLD, the class exactly as it is now "
                   "(verbatim), then NEW, the whole class with the comments added.", 3500),
    ("code", "Write a Python LRU cache class with comments.", 512),
]
def health(): return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + "/health").read())
def chat(content, n, draft=True):
    body = {"model": "m", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}], "max_tokens": n, "temperature": 0,
            "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}, **({} if draft else {"draft": False})}
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req).read())
for name, prompt, n in TASKS:
    chat(prompt, 1)                                   # the prompt cached first: the timed run is decode
    h0 = health(); o = chat(prompt, n); h1 = health()
    rounds = h1["rounds_total"] - h0["rounds_total"]
    tps = (h1["completion_tokens_total"] - h0["completion_tokens_total"]) / (h1["decode_seconds_total"] - h0["decode_seconds_total"])
    text, ref = o["choices"][0]["message"]["content"], chat(prompt, n, draft=False)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    print(name, hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:10], hashlib.sha256(ref.encode()).hexdigest()[:10],
          f"{tps:.1f} tok/s", f"{(h1['accepted_total'] - h0['accepted_total'] + rounds) / rounds:.2f} tokens a round")
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo.
- [x] No precision traded for speed. The bits don't change (a copy is only proposed; every row is verified as before).
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release.
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: feat(cuda): wire the spill tier into glm5_next serving (#373)
items.body:
Closes #373.

## What was wrong

`--spill-gib` and `--snapshot-dir` were accepted by the CLI but only wired
into the MLX serve path: the CUDA `glm5_next` engine silently ignored them,
so evicted conversations went nowhere and an engine restart dropped every
kept state — a returning 100K-token conversation paid its cold prefill again.

## What this does

- Evicted kept states go to a per-rank disk directory. The ranks decide alike
  (as they already do in memory); each rank writes its own
  `{key}.rank{r}.safetensors`, since a TP2 rank's tensors are its own shards.
- A matching prompt resumes from the longest on-disk strict prefix. Rank 0
  chooses resume lengths exactly as it does for in-memory hits (the header's
  cached length is the contract); rank 1 loads its own file for that length
  from the same key, raising the same error it raises for a missing
  in-memory snapshot.
- A clean shutdown spills what eviction has not. Rank 0 rings rank 1 with a
  one-int header on the existing doorbell protocol: rank 1 spills its own
  kept states (waiting out an in-flight request first) and stops — without
  that, a restart would resume a conversation only one rank has.
- The writer is a daemon thread: the dying snapshot's device tensors are
  copied to disk off the request path, a partial write is renamed only when
  whole, and a rank's own files are pruned to `--spill-gib` newest-first.
- The snapshot key is the model's resolved directory with the tensorfold and
  torch versions and the cache-layout flags (`TF_GLM_LATENT`,
  `TF_GLM_DRAFT_RING`, `TF_GLM_MTP`, drafter), so another configuration's
  engine finds nothing of this one's. (`TF_GLM_KV`/`TF_GLM_DENSE`/
  `TF_GLM_KDA_CHUNKED` from the issue do not exist in this tree.)
- `prefix_snapshots` imports mlx lazily now, so the CUDA side reuses its
  snapshot key, metadata reader and stale-partial cleanup without mlx
  installed. (Side effect: `test_prompt_memory`'s oversized-disk-snapshot
  test passes without mlx.)

## Exactness and tests

New `tests/cuda/test_glm_spill.py` on the tiny synthetic checkpoint:
an evicted conversation resumes from disk with a fresh prefill's **exact**
reply, a restarted engine reads the spill back identically, an MTP-off engine
(a different model id) resumes nothing, and the shutdown save writes.

GLM blocks after the change: `test_glm_spill` + `test_glm_engine` +
`test_glm_draft_ring` + `test_glm_long_context` + the `__new__`-mocked
kept-state tests (class-level engine defaults keep them working) — 60 passed.

## Not run

- A real checkpoint's cold-vs-resume comparison (no Flash checkpoint on this
  disk; the serving cluster holds the GPU). The issue's 60 s cold prefill for
  100K tokens is what this removes on a hit.
- The true two-machine rank-1 path (tests use the `_TwoCopies` stand-in; the
  rank-1 header parse and file naming are symmetric by construction).
- On a small harness a 1.9K-token spill is 1.0 MiB and the resume is noise
  next to the prefill; the ratio that matters is a real 100K-token snapshot.

## Design boundary (unchanged from main)

Spilled snapshots are rows-saved states: like their in-memory counterparts
they resume MTP and serial policies, not DFlash-drafted ones
(`decode.save_rows` keeps no DFlash2 caches). An `auto`-policy request with
the drafter loaded re-prefills either way. Stashing drafter ring windows at
keep time would be a separate feature.

items.title: tests(glm cuda): GLM-5.3-Flash's CUDA forward on the CPU, two ranks over gloo, against a float64 reference
items.body:
Tests only, CPU only: three new files under `tests/`, no change to `src/`.

The GLM-5.3-Flash CUDA engine's tests run on a GPU (`tests/cuda`), on one GPU playing rank 0 of two
(`_TwoCopies` hands back two copies of its own partials), and they check the engine against itself: drafted against
serial, resumed against fresh, one chunking against another. Nothing checks the forward's numbers against the model's
definition, or runs the two ranks' real halves together. These tests do both, on any Linux machine with PyTorch and
Triton, no GPU needed (about 80 s).

## What the tests run

- **The CUDA path itself** (`families/glm5_next/cuda`: `weights.load` and `split`, `forward.Buffers` / `State` /
  `compute` / `commit`, `mtp.mtp_compute`), with every Triton kernel in it run by Triton's interpreter
  (`TRITON_INTERPRET=1`): the embedding, RMSNorms, the HC split and write-back, the BF16 matmuls with their split-K
  sums, the router and top-k, SwiGLU and the combine, the latent attention (dense chunks, merge, absorb / expand), the
  indexer writes, pool keys, pool scores and radix top-k, the sparse latent attention, the KDA conv-window shift.
- **Two ranks as two processes** joined by gloo (`forward.gather`'s all-gather), each loading its own half of the
  checkpoint through `RankReader`.
- **A tiny random checkpoint in GLM-5.3-Flash's EXL3 layout**, adapted from the synthetic model of
  `tests/cuda/test_glm_engine.py` (2 layers, KDA + DSA, dense MLP + MoE, MTP head): 8 index heads, expert scales that
  make the experts' share of the output as large as the rest's, and `index_topk` 16, so rows past 19 tokens attend to
  their top 4 pools and their tail. `sparse.TOPK_POOLS` is set to 16 // 4 to match, the
  only constant the tests change.
- **Torch stand-ins for the two CUDA extensions** the path calls: `kda.cu`'s chain and replay (written from the
  kernel: the same fp32 sums and bf16 roundings, rows one after another) and the routed EXL3 experts (the weights from
  `cuda/exl3.py`'s float64 reference decoder). Those kernels keep their GPU tests in `tests/cuda`.

## What they check

- `test_prompt_and_windows_match_the_reference`: a 12-token prompt chunk, then four 4-row decode windows (one keeping
  2 rows), dense, crossing the dense limit and wholly past it, against `tests/glm_flash_reference.py`: GLM-5.3-Flash
  in float64 torch, written from the Mac engine's definition (`model.py`'s hyper-connections, `kda.py` with mlx-lm's
  gated delta rule, `mla.py` and `caches.py`'s pooled keys, `mlp.py`, `mtp.py`). It shares no code with the CUDA path
  but the EXL3 decoder.
- `test_a_prompt_chunk_past_the_dense_limit_matches_the_reference`: a 26-token prompt chunk, its rows past 19 sparse.
- `test_mtp_head_matches_the_reference`: the MTP head as the engine feeds it, the prompt's rows on the prompt buffers,
  then a window's rows past the dense limit.
- `test_drafted_windows_equal_serial_steps`: every committed row of those windows has its one-row step's logits, and
  the KDA states, conv windows, latent cache, index keys, gates and pools left are the same, bit for bit.
- `test_prompt_chunking_keeps_the_bits`: the 26-token prompt as one chunk or 16 + 10 leaves the same logits and
  state, bit for bit.

Against the reference: every logit within 8% of the logits' range (bf16's drift from float64 is up to 5% on this
model), and the same best token wherever the reference's lead is over twice the row's error. A row whose choice of
pools or experts is within a whisker of a tie in the reference is left out (`Reference.tied`): bf16 rounding may
choose the other side there, and the two answers then differ by far more than the drift.

To see that the tolerance still catches what it is for, we broke the source one way at a time (not part of this pull
request). Caught: the all-gather dropped (only this rank's partial summed), the HC mix matrix transposed in
`_hc_post`, the sparse tail tokens off by one, kv_b's key and value rows swapped at load, the top-k weights left
unnormalized, and KDA's replay keeping one row too few (the bitwise test). Not caught: a 5% scale on the sparse
attention scores, a pool key built with the wrong positional bias, and the MTP head's position-0 embedding left
unzeroed (the last moves the MTP logits about 2%, inside the drift).

## Triton's interpreter

Triton 3.7's interpreter multiplies bf16 `tl.dot` operands as their raw bits (a 16 x 32 x 16 bf16 dot comes out
~5e10 off) and truncates fp32 to bf16 where the GPU rounds to nearest even. `tests/glm_cuda_cpu.py` widens bf16
operands to fp32 (exact, as the tensor cores multiply them) and rounds to nearest even, in the rank processes only.
The test process itself never imports the CUDA path, so nothing else in a test session sees the interpreter.

## Receipt

- **Environment.** TensorFold 0.6.5 (`609ca41`); NVIDIA's `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3` (Python 3.12.3,
  PyTorch 2.13.0a0+9186a08b2c, Triton 3.7.1, NumPy 2.1.0) with `pip install 'tensorfold[test] @ ...@609ca41'`, run
  with no GPU (the container started without `--gpus`, 8 CPUs, 6 GB; 10 GB for the whole suite) on a DGX Spark (aarch64). No checkpoint: the
  tests write their own.
- **Exactness.** Not applicable: no source change. The new tests check drafted against serial on the CPU path.
- **Decode / prompt speed.** Not applicable: no source change.
- **Tests.** `python -m pytest -q tests/test_glm_cuda_cpu.py`: 5 passed (79 s).
  Whole suite (`python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly --timeout=300 tests`, no GPU): main 4,047 passed, 135 failed,
  172 skipped, 11 errors; this branch 4,052 passed, 135 failed, 172 skipped, 11 errors. The failures and errors are
  the same tests on both, already failing on main in this Linux container without MLX; none is in the new files.
- **Not run.** On a GPU machine (they need none; with PyTorch and Triton there they run as here, on the CPU). On a
  Mac they skip at collection (no Triton).

items.title: perf(glm cuda): KDA prompt step kernel: eight warps a block, four warp sums in one (same bits)
items.body:
The prompt chain's `step_kernel` walks a chunk's rows one by one per (head, block of value rows). It cost 2.97 of the
chain's 4.2 ms for a 2,048-row call (32 heads, GB10), about 2 s of a 38,960-token prefill.

## What changes

- Every block of a head stages the same k, q and decay rows into shared memory. With 4 warps a head had 8 blocks
  doing it, with 8 warps 4. I swept 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 warps with 4 to 16 staged rows; 8 x 16 was fastest. A warp's
  arithmetic does not depend on the block it sits in.
- `warp_sum4`: a warp's four value rows' sums (and its four read-outs) in one reduce-scatter. Each level adds the lane
  pairs `warp_sum` adds (`l ^ 16`, `^ 8`, `^ 4`, `^ 2`, `^ 1`), so each sum has `warp_sum`'s bits: 6 shuffles for four
  sums instead of 20, then a broadcast of the four kv sums.

Step 2.97 -> 1.80 ms (2.82 with eight warps alone); the chain 4.2 -> 3.0 ms. The fused decode chain and replay keep
`update`. Prefetching the next staged rows into registers was slower (2.07 ms), so it is not kept.

## Tests

`tests/cuda/test_glm_kernels.py::test_kda_wide_chain_gives_the_fused_chains_bits` (rows 64, 300 and 2,048; 32 heads)
still passes: the wide chain equals the fused chain bit for bit.

## Receipt

- **Environment.** 0.6.4; PyTorch 2.13.0a0+9186a08 (NVIDIA's 26.07 container, CUDA 13.3, NCCL 2.30.7); two DGX Sparks (GB10, 128 GB each,
  GPU clock capped at 2,200 MHz), TP=2 over one RoCE link; `--context 0`, MTP drafts only;
  `TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP@d2b17f52`.
- **Exactness.** `token_sha` of greedy 64-token replies to prompts of 14 to 32,762 tokens: 5 of 5 the same as main's;
  drafted / `"draft": false`: 5 of 5; `tools/bench_concurrent.py … --alone --serial` 48 of 48 and 10 of 10.
- **Decode.** Unchanged (one-row steps keep their kernel): main / this 51.86 / 51.33, 42.81 / 42.66, 62.22 / 61.99,
  46.84 / 46.87 tok/s (code / chat at temperature 1, then 0).
- **Prompt**, main -> this, alternated (main, this, this, main), median of 3 a length, mean of two starts each: 1,107 -> 1,129 (+2.0%), 1,033 -> 1,055 (+2.1%),
  1,044 -> 1,066 (+2.0%), 1,042 -> 1,066 (+2.3%), 1,032 -> 1,056 (+2.3%) tok/s at 2k / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k tokens.
- **Tests.** On both Sparks, `tests/test_cuda_*.py tests/test_glm*.py` and the GLM files of `tests/cuda`: 1,506
  passed, 14 skipped, the same as main (the wide-chain test included).
- **Not run.** Metal. RTX PRO 6000.

items.title: perf(glm cuda): DSA's prompt absorb/expand and pool scores on more programs (same bits)
items.body:
Two DSA prompt kernels kept a chunk's rows in one program's loop.

## What changes

- `_absorb_q` / `_expand_v` (BF16 `kv_b`: EXL3's) ran every row of a 2,048-row chunk inside each (head, column block)
  program. `_absorb_q_rows` / `_expand_v_rows` take the same loop body, shapes and warps over blocks of 64 rows, so the
  same per-row sums: 6.94 -> 5.70 ms and 7.62 -> 6.49 ms a call at 2,048 rows. Windows under 64 rows (decode) keep the
  old kernels.
- `select_tokens` scored prompt chunks one row per `_scores` program (`RB=1`), each loading its pool tile alone.
  `_scores` already masks each row's keys to its own pools before the dot, so `RB` never changes a row's bits. Prompt
  windows (64 rows or more) now take `RB=4`: 6.05 -> 5.36 ms a 2,048-row chunk at 36k tokens, with the same tokens and
  counts. This one runs for every checkpoint once a prompt passes the dense window.

`RB=4` follows the `score_rows` default of MiaAI-Lab's patch 0009-glm-prefill-kernels for TensorFold v0.6.0
(Apache-2.0, credited in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`). No code is taken; `_scores` already had the parameter.

## Tests

`tests/cuda/test_glm_latent.py`:

- `test_prompt_absorb_and_expand_keep_the_one_loop_bits` (64, 100 and 2,048 rows): the row-block kernels give every
  row the bits of the kernels that loop over all rows in one program.
- `test_prompt_pool_scores_on_row_blocks_keep_the_lists` (2,048 rows at 36k, 513 at 9k, 64 at 2,047): `SCORE_RB` 4
  gives every row the tokens and count of `SCORE_RB` 1.

Both fail before the change (the constants they switch do not exist) and pass after.

## Receipt

- **Environment.** 0.6.4; PyTorch 2.13.0a0+9186a08 (NVIDIA's 26.07 container, CUDA 13.3, NCCL 2.30.7); two DGX Sparks (GB10, 128 GB each,
  GPU clock capped at 2,200 MHz), TP=2 over one RoCE link; `--context 0`, MTP drafts only.
- **Pool scores** (every checkpoint): `TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP@d2b17f52`, main / this, alternated (main, this, this, main), median of 3 a length, mean of two starts each:
  1,105 / 1,102, 1,030 / 1,029, 1,040 / 1,037, 1,040 / 1,036, 1,030 / 1,028 tok/s at 2k / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k tokens, within noise (the change
  saves 0.7 ms of a chunk that takes about 2 s here). `token_sha` of greedy 64-token replies to prompts of 14 to 32,762 tokens: 5 of 5 the same as main's;
  drafted / `"draft": false`: 5 of 5; `tools/bench_concurrent.py … --alone --serial` 48 of 48 and 10 of 10.
- **Absorb / expand and pool scores together** (BF16 `kv_b`): `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4@423acf37`, which main does not
  load, so on top of the NVFP4 loader change of issue #308 (not filed yet): loader / loader + this, alternated, median of 3 a length, mean of two starts each: 749 / 757 (+1.1%), 708 / 715 (+0.9%),
  712 / 717 (+0.8%), 711 / 718 (+1.1%), 715 / 720 (+0.7%) tok/s at 2k / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k tokens. `token_sha`
  of greedy 64-token replies to prompts of 14 to 32,762 tokens: 5 of 5 the same as the loader's; `--alone --serial`
  48 of 48 and 10 of 10.
- **Decode.** Unchanged (decode windows keep the old kernels): NVFP4 loader / loader + this 29.60 / 29.60, 27.77 / 27.72,
  33.80 / 33.85, 27.54 / 27.53; MLX main / this 51.91 / 51.99, 43.04 / 42.95, 62.16 / 62.58, 46.84 / 47.27
  tok/s (code / chat at temperature 1, then 0).
- **Tests.** On both Sparks, `tests/test_cuda_*.py tests/test_glm*.py` and the GLM files of `tests/cuda`: 1,512
  passed, 14 skipped (main: 1,506 passed, 14 skipped); the two new tests pass for all 6 cases.
