items.title: deepseek_v41: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on two DGX Sparks (EXL3 routed experts, DSpark drafts)
items.body:
Refs #299; it does not close it. This is an independent implementation of the family, and the second of two
stacked pull requests: it sits on PR A, #390 (App hooks for a family's prompt renderer and call markup, and DeepSeek-V4.1's
DSML spelling), which sits on `main` at 0.6.4 (`6ea5ade`). Its branch is PR A's branch (`6d11e57`) plus this PR's
commits, so review PR A first; the diff against PR A is the family alone.

## What it adds

A new CUDA family, `src/tensorfold/families/deepseek_v41/`, for `model_type` `deepseek_v41`, serving the EXL3 export
`sfxnz/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-EXL3` at revision `982b70452f399814f56b46272fd30394ae10d58c` on two GB10s, one rank each.
The repository's `main` holds only the model card, so the checkpoint is fetched by revision, as the recipe shows for
turboderp's EXL3 branches:

- Host side (no torch, so family discovery works on a Mac): `check()` refusals from `config.json` and the index,
  `cuda_engine()` argument checks, the per-layer roles from the config, DeepSeek's prompt encoder (vendored
  unmodified, MIT, the V4 precedent) behind a `Template` for PR A's `template_class` hook, Engram n-gram hashing
  (numpy, exact) and the Engram table reader (buffered `pread` of the checkpoint's own shards, reusing
  `qwen4_exp/ssd_table.py`'s `_no_cache` and `_fill`).
- `cuda/`: split rules and exact load-time conversions (FP8 32x32 scales repeated per row for `Mx8Linear`, the
  DSpark experts' MXFP4 repacked losslessly as NVFP4 `Experts4`, EXL3 gate/up halves), the loader, admission
  geometry, Triton kernels for DeepSeek's RMSNorm and mHC, RoPE/YaRN, the FP8/FP4 activation quantize-dequantize,
  sparse attention over the window and a compressed list with a sink, the compressor and index keys, the lightning
  indexer with candidate blocks and top-k, sqrt-softplus routing over the shared EXL3 grouped experts, the Engram
  device path, the target forward, prompt prefill in 2,048-row chunks, DSpark drafting (absorb, the 5-row block, the
  Markov chain, the draft-count policy), decode rounds with CUDA graphs per window size, kept prompt snapshots in an
  arena allocated at startup, the rank protocol and the engine, and `DeepSeekV41App` on PR A's hooks.
- Tests: host tests for every host module and the App, an fp32 port of DeepSeek's `inference/model.py` as a test
  comparator (`tests/dsv41_reference.py`), a tiny synthetic checkpoint in the real layout (`tests/dsv41_tiny.py`),
  and GPU tests in `tests/cuda/test_dsv41_*.py`: every kernel against the fp32/fp64 reference and for row
  invariance, the forward eager against graphs, drafted against serial, resumed against fresh, two ranks as two
  threads on one GPU against one rank, and real-weight blocks and a reduced 8-layer model against the reference when
  `TF_DSV41_MODEL` names the checkpoint. `tests/cuda/dsv41_tp_check.py` runs the reduced model over NCCL on two
  machines for comparison with the one-GPU pair.
- Docs: `docs/recipes/deepseek-v4.1-flash.md`, a row in the README's models table and in `docs/recipes/cuda.md`,
  the recipe book, the families table, a two-rank note in `RUNBOOK.md`, integer efforts and the refused thinking
  budget in `docs/api.md`, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

Outside the family it adds one entry to ruff's `extend-exclude` in `pyproject.toml` (the vendored encoder, as
V4's is) and adds a DeepSeek-V4.1 case to the lanes test in `tests/test_cuda_cli.py`. No shared kernel, engine,
sampling or server code changes, so every other family runs the same code as on PR A.

Every new file is under 600 lines except the vendored encoder (979 lines, unmodified). `ruff check` finds nothing in
the new files; `tests/test_cuda_cli.py` keeps the 6 findings it has on PR A, all in lines this PR does not touch.

## Receipt

**Environment.** PR A tip `6d11e57`; this PR's tip `0d91389`. Every server receipt and the `tests/cuda` run below come
from a clean checkout of `0d91389`, the same files on both machines. The host suite ran on `eb0bac7`, whose tree is
identical, and the checkpoint hashes are from the previous receipt run, with no file in the snapshot newer than that check. Two DGX Sparks (GB10, 128 GB each) on their direct cable (RoCE,
`NCCL_IB_HCA` with both devices). Image
`nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3@sha256:2140e699b3beaf7f96a0081fd9c9406bc3832b435cdb60dfa2d261f7d2f34a1c` on both,
PyTorch 2.13.0a0+9186a08b2c.nv26.07, CUDA 13.3 in forward-compatibility mode (user-mode driver 610.43.02, kernel
driver 580.173.02). Checkpoint `sfxnz/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-EXL3` at `982b70452f399814f56b46272fd30394ae10d58c`
(`hf download sfxnz/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-EXL3 --revision 982b70452f399814f56b46272fd30394ae10d58c`): 48 shards,
357,466,041,064 bytes. On both machines every file the engine reads (the 48 shards, the index, `config.json`, the
tokenizer files) and `LICENSE` has the Hub's sha256. Two files the engine does not read differ: `README.md` on
rank 0, and `requant-viterbi-manifest.json` on rank 1 (one timestamp). Served with:

```
tensorfold serve MODEL_DIR --tp 2 --rank 1 --master ADDR --master-port PORT --name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --no-thinking --no-update-check --context 65538
tensorfold serve MODEL_DIR --tp 2 --rank 0 --master ADDR --master-port PORT --name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --no-thinking --no-update-check --context 65538 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
```

**Exactness.** `python3 tools/bench_concurrent.py http://127.0.0.1:8080 deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --alone
--serial` (4 streams, which this engine serves one after another; code and chat prompts; 256 tokens):

| Prompt | Temp | Concurrent vs alone (equal / unequal / failed) | Alone vs `"draft": false` |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | 1.0 | 12 / 0 / 0 | 4 / 0 / 0 |
| chat | 1.0 | 12 / 0 / 0 | 4 / 0 / 0 |
| code | 0 | 12 / 0 / 0 | 1 / 0 / 0 |
| chat | 0 | 12 / 0 / 0 | 1 / 0 / 0 |

One chat request with `tools` (a `get_weather` function, "What is the weather in Paris and in Tokyo right now? Use the
tool."), sent twice with the second `"draft": false`, at temperature 0 and at 1.0 with a seed, streamed and not: all
4 pairs have equal `token_sha` (`c842840edcbb` greedy, `33abb08812a7` sampled), each reply ends with
`finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and two calls. Three chat prompts, 160 tokens with `ignore_eos`, `top_k` 20, drafted
against `"draft": false` at temperatures 0 and 1: 6 of 6 equal.

**Family default sampling.** The family's default is DeepSeek's recommendation, `top_k` off (the receipt tools
always send `top_k` 20 or greedy). One request without `top_k` at temperature 1 with a seed, drafted, then
`"draft": false`, then resent: the same `token_sha` (`bd50e30b4d41`) three times, the resend resuming 17 of its 18
prompt tokens.

**Oversized `top_k`.** A request with `top_k` 2,147,483,648 (past int32) at temperature 1 with a seed returned 200,
with the same `token_sha` (`7d80106ecd4d`) as the same request without `top_k`; the next request (17*19, greedy)
answered `323`, and `/health` returned 200 after each.

**Long prompt and memory.** A cold 65,536-token prompt and three resends gave the same reply; the resends resumed
65,535 tokens. `torch.cuda.memory_reserved` stayed at 86,578,823,168 bytes on rank 0 (86,679,486,464 on rank 1)
after the cold prompt and after each resend (a separate `--context 65538` boot). Admission lines of the receipt session
at `--context 65538`:

```
[tensorfold] CUDA rank 0 startup estimate 78.46 GiB within 99.76 GiB; native 1048576, allocated prompt/reply window 65538, cache slots 65544
[tensorfold] CUDA rank 1 startup estimate 78.46 GiB within 101.46 GiB; native 1048576, allocated prompt/reply window 65538, cache slots 65544
[tensorfold] rank 0 of 2: 40 layers and DSpark, 73.23 GiB of weights in 30.3 s
```

Without `--context` (the model's whole window), both ranks admitted 1,048,576 tokens (`startup estimate 79.09 GiB
within 98.95 GiB` on rank 0, `within 101.55 GiB` on rank 1), and after a smoke request `free -h` showed 23 and
26 GiB available. After this receipt's session at 65,538: 28 and 30 GiB.

**Two ranks.** `tests/cuda/dsv41_tp_check.py` (the reduced 8-layer model, prompts of 300 and 2,100 tokens, greedy and
keyed, serial and drafted) printed the same 9 lines per rank over NCCL across the two machines (CUDA graphs) as with
`--pair`, two threads on one GPU (eager): every prompt-head, verify-step and DSpark-block logits hash, every reply
and every committed-cache hash.

**Quality** against the vLLM recipe on the same weights, with vLLM's own repeat runs as the noise floor:
teacher-forced NLL 0.1371 over 40 passages from ten Project Gutenberg books (19,828 positions), against vLLM's
0.1389-0.1391; TensorFold's repeat is bit-identical. Top-1 disagreement with vLLM is 1.08% (gate 5.5%) and median
|dlogprob| 1.0e-4. GSM8K 97/100 (vLLM 96 in its run on these weights, 97 in the recipe's baseline). Tool calls 22/22
with exact arguments, needles 6/6 at 8k and 32k tokens, and 12 of 12 greedy chats identical across repeats. All of
these ran on this tip; every teacher-forced log-probability (142 prompts) is bit-identical to the run on an earlier
commit of this branch, whose MMLU 204/228 (vLLM 204 and 205) and needles 9/9 up to about 130k tokens were not re-run.

**Decode speed.** This PR adds a family, so there is no before. `python3 tools/bench_openai.py
http://127.0.0.1:8080 deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, median tok/s of 5, with the vLLM recipe on the same
machines and weights for comparison:

| Prompt | Temp | This PR | vLLM |
|---|---|---|---|
| fibonacci-raw | 1.0 | 42.0 | 47.3 |
| gpu-chat-no-think | 1.0 | 37.6 | 44.3 |
| fibonacci-raw | 0 | 55.9 | (greedy reply is end tokens; the tool fails on it) |
| gpu-chat-no-think | 0 | 41.1 | 43.1 |

**Prompt speed.** This PR adds a family, so there is no before; no shared prompt-path code changes.
`python3 tools/prefill_cold.py build MODEL_DIR prompts.json` renders through PR A's hook with this
family's template; its 16 prompts are the same messages, with the same token counts, as vLLM's run of the tool's
corpus. `run`, prompt tok/s (median of 3):

| Tokens | This PR | vLLM |
|---|---|---|
| 2,048 | 519 | 778 |
| 8,192 | 547 | 769 |
| 16,384 | 557 | 772 |
| 32,768 | 560 | 777 |
| 65,536 | 568 | 774 |

**Against the vLLM recipe's tuned serve.** Its own decode cells (greedy, thinking off, 200 tokens, one stream; its
`bench_decode.py`), against its published round. This PR's decode tokens a round count the 199 tokens after the
prompt's first over its rounds, as vLLM's acceptance length does; both sides draft 3 a round (this PR's default; the
DSpark block holds 5):

| Cell | This PR, tok/s (decode tokens a round) | vLLM, tok/s (acceptance length) |
|---|---|---|
| prose | 45.5 (2.80) | 50.7 (2.45) |
| structured | 63.5 (3.90) | 84.3 (4.00) |
| prose_long | 34.0 (2.12) | 43.8 (2.17) |
| L.A.I.L, temperature 0.2 | not run | 42.6 |

This PR is slower than the vLLM recipe: decode tok/s is 5-15% lower in `bench_openai` and 10-25% lower in the
recipe's own cells, and prompt tok/s is 27-33% lower. The vLLM numbers come from its run on the same machines and
weights the day before; they were not interleaved with these, and vLLM's sampled fibonacci-raw reps range from 40 to
65 tok/s. Drafting is not the gap: this PR keeps more tokens a round on prose and slightly fewer on structured and
prose_long. A round takes about 62 ms (inter-chunk p50 61.5-62.3 ms) against vLLM's 48. Of that, the host's
synchronous Engram reads take 3.5-4.6 ms (4.0-6.8 ms with `top_k` off), target sampling 2 ms, and a serial token's device
time is 35 ms. With `top_k` off (the family default), the target's draw reads whole vocabulary shards to the host
whenever the nucleus runs past 1,024 candidates: 68-70 ms of sampling a round, and 24.5 tok/s against 50.0 at `top_k`
20 on the same prompt. Prompt chunks re-decode each routed expert's EXL3 tiles for every 16 rows. This PR is the correctness path;
the speed work follows as separate pull requests, stacked on this one, each with its own before/after receipt and
bit-equality tests:

1. C1: skip, in the last 20 layers, the prompt rows no later row or the reply reads (bit-identical by
   construction; the largest prompt lever).
2. C2: CUDA graphs over whole rounds and launch fusion.
3. C3: an EXL3 prompt-window grouped kernel in the shared `cuda/exl3` (reuse a decoded tile for 64 rows, same
   per-row arithmetic), with Flash Next receipts too.
4. C4: a native GIL-free Engram reader off the critical path, and resident scale halves.
5. C5: DSpark's draws on the device inside its graph, and the draft-count policy.
6. C6: the exact `top_k`-off draw on the device in the shared `cuda/sampling.py` (the same keyed rule).
7. C7: packed FP4/FP8 KV and index-key storage for long contexts.
8. C8: overlapped prompt-chunk gathers.

## Precision decisions

Which sums change against DeepSeek's reference (`inference/model.py` and `inference/kernel.py` of
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at `dba1be0`; the EXL3 export does not ship them). Each is equal or higher precision
or a reorder, and each changes bits:

| Operation | DeepSeek's reference | This PR | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 projections | FP8 1x32 activation quantization before each FP8 matmul | bf16 activations x exact FP8 weights (`Mx8Linear`, scales repeated per row) | higher |
| Row-parallel partials (`wo_b`) | each rank's bf16 partial, then an fp32 all-reduce | fp32 partials gathered and added in rank order | higher |
| Indexer scores | bf16 einsum, heads split, bf16 all-reduce | fp32, every head on both ranks | higher; a row may keep a different 512th entry |
| Routed experts | FP8 act x FP4 W; routing weight before `w2`, rounded to bf16 | fp16 act x EXL3 W (the export's choice); routing weight after `w2` in the fp32 combine | reorder at equal or higher precision |
| Shared expert | computed whole on every rank; its bf16 `w2` output added to the fp32 sum after the routed all-reduce | inner dim split over the ranks; each rank's fp32 `w2` partial added into its fp32 MoE share, then the shares gathered and added in rank order | higher, and a reorder |
| LM head | fp32 logits of bf16 activations | bf16 activations x MXFP8 weights, fp32 logits | equal |
| Window / compressed / index-key QDQ | FP8 / FP4 quantize-dequantize | the same, stored as the bf16 values | equal |
| Decode indexer at even positions (layers 2, 8, 14 and their reusers) | scores against layer 20's index keys when the layer's ratio-2 compressor emitted nothing (`model.py:537-554`) | its own source's index keys, as the reference's prefill does | a reference defect, not reproduced: reproducing it would make decode differ from prefill |

Prompts always take bf16 activations; the family does not set `CUDA_PREFILL_FP8`, so `--prefill-fp8` is refused.

**A question for you.** The model applies FP8 (window keys) and FP4 (compressed and index keys) quantize-dequantize
inside its own forward and was trained with it, so this PR treats it as model semantics, always on, with no
`--kv-dtype` switch. Do you read it that way, or as "a precision mode a checkpoint format defines" that wants its own
issue? Also: the fp32-output path for `Mx8Linear` lives family-local (`cuda/mx8.py`, calling the same entries with
their `f32` flag and importing `FUSED_ROWS`, `qmm.split_k` and `qmm.bucket` rather than copying them). Would you
rather have an `f32` keyword on `Mx8Linear`?

## Tests

- Fails before: on PR A's tree with this PR's test files copied in, the 14 new host test files fail to collect
  (`No module named 'tensorfold.families.deepseek_v41'`) and the new lanes case in `tests/test_cuda_cli.py` fails
  (1 failed, 58 passed). With this PR: 360 passed, 10 skipped (the skips need a GPU or the checkpoint). The
  fixes for an oversized `top_k`, startup failures on one rank, the thinking budget and image blocks each come with
  a host test that fails without the fix; the engine's two-rank startup case also has a GPU test.
- Host suite, file by file, in a Linux venv without MLX and with no GPU visible (240 s per file): this PR has 3745
  passed, 170 failed, 11 errors and 520 skipped; PR A's tip has 3444 passed with the same failures, errors and skips
  apart from the new files, and the failing test IDs are identical. The failures need MLX, Metal, macOS or a GPU;
  `tests/test_cancellation.py` and `tests/test_qwen27_prompt_end_cache_host.py` time out on both when run this way.
- `tests/cuda`, file by file, in the image above on one Spark with `TF_DSV41_MODEL` set (600 s per file, 3,600 s
  for this family's): 1706 passed, 0 failed, 94 skipped. The family's 18 files: 412 passed, 1 skipped (this torch
  cannot cast to `float4_e2m1fn_x2`, the dtype one cross-check uses). The other 79 files give the same per-file
  results as on PR A. Among the family's files, a verify window's rows are checked bit for bit (logits, window KV
  and DSpark taps) against the same rows run alone at positions across the indexer's transitions and the ring's
  wrap, and every kept row of the drafted runs against the serial run's logits.
- `tests/cuda/dsv41_tp_check.py` over NCCL on two Sparks against `--pair`: identical (above).

## What I did not run

- Metal and MLX: the family is CUDA-only; its host modules import without torch, and the host suite ran in a Linux
  venv without MLX.
- Vision (no image frontend), grammars and `response_format`, `logprobs`, `tool_choice` required or named, `n` > 1:
  each refused with HTTP 400, checked once each against the server. `thinking_budget` (both ranks decode a request to
  its end, so a budget's cut would decode the whole first reply before the budgeted one) and Anthropic-style `image`
  blocks are also refused with HTTP 400; host tests cover those two.
- Thinking mode: every receipt ran with `--no-thinking`. One request with `reasoning_effort` 40 returned
  `reasoning_content`; there is no quality or speed receipt with thinking on.
- Prompts past 131,074 tokens: needles reached about 130k on an earlier commit of this branch, and 32k on this tip,
  whose cold prompts reached 65,536. The 1M window was only admitted and answered a smoke
  request.
- vLLM side by side in one session: its numbers come from its run on the same machines the day before. The recipe's
  prose cell stops naturally at 74 tokens, so 63% of its 200 measured tokens come after the end token.
- Concurrent streams: requests run one at a time (`--parallel` is accepted and ignored).
- One GPU, discrete cards, other machines than two GB10s.
- Other families: not served, since no shared code changes; their tests give the same results as on PR A.
- The vLLM recipe's L.A.I.L cell (its own harness), and thinking-mode A/B with named efforts against vLLM, whose
  encoder maps the names to other budgets (25/50/75 against DeepSeek's 50/75/100).
- `Mia-AiLab/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-EXL3-3.0bpw`: not checked. `Mia-AiLab/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-EXL3-2.9bpw`: `check()` on its
  `config.json` refuses it (its non-routed weights are EXL3 too).

## Data from text

No data file built from text is added. The Engram tables are the checkpoint's own (DeepSeek's). The test fixture
`tests/fixtures/deepseek_v41/engram_ids.json` holds ids DeepSeek's `inference/engram.py` computed from fixed token
sequences. The long-context prompts come from `tools/prefill_cold.py`'s corpus, the CPython 3.12 standard library
sources; the quality comparison scored ten Project Gutenberg books (1232, 1342, 1661, 2009, 2701, 3300, 345, 74, 84,
98).

items.title: feat(qwen4_exp cuda): Flash Next on four ranks (--tp 4), each rank's sums over the shared rank-sum transports
items.body:
## What this changes

Part of #313. Stacked on #378. The earlier commits on this branch are #378's (see #376 for what they carry). This pull request is the last two commits: the four-rank change and a fix from review (MLX key/value heads, below). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs on one GPU, two ranks or four:

- Heads split by the rank count, refused by name where they do not divide; key/value heads past the rank count are
  shared, each rank keeping the one its query heads read. Expert and shared-expert widths split on whole
  quantization groups (`ranks.share`: the lower ranks one block more where they do not divide). The MTP layer's bf16
  experts keep each rank's gate rows and its up rows.
- Rank 0 posts each request to every following rank; settings are gathered from every rank; the rank sums install
  over the engine's communicator, and row-parallel branches sum through them (one launch, or copies for
  prompt-sized partials). NVFP4 bf16 faces return fp32 partials; an NVFP4 checkpoint's prompt partials are bf16.
  NVFP4 checkpoints still run on one GPU here.
- `gdn` / `gdn_io` take a rank's share of four (4 key and 12 value heads).
- The MLX loader's attention takes the same shared key/value head as the NVFP4 loader (`kv_local` / `kv_first`);
  before, 2 key/value heads over 4 ranks gave every rank empty k and v projections.
- Admission counts a rank's expert share, shared key/value heads, and bf16 MTP experts as NVFP4.
- On a discrete GPU the n-gram tables are locked only as far as the host's available memory allows; read-ahead pins
  host pages on the caller's device.

items.title: feat(deepseek_v41): DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Macs, a serial reference for oMLX's converted checkpoint
items.body:
## What this changes

A new Mac family for `model_type: deepseek_v41` that serves `Jundot/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-oQ4e-mtp` as oMLX converts it
(mxfp8 dense projections, mxfp4 routed experts, bf16 small linears, head and embedding, affine 4-bit Engram tables
memory-mapped and read a row at a time). Decode rows run one at a time through each layer, so this is the serial
reference that the stacked PRs speed up. Refs #267; the package layout next to #299's CUDA family is agreed there first.

Related: #342 (draft) adds a CUDA `deepseek_v41` family for the EXL3 checkpoint on two DGX Sparks and writes the
same `families/deepseek_v41/` package; #300 is a CUDA lane decoder for #299. This family is Mac-only (MLX), so the
two can share the package name only if the layout is agreed; we are happy to rename or nest ours.

The arithmetic follows oMLX's `patches/deepseek_v41` (MIT), itself a port of DeepSeek's reference code: single-pass
mHC, CSA2 attention (an FP8 window plus FP4 compressed pools from KV-source layers shared by later layers, index top-k
over candidate blocks), FP8 activations into quantized projections, and Engram n-gram hashing on the host. Metal
kernels ported from oMLX: the head, `hc_post`, `hc_pre_norm`, fused attention and index scores. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`
names the source.

"Serial reference" describes how a window's rows run inside each layer, not a separate decode path: the family serves through V4's lane runtime (`LANES = True`), so every token goes through the lane rounds (one row a round without a drafter, or a window the engine verifies), and drafted == `"draft": false` above. "Prompt no slower" has no before on this checkpoint: a

items.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash CUDA family: TP=2 multi-stream serving on 2x DGX Spark
items.body:
**Draft. Opened for visibility and discussion, not yet for merge.**

This adds a `deepseek_v41` CUDA family that serves **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (the EXL3 2.9 bpw checkpoint) at TP=2 on two DGX Spark (GB10) nodes, plus the shared CUDA-server pieces it needed.

## What's in it
- **Engine** (`src/tensorfold/families/deepseek_v41/`):
  - hyper-connections, compressed and windowed MQA with sinks, the sparse indexer with a radix top-k, Engram tables, a DSpark draft head;
  - EXL3 experts with 16-byte loads;
  - narrow key-width decode CUDA graphs that share one pool.
- **KV cache in the model's native numerics:** FP4 by default, `TF_DSV41_KV=fp8` for the V4 layout (see below).
- **Multi-stream serving:**
  - a shared KV extent pool (grow / move / evict), and kept prompts that resume at any covered position, in memory and on an NVMe tier;
  - exact chunk-invariant prefill with a bounded tail;
  - decode rows that are bit-identical whether batched or alone.
- **Serving and operations:**
  - a lenient DSML tool-call parser and an xgrammar tool-call grammar;
  - `/health` fatal and stalled reporting, a watchdog, and soak, stress, structured-output and client harnesses;
  - prepared per-rank weight folders, plus Triton and PTX caches in the cache volume (boot about 44 s);
  - a two-rank RoCE all-gather, used by default with NCCL as fallback. The RoCE v2 GID is found per device, not from a fixed index;
  - rank 1 idles on a CPU socket, so its GPU doesn't spin while the server is idle.
- **Dev loop** (`notes/dsv41/DEV.md`):
  - one-load test suites with quick and full tiers;
  - prepared weights in dev runs;
  - an OOM guard;
  - `make hot` (serve the current source without an image build);
  - paired MMLU and teacher-forced quality tools.
- **Deployment:** `deploy/dsv41-tp2/` (compose, Makefile, Dockerfile) and `tools/dsv41_*` dev scripts.
  - Note: these contain **site-specific hosts, interfaces and paths** (our two nodes) and need to be made generic before merging.

## Results on 2× GB10, 16 streams × 614K context (compose server, FP4 KV, carveout on)
| | FP4 KV (default) | FP8 KV |
|---|---|---|
| Shared KV pool | **6.41M tokens** | 3.11M tokens |
| Single stream decode (code, drafts on) | 100.2 tok/s | 98–105 tok/s |
| C3 / C4 aggregate | 154.7 / 154.2 tok/s | |
| Hard prose | 38.3 tok/s | 38.4 tok/s |
| Prefill 8K / 100K cold | 1658 / 2569 tok/s | 1596 / 2428 tok/s |
| 16 concurrent clients | 122.6 tok/s | 128.0 tok/s |

The C1 bench samples at temperature 0.2, so its runs vary by more than the FP4-FP8 difference. With 6 fixed greedy prompts, FP4 gives 101.2 tok/s and FP8 98.2.

Other results:
- warm resend of a 100K prompt: 0.4 s;
- 590K needles found in both KV formats.

Bit-exactness was checked for:
- batched vs alone;
- chunked vs whole prefill;
- kept-prompt resume vs fresh prefill, in memory and on NVMe;
- the kept state's bytes across the two ranks;
- RoCE vs NCCL.

## FP4 KV (DeepSeek-V4.1's native KV numerics)
The cache uses the formats the model was trained with (V4.1 report §2.4.4; DeepSeek's MIT inference code):
- compressed entries: NVFP4, E2M1 with an E4M3 scale per 16, RoPE dimensions included, 288 B;
- indexer keys and queries: MXFP4, a UE8M0 scale per 32, 68 B;
- window keys: FP8 with UE8M0 scales per 32;
- the compressor output is rounded to bf16 before its norm.

That is 890 B per token instead of 1845. The quantizers are bit-exact to the reference.

Making FP4 as fast as FP8 took three kernel changes:
- **Decode attention in CUDA** (`mqa_fp4.cu`): each 32-entry stage is unpacked once into shared memory and used by 16 heads, with a fixed-tree merge so batched rows equal rows alone. 0.33 ms per step, against 1.6 ms for the Triton FP4 path and 0.9 ms for FP8.
- **A shared-tile indexer:** each MXFP4 key tile is unpacked once for all rows of one stream. Its scores are bit-identical to the per-row kernel.
- **Restructured FP4 prefill:** row-tiled segment scores, one tie-keyed pick per pass, and entries unpacked once per chunk. It is bit-identical to the earlier FP4 path, and faster than FP8 at 8K and 100K.

Quality against FP8:
- **Teacher-forced over 26 documents** (53K positions, 8K–64K): top-1 agreement with bf16 is 96.75% (FP8 97.69%), and NLL changes by +0.0012. Accuracy against the actual next token is the same for both formats (76.3%).
- **Paired MMLU, 2280 questions:** 85.75% vs 86.23% (McNemar p = 0.11). The difference comes from FP4 overrunning a 16-token answer budget more often. Re-asked with room to finish, the two formats are 90.0% vs 89.9%.
- **Tool-call eval:** 111 vs 117 of 138 in one run each (4 scenarios differ, sign test p = 0.125).

## Overlap
#300 (jayleaton) starts upstreaming a different DeepSeek-V4.1 port. Several pieces here come from his recipe (see Attribution), so the two should be reconciled rather than merged side by side. I'm happy to split this into smaller PRs in whatever order is most useful.

## Attribution

This branch builds on several open projects. Each adapted file says what it took and what changed. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and NOTICE list everything.

- **Jay Leaton, [deepseek-v41-tensorfold-spark](https://github.com/jayleaton/deepseek-v41-tensorfold-spark)** (MIT for its DeepSeek-V4.1 family and GLM Spark engine files; Apache-2.0 for the rest, whose NOTICE line is in our NOTICE).
  - Adapted code: the DSML reply parser and tests, the DSML tool grammar (also from his GLM Spark engine), the NVMe session tier (`kvdisk.py`), the routed-expert load path (`x3ld.cu/.cpp/.py`), fast boot (`fastboot.py`), and the bulk L2 prefetch (`l2pf.cu`, ported to Triton and used in `tools/l2probe.py`).
  - Apache-2.0: the watchdog, systemd units and soak/stress/structured benches.
  - Ideas only: the `/health` fields, the radix top-k (`csa2/dtopk.py`), the bounded prefill tail (an exact form of his CED replay) and the THP guards.
- **MiaAI-Lab, [GLM-5.3-Flash TensorFold recipe](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold)** (Apache-2.0, Copyright 2026 MiaAI-Lab; its NOTICE line is copied word for word into our NOTICE).
  - Adapted code: the shared KV pool (`pool.py`, patch 0030), the extent lifecycle and rank-0 protocol in `multi.py` (patches 0030 and 0040-0042), copy/prompt-lookup drafts (`copy_drafts.py`, patches 0007/0032), and the RoCE all-gather port (patch 0006).
  - Ideas only: the visible-pools bound (0043, whose idea its credits trace to TensorFold PR #140) and `/tokenize` (0037).
- **[b12x](https://github.com/local-inference-lab/b12x) "RoCEnante"** (Apache-2.0, Luke Alonso and the b12x contributors; b12x ships no NOTICE file). `src/tensorfold/cuda/rdma/` is a two-rank, single-HCA re-implementation of its one-shot RoCE all-gather (`b12x/comm/roce/` at commit 8a99d63), taken from MiaAI-Lab's port. The parked multi-HCA port was not merged.
- **FlashInfer "Cake" DeepSeek-V4.1 mixed-cache decode** ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer) PR #5983, commit 2c1c0525; Apache-2.0, NVIDIA and the FlashInfer community). `mqa_fp4.cu` adapts its recipe: 16-head tiles sharing one gathered candidate set, NVFP4 widened exactly to bf16 for `mma.sync`, and V^T through `ldmatrix.trans`. It is rewritten by hand for our cache planes and window ring, with its own fixed-tree merge. Its NOTICE line is in our NOTICE.
- **DeepSeek** (MIT). The FP4 KV quantizers are bit-exact to the reference's `fp4_act_quant` / `act_quant`; the tests port them to torch with credit. The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash architecture and DSML format are implemented without copying reference code. The test fixture is the checkpoint's `config.json`. Engram tables are read from the original checkpoint at run time.
- **[vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm)** (Apache-2.0). The DeepSeek-V4.1 model and DSpark code were the spec for the math and the goldens, and `engram.py` ports its hashing helpers so the hashes match bit for bit. The TP=2 layout, the eagle3 tap layout, the fixed-k policy and `/tokenize` follow vLLM's conventions.
- **[ExLlamaV3](https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3)** (MIT, Turboderp). The EXL3 format is read by the DeepSeek-V4.1 loaders and the prompt expert kernel, whose Hadamard order follows `rot_in`. The comparison tool uses ExLlamaV3 at run time; it is not bundled.

The GB10 display-scanout carveout idea and the candidate-block semantics. MiaAI-Lab's [DeepSeek-V4.1 vLLM recipe](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks) (AGPL-3.0) was used as a reference for one convention and as the vLLM baseline; none of its code is included.

- **Libraries and image:** xgrammar (its `deepseek_v4_1` structural tag), transformers/tokenizers, NVIDIA's PyTorch container, and libibverbs. These are dependencies only; none is bundled.

items.title: perf(flash next cuda): opt-in graphs for uniform and mixed four-stream targets
items.body:
## What this changes

Adds two experimental, default-off CUDA graph paths for Flash Next target verification with four concurrent text streams. `TF_FOUR_STREAM_TARGET_GRAPH=1` enables uniform windows; `TF_MIXED_ROW_TARGET_GRAPH=1` enables the mixed-window extension. The switches can be enabled together. Eligible rounds replay the existing model computation, with SSD staging, sampling, acceptance and commits outside the graph. Checkpoint precision and target arithmetic are unchanged.

The uniform family holds at most four graphs: per-stream windows of 2 or 7 rows, each with two recurrent-scratch parities. The mixed family holds four more: non-uniform windows totalling 13 or 18 actual rows, each with two parities. A table-driven Triton PLE convolution refreshes each row's stream, start and tail mapping so different layouts with the same total rows can reuse a graph without padding expert rows.

Admission requires TP1, six drafts, pending counts at most 7, distinct text states, and dense attention ending at or before 512 tokens within the attention budget. Unsupported shapes and modes retain their existing fallback. Pointer/integer tables and PLE tails refresh before replay; capture-time writes are restored, stale static buffers invalidate entries, and graph metadata does not retain replaced States.

The code is based on v0.6.5 (`609ca41`) and restores the tested `0a33ef0` graph tree. SSD reader support is separate in [#334](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/334); batching is separate in [#413](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/413). Neither PR303 nor PR304 is included in this code or the comparisons below.

## Receipt

**Environment:** one DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 128 GB unified memory, local NVMe); NVIDIA driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.3, PyTorch 2.13.0a0 NVIDIA 26.07, Triton 3.7.1. Four server slots, context 69,632, int8 KV, six MTP drafts at confidence 0.60, and n-gram SSD offload. Existing solo graphs remain enabled. NVFP4 uses `Mia-AiLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` revision `925d7be6c14c6c9442ef83e8f05b5a3c39304f69`; the MLX4 diagnostic uses `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP` revision `dadefa8066e3be900a0d148d0f5a2f4eb1cf6534`.

**Original uniform path, isolated from batching:** PR334 versus PR334 plus the original graph change (`7c78d3e`), 256 output tokens per stream and five repetitions per cell. NVFP4 balances baseline/candidate and candidate/baseline runs; MLX4 is one ordered baseline/candidate diagnostic. Ratios use each process's median concurrent throughput, then geometrically balance the NVFP4 orders.

| Four-stream cell | NVFP4 graph on/off | MLX4 graph on/off |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Coding, greedy | +3.64% | +2.69% |
| Chat, greedy | +3.44% | +2.33% |
| Coding, sampled | −0.24% | −0.27% |
| Chat, sampled | +0.29% | −0.41% |
| Four-cell geometric mean | +1.77% | +1.07% |

These are within-checkpoint comparisons. Greedy cells improved; sampled cells were essentially flat. All repetitions, including first-use captures, are retained. Four initial captures accumulated about 0.68 seconds during each NVFP4 interval; counters confirmed 590 target replays in the NVFP4 interval and 565 in the MLX diagnostic. No capture time is subtracted or attributed to a specific throughput penalty.

**Serial validation with guarded batching held constant:** two further NVFP4 comparisons tested the additions one at a time. Each used four fresh processes in ABBA order and three 20-request panels per process: 240 timed requests plus 24 separate correctness requests, with the same 128-input/256-output, coding/chat, greedy/sampled, one/four-stream workload. Repeated panels are the geometric mean within each process, then balanced across the two processes per version.

| Addition | Fixed comparison control | Repeated single-stream decode | Repeated four-stream aggregate decode | Four-stream AB / BA |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original uniform graphs | PR334 + guarded batching | −0.17% | +0.66% | +1.21% / +0.12% |
| Mixed extension | Same control + original uniform graphs | −0.31% | +0.70% | +1.88% / −0.45% |

These incremental effects are smaller and workload-dependent. For the uniform path, repeated four-stream greedy chat was −2.43% overall, negative in both orders. For the mixed extension, first-panel four-stream throughput was −0.38% overall; repeated actual individual-stream throughput was +1.06%. Its repeated aggregate result reverses sign by order and does not establish a robust additional gain over batching. Ordinary target/MTP graph captures occurred in every repeated panel and are retained in the timings. The isolated and serial percentages must not be added or compounded into an overall speedup. There are two independent fresh processes per version, not 240 independent performance replicates.

**Prefill and TTFT, original uniform path only:** a separate ABBA test compared PR334 with PR334 plus `7c78d3e`, without batching or the mixed extension. Each code/chat prompt had two observations per version at 4,096 and 32,768 actual input tokens, one request at a time, greedy, four output tokens and zero cached-prefix tokens.

| Checkpoint | Prompt tokens | Prefill tok/s, baseline → graph | Client TTFT (s), baseline → graph |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| NVFP4 | 4,096 | 2,038 → 2,030 | 2.286 → 2.294 |
| NVFP4 | 32,768 | 1,855 → 1,845 | 17.966 → 18.069 |
| MLX4 | 4,096 | 3,732 → 3,715 | 1.522 → 1.528 |
| MLX4 | 32,768 | 2,833 → 2,824 | 11.994 → 12.029 |

These checkpoint/length averages changed by less than 0.6%, slightly slower. No prefill gain or statistical equivalence is claimed. Prefill rate is actual input tokens divided by the host-timed `tensorfold.prefill_s` diagnostic, not isolated GPU execution. Long single-request prompts use the eager fallback. All 64 warm/timed requests across the two checkpoints retained fresh-cache semantics and matching literal outputs and speculative work within each checkpoint. This receipt does not qualify the mixed extension's long-prompt performance.

**Correctness and tests:** 65 graph host tests passed at the restored tree. The original uniform path previously passed 31 CUDA cases without failures or skips. The mixed extension passed 12 actual-model byte-exact qualification cases in each of its two isolated runs, covering layouts at fixed total rows, both parities, State replacement/reorder/reset/resize, PLE tails, pointer refresh, 512/513 fallback, buffer invalidation and commits/continuations. Its standalone CUDA pytest entry point was collected but not run separately. The complete serial panels and separate 64-token correctness arrays matched literal outputs and speculative work across versions. Source/process identity, graph exposure, thermal/memory guards and service restoration were independently verified.

**Limits:** single-stream and sampled benefits are not established. Mixed graphs retain 31.55 MB of explicit tensors, excluding CUDA graph-pool allocations; total incremental graph memory was not isolated. No mixed-extension MLX4 timing, long-context graph path, other-GPU qualification, arbitrary stream-count, grammar, EXL3 or TP claim is made. Both opt-ins remain experimental and default off.

**Related work:** [#422](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/422) changes garbage collection before capture in `graphs.py`; it does not add these target-window graph families or touch their implementation files. [@jayleaton's #300](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/300) proposes generic lane interfaces and `RowGraphs`; this bounded path uses the existing Flash Next decoder. [@grearjake-star's #337](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/337) addresses lone-stream graph-slot retention for [#317](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/317). These four-stream opt-ins preserve the solo-slot policy; shared `multi.py` changes need merge review. The guarded batching control adapts optimisme's [issue #368](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/368) work and is not included in this graph diff.

items.title: feat(flash next cuda): support NVFP4 n-gram SSD offload
items.body:
## What this changes

Enables the tested Flash Next NVFP4 checkpoint to run on a single DGX Spark by offloading its n-gram tables to SSD. This supported path was previously unavailable in stock TensorFold, which rejects `--ple-on-ssd` for NVFP4 checkpoints. The existing opt-in reader is extended to read rows on demand without mapping the complete table as resident arrays.

- Supports packed NVFP4, scalar FP8 and BF16 rows, including indexed components in separate files, with the resident reader's scales and BF16 rounding.
- Bounds individual reads and closes file descriptors and read workers with the engine. Existing MLX affine tables remain supported.
- Changes storage and loading only: checkpoint weights, routed-expert kernels, target arithmetic and drafting policy stay unchanged.

Linux uses buffered `pread` with `POSIX_FADV_RANDOM`. Filesystem page-cache use remains possible; this is not direct I/O or a zero-page-cache claim.

The tested NVFP4 checkpoint is slower overall than the MLX4 checkpoint on this Spark. The exports use different precision recipes: the NVFP4 checkpoint retains higher-precision weights in some dense components and the output head, with different storage and kernel work. This PR adds a previously unsupported capability; it is not a speedup claim. Because stock TensorFold cannot run this NVFP4 SSD-offload configuration, there is no suitable like-for-like pre-change performance baseline for the new path.

## Receipt

**Environment:** v0.6.5 (`609ca419abecebdc5a059498a613680bd3aa847f`) and this SSD reader on one DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 128 GB unified memory, local NVMe). NVIDIA driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.3, PyTorch 2.13.0a0 NVIDIA 26.07 and Triton 3.7.1. Serving used four streams, context 69,632, int8 KV, six MTP drafts at confidence 0.60 and `--ple-on-ssd`.

**Checkpoints:** `Mia-AiLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` at `925d7be6c14c6c9442ef83e8f05b5a3c39304f69`; MLX compatibility/reference checkpoint `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP` at `dadefa8066e3be900a0d148d0f5a2f4eb1cf6534`.

**Exactness:**

- Mia SSD-only smoke: six literal 64-token replies preserved fresh/resumed/serial equality across two prompts (token hashes `f670a977fd2c` and `88e6afad2e4f`). All four public concurrent/solo/serial cells passed. Startup confirmed SSD n-gram reads; the original service was restored healthy.
- MLX compatibility: all same-request token arrays matched across the four ABBA arms; 24 ordinary 64-token reply arrays preserved drafted/serial and fresh/resumed equality. All 16 public concurrent/solo/serial cells passed.

**Tests:** 177 host checks passed, with three MLX-dependent checks skipped in that environment and subsequently passed separately as CPU fixtures with MLX 0.32.0. All three isolated CUDA BF16/FP8/NVFP4 SSD loader layout cases passed without failures or skips. Fixtures cover resident/SSD equality, split-file components, invalid layouts, bounded and short reads, and cleanup.

**Limits:** the full NVFP4 2k–64k prefill matrix, other CUDA devices and full-model Apple Silicon GPU tests were not run. Mac checks were small CPU fixtures. Row-format support does not qualify every complete checkpoint using that format. Performance equivalence for the existing MLX path has not been established, and no quality advantage is claimed.

## Related work and attribution

Further performance work builds on this support in two separate PRs:

- [PR338: opt-in graphs for uniform and mixed four-stream targets](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/338) reduces target-launch overhead for eligible concurrent workloads. Its receipt reports the workload-dependent gains and limits.
- [PR413: guarded SSD n-gram batching](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/413) combines gathers across multiple windows, with measured multi-stream gains and essentially unchanged single-stream throughput.

Their implementation and performance receipts remain separate from this feature PR.

Native FP4 compute remains separate in [Jürgen Schmied's #211](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/211), including the MTP scale fix credited there to @SvangenStudios. No native kernel from that PR is included here. The contribution also stays separate from [`shards.N` admission (#330)](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/330), [EXL3 read-ahead (#252)](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/252), and [server file-descriptor limits (#294)](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/294). Main, open PRs and the [Landing next list](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/286) were checked before submission; #332 and #333 concern other families/shared geometry, not this row reader. Neither optimisation, nor PR303/PR304, is included in this SSD-support diff.

items.title: fix(cuda): tool_choice "none" keeps the tools in the prompt
items.body:
## What this changes

On the CUDA server, `tool_choice: "none"` rendered the prompt without the request's tools. The tools open the prompt (the chat templates list them in the system block), so an answer-only turn at the end of an agent's tool rounds had a different prefix from every earlier turn and could not resume from any kept prompt state: it prefilled the whole conversation again.

`"none"` now renders the tools the request lists, as vLLM does by default (`exclude_tools_when_tool_choice_none` is off). It still forbids a call: the reply is parsed with no tools, exactly as before. `"required"`, a named function and `"auto"` are untouched, as is the Mac server.

The existing `test_tool_choice_shapes_the_tools_offered` asserted the old rendering for `"none"`; it now asserts the new one.

## Receipt

- Environment: this change on v0.6.4 (`6ea5ade`), against stock v0.6.4, nothing else patched. One DGX Spark (GB10), NVIDIA PyTorch 26.07 container, `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`, `serve --parallel 4 --context 98304 --kv-dtype int8` for the tool runs and `--parallel 2` for the scenario. Unit tests: macOS, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU.
- The case, three repetitions per build: a fresh agent conversation each time (system prompt, six tool calls with long results, about 57.4k tokens), greedy, thinking off, `max_tokens` 1. Request 1 is the conversation with `tool_choice: "auto"`; request 2 adds a user turn with `"none"`; request 3 is the control, the same request with `"auto"`.

  | build | request 1, cold (auto) | request 2 (none): cached tokens, seconds | request 3 (auto): cached tokens, seconds |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | stock v0.6.4 | 22.37 / 22.64 / 22.73 s | 0 of 57,085 / 57,047 / 57,001: 22.27 / 22.45 / 22.53 s | 57,477 / 57,439 / 57,393: 0.15-0.17 s |
  | this change | 22.74 / 22.80 / 22.89 s | 57,477 / 57,439 / 57,393 of 57,498 / 57,460 / 57,414: 0.17 / 0.16 / 0.18 s | 57,497 / 57,459 / 57,413: 0.11-0.12 s |

  Cold prefill is the same on both builds within run-to-run noise (request 1 differs by about 1 %), since nothing on that path changes.
- Exactness: `tools/bench_concurrent.py --levels 1,2,4 --tokens 128 --reps 2 --alone --serial`: concurrent against alone 56 of 56 equal, alone against `"draft": false` 30 of 30 equal, 0 failed (stock: the same counts). That tool does not send `tool_choice`, so I also sent a `"none"` request with tools three times (47, 120 and 53 completion tokens), each with `"draft": true` then `false`: the `token_sha` matched on all three. That check ran on an earlier build that also carried #263, #302 and two local CPU-side patches.
- Decode speed, `tools/bench_openai.py --tokens 64 --reps 5`, median tok/s, stock / this change / this change / stock: fibonacci greedy 69.8 / 69.2 / 69.0 / 68.9, fibonacci sampled 73.3 / 73.9 / 75.3 / 74.8, chat greedy 65.5 / 65.3 / 65.4 / 65.2, chat sampled 61.2 / 61.2 / 62.1 / 62.7.
- Prompt speed, `tools/prefill_cold.py`, cold TTFT in seconds at 2k / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k tokens, stock / this change / this change / stock: 1.33 / 4.09 / 7.11 / 13.21 / 26.83, then 1.26 / 3.95 / 6.90 / 13.39 / 27.10, then 1.20 / 3.63 / 6.82 / 13.22 / 26.78, then 1.20 / 3.64 / 6.78 / 13.27 / 26.97. The first stock pass is the cold one.
- Tests run: `tests/test_cuda_tool_choice.py`, 10 passed. The changed assertion and the new `test_none_keeps_the_prompt_auto_renders_and_the_reply_stays_prose` fail on v0.6.4 and pass here. Full `tests/` on the Mac: 19 failed and 1 collection error (`tests/test_glm_exl3_bits.py`, no `triton`) with and without the change; 5,119 passed before and 5,120 after. I did not compare the 19 failures name by name.
- Not run: Metal (the Mac server is unchanged), two ranks, `--vision`, and the concurrent-against-solo hash with `"none"` requests.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo.
- [x] No precision traded for speed. If the bits change, the description says which sums change and why.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release.
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: feat(flash next cuda): --checkpoint-slots sets the kept prompt states of the concurrent decoder
items.body:
## What this changes

Closes #257. Flash Next's concurrent decoder kept a hardcoded 8 prompt states (`KEEP` in `qwen4_exp/cuda/engine.py`). `--checkpoint-slots N` now sets that count for `--parallel 2` or more, as it already does for Qwen3.8-27B. The same N goes into the startup memory estimate (`indexed_stream_geometry`) and into `MultiDecoder`, so a larger N admits a smaller window instead of running over budget. The default stays 8. The value is checked on both `--tp 2` ranks, which refuse to start if they differ, and the startup line reports the count. One stream still keeps 4 and refuses the flag, as it does for the 27B.

## Receipt

- Environment: TensorFold `main` at 6ea5ade plus this branch; PyTorch 2.13 and CUDA 13.3 in the `tensorfold-dev:26.07` container; one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (96 GB, sm_120) at its 300 W default; checkpoint `turboderp/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-exl3` revision `69e33439` (EXL3 3.05 bpw, the one-GPU pack; not the MLX 4-bit checkpoint). Greedy requests, thinking off, 8 new tokens, one request at a time (interleaved, not concurrent); a fresh server for every run.
- Scenario: `--parallel 16 --context 8192`. N conversations, each with its own 300-token system prompt and a 1,500-token opening, then four rounds in round-robin order, each follow-up adding about 200 tokens. N = 6 and N = 12. The slots flag is the only difference between runs.
- Exactness: the reply hash (`token_sha`) of every turn is identical between the default and `--checkpoint-slots 16` (24 of 24 for N = 6 and 48 of 48 for N = 12, in every run). Greedy and 8 tokens, so it shows a resumed turn equals a re-read one here; `bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial` was not run.

  | Follow-up turns (rounds 2 to 4) | Kept states | Cached | Median s (p90) |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | N = 6, run 1 | 8 | 0% | 1.18 (1.27) |
  | N = 6, run 2 | **16** | **90.4%** | **0.20** (0.22) |
  | N = 6, run 3 | **16** | **90.4%** | **0.20** (0.22) |
  | N = 6, run 4 | 8 | 0% | 1.18 (1.27) |
  | N = 12, run 1 | 8 | 0% | 1.18 (1.27) |
  | N = 12, runs 2 and 3 | 16 | 0% | 1.18 (1.27) |
  | N = 12, run 4 | 8 | 0% | 1.18 (1.27) |

  Order was 8, 16, 16, 8 for each N. At N = 6 the 16 slots keep the conversations resident; at N = 12 they do not, as #257 reported: the conversations need more kept states than 16, so they still evict one another. The startup line reports the count ("8 kept prompt states" and "16 kept prompt states") and the startup estimate rises from 59.62 to 60.48 GiB, so the extra states are in the memory plan.
- Decode speed before and after: not run. Prompt speed before and after: cold prompts not run; the flag does not change prefill.
- Tests run: the new tests, the existing CLI and KV-dtype tests and the rank-settings test, 87 passed; the whole suite on macOS gave 5,129 passed, 18 failed, 1 collection error, the same failures and error as `main` there (`triton` not installed).
- Not run, and why: `--tp 2`; the MLX 4-bit checkpoint; vision; Metal.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [ ] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo. (resumed equals fresh was checked by reply hash on greedy requests; `bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial` was not run)
- [x] No precision traded for speed.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release. (no prefill or kernel change; cold prompt speed not measured)
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.
- [x] Comments and docstrings are one line. No measurements or history in the source.
- [x] No personal data, machine names, internal hosts or local paths. No AI attribution lines.

items.title: fix(flash next cuda): image prompts resume and keep prompt states, matched on their images' pixels
items.body:
**TL;DR:** with `--vision --parallel 2+`, Flash Next on CUDA never resumed a prompt that held an image, so one
screenshot in an agent's history made every later turn prefill the whole conversation again. Kept prompt states are
now matched on the prompt's ids with each image's rows replaced by a key of that image's pixels and grid. A follow-up
turn that resends the same images resumes past them, as a text turn does; a different image resumes only the text
before it. Replies are the same tokens as a fresh prefill.

## The problem

`MultiDecoder.admit` called `_slot_for(prompt, s.draft and s.vision is None)`, and `_keep_at` / `_point` returned
`None` for a stream with image positions. The guard is right as far as it goes: every image's rows are the same
placeholder id, so two prompts with different pictures in the same places would match on token ids. But it also
means an image request neither resumes nor keeps anything.

Agent clients (pi, Hermes, omp and others) keep tool-result screenshots in the history and resend it every step. From
the first image on, every step re-reads the whole conversation: at ~2,000 tok/s on a DGX Spark, a 140k-token session
spends ~70 s a step in prefill. Reported on the Flash Next Spark recipe
(MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Single-DGX-Spark-TensorFold#5: 45 min of a 60-minute pi session was prefill) and for
GLM-5.3 on Macs (#220). The GLM recipe carries the same fix for GLM's CUDA path
(MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold#11).

## The change

- `image_rows.key(prompt, vision)`: the prompt's ids with each image span's rows set to one negative int derived from
  `sha256(content_hash / grid)`. `content_hash` is the sha256 of the decoded RGB pixels the frontend already
  computes (`ImageInput.content_hash`, carried as `PreparedVisionPrompt.image_hashes`); the grid tells apart the same
  pixels resized differently. No token id is negative, so a text prompt never matches past a placeholder row.
- `MultiDecoder` matches, keeps and forks on that key instead of `s.prompt`: `_slot_for`, `_remember`, message-start
  stops, `_keep_at` and `_point`. The key lives in `fills[sid][4]`.
- A request whose images carry no hashes (spans, hashes and grids missing or inconsistent) gets `key = None` and keeps
  the old behaviour: no resume, no kept state.
- `prefill_begin(..., vision=)` attaches the prompt's image positions after `restore()` / `reset()` and **before**
  the resumed MTP tail is absorbed, so the tail rotates at the prompt's image positions as in a fresh prefill.
  `image_rows.begin` now only encodes and returns the payload. The serial `prefill` passes its `vision` the same way
  (it still refuses resume and keep points for images).

## Why a resumed state is exact

- Qwen's 3-D positions of a row depend only on the tokens and image grids before it (`image_positions`), so a prefix
  with the same ids and the same images has the same positions in any longer prompt. Text after the last image keeps
  its offset, so a kept point past an image rotates the same way in the next turn.
- `attach` installs the whole new prompt's positions; `embed` only writes image rows at or past `st.pos`, so features
  before the resume point are never used. Pooled QSA blocks that straddle the resume point are pooled once they
  complete, at their start row's position from the same table.
- Kept points are message starts and `entry_end`, never inside an image span (a span is only placeholder ids between
  `vision_start` and `vision_end`), so a resume never splits an image.
- Text rows before the first image sit at identity positions `(i, i, i)`, which give the same bits as plain rotary
  (`test_identity_image_positions_preserve_text_state_bits`). So an image prompt can resume from a text prompt's kept
  message start (a shared system prompt), and a text prompt from an image prompt's state before its first image.

## Not changed

- Every image is still encoded by the tower on each turn; only rows past the resume point are embedded. Encoding just
  the images past the resume point would save tower time but needs `QwenCudaVision.encode` and `validate_encoded` to
  accept a subset, so it is left for a follow-up.
- The serial engine (`--parallel 1`) has no image input, and GLM's CUDA path is untouched.
- Background replay already skips image streams (`Scheduler._yield`), so a replay never loses its images.

## Testing

- `tests/test_flashnext_image_keys.py` (CPU, 10): text ids unchanged, one negative key per image, keys follow pixels
  and grid, no key when images can't be told apart.
- `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_vision.py`, on the tiny model:
  - `test_a_follow_up_with_the_same_picture_resumes_like_a_fresh_prefill` (bf16 / int8 / int4 KV, image at rows 1,
    9 and 30): turn 2 resumes `len(turn 1) - 1` tokens, its tokens equal the serial reference, and its rounds, drafted
    and accepted counts equal the same request on a fresh decoder (the resumed MTP head drafts as a fresh one).
  - `test_a_resumed_picture_prompt_leaves_a_fresh_prefills_caches` (bf16 / int8): after a resumed turn the main and
    MTP KV rows are bit-identical to a fresh prefill's. It fails if the positions are attached after the MTP tail
    (the order before this change), which the token-level tests above don't catch.
  - `test_a_different_picture_or_text_resumes_only_the_text_before_it` (a different picture, the same pixels at
    another grid, the same ids as text): each resumes exactly the kept message start before the image and matches
    its reference.
  - `test_a_picture_follows_a_text_prompts_kept_message_start`: an image prompt resumes a text prompt's kept message
    start and matches its reference.
  - The existing tests still pass, including the ones that use payloads without hashes and assert nothing is kept.
- `test_flashnext_vision`, `test_flashnext_prompt_cache`, `test_flashnext_multi`, `test_flashnext_fill_arrivals` and
  `test_flashnext_fork_lanes` pass on a DGX Spark (GB10): 136 passed; the CPU files above plus `test_flashnext_fill_order`, `test_flashnext_prefix_fork`, `test_vision_server` and `test_vision_cuda`: 67 passed.

## Measured

One DGX Spark, `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` rev `7c4f1bc1`, `--parallel 2 --kv-dtype int8 --vision
--thinking` (thinking off in the requests), greedy, 64-token replies. A two-turn chat: a ~75k-token system prompt, a
user turn, the reply, a second user turn; the second request resends everything before it.

| Second turn | text only | a 640x400 PNG in the first user turn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 75,610 cached, 0.54 s | **0 cached, 67.6 s** (whole prompt again) |
| with this change | 75,610 cached, 0.30 s | **75,857 cached, 0.37 s** |

Both builds are v0.6.2 plus local patches this checkpoint needs or that don't touch prompt caching: loading its
MXFP8/NVFP4 vision tower (as #249 does), copy drafts and prompt-piece rows, and #235/#239 (in the "with" build only).
The "with" build adds this commit, merged over those.

Both versions answered the second turn correctly from the picture. The same history with the picture swapped
(red/blue, then green/yellow, then red/blue again) resumed the 75,588 tokens before the picture each time and named
each picture's colours.
