items.title: Qwen3.8-27B CUDA: --kv-dtype int8 (packed -cq 8 rows; drafted rounds -6% at 90k, -13% at 242k)
items.body:
The 27B's CUDA engine can now keep its attention caches in int8 with `--kv-dtype int8` (one GPU). The default stays bf16, and the bf16 path's output is byte-identical to 0.6.1/0.6.2 (checked on fixed inputs, 1 to 128 rows, up to 90k keys).

Why: on a DGX Spark the 27B's decode slows with depth because every round reads the whole bf16 cache (64 KiB a position over the 16 attention layers). Real long agentic sessions here sit at ~100k tokens, where a drafted round costs ~145 ms against ~106 ms at 3k. int8 halves those bytes.

## Design

- **Same scheme as Flash Next's cache**: ExLlamaV3 `-cq 8` (each group of 32 values rotated by a 32-point Hadamard, fp16 absmax scale, midpoint grid). The quantizer is Flash Next's own `kvquant.quant_groups_8`/`dequant_group_8`, so the codes and scales are bit-identical to `kvcache.quantize_ref`.
- **Packed rows** (`tensorfold/cuda/kernels/kvpack.py`): a (position, KV head) row is `head_dim` int8 codes followed by `head_dim/32` fp16 scales (272 bytes at head dim 256). A layer's cache is still one tensor indexed by position, so `grow`, `reserve`, commit copies, clones, kept states and the KV room work unchanged.
- **Drafts equal serial**: a verify window packs its keys and values *before* attention, and the tree attention dequantizes committed rows and the row's own path alike. A drafted row therefore reads exactly what serial decoding reads after a commit, which is now a byte copy of the accepted packed rows.
- **Prompts keep their bits in any chunking**: prefill stores packed rows and attends over the dequantized prefix (`kvpack.unpack`, rotated back to the model's basis). Every key, the chunk's own included, passes through its codes, so a resumed prompt equals a fresh one. The CUDA prefill attention kernel is unchanged.
- The query is rotated once (`kvpack.rotate`) and the merged output rotated back in `_merge`.
- int8 plans hold 32 (row, head) pairs an item (`PACKED_TILE`). With 16, a 16-row window over 24 heads dequantizes each key tile six times and int8 gained nothing over bf16 at 16 rows. 64 pairs spilled registers. 32 with Flash Next's reshape dequant was the fastest of the variants measured on GB10.
- Admission counts the packed bytes plus one layer's dequantized prompt read. The concurrent decoder's memory gate uses the packed row size. `--tp 2` refuses `--kv-dtype int8`.

## Measured on one DGX Spark (GB10)

Two public checkpoints:
- `Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit`, the docs' standard checkpoint;
- [`armin1/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-FP8-Mixed-LH`](https://huggingface.co/armin1/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-FP8-Mixed-LH), a ModelOpt mixed checkpoint (NVFP4 MLP with the last 8 layers in FP8, FP8 attention/DeltaNet/head), served with `--precision full`.

Both used `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` and `--parallel 3 --thinking --prefill-fp8`, with both cache dtypes in the same build (0.6.2 + this branch). Round time = decode seconds over rounds from `/health` (it separates the cache's cost from acceptance). Prompts are seeded non-repeating log lines plus one 512-token code request, greedy.

ms a drafted round:

| Prompt tokens | MLX 4-bit, bf16 | int8 | NVFP4/FP8 mixed, bf16 | int8 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,890 | 82.9 | 82.8 | 106.1 | 105.8 |
| 45,100 | 102.2 | 96.3 | 125.4 | 120.5 |
| 90,220 | 121.6 | 113.6 (−7%) | 144.9 | 136.0 (−6%) |
| 180,500 | 159.9 | 144.1 (−10%) | 184.0 | 168.3 (−9%) |
| 242,500 | 188.6 | 164.5 (−13%) | 213.1 | 186.4 (−13%) |

`"draft": false`, ms a token: MLX 4-bit 96.4 → 86.5 at 90k and 143.1 → 114.4 at 242k (−10%, −20%); NVFP4/FP8 mixed 118.4 → 108.3 and 164.3 → 136.5 (−9%, −17%). Prompt fill is within 2% of bf16. The startup estimate at the 262,144 window drops from 37.39 to 30.38 GiB (MLX) and from 43.60 to 36.59 GiB (NVFP4/FP8). Short-context decode is unchanged (code / prose tok/s, bf16 vs int8: MLX 78.8 / 50.2 vs 81.2 / 50.1, NVFP4/FP8 mixed 66.5 / 39.4 vs 66.3 / 38.6).

Tree attention alone (24 q heads / 4 KV heads, head dim 256, median of 50), ms a layer:

| Keys | 16 rows bf16 | int8 | 1 row bf16 | int8 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,048 | 0.112 | 0.134 | 0.067 | 0.097 |
| 32,768 | 0.893 | 0.729 | 0.622 | 0.427 |
| 90,000 | 2.336 | 1.839 | 1.713 | 1.125 |
| 131,072 | 3.320 | 2.576 | 2.485 | 1.587 |
| 180,000 | 4.536 | 3.507 | 3.415 | 2.162 |

Quality (100 local tasks, greedy, thinking off, 1,024 tokens; needle at 194,893 tokens):

| Checkpoint, cache | GSM8K | JSON | Code | Instructions | Greedy agreement with BF16 | Needle |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| MLX 4-bit, bf16 | 48/50 | 14/15 | 25/25 | 8/10 | 41.9% | correct |
| MLX 4-bit, int8 | 47/50 | 14/15 | 24/25 | 9/10 | 43.0% | correct |
| NVFP4/FP8 mixed, bf16 | 48/50 | 14/15 | 25/25 | 8/10 | 55.8% | correct |
| NVFP4/FP8 mixed, int8 | 49/50 | 14/15 | 25/25 | 7/10 | 55.2% | correct |

Items change in both directions:
- On NVFP4/FP8 mixed, int8 answers one GSM8K question bf16 misses and misses one instruction task. On both, it gives the unquantized model's result.
- On MLX, int8 runs one GSM8K answer to the token cap and fails one code test.
- On MLX, int8 also passes an instruction task that bf16 and the unquantized model both miss.

The EXL3 path shares the same forward and cache code but was not run end to end here.

## Tests

`tests/cuda/test_qwen27_kv_int8.py` (22 tests):
- packed codes and scales equal `kvcache.quantize_ref` bit for bit;
- `unpack` and `rotate` equal the reference H32;
- branch nodes equal their serial bits with packed caches, from 0 to 20,501 keys;
- streams in one launch equal each alone;
- packed attention matches torch on the dequantized rows;
- bf16/packed mixing and a wrong-tile plan are refused;
- every int8 prefill chunking gives the same state;
- an int8 resume equals fresh, and drafts equal serial;
- the int8 prompt tracks bf16 closely.

`tests/test_cuda_cli.py` now expects the 27B to accept `int8`. GLM still refuses it, and `int4` stays refused for the 27B. On one GB10, the attention, prefill-attention, Flash Next kvquant, all `test_qwen27_*`, CLI, geometry and KV-room suites pass (415 passed, 20 skipped).

## Not in this PR

- `int4` for the 27B.
- Two ranks.
- Fusing the dequant into the CUDA prefill attention kernel. Prompts read a bf16 copy of the prefix, one layer at a time, and admission counts it.
- The fp32 chunk partials that `_shared` writes and `_merge` reads back. They cost int8 and bf16 alike, about 0.6 ms a layer at 90k with 16 rows, and are a separate change.

items.title: feat(flash-next cuda): TENSORFOLD_PREFILL_ROWS sets the prompt piece rows
items.body:
**TL;DR:** `TENSORFOLD_PREFILL_ROWS=N` (256 to 16,384) sets Flash Next's prompt piece rows on CUDA. Unset or empty keeps today's behaviour exactly.

## The problem

Flash Next fills prompts in 2,048-row pieces, or 4,096 while idle on a DGX Spark serving the MLX checkpoint without `--vision` when the admitted window leaves room (`prompt_plan.choose`). Neither suits every deployment: the best piece size depends on the machine and on where the n-gram tables are read from, and an operator could not change it without editing the source.

## The change

- `cuda/geometry.indexed_prefill_rows()` reads `TENSORFOLD_PREFILL_ROWS`: None when unset or empty, the rows when 256 to 16,384, and a startup refusal for anything else.
- `FlashNextEngine` sizes the startup geometry's prompt buffers for N rows (one GPU or two), so the admitted window matches, and the idle plan no longer applies. A round beside live replies still takes at most 2,048 rows (`prompt_plan.pass_limit`).
- EXL3 packs keep their own buffers and ignore it.
- `docs/recipes/qwen3.8-flash-next.md` describes the pieces and the variable.

Replies are the same tokens at any setting; only prompt speed and the startup estimate change.

## Testing

- `tests/test_flash_next_prefill_rows_env.py`: unset and empty, accepted values, refused values.
- On one DGX Spark (Flash Next MLX 4-bit, `--parallel 5 --context 262144 --kv-dtype int8 --ple-on-ssd --vision`), `TENSORFOLD_PREFILL_ROWS=3072` starts with "idle prompt pieces 3072 rows".
- The geometry, capacity and Flash Next memory tests pass. `tests/test_flash_next_pass_rows.py` fails the same way on `main` (`MultiDecoder` has no `streams` in its fixture).

items.title: fix(server): image parts in tool-result messages are accepted, rendered inside the tool response
items.body:
**TL;DR:** with `--vision`, a tool result that carries an image (`{"role": "tool", "content": [text, image_url]}`, an agent's screenshot) is now accepted and rendered by the checkpoint's own template inside its tool response, as a user image is. Until now it was HTTP 400, and since agents replay their history, every later request of the session was refused too.

## Problem

`normalize_messages` (`server/messages.py`) and `split_images` (`vision/images.py`) refuse any image part outside a user message:

```
HTTP 400: image_url parts are supported only in user messages
```

Agent harnesses keep screenshots and other vision results in tool messages, and every later request resends that history. Once one tool returns an image, each request is refused until the client edits its history. The session is stuck. Reported on the GLM-5.3 two-Spark recipe (MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold#28, thanks @d4rkdpg), whose agents now have to strip the images and retry.

The vision templates already handle this case. GLM-5.3's `render_tool_response` passes a tool message's content through `visible_text`, which writes `<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>` for an image part. Qwen3.5/3.8's tool branch renders `render_content(message.content, true)`, which writes `<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>` and counts the image. transformers' `apply_chat_template` (the Mac) renders them the same way as the CUDA server's `ChatTemplate`, so both servers render the image once the validators let it through.

## Fix

- `normalize_messages` and `split_images` take `image_url` parts in **user and tool** messages. System, developer and assistant images are still refused.
- The image becomes the processor's image part in place, so the template renders it inside the tool response. The frontends' check (one marker for each image) still guards against a template that would drop one.
- Responses API: a `function_call_output` may carry `input_image` parts beside `input_text`. The tool message then gets `image_url` parts. A text-only output is still one string, as before.
- Limits are unchanged. Tool-result images count toward `--vision-max-images` with the rest of the history, as `docs/vision.md` already said for images a client resends.
- Without `--vision`, any image part is still refused, as before.

**Same bits:** text-only requests take the same code path and render the same prompt. Only requests that were refused before change.

## Evidence

- On the real checkpoints' templates (`chat_template.jinja` from `Vontra/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP` and `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`), a session with a user image, a screenshot tool call and a follow-up renders exactly two image markers, with thinking on and off. The screenshot sits inside its `<tool_response>`, after its text, and after the user's image.
- Before this change, 15 of the new and updated tests fail: the refusal, plus the role tests' new message. With it, they all pass.

## Tests

- `tests/test_vision_tool_results.py` (new): the session above through each cached checkpoint's own template, rendered with `ChatTemplate` (GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B, Flash Next; a checkpoint that is not cached is skipped).
- `tests/test_vision_images.py`: system, developer and assistant images are refused, and a tool result keeps its images in prompt order without touching the caller's messages.
- `tests/test_vision_server.py`: `normalize_messages` keeps a tool result's images and still refuses them without vision. The Mac `prepare_prompt` path and the CUDA `prepare` path both render the screenshot in place.
- `tests/test_responses_api.py`: a `function_call_output` with `input_image` becomes a tool message with an `image_url` part, and other part types are still refused.
- CPU only, in an NVIDIA PyTorch container (aarch64, no `mlx`):
  - The touched files: 168 passed, 2 skipped (the Qwen3.8-27B template is not cached here).
  - `pytest tests --ignore=tests/cuda -k 'vision or image or responses or messages or template or server or tool'`: 831 passed on this branch and 824 on `main`, with the same 44 failures and 2 collection errors on both. All of them need `mlx` (`test_lane_server`, `test_request_reasoning`, `test_history_after_tool`, `test_alternating_kv`, `test_dflash_tree_search`).
- Still to run: a live request with a screenshot tool result on a vision server (CUDA: Qwen3.8 or Flash Next with `--vision`; Mac: GLM-5.3-Flash). I'll post the replies here.

Docs: `docs/vision.md` and `docs/api.md` name tool results as a place for images.

items.title: Flash Next CUDA: /v1/decisions scores labels from the prompt's last logits, the questions filling in one pass
items.body:
0.6.1 added `POST /v1/decisions`, but on CUDA it needs the engine's `score_labels`, which Flash Next does not have:
`this model's CUDA engine does not score decision labels`. This adds it, on one GPU.

## What changes

- **`FlashNextEngine.score_labels` / `score_labels_many`** (`families/qwen4_exp/cuda/engine.py`): a one-token greedy request with `draft=False`, whose collector reads the label logits and the full-vocabulary logsumexp at the prompt's last position. `draft=False` means the decision neither resumes from nor leaves a kept prompt state, so decisions never evict a conversation's kept end (that table is only 8 entries). One GPU only, like logprobs (`supports_logprobs`).
- **`LabelProbabilities`** (`engine/probabilities.py`) and **`capture`** (`cuda/logprobs.py`): when the collector carries `labels`, `capture` also gathers those columns of the row it already reduces; nothing else changes for logprobs.
- **`Scheduler.submit_many`** (`cuda/scheduler.py`): queues several one-shot requests from one thread. Submitted one by one from threads, the first woke the worker, which filled it alone; queued together they fill in one pass (`ENDS = 16`).
- **The decisions route** (`cuda/server.py`) uses `score_labels_many` when the engine has it and there are several questions; otherwise it keeps the per-question loop.
- **`MultiDecoder._pass_rows`** (`families/qwen4_exp/cuda/multi.py`): while a decision fills, a round's prompt pass is not share-limited. A decision waits on its whole prompt and nothing after it; share-sized pieces between rounds made three short prompts take ~0.9 s beside decoding chats.

## Measured (one DGX Spark, GB10; MLX 4-bit checkpoint, `--parallel 5`, int8 KV, v0.6.1 + this branch)

A decision request of 2 or 3 choice questions (4 to 7 options, ~150 tokens of prompt each):

| | 1 question | 2 questions | 3 questions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle server, median | 265 ms | 368 ms (2-question schema: 428 ms with 7 + 5 options) | 457–470 ms |
| Beside 1 / 2 decoding chats (3 questions) | | | 542–577 / 608 ms |

The 3 prompts fill in one pass (`rows=458 pieces=3`, 0.415 s). A prompt pass has a large fixed cost at this size
(1,100 tok/s at 458 rows against 1,730 at 4,096), which is most of the request. With `--parallel 5` and 3 decoding chats, a third question waits for a free slot (two passes, ~0.9 s).

## Checks

- **Same bits alone and grouped:** each question's probabilities alone equal the same question's in a 3-question request (9/9 cases), and a request beside 2 decoding chats equals the same request on an idle server.
- **Chats unchanged:** greedy outputs of our fixed 5-prompt fingerprint are byte-identical with and without this branch.
- **CPU tests:** `tests/test_flash_next_decisions.py` (collector; the route scores every question in one call, and falls
  back to one by one without `score_labels_many`) plus `tests/test_decisions.py` and `tests/test_cuda_server_errors.py`: 241 passed, 2 skipped.
- **Not tested:** two ranks (`--tp 2`, refused as for logprobs), image inputs in a decision, a CUDA test under `tests/cuda`.

## Context

We use it to route an assistant's messages before the answer (does it need the user's records, how to fetch them,
which period): on 43 labelled messages, the decisions matched the labels 43/43, 24/25 and 24/25, against three constrained generations before at 400–720 ms.

items.title: feat(cuda): add Flash Next image input and offline EXL3 vision adapter
items.body:
Enable image prompts for the Flash Next CUDA engine on one GPU with `--parallel 2` or more. Stock v0.5.0 restricts its vision path to dense Qwen3.5, while Flash Next needs feature injection across hyperconnection streams and multimodal positions in sparse attention.

This is an image-only port of MiaAI-Lab patch 0008, adapted to v0.5 forward/scheduler/grammar APIs with attribution and the original MIT license. It adds image-row embeddings, interleaved mRoPE and decode offsets, pooled-key positions, frontend/family validation and tower admission/warmup. Image states never enter the text-prefix cache; equal placeholder IDs are insufficient to identify pixels. Video, distributed vision and yieldable image requests are excluded.

EXL3 vision sidecars need a separate offline adapter: reconstruct represented quantized weights into a hashed FP16 artifact, combine split QKV in preference to retained fused copies, trim configured MLP padding and load it explicitly via `TENSORFOLD_VISION_WEIGHTS`. Hash both source weights and config before following HF blob symlinks. Conversion is not part of cold serving startup. An external tower is counted once in admission. BF16 tower arithmetic differs from native EXL3 execution; this is not a claim of numerical identity.

Validation on DGX Spark/GB10:
- 157 relevant CPU tests passed; one optional test skipped.
- Independent vision CUDA suite: 16 passed, including chunk invariance, BF16/int8 KV, drafted-versus-serial output and image cache isolation.
- Combined with #124 and the consolidated EXL3 fix: 70 CUDA tests passed.
- Actual 4.05-bpw EXL3 pack with four 262K streams: loaded with the converted 0.84-GiB tower and passed color changes, counting, OCR, chart reading, two images and image follow-up (7/7).

This branch is based on v0.5.0 and is independent of #124 and #145. The native 4.05 pack additionally requires #145 for its consolidated n-gram layout. #124 overlaps the prefill functions and needs integration preserving its text snapshots while keeping image states uncached. Paired native control also passed 7/7 image fixtures. Full encoders on five identical processed-patch inputs had cosine similarity 0.997970–0.999716 and relative L2 difference 2.389–6.398%; this is close, not numerical identity or general vision quality parity. The reconstructed tower uses BF16 arithmetic versus native FP16 EXL3 execution.

Text regression with the combined branch: 20/20 coding, 10/10 tools, 10/10 JSON, 4/4 retrieval through 240K and 3/3 actual drafted/serial token sequences. Same-checkpoint arithmetic was 49/50 versus native EXL3 50/50 with matched 4096-token budgets; the runtime discrepancy remains under investigation and this PR does not claim universal parity. These fixes remain experimental and have not replaced our production service.

items.title: fix(qwen4_exp cuda): resume identical resends and thinking turns
items.body:
Fixes #98.

Flash Next kept each prompt's state at its end, and a resume needs a strictly shorter prefix. So an identical
resend, or a next turn with thinking on (which renders the last prompt token differently), always prefilled in
full. This keeps the entry at `len(prompt) - 1`, as the 27B does, for one stream, `--parallel` and `--tp 2`.

One DGX Spark, `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`, 11.7K-token prompt, time to first token:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same prompt again | 5.2 s | 0.07 s |
| Next turn, thinking on | 5.2 s | 0.13 s |
| Next turn, thinking off | 0.20 s | 0.20 s |

The same holds with `--parallel 4`, and every reply equals its `"draft": false` reply. The kept state is taken
inside the chunk that holds it, as the 27B's prefill does, so a prompt costs no extra forward.

items.title: perf(glm5_next cuda): DFlash2's block attention reads only its sliding window; its context in a ring of that window
items.body:
**TL;DR:** every layer of GLM-5.3-Flash's DFlash2 drafter is `sliding_attention` with a 2,048-row window, but `_dattn_kernel` read every context row from position 0 and masked all but the window, and the drafter kept `capacity` rows of keys and values. The block attention now starts at the window's first tile, and the context lives in a ring of window + block + a tile (2,176 rows). Same draft bits; at 196k context the block attention goes from 16.2 ms to 0.20 ms, and the drafter's context memory no longer grows with the window.

## The problem

- `_dattn_kernel` looped `for start in range(0, klen, BK)`: at context end `s` it loaded every key and value from 0 to `s + block`, then masked everything older than `s - window`. A block pass cost grew linearly with the context although only ~2,048 rows can contribute.
- `Drafter` allocated `capacity + block` rows of K/V for each of its 5 layers: 10 KiB a token on each rank, 10 GiB at a 1,048,576-token window. The startup estimate (`draft_geometry`, shared with the 27B's drafter) counted two copies of it, 20 GiB.
- The estimate also counted the draft model's weights as its checkpoint at 4 bytes a value (4.36 GiB a rank). The engine actually holds 4-bit copies (0.63 GiB a rank).

## The change

- **Window loop** (`dflash2._dattn_kernel`): the loop starts at the 64-row tile holding `s - window`. Every skipped tile is masked for every query, and a fully masked tile leaves the running max, sum and accumulator bit for bit unchanged (`max(-1e30, -inf) = -1e30`, `alpha = exp(0) = 1`, `p = 0`). The tiles that still run are the same tiles at the same offsets, so the output has the same bits. `SKIP=False` keeps the old loop as the reference the tests compare against.
- **Ring** (`Drafter(ring=True)`, `TF_GLM_DRAFT_RING`, default on): keys and values go in a ring of `geometry.draft_ring_rows(window, block)` = 2,176 rows, addressed modulo the ring (`RING` in the kernel, `Drafter._slots` for writes). The drafts are unchanged. When the window already exceeds `capacity + block`, the flat buffer is kept. `TF_GLM_DRAFT_RING=0` keeps the flat buffer, and it joins the two ranks' settings check.
- **Kept prompts** (`decode`): a flat buffer still holds a kept prompt's drafter rows after the reply, but a ring overwrites them. So `take_snapshot` copies the window (`Snapshot.drafter_rows`, 20 MiB a rank at DFlash2's sizes), `restore` puts it back and refuses a ring restore without one, `save_rows` drops it along with `drafter_end`, and `snapshot_bytes` counts it within `TF_GLM_CACHE_GIB`.
- **Estimate** (`geometry.dflash2_geometry`, `geometry.dflash2_weights`, `capacity.admit(draft_weights=)`): one context copy, the one the engine allocates. With the ring it is a constant 21.25 MiB; flat, it is 10,240 B a slot, where it used to be 20,480. The weights are counted as held: 4-bit copies (k and v twice, as in `qkv` and `kv`), BF16 norms and selector projection, and the selector's float32 codebooks. The 27B's `draft_geometry` is untouched.
- `docs/recipes/glm-5.3-flash.md`: one paragraph.

## Measurements

One DGX Spark (GB10), one rank's dimensions of GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2 (16 query heads, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128, block 8). These are **kernel-only** timings of the block attention, not end-to-end decode:

| Context | Before (5 layers) | After (5 layers) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 196k | 16.2 ms | 0.20 ms |
| 524k | 43 ms | 0.20 ms |

A re-run of the same kernel on this branch, on the same Spark while another model server was resident (one layer, fastest of 7): old loop 0.51 / 6.40 / 17.8 ms at 16k / 196k / 524k, window loop 0.037 ms and ring 0.039 ms at all three. The old loop's absolute times vary with what else holds the memory bus. The new loop's time doesn't depend on the context.

Memory, per rank, at a 1,048,576-token window: the drafter's context is 21 MiB (was 10 GiB allocated and 20 GiB in the estimate). The drafter's weights are estimated at 0.63 GiB (was 4.36 GiB).

## Tests

- `tests/cuda/test_glm_draft_ring.py` (new, small, no engine): **8 passed** on the Spark.
  - The window loop and the ring give bitwise the output of the loop from tile 0, for windows 2,047 and 48, causal and not, and context ends up to 12,345 rows, with stale rows in the ring.
  - The synthetic drafter of `test_glm_engine` gives the same candidates, logits and selector rows with the ring as with the flat buffer, bit for bit, over 160 rounds. The contexts run from 3.5k to 9k rows, and a kept state is taken, the ring overwritten by 3,000 rows and the state restored. This runs both eager and with CUDA graphs.
- `tests/test_glm_draft_ring.py` (new, CPU): the ring size, both estimates (checked against GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2's shapes), and the kept-state plumbing. The plumbing check: after a reply has wrapped the ring three times, a restored state reads the same window as a flat drafter and a cold start, a saved state drops the window, and a ring restore without a window is refused.
- CPU, in the `tensorfold` CUDA image: `test_glm_draft_ring`, `test_glm_cuda_kept`, `test_cuda_geometry`, `test_cuda_capacity`, `test_cuda_admission`, `test_cuda_failed_admission`, `test_cuda_parallel_admission`, `test_flash_capacity_dispatch`, `test_glm_drafter_choice`, `test_glm5_memory`, `test_glm5_next_family` and `test_glm_tool_calls`: **188 passed, 2 skipped**. The whole `tests/` directory was not run to completion here: in this image two MLX-only modules fail to collect, and the run was stopped for time.
- `tests/cuda/test_glm_engine.py`: **14 passed, 5 errors**. The passing tests include DFlash2 replies equal to serial, the drafter choice, and resumed prompts equal to fresh prefills; the ring is on by default there, since 2,176 < 2,560 + 8. The 5 errors are the `engine_n` (no MTP head, DFlash2 only) and `engine_long` (past the dense limit) fixtures. Admission refused them ("startup memory budget cannot fit requested context 2600") because another model server was holding that Spark's memory. They didn't run; they did not fail on the change.
- Not run: two-Spark serving with the real GLM-5.3-Flash and DFlash2 checkpoints on this branch.

items.title: perf(glm): an idle rank 1 waits on the rendezvous TCP store, not in a spinning all-gather
items.body:
**TL;DR:** on GLM-5.3-Flash's two-rank CUDA engine, an idle rank 1 no longer busy-waits for the next request. Rank 0 rings a key in the rendezvous TCPStore that NCCL already holds before each request's header; rank 1 blocks on that socket first, then runs the same all-gathers as before. Replies and the request exchange are unchanged.

## The problem

Between requests, rank 1 waits for the next request inside the header's all-gather (`follow` -> `_share`). That wait is an NCCL kernel spinning on its GPU plus a host thread spinning in the device-to-host copy that waits for it, and it lasts for as long as the server stays idle. On two DGX Sparks serving GLM-5.3-Flash, an idle rank 1 sits at **~96% GPU utilization and ~210% CPU** (two cores) with no request in flight: power, heat, and a GPU that other work on that machine can't use.

## The change

In `families/glm5_next/cuda/engine.py`:

- `_ring()` (rank 0): right before each request's `_share(header)`, sets `tf_glm_request_<n>` in `self.comm.store`, the `TCPStore` `NCCL` already creates for the rendezvous.
- `_await_bell()` (rank 1): at the top of each `follow()` iteration, blocks on `store.wait([key])`, deletes the consumed key, then enters the all-gathers as before.
- Keys are numbered per request, so a ring sent while rank 1 is still busy with the previous request is not lost.
- An idle hour's wait timeout is retried; any other store error (rank 0 gone, connection reset) raises instead of waiting forever.
- Communicators without a `store` attribute (test fakes) skip the doorbell entirely.

The header, prompt and grammar still go through `_share` exactly as before; the bell only decides when rank 1 starts waiting on the GPU.

## Measurements

- Before: idle rank 1 at ~96% GPU and ~210% CPU on two DGX Sparks.
- After (measured on two DGX Sparks serving GLM-5.3-Flash with this change on top of other local patches): idle rank 1 at **0% GPU and ~10% CPU**. Replies were unchanged (the same greedy reply hashes for 12k/50k/149k-token prompts, and drafted replies equal to `"draft": false`). The per-request cost of the extra store round trip (one small TCP set/wait on the rendezvous link) was not measured separately; prefill timings stayed within run-to-run noise.

## Tests

- `tests/test_glm_idle_bell.py` (CPU only, a real `TCPStore` on localhost with the two ranks as threads): rank 1 stays blocked until rank 0 rings, then follows 3 requests in order and the consumed keys are deleted; rings sent before rank 1 waits are not lost; idle timeouts are retried and other store errors raise; no store means no doorbell. **4 passed.**
- Checked that torch's real timeout text matches the retry test (`DistStoreError: wait timeout after 1000ms, keys: /nope`).
- In `tensorfold-glm53:v0.5.0` (NVIDIA PyTorch container, aarch64), `pytest tests --ignore=tests/cuda -k 'glm or capacity or geometry or cuda'`: **1005 passed, 79 skipped**. That's the same as unmodified `main` (1001 passed) plus the 4 new tests. The 2 collection errors (`test_alternating_kv.py`, `test_dflash_tree_search.py`) need `mlx` and fail the same way on `main`.
- Not run: the GPU engine tests (`tests/cuda/test_glm_*`), and a two-rank GLM-5.3-Flash server with this patch.

items.title: fix: stream tool-call arguments from the CUDA server
items.body:
The CUDA server sends nothing while a tool call is being written. A reply that writes a whole file in one `write` call streams no bytes until the reply ends, so clients with an idle timeout drop it: pi through LiteLLM, and Node's `fetch` (undici), both cut the body after ~300 s of silence and report `terminated`. The harness retries, the same prompt regenerates the same call, and it fails again at the same place.

This is the second half of #99, which its author closed. That PR sent empty keepalive deltas. This one streams the call's arguments as they are written, the way the Mac server already does, so the client sees progress and gets the call without waiting for the end parser. References are at `main` (7a00336).

## Cause

`App.run` hides tool-call markup from the answer (`src/tensorfold/cuda/server.py:304`), `on_tokens` emits only visible text (`:332`), and the handler sends the calls only after `run` returns (`:532`). The Mac server feeds the answer into `ToolCallStreamer` and emits its deltas as they arrive (`src/tensorfold/server/app.py:431`). The CUDA server never got that step.

## The change

- `run` builds a `ToolCallStreamer(tools)` when the request has tools and allows parallel calls. Each round it feeds the raw answer (never the reasoning) and emits the streamer's deltas after the visible-text delta: a header with the call's `id` and `name`, then `arguments` pieces.
- `run` returns `calls_streamed`, the number of calls already sent. The handler sends only the calls after those, i.e. the ones the streamer could not follow, from the end parser as before.
- Requests with `parallel_tool_calls: false` keep the end parser, which picks their single call (#21).
- The cancellation check still runs every round, with or without new text.

## Tests

- `tests/test_cuda_tool_choice.py`: the streamed required call now arrives as one header naming `get_weather` followed by argument deltas that join to `{"city": "Oslo"}`. A new test checks that `parallel_tool_calls: false` still sends the call in one piece.
- `tests/test_cuda_stop_strings.py`: the streaming helper merges argument deltas by index. The stop-string test that puts a second call after `STOP` still gets only the first call, so a call past the cut does not stream.

On macOS the full suite gives 2956 passed, 701 skipped. On a DGX Spark (NVIDIA PyTorch 26.07), the 21 files that exercise the CUDA server and `ToolCallStreamer` give 649 passed, 15 skipped, against 648 on `main`; the extra one is the new test.

## On the GPU

One DGX Spark (GB10), `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`, `--parallel 3 --context 262144 --kv-dtype int8 --mtp-drafts 6 --mtp-confidence 0.60 --ple-on-ssd`. One streamed request offering a `write(path, content)` tool, asking for a single-file Breakout game in one call:

| Thinking off | `main` (7a00336) | this branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| reply | 16,170 tokens, 220 s | 16,170 tokens, 223 s |
| first tool-call bytes | 220.1 s | 0.9 s |
| longest gap between SSE events | 219.4 s | 0.7 s |
| tool-call chunks | 1 | 4,123 |
| the call | `index.html`, 47,443 chars | the same bytes |

The two replies are identical: the change sends the same tokens, only earlier. With thinking on, this branch streamed 25k characters of reasoning, then the call from 156 s to the end at 517 s (35,035 tokens, a 71,617-character file) with no gap over 0.5 s. On `main` that call's 361 s would pass silent, over the ~300 s idle cut of Node's `fetch` and LiteLLM.

## Not covered

- A non-streamed reply still sends its headers only when done.
- A very long prefill before the first token is still silent.
- `parallel_tool_calls: false` requests still hold their call until the reply ends.

items.title: Fix #98: engage CUDA prefix retention on Flash Next (keep cache entry one token early)
items.body:
Fixes #98.

## Problem

On the CUDA lane, Flash Next (`qwen4_exp`) remembered the **whole prompt** as its prefix-cache entry and matched only an exact token-prefix-extension. Flash Next is a reasoning model, so the next turn re-renders the assistant boundary (a stripped `<think>` plus two newlines), which changes the **last token** of the previous prompt. The stored full-prompt entry is then no longer a prefix of the next turn, `_slot_for` / `_resume` find nothing, `cached = 0`, and every turn pays a full prefill — exactly what #98 reports.

It reproduces only with **thinking on** (the default): with the reasoning boundary the last token diverges by exactly one token (`…assistant\n` → `…assistant\n<think>\n\n…`); with thinking off the full-prompt entry already matches.

## Fix

The dense 27B (`qwen3_5`) already avoids this by keeping its cache entry **one token early** (`entry_end`). This ports the same idea to `qwen4_exp`:

- `decode.prefill` gains `keep_at`: it forces a chunk boundary onto `keep_at`, captures the committed state there (a `resume` dict `{state, tail}`), then absorbs token `keep_at` into the MTP head exactly as a resume does. The kept state's bits match a fresh `prefill(prompt[:keep_at])` and the current request is unchanged; it returns `(first, kept)` when `keep_at` is set.
- `engine.entry_end` + both remember paths (concurrent `MultiDecoder.admit` and single-stream `_decode`) store `prompt[:entry_end]` with that early state. `entry_end` is applied on one GPU only, so the two-rank path (which hands rank 1 a fixed resume point) is untouched.

Output stays exact regardless: every drafted token is verified against the target and the reused KV rows come from the retained slot, so a wrong MTP resume tail could only lower draft acceptance, never change the reply.

## Results

1× DGX Spark (GB10), `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`, `--parallel 5 --context 262144 --kv-dtype int8`, thinking on. Controlled A/B: clean `v0.5.0` (worktree at `9cd52ab`) vs the same + this patch, identical image and flags.

| ctx | prompt toks | PP tok/s | TG tok/s | cold TTFT | warm TTFT (this PR) | speedup | cached toks | answer correct |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2k   | 1,989   | 1,912 | 53.8 | 1.04 s   | 0.316 s | 3×   | 1,988   | yes |
| 16k  | 15,782  | 2,214 | 55.2 | 7.13 s   | 0.193 s | 37×  | 15,781  | yes |
| 64k  | 65,222  | 2,154 | 67.0 | 30.28 s  | 0.198 s | 153× | 65,221  | yes |
| 128k | 131,166 | 1,985 | 61.1 | 66.09 s  | 0.205 s | 323× | 131,165 | yes |
| 200k | 206,917 | 1,839 | 51.4 | 112.50 s | 0.216 s | 521× | 206,916 | yes |

- **Before (stock v0.5.0, same config):** `cached = 0` and warm TTFT = cold TTFT (1×) at every size — full re-prefill each turn.
- `cached` = prompt − 1 confirms the one-token-early entry.
- **Correctness:** a fact buried at ~80% depth is retrieved correctly on the resumed turn at every size up to 200k (thinking on and off); output is deterministic on re-run; draft acceptance on a resumed turn is not degraded (57% vs 53% cold).
- **No regression:** cold PP/TG match the unpatched build; `tools/bench.py` decode 69.3 code / 55.7 chat tok/s; `tools/toolcheck.py` OK.
- Validated on both CUDA paths: concurrent (`--parallel 4/5`) and single-stream (`--parallel 1`).

## Not in this change (follow-ups)

- Message-start snapshots via `resume_points` / `points` (needs multi-stop capture in `prefill`), for reuse when an earlier turn is edited.
- Resuming past the previous reply (this reuses up to the prompt end, one token early, like `qwen3_5`).
- The two-rank path.

items.title: perf: Flash Next lists QSA blocks past 131,072 keys in tiles (256k prompts 2.1x faster, same bits)
items.body:
**TL;DR: prompts past 131,072 tokens no longer slow down sharply, with the same bits and no setting to change.** A 250k-token prompt on one DGX Spark takes 143-145 s instead of 306-311 s. Up to 131,072 keys nothing changes.

## The problem

Flash Next's QSA selection (`_select` in `families/qwen4_exp/cuda/attention.py`) holds a row's block scores in registers: `next_pow2(blocks)` values a row, one 4-key block each. Up to 32,768 blocks (131,072 keys) that fits. Past it the array spills to local memory, and the kernel gets about 34x slower from one position to the next. One layer, one 256-row prompt block, one DGX Spark:

| Keys | `_scores` | `_select` | attention |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 65,536 | 0.84 ms | 0.20 ms | 1.31 ms |
| 131,072 | 1.66 ms | 0.78 ms | 2.24 ms |
| 135,168 | 1.72 ms | **26.41 ms** | 2.36 ms |
| 262,144 | 3.31 ms | **27.21 ms** | 2.93 ms |

A 256k-token prompt runs its second half as 512 row blocks x 12 QSA layers at ~27 ms each: about 165 s, half of its prefill. Decode windows past 131,072 keys pay it too (0.51 ms a layer at 7 rows).

## The change

`_select_tiles` lists the same blocks for rows with more blocks than `_select`'s registers hold. It reads the row in tiles (4,096 blocks for a prompt's row blocks, 8,192 for decode windows). It finds the same cut, the 512th largest order-preserving key, by radix select: one byte a pass from the top, with `tl.histogram` over the keys that share the cut's leading bytes. Then it places every key above the cut, and the lowest-id keys equal to it, in block order, exactly as `_select` does. `_launch_select` keeps `_select` while a row fits its registers, so every row up to 131,072 keys runs the same kernel as before.

| Keys | `_select` | `_select_tiles` |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 135,168, 256-row prompt block | 26.41 ms | 0.69 ms |
| 262,144, 256-row prompt block | 27.21 ms | 1.51 ms |
| 262,144, 7-row decode window | 0.51 ms | 0.25 ms |

## Results

One DGX Spark, MLX 4-bit checkpoint.

In one process with a 262,144-token cache (`select_ab`: the release's selection and this PR's, same engine):

| Prompt | 0.3.6.3 | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 250k tokens of prose, bf16 KV | 311.4 s | **145.0 s** |
| 250k tokens of prose, int8 KV (this PR first) | 306.4 s | **143.4 s** |
| 140k tokens of code, int8 KV (this PR first) | 86.3 s | **73.8 s** |

Served: `--parallel 2 --context 262144 --kv-dtype int8`, prompt to first token (sparkDash's prefill ladder). The "before" column is 0.3.6.2, whose `attention.py` is 0.3.6.3's.

| Prompt | Before | This PR |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8k | 3.4 s | 3.3 s |
| 32k | 13.1 s | 13.1 s |
| 256k | 300.9 s | **130.3 s** |

`llm_context_benchmarks` (ivanfioravanti), same server, real prose and Python at 256k:

| Prompt | Before | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| prose, prompt tok/s | 783 | **1,714** |
| code, prompt tok/s | 805 | **1,713** |

## Checks

- New test `test_qsa_rows_past_the_register_width_list_the_same_blocks`: a 7-row decode window and a 256-row prompt block, rows straddling 131,072 keys, 200k keys and the full 262,151-slot cache. It covers real, tied and all-equal scores, and checks two things: `_launch_select`'s lists equal `_select`'s at full width, and they equal the plain reference (the 512 best blocks, lower ids among equal scores, in block order, then the tail).
- In one process, bf16 and int8 KV: the state after 140k- and 250k-token prompts is identical with both selections. That covers the first token, the last row's streams, the DeltaNet states and conv windows, the n-gram tail, every KV, indexer and pooled cache, and the MTP caches (82 tensors). So are 64 drafted tokens after the 140k prompt, greedy and sampled.
- Flash Next CUDA and CPU tests: 364 passed, 11 skipped (Metal-only modules, optional EXL3 and kernel modules), 0 failed.
- Teacher-forced NLL through the prompt and the decode path: 119,980 of 119,980 values equal to the values stored from release 0.3.5.1.
- Server, bf16 KV, two streams at 262,144: 55 replayed benchmark replies (GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, HumanEval) byte-identical to the replies stored from an earlier release. Repeat, concurrent and drafted-vs-serial each 9/9. Needles at 6k, 16k, 60k, 140k and 250k found 15/15.
- Server, int8 KV: repeat and concurrent 9/9.

items.title: fix: the CUDA server types Qwen tool parameters by the tool's schema
items.body:
**TL;DR:** on CUDA, a Qwen tool call's array, object, number and boolean parameters reach the client as JSON *strings*. With this change they arrive as typed JSON values, as the Mac server has returned them since 0.3.5 (#28). It changes 6 lines in `cuda/reply_text.py` and reuses the Mac server's `decode_parameter`.

## The problem

Qwen3.8 writes tool calls as `<function=name><parameter=k>value</parameter></function>`. The Mac server decodes each value by the tool's JSON schema (`tool_parameters.decode_parameter`, from #28). `cuda/reply_text.parse_tool_calls` never got that step and keeps every value as text. For example, a research agent's `finish(paths: array)` call on a DGX Spark (0.3.6.2, Qwen3.8 Flash Next, MLX 4-bit):

```
before: {"paths":"[\"https://a.example/1\", \"https://b.example/2\"]"}
after:  {"paths":["https://a.example/1","https://b.example/2"]}
```

Clients that validate arguments against the schema reject the call, and clients that don't pass a string where the tool expects a list.

## The change

`parse_tool_calls` builds `parameter_schemas(tools)` once per reply. Each `<parameter>` value then goes through `decode_parameter(value, schema)`, the same function and rules the Mac server uses:
- array, object, boolean, integer, number and null parameters decode when the text is valid JSON of that type;
- anything else keeps its exact text, including strings, untyped parameters, parameters missing from the schema, and text that isn't valid JSON of the declared type.

JSON-bodied and GLM calls are unchanged: they were already typed.

## Tests

- `tests/test_tool_parameter_types.py`: the existing parametrized check (8 kinds × 3 stream steps) now also runs the CUDA parser, with and without `max_calls`.
- `tests/test_glm_tool_calls.py::test_qwen_function_blocks_are_unchanged`: this test pinned the difference ("the CUDA server keeps them as text", added in 1fc5915). It now expects `days: 3` from both parsers. If that difference was deliberate, say so and I'll rework this.
- Without the fix, the updated tests fail 16 cases; with it they pass.
- Tool-call and server tests in `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3` (`test_tool_*`, `test_glm_tool_calls`, `test_cuda_tool_choice`, `test_cuda_server_stream`, `test_server_openai_compat`): **132 passed, 5 skipped, 2 failed**. The 2 failures are in `test_tool_parameters_null.py::test_http_*` and fail the same way on unmodified `main`, because they import `mlx`, which isn't available on Linux.
- Live check on one DGX Spark (`tensorfold serve Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP --parallel 4 --kv-dtype int8`): a `finish(paths: array)` call returns `paths` as a JSON array, both streamed and non-streamed.

items.title: perf(qwen3_5 cuda): keep the prompt-end cache entry one token before the prompt's end
items.body:
## Summary

The Qwen3.8-27B chat template ends the generation prompt in `<think>` and a newline (token 198). When the next request sends that turn back without its reasoning, the template renders it as `<think>`, two newlines (token 271), `</think>` (the checkpoint's `chat_template.jinja:111-117` and `:168`). The next prompt then differs from the previous one in the previous prompt's final token. The cache entry for the whole previous prompt is not a prefix of it, so the conversation is prefilled from an older entry or from the start.

A turn comes back without reasoning when the client drops `reasoning_content` from the assistant message, when the reply had no reasoning (the server then omits the field, `cuda/server.py:469-470`), or when the history was produced elsewhere.

Since 0.3.6.2 the 27B also keeps states at message starts (`cuda/markers.py:28-46`, `engine.py:128-144`): the second message's start and the last assistant start, each at least `MIN_GAP` = 256 tokens past the resumed prefix. A prompt whose last assistant start is kept keeps no prompt-end entry, since that start lies a few tokens before its end, and its next turn resumes from that start, on `main` as here. A prompt whose last assistant start is less than 256 tokens past its resumed prefix keeps a prompt-end entry, and that is the entry that misses.

Both 27B prefix caches now keep the prompt-end entry at `len(prompt) - 1` (`engine.entry_end`; a one-token prompt keeps its whole prompt):

- the one-stream cache (`engine.py`, `KEEP_ONE = 4` entries, one GPU and both ranks of two);
- the concurrent decoder's `PrefixCache` (`multi.py`, `KEEP = 3` entries, one GPU and two ranks).

Visible changes:

- A next turn sent back without its reasoning resumes from the previous prompt's entry instead of an older entry or the start.
- A prompt that extends the whole previous prompt prefills one token more. This includes a next turn sent back with its reasoning, and every next turn with thinking off.
- An identical prompt sent again resumes with one token to prefill. Before, it resumed from the longest other entry that is a prefix of it, or from the start.
- `stats["cached"]` reports the entry's length. Tests in `main` that expect whole-prompt entries change for this: `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_multi.py` (a longer prompt's `cached`, and the failed prompt-end copy), `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_client_gone.py` (`cached`) and `tests/test_cuda_failed_admission.py` (the entries). The stand-ins in `tests/test_cuda_failed_admission.py` and `tests/test_qwen27_kv_limit.py` take `keep_at`, `cut` and `owned`.

## Design

References are at `main` (71377a5, 0.3.6.2). `prefill.py`, `decode.py`, `engine.py`, `multi.py` and `dflash2.py` are in `src/tensorfold/families/qwen3_5/cuda/`; `geometry.py`, `markers.py` and `kernels/gdn_prefill.cu` are in `src/tensorfold/cuda/`.

The prefill runs in even chunks of up to 4,096 rows and commits the GDN state from the chain kernel (`prefill.py:88-94`). The state at `n - 1` can come from:

1. **A one-row last span.** Exact, since any bounds give the same bits, but "a short one costs a whole weight pass" (`prefill.py:131`). For the 27B's MLX 4-bit checkpoint that is 13,697,187,840 B read once more on every request. `prefill_stops` keeps message-start states this way.
2. **The chain kernel also writing the state after row `W - 2`.** A CUDA and binding change.
3. **Two launches of the existing chain kernel in the chunk that holds the point** (chosen). No kernel change, no extra weight pass, no extra forward.

Option 3 is exact because the chain kernel loads the fp32 state into registers once (`gdn_prefill.cu:33-38`), steps one row at a time (`:39-94`) and stores fp32 (`:95-98`). A launch over rows `[cut, W)` from the state stored after `[0, cut)` performs the same operations in the same order as one launch over `[0, W)`, so the output rows and the final state keep their bits. Everything else in the chunk still runs once over all rows.

In `prefill.py`:

- `prefill_chunk(cut=c)` runs each GDN layer's chain as `[0, c)` then `[c, W)`, joins the two outputs, and also returns the state at `p0 + c`: the GDN states between the launches, a copy of the last three conv rows of `[old rows | QKV rows before the cut]`, and the chunk's key/value buffers.
- `prefill_state(keep_at=k)` keeps the spans unchanged, passes `cut` to the chunk that strictly holds `k`, and copies the state when `k` is a chunk start or the prompt's end. The kept state's conv rows own storage of their own size (`_own`): a chunk's conv rows are the last three rows of the join `[old rows | chunk rows]`, and `.contiguous()` on them returns a view that holds the whole join. The kept state then points at the prompt state's final key/value buffers. `_grow` can reallocate inside the cut chunk (`prefill.py:43-53`). It copies every committed row, so the kept state's rows are the same bytes. The kept state takes its key/value buffers only after the chunk, so a buffer that a grow replaces is freed at once, as without `keep_at`.
- The drafter's taps start `window` rows before `k` instead of before `n`. The drafter absorbs the cut chunk's rows before the point, is snapshotted, then absorbs the rest. At the prompt's end it holds the same rows as before.
- `prefill`, `prefill_tp` and `prefill_stops` (in `decode.py`) pass `keep_at` through, to the span past the last stop, and return a third item. Two ranks add no collective, since the split chains are each rank's own.

An EXL3 pack of the 27B (one GPU) runs the same `prefill_chunk` and `prefill_state` and uses the same caches. `prefill_chunk` picks only its prompt glue from `w.fast_prefill` (`prefill.py:62`), and the split chain does not depend on it.

The one-stream engine keeps the entry where `main` keeps its prompt-end entry, and keeps the prompt state out of the cache, so the decode can commit into it: `draft_decode` and `decode_tp` take `inplace=True`, which commits into the state given instead of a copy. (`commit(in_place=True)`, new in 0.3.6.2, is a different option: the replay writes into a state's tensors.) Otherwise `generate` would hold the prompt state for the whole reply, one GDN state set more than `main`, whose entry is that state.

The concurrent decoder keeps the entry in the prefill step that reaches the prompt's end (`_step`, `keep_at`). The kept state's GDN states and conv rows are the prefill's own, and no stream decodes into them, so the entry holds them without the copy that `kept` makes of a stream's state (`kept(owned=True)`). Its key/value rows are views of the stream's buffers, as `main`'s entries are. A one-token prompt's entry is the stream's own state and is copied, as on `main`. After each prefill step the drafter keeps no reference of its own to the stream's context (`skip(0)` after the stream's snapshot, `multi.py:158`). On `main` its lists hold the last prefilled stream's prompt-end context until the next prefill step; where a prompt-end entry is kept, that context is also the entry's, and here the entry holds a context of its own. The rounds read and replace a stream's context only through its snapshot (`multi.py:273`, `:307`; DFlash2's reference path restores each snapshot first, `dflash2.py:339`, `:495`), so no proposal changes.

## Exactness

The goal is bit-identical results to `main` on the prompt's state, last logits and first token, and a kept state equal to a fresh prefill of `prompt[:n - 1]`.

- **Prompt state, logits, first token.** Unchanged: the only change in the forward is the split chain, above.
- **Kept state.** It is a fresh prefill of the first `n - 1` tokens under the existing contract that prefill bits do not depend on chunking (`prefill.py:1`, `:131`; `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_prefill.py:74`, `:83`, `:161`, `:182`). The GDN state is the chain's after row `cut - 1`, the conv rows are that row's window, and the key/value rows below the point are the rows the chunk wrote.
- **Resumes.** A resume from the kept state follows the existing rule: a kept state resumes with a fresh prefill's bits.
- **Drafter.** It only proposes, and the target verifies every token.

This is argued from the kernel and checked on the host with CPU stand-ins for the kernels. It has not been checked on a GPU.

## Memory and cost

Derived from sizes and code, not measured. Sizes are from the checkpoint's `config.json`: 48 of 64 layers are GDN, with 48 value heads of 128, 16 key heads of 128 and 3 conv rows; the other 16 have 4 key/value heads of 256.

- **Entries.** The number of entries is unchanged. A prompt-end entry now holds the state after `prompt[:n-1]`, so it has `n - 1` key/value rows instead of `n`; a concurrent entry views those rows of its stream's buffers.
- **Key/value buffers.** None beyond `main`'s. The kept state takes the final buffers after the cut chunk, so a grow inside that chunk frees the old buffers at once. For a fresh 64,001-token prompt without a limit, the cut chunk grows them from 64,000 rows to 128,000 (the one-stream engine caps them at its admitted window); the old ones are 4,194,304,000 B (65,536 B a row over the 16 attention layers).
- **GDN state sets.** The kept state owns one set (153,944,064 B with its conv rows). One stream: one set more than `main` during the prefill's last chunk. During the decode, the same as `main` where an entry is kept at the end, and one set fewer where a message start covers the end, since `main` then holds the prompt state for the whole reply while it decodes into a copy. `--parallel N`: in the prefill step that ends a prompt, the kept state holds one set beside the stream's from the cut on, and `main` makes its second set at the step's end by copying the stream's (`kept`). The step's count at its end is `main`'s and inside `(2 * streams + keep + 2)` sets (`geometry.py:280`).
- **A turn that resumes from the `n - 1` entry where `main` misses** (one stream; turn 3 of the three-turn conversation): this branch keeps the entry it resumed from, which `main` drops, so that turn holds one GDN state set more than `main` in both the prefill and the decode, beyond the set above, and one drafter context more with the drafter: 153,944,064 B per phase, 196,050,944 B with the drafter.
- **Drafter contexts** (with a drafter). The prefill can hold one drafter context more: 42,106,880 B for the DFlash2 checkpoint (`draft_geometry`'s size of one context, `geometry.py:257-260`). From the decode's second round both branches hold the same number of contexts and GDN state sets (with `--parallel N`, where a message start covers the prompt's end, this branch holds one context fewer: `main`'s drafter lists keep that stream's prompt-end context until the next prefill step); a one-round reply holds one GDN state set and one drafter context more than on `main`. With one stream, the drafter's admission prices no context for the entries' snapshots (`geometry.py:257`, `engine.py:71-73`), on `main` as here, so the added context is outside it, as those snapshots are.
- **Transient.** Joining the two chain outputs holds one more output buffer, one GDN layer at a time: up to 50,331,648 B (4,096 rows × 12,288 B).
- **Per request, on the chunk that holds the point:** 48 more chain launches; one copy to join the outputs, 589,824 B a row over all GDN layers (2,415,919,104 B written and read for a 4,096-row chunk); with a drafter, one more tap row and one more `add_taps` call. No extra pass over the weights.

## Evidence

Surface: a host fixture on the public checkpoint's chat template and tokenizer, `Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit` at revision `70ae7fac63274ff2eac54152031433374cb80f2f` (the repository's head on 2026-09-28). Prompts are rendered and encoded as the CUDA server does (`ChatTemplate`, then `Tokenizer.encode`, `cuda/server.py:171-176`), and this branch's own lookups (`Qwen27Engine._resume`, `PrefixCache.longest`) pick the entry. No model ran.

The conversation: user "What is the capital of France?", assistant "Paris.", user "And of Italy?". Its prompts are too short for a state at a message start.

| Case | Turn 1 prompt | Turn 2 prompt | Whole-prompt entry (`main`) | Entry at `n - 1` (this change) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Thinking on, reply sent back without reasoning | 59 tokens, ends `<think>` 198 | 79 tokens, 271 at position 58 | no match | resumes at 58 |
| Thinking on, reply sent back with `reasoning_content` | 59 tokens, ends `<think>` 198 | 89 tokens, extends turn 1 | resumes at 59 | resumes at 58 |
| Thinking off | 19 tokens, ends `</think>` 271 | 39 tokens, extends turn 1 | resumes at 19 | resumes at 18 |

In the first case turn 2 prefills 79 tokens on `main` (there is no other entry) and 21 with this change. In the other two, this change prefills one token more.

With the checkpoint's message starts (`markers.resume_points`) and a long first user message, through the one-stream engine's own bookkeeping (`_resume`, `_stops`, `_ends`): thinking on, replies ("Paris.", then "Rome.") sent back without reasoning.

| Turn | Prompt | `main` | This change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 601 tokens | keeps the state at the last assistant start (596), no prompt-end entry | the same |
| 2 | 621 tokens | resumes at 596 (25 to prefill), keeps an entry at 621 | resumes at 596 (25 to prefill), keeps an entry at 620 |
| 3 | 642 tokens | the entry at 621 does not match; resumes at 596 (46 to prefill) | resumes at 620 (22 to prefill) |

To reproduce (the weights are not needed):

```
hf download Vontra/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit config.json tokenizer.json tokenizer_config.json chat_template.jinja --revision 70ae7fac63274ff2eac54152031433374cb80f2f
python3 -m pytest tests/test_qwen27_prompt_end_template.py -v
```

Measured effect on a GPU (exactness of each turn and the resumed turn's prefill time on these conversations): GPU run pending.

## Tests

Host: macOS, Python 3.13.5, PyTorch 2.11.0 CPU, an import-only Triton stand-in. No kernel ran.

- `tests/test_qwen27_prompt_end_cache_host.py` (new, 262 cases):
  - the one-stream engine's entries and resumes with stand-ins for `prefill`, `prefill_tp`, `draft_decode` and `decode_tp`, including both ranks of two, and beside message starts (the last one 256 tokens or more before the prompt's end, and less);
  - the concurrent decoder on the real `prefill_state`, `private` and `kept` with a stand-in chunk: entries and resumes on one GPU and both ranks of two, prompts filled in steps of `STEP` rows, message starts, a one-token prompt, and entries that keep their GDN states while their streams decode in place;
  - the concurrent decoder's drafter contexts, with a stand-in drafter that allocates them as DFlash2's fused path does, on one GPU and both ranks of two: at a decode's start and after its first commit every context allocated is an entry's or a decoding stream's, and after the first commit no more rows are allocated than with the whole-prompt entry;
  - `prefill_state`'s spans, cuts and drafter calls with a stand-in chunk;
  - the prefill on row-wise CPU stand-ins for the kernels, which checks the code around the kernels, not the kernels, including message starts with a point past them;
  - `prefill_tp` itself on the same stand-ins, as one process holding every weight, ranks 0 and 1, against `prefill`;
  - a fresh prefill with `keep_at` holds no key/value buffer after a grow replaces it;
  - the kept state's conv rows own storage of three rows a layer, at a cut, a chunk start and the prompt's end, from a fresh prefill and a resumed one.
- `tests/test_qwen27_prompt_end_template.py` (new, 5 cases): both conversations above on the checkpoint's own template and tokenizer. It skips unless those files are in the Hugging Face cache.
- `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_prompt_end_cache.py` (new, GPU): a toy model with the 27B's layer pattern, with raw-byte comparisons of every GDN state, conv window, key/value row below `pos`, and the sampled logits:
  - a cut chunk against one launch: cuts at 1 to 4, 31 to 33, 64, 128, 298 and 299 of 300 rows, from 0 and from 137 tokens;
  - `keep_at` against none: prompts of 1 to 4, 127 to 129, 300, 4,097 and 4,099 tokens, points at chunk starts, inside chunks and at the end; spans of 7 and 64 rows;
  - the next turn (`<think>\n` then `<think>\n\n`), a resumed prefill, longer and repeated prompts, each resumed from the kept state against a fresh prefill, greedy and sampled;
  - buffers grown inside the cut chunk (resumes at 1,000 and 2,000 tokens);
  - the drafter's taps against a prefill without `keep_at` and a prefill of the prefix;
  - `inplace` decoding;
  - the engine end to end, with and without message starts, against a fresh engine and the serial reference, with every entry against a fresh prefill;
  - the concurrent decoder end to end against the serial reference, and every entry against a fresh prefill after its stream decoded in place: a one-token prompt, and prompts filled in steps of 5 rows, one of them from the point.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_qwen27_prompt_end_cache_host.py` on this change | 262 passed |
| `test_qwen27_prompt_end_template.py` on this change, tokenizer files at the revision above | 5 passed (5 skipped without them) |
| Both files on `main`'s sources | collection error: `entry_end` does not exist |
| `test_qwen27_kv_limit.py` and `test_cuda_failed_admission.py` on this change | 20 passed |
| Whole host suite (`tests` without `tests/cuda`), `main` | 136 failed, 2,082 passed, 299 skipped, 18 errors |
| Same, this change (no tokenizer files in the cache) | 136 failed, 2,344 passed, 304 skipped, 18 errors |
| GPU file, CPU dry run (row-wise kernel stand-ins, dequantising matmul) | 85 passed; the 20 tests that decode were deselected, since they need the tree kernels |

The same 154 ids fail or error in both whole-suite runs, none in a file this PR adds or changes. Their causes include the import-only Triton stand-in (no `triton.backends`), no `transformers` tokenizer, MLX 0.31.1 where GLM-5.3-Flash needs 0.32.2, a memory-window test that expects a Mac with 64 GiB or more (this one has 36 GiB), and files outside the test tree used here (`tools/`, `CHANGELOG.md`). The five added skips are the template file.

Twenty-eight one-line breakages of the change were each applied alone. Twenty-six fail the host file, among them a concurrent entry that shares its stream's GDN states, one that copies them, an entry kept where a message start covers the prompt's end, and a concurrent drafter that keeps its own lists after a prefill step. The other two make `draft_decode` or `decode_tp` ignore `inplace`; they change memory only (the decode commits into a copy, so the prompt end's GDN states stay held for the reply). `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_prompt_end_cache.py` checks `draft_decode`'s `inplace` on a GPU. No test checks `decode_tp`'s. An entry at the whole prompt also fails the template file.

## GPU status

GPU run pending, in this order. A timing counts only after every exactness step before it has passed.

1. On a GB10: `python3 -m pytest tests/cuda/test_qwen27_prompt_end_cache.py tests/cuda/test_qwen27_multi.py tests/cuda/test_qwen27_client_gone.py -q`, then `python3 -m pytest tests/cuda -q`.
2. The 27B on one GPU through `Qwen27Engine`, with the drafter, this branch against `main`:
   - the fixture's two turns (thinking on, reply sent back without reasoning): after each turn's prefill, the committed state's hashes (48 GDN states, 48 conv windows, 16 layers' key/value rows below `pos`) and the last-row logits' hashes are equal, taken from `prefill`'s return before the decode; the entry at `n - 1` (58 tokens) equals `main`'s fresh prefill of the same tokens; turn 2, resumed from it (`stats["cached"]` 58 here, 0 on `main`), equals a fresh prefill (state, last logits, first token);
   - the three turns with message starts: the state at 596 and the entry at 620 equal fresh prefills of those tokens; turn 3, resumed from 620 (`stats["cached"]` 620 here, 596 on `main`), equals a fresh prefill.
3. One reply hash per turn, equal to `main`'s and to the serial reference's.
4. Peak memory, reset before each phase, over each turn's prefill and over its decode, and over the prefill of a fresh 64,001-token prompt (its cut chunk grows the key/value buffers), this branch against `main`, without and with the drafter, one stream and `--parallel 2`. Compared in bytes requested by tensors (`torch.cuda.memory_stats()["requested_bytes.all.peak"]`); allocated bytes (`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated`), which count cache blocks rather than tensor sizes, are recorded too. Expected from the code, in requested bytes: the prefill at most 204,275,712 B higher (one GDN state set and the join), plus 42,106,880 B with the drafter; the decode no higher for a reply of two rounds or more. Exception, one stream: a turn that resumes from this branch's `n - 1` entry where `main` misses its prompt-end entry (turn 3 of the three-turn conversation: 620 here, 621 missed on `main`) also keeps that entry, which `main` drops, so it holds one GDN state set more in both phases: 153,944,064 B more in each limit, 196,050,944 B with the drafter (one more drafter context).
5. `--parallel 2`, two ranks (two GB10s), and an EXL3 pack of the 27B on one GPU (`turboderp/Qwen3.8-27B-exl3`, `4.00bpw`): the same hashes against `main`; on two ranks, both hold the same entries. Until then, two ranks are covered by host tests only, EXL3 packs by none, and `decode_tp(inplace=True)` runs in no test.
6. Prefill time of the resumed turn on this branch against `main` (`stats["prefill_s"]`, which ends after the first token's copy to the host, `cuda/sampling.py:18-28`): on the fixture, on turn 3 of the three-turn conversation, and on the fixture with the first user message lengthened so that turn 2 spans more than one 4,096-row chunk. Also the cost on a prompt with no follow-up: the same prompt on both branches, alternating, for a 4,096-row chunk and a short one.

## Overlaps

- Issue #38's cross-request prefix caching is in `main` since 0.3.6.2 (2fbebf7): states at message starts in both caches, and prefill steps in the concurrent decoder. This PR keeps those rules. The states at message starts are unchanged, and no prompt-end entry is kept where a start covers the prompt's end. Where a prompt-end entry is kept, it now ends one token earlier.
- #57, #58 and #59 are in `main` since 0.3.6.2. This PR is rebased onto them: the one-stream prefill passes `limit=` and `keep_at=`, and the concurrent entry is kept in `_step`, which replaced `_admit`. Their tests that expect whole-prompt entries, or that stand in for functions this PR extends, change here (listed in the Summary).
- The `ignore_eos` change in #63, as rebased onto 0.3.6.2, passes `stop_eos=` where this PR passes `inplace=True`: 2 conflict blocks in `engine.py`, both on keyword lines; `multi.py` merges clean. On a host merge with both sides kept, both PRs' host files pass once the stand-ins take the other's keywords (`draft_decode` and `decode_tp` here; `prefill`, `prefill_tp`, `prefill_state` and `kept` there): 477 passed, 5 skipped. Its GPU test `test_engine_decodes_past_end_tokens_and_keeps_only_prompt_ends` expects whole-prompt entries. With this change a repeated or longer drafted prompt resumes from an earlier prompt's entry at `n - 1`, so the test's expected `cached` values (0, 0, 5, 5 for its drafted runs) become 0, 4, 4, 7, and its entries end one token earlier (read from the code; GPU only, not run).
- #80 (response_format JSON schemas on the 27B) edits `decode.py`, `decode_tp.py`, `engine.py` and `multi.py` of this family: 6 conflict blocks. In `decode.py` (3): `prefill`'s signature and its end (this PR's `keep_at` item against #80's grammar mask and advance on the last row) and `draft_decode`'s signature (`inplace` against `constraint`). In `engine.py` (2): the one-GPU prefill (the entry at `entry_end(prompt)` against `constraint=`) and the `draft_decode` call (`inplace=True` against `constraint=`). In `multi.py` (1): `_step`'s first token and entry (the entry at `end` against `first_token(..., s.constraint)`). `decode_tp.py` merges clean. Resolution tested: both keywords in the signatures and calls; at `prefill`'s end, #80's grammar mask and advance on the last row, then the kept state returned as the third item; in `multi.py`, #80's grammar-aware first token and this PR's entry at `n - 1`. The grammar follows only the reply's tokens, so resuming from the entry at `n - 1` does not change what it masks (from the code). With this PR's one-GPU `prefill` and `draft_decode` stand-ins taking `constraint`, both PRs' host test files pass: 307 passed; 19 skipped (this PR's 5 template tests without the tokenizer files, and 14 of #80's cases that need xgrammar, which is not installed on the test host). #80's GPU test checks no cache entries. These results are for the merged tree.
- #61, as rebased onto 0.3.6.2, also edits `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_client_gone.py`, on another line; the merge is clean. #62, #64, #67, #73, #74, #75, #78, #79 and #82 share no file with this PR.

## Not in this change

- **Other families.** `glm5_next`, `qwen4_exp`, `nemotron_h` (`cuda/app.py`) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (`qwen3_5_moe`) have their own prefix caches. Qwen3.6 keeps whole-prompt entries by the same rule as the 27B on `main` (`qwen3_5_moe/cuda/engine.py:105-106`). They are unchanged here and were not checked for the same one-token miss.
- **`preserve_thinking: false`.** With it, earlier assistant turns render without `<think>` (`chat_template.jinja:116`, `:119`), so neither entry is a prefix of the next prompt.
- **More entries.** The counts stay `KEEP_ONE` and `KEEP`.
